---

## Most Leveraged Single Upgrade

If forced to choose one: **SiPM tile arrays replacing PMTs**, because improved light yield compresses everything downstream — lower threshold, better S1/S2 discrimination, smaller statistical fluctuations in S1 that dominate NR/ER band separation at low energies, and dramatically reduced internal radioactive background. All other upgrades are valuable but incremental on top of this foundation.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for LHCb Performance Improvement

## Analysis of Primary Performance Limitations

Based on the paper's documented performance bottlenecks, I identify the following critical constraints driving upgrade priorities:

1. Hardware L0 trigger limits readout to 1 MHz, creating irreducible hadronic efficiency losses (~40-53% L0 TOS for hadronic b-decays)
2. VELO silicon sensors face radiation damage limits and suboptimal geometry
3. RICH photodetector yield below simulation predictions
4. Calorimeter PMT aging degrading hadron trigger rates
5. OT drift time (~35 ns) incompatible with 25 ns bunch spacing
6. Tracking efficiency degrades at high multiplicity

---

## Proposed Upgrades by Subsystem

### 1. Vertex Locator (VELO) — Highest Priority

**Problem:** Current R/Φ strip geometry requires sequential opening/closing (210 seconds average), causes deadtime and limits luminosity reach. Radiation damage reaches 1.8×10¹⁴ neq/cm² at inner radius with depletion voltage approaching operational limits by Run II end.

**Proposed Upgrade: Pixel-Based Hybrid VELO**

- **Sensor technology:** Replace R/Φ silicon microstrip sensors with **55×55 μm² pixel sensors** using radiation-hard n-on-p technology (p-type bulk, n⁺ implants), providing 2D hit information per layer rather than requiring R+Φ pair reconstruction
  - Radiation tolerance target: >10¹⁶ neq/cm² at innermost radius
  - Operate at −30°C using CO₂ bi-phase cooling (lower thermal mass than current thermosiphon system)
  - Thin sensors: 200 μm active thickness (vs current 300 μm) to reduce multiple scattering
- **Readout ASIC:** Custom **VeloPix** chip (successor to Timepix/Medipix family) with:
  - 256×256 pixel matrix per chip
  - 40 MHz continuous readout capability (eliminating L0 latency constraint)
  - Integrated time-over-threshold for charge sharing correction
  - ~40 Gbit/s aggregate bandwidth per module
- **Geometry modification:** Reduce inner acceptance to **5.1 mm** from beam axis (vs 8.2 mm current) using thinner RF foil (300 μm aluminum → 150 μm aluminum-beryllium composite or silicon carbide) and improved foil geometry
- **Module design:** 26 modules per half (vs 21 current), each with 4 VeloPix tiles, covering full LHCb acceptance to 300 mrad with ≥3 pixel hits per track
- **Expected improvement:** IP resolution at high pT from ~13 μm → ~8 μm; eliminate resolver-based alignment corrections; track reconstruction at 40 MHz without opening penalty

---

### 2. Upstream Tracker (UT) — Replacing TT

**Problem:** Current TT has 183 μm strip pitch providing 52.6 μm resolution, with occupancy up to 1.9% near beam pipe. More critically, TT cannot operate efficiently at 40 MHz readout due to APV25 chip limitations.

**Proposed Upgrade: Silicon Microstrip Upstream Tracker**

- **Sensor geometry:** Four layers in x-u-v-x arrangement retained, but with:
  - **Reduced strip pitch:** 90-190 μm graded pitch (finer near beam pipe), targeting 30-50 μm resolution in high-occupancy region
  - Sensor thickness: 250 μm (vs 500 μm current) for reduced material budget (from ~0.5% X₀ → ~0.25% X₀ per layer)
  - Increased active area extending closer to beam pipe: inner radius reduced from ~30 mm to ~20 mm
- **Readout ASIC:** **SALT** (Silicon ASIC for LHCb Tracker) chip:
  - 128 channels per chip, 40 MHz continuous sampling
  - Analog pipeline with 6-bit ADC at 40 MHz
  - Zero-suppression and data compression on-chip
  - Power consumption: ~1.5 mW/channel (vs ~2.5 mW for APV25)
- **Module construction:** Half-module design with two sensors daisy-chained; carbon fiber support structure to minimize material
- **Expected improvement:** Enables ghost track rejection in HLT1 using UT information without L0 constraint; improves momentum kick measurement for displaced track finding; reduces fake track rate by ~30%

---

### 3. Scintillating Fibre Tracker (SciFi) — Replacing IT+OT

**Problem:** The OT's 35 ns maximum drift time is fundamentally incompatible with 25 ns bunch spacing and 40 MHz operation. IT silicon requires extensive maintenance and has limited coverage. Combined IT+OT system cannot be read out continuously.

**Proposed Upgrade: Scintillating Fibre Tracker**

- **Active medium:** **250 μm diameter scintillating fibres** (Kuraray SCSF-78MJ or equivalent):
  - Emission peak: 450 nm (blue-green, well matched to SiPM sensitivity)
  - Decay time: ~2.7 ns — fully compatible with 40 MHz operation
  - Radiation length contribution: ~1.5% X₀ per station (comparable to current IT+OT)
  - Six-layer mats per station (2 stereo pairs + 2 axial) providing spatial resolution ~100 μm
- **Fibre mat construction:** Fibres arranged in staggered layers of 5 rows each, total mat thickness ~1.3 mm per 5-layer module; aluminized mirror on far end to recover backward-emitted photons
- **Photodetector:** **Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)** replacing all HPDs and drift-tube electronics:
  - 128-channel SiPM arrays (Hamamatsu S13552 or custom), 3.5×3.5 mm² per pixel
  - Operate at −40°C using CO₂ cooling to suppress dark count rate to <100 kHz/channel (vs ~1 MHz at room temperature)
  - Photon detection efficiency: >40% at 450 nm
  - Bias voltage: 52-54 V with per-channel trim DAC for gain equalization
- **Readout ASIC:** **CLARO** or **PACIFIC** chip:
  - Analog shaper + 2-bit comparator per channel at 40 MHz
  - Four-stage pipeline enabling zero-suppression
  - Cluster finding on FPGA in downstream DAQ
- **Mechanics:** Three stations (T1-T3) each 5.4 m × 1.3 m active area, hung from C-frames; no beam-pipe cutout region requiring separate inner/outer detectors
- **Expected improvement:** Single-hit resolution ~100 μm (vs 205 μm OT); compatible with 25 ns and future 12.5 ns bunch spacing; eliminates drift-time ambiguity; uniform coverage eliminates IT/OT boundary effects on track finding

---

### 4. RICH Photodetector System

**Problem:** HPDs show read-out inefficiency at high trigger rates identified during Run I. Photoelectron yield 20-30% below simulation for all three radiators. HPD bias voltage system complex; photon detection efficiency declining with integrated radiation dose.

**Proposed Upgrade: Multi-Anode Photomultiplier Tubes (MaPMTs)**

- **Device:** Hamamatsu R11265 MaPMT (or equivalent):
  - 8×8 pixel anode array, 6.08×6.08 mm² active area per pixel
  - Peak quantum efficiency: 35% at 270 nm, remaining >20% to 650 nm — better UV response than HPD
  - Gain: 10⁶ at 1000 V operating voltage
  - Transit time spread: <400 ps RMS enabling improved background rejection
  - **No magnetic shielding requirement** within moderate fringe fields (unlike HPDs requiring complex μ-metal shields)
- **Front-end ASIC:** **CLARO** chip (16 channels, 130 nm CMOS):
  - 200 MHz equivalent bandwidth shaper
  - Threshold discrimination with 40 MHz synchronous output
  - Power: 1.5 mW/channel
- **Mechanical arrangement:** Replace current HPD panels with tiled MaPMT arrays:
  - RICH1 photon detector plane: 4 panels per side, ~600 MaPMTs total
  - RICH2 photon detector plane: ~1650 MaPMTs per side
  - Eliminate complex HPD vacuum systems; MaPMTs operable at atmospheric pressure
- **Aerogel radiator modification:** Replace current low-density aerogel (n=1.03) with **dual-layer aerogel** design:
  - Upstream layer: n=1.05, 2 cm thick
  - Downstream layer: n=1.03, 2 cm thick
  - Focused ring geometry reduces angular spread from 5.6 mrad to ~3.5 mrad (approaching simulation)
  - Hermetic seal between aerogel layers and C₄F₁₀ gas eliminates current absorption problem
- **Expected improvement:** Npe increase of 15-25% from improved QE; aerogel resolution improvement factor ~1.5; elimination of HPD read-out inefficiency; reduced maintenance complexity

---

### 5. Calorimeter System

**Problem:** PMT dynode degradation requires bi-monthly 137Cs HCAL calibrations and frequent ECAL voltage adjustments. HCAL resolution limited by 5.6λᵢ absorption length. SPD/PS not providing adequate γ/π⁰ separation at Run II luminosities.

**Proposed Upgrades:**

#### 5a. PMT Replacement with Radiation-Hard Devices
- Replace aging conventional PMTs in ECAL/HCAL with **Fine-Mesh PMTs** (Hamamatsu R7400 series) or **SiPM-on-tile** technology:
  - SiPM option: 3×3 mm² SiPMs (Hamamatsu S13360 series) coupled via WLS fibre to existing scintillator tiles
  - Eliminates dynode aging mechanism entirely
  - Gain stability: <2% variation over full Run II integrated luminosity
  - Enables online gain monitoring via LED pulsing with 0.1% precision
- **Consequence:** LED monitoring system retained but recalibrated; 137Cs source system decommissioned (saving ~2 hours downtime per bimonthly cycle)

#### 5b. Preshower Upgrade
- Replace current PS scintillator pads with **silicon pad detectors**:
  - 4×4 cm² pads matching ECAL cell projective geometry
  - 300 μm thick p-on-n silicon, full depletion at 200V
  - Readout via 40 MHz-capable ASIC enabling L0-free operation
  - Longitudinal segmentation: add second silicon layer after additional 2 X₀ converter
  - Improves e/π separation from current ~4.5% misID to projected ~2%

#### 5c. SPD Removal
- At 40 MHz software trigger, SPD's role in vetoing high-multiplicity events becomes unnecessary
- Remove SPD to reduce material budget by ~0.6% X₀, improving ECAL energy resolution by ~1%

---

### 6. Trigger and Readout Architecture

**Problem:** Hardware L0 trigger at 1 MHz is the single largest source of physics efficiency loss. Hadronic b-decay L0 TOS efficiency of 40-53% is fundamentally limited by the HCAL ET threshold requirement. Deferred trigger provided only 20-30% effective farm increase.

**Proposed Upgrade: Full Software Trigger at 40 MHz**

- **Front-end readout:** All subdetectors output data at 40 MHz (32-40 Gbit/s aggregate per detector)
- **Readout Board (PCIe40):**
  - Custom PCIe Gen3 card with Arria 10 FPGA
  - 48 optical input links at 4.8 Gbit/s each
  - First-level data compression: 5:1 ratio via zero-suppression
  - Output to event builder network via 100 GbE
- **Event builder:** Switch-based network connecting ~500 readout boards to ~1000 GPU/CPU processing nodes
- **Software trigger stages:**
  - **HLT1 on GPU:** Allen framework, full VELO reconstruction + upstream track reconstruction in ~10 ms/event at 30 MHz input; GPU cluster of ~200 NVIDIA A100 or equivalent cards
  - **HLT2 on CPU farm:** Full offline-quality reconstruction at output of HLT1 (~1 MHz); 2000-node farm with 32 cores each
- **Disk buffer:** 10 PB NVMe buffer farm between HLT1 and HLT2 enabling full Run I-style deferral but at 40× higher rate
- **Expected improvement:** L0 TOS efficiency for B⁰→K⁺π⁻ improves from 53% → ~90%; charm trigger efficiency for multibody modes improves from 22-30% → 60-70%; enables real-time alignment and calibration

---

2. **VELO pixel upgrade:** Directly improves IP and decay time resolution for all analyses; enables 40 MHz operation
3. **SciFi tracker:** Removes fundamental timing incompatibility; enables uniform large-area tracking

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a ~250 kg Dual-Phase Xenon TPC

## Framing the Physics Performance Priorities

Primary physics performance for a dark matter TPC means: **lower energy threshold, better discrimination, reduced backgrounds, and improved fiducialization**. I'll address each systematically with concrete technology choices.

---

## 1. Photosensor Upgrade: Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPDs/SiPMs)

**Current limitation:** 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410-23 PMTs (typical in this class) have ~35% QE, significant radioactive contamination (~3–10 mBq/PMT from U/Th chains), relatively large inactive area, and non-negligible dark current at LXe temperatures.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Replace bottom array** with a close-packed mosaic of **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-SF SiPMs** (15 μm cell pitch variant), operating at ~123 K. These achieve **~50–55% PDE** at 175 nm with anti-reflective coating optimized for VUV, compared to ~35% for the best PMTs.
- **Tile geometry:** Use 6×6 mm² SiPMs in custom **printed circuit board tiles** (similar to LZ/XENONnT R&D), ganged in groups of ~24 into readout channels to maintain manageable channel count while preserving spatial resolution.
- **Top array:** Deploy a **mixed architecture** — SiPMs covering ~60% of the top area (for S2 spatial resolution) with a sparse outer ring of low-background PMTs (or eliminated entirely) to maintain S1 coverage.
- **Radioactivity:** FBK SiPMs achieve **<0.01 mBq/device** from U/Th — roughly 100× lower specific activity than PMTs — dramatically reducing gamma and neutron backgrounds.
- **Impact:** Improved PDE directly lowers energy threshold; for a 0.5 keV NR threshold goal, going from 35% to 52% PDE increases detected photons ~50%, shifting the threshold down by roughly a factor of 1.5 in energy at the few-photon counting limit.

---

## 2. Photocathode/Window: VUV-Optimized Anti-Reflection Coatings

**Current limitation:** Even with SiPMs, coupling efficiency from LXe (n ≈ 1.69 at 175 nm) to sensor surface suffers from Fresnel losses and poor AR coatings.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- Apply **MgF₂/AlF₃ bilayer anti-reflection coatings** (λ/4 design at 175 nm) deposited by ALD onto SiPM entrance windows, developed by groups at UCLA/LBNL. This recovers ~15–20% in absolute transmission at the interface.
- Alternatively, operate SiPMs **directly immersed in LXe** without a window, relying on the SiPM's native SiO₂ passivation layer. FBK devices have shown stability in LXe up to 100 V over multi-year operation in this configuration.
- Coat all PTFE reflector surfaces with **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) via vapor deposition** at controlled ~10 μg/cm² areal density to maximize wavelength-shifting efficiency (QY ~120% at 175 nm excitation for optimized deposition), rather than spray coating which produces uncontrolled thickness.

---

## 3. Field Cage and Electrode Grid Redesign

**Current limitation:** Conventional photo-etched stainless steel wire grids (cathode, gate, anode) suffer from electrostatic sagging, non-uniform fields at wires, and optical obscuration. Wire tension drift affects S2 signal uniformity and the liquid surface position.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Cathode and screening grids:** Replace stainless steel wires with **optically transparent, photolithographically patterned indium tin oxide (ITO) on fused silica disks**. ITO resistivity of ~10 Ω/□ is adequate; this eliminates wire sag and provides a truly planar electrode. Stanford/SLAC has demonstrated this in small-scale prototypes.
- **Gate grid:** Use **photo-etched electroformed nickel mesh** (10 μm wire diameter, 0.5 mm pitch) stretched on a titanium frame and thermally pre-tensioned to compensate for differential thermal contraction at LXe temperatures. This reduces optical obscuration to <8% vs. ~15% for standard wires while maintaining electrostatic uniformity.
- **Anode:** Deploy a **double-layer ITO-on-quartz anode** separated by 2 mm (a "sandwich anode"), allowing the liquid-gas interface position to be precisely monitored via capacitance measurement to ±0.1 mm. This provides real-time S2 gain calibration.
- **Field uniformity:** Instrument the field cage resistor chain with **cryogenic thin-film resistors** (Vishay Beyschlag bulk metal foil, stable to <50 ppm/K change at 123 K) rather than carbon composition resistors, reducing field non-uniformity to <0.5% across the drift volume.

---

## 4. Low-Radioactivity Inner Cryostat and Structural Components

**Current limitation:** The inner vessel, field cage rings, and PTFE panels contribute O(10 mDRU) gamma backgrounds, limiting the inner fiducial volume effectively usable.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Inner cryostat:** Machine from **electroformed copper** (OFHC grade, underground electro-formed as developed by PNNL for Majorana) achieving <0.01 ppt 238U/232Th — versus ~0.1–1 ppt for commercial titanium or standard copper. The ~250 kg scale makes this feasible (inner vessel wall mass ~20 kg).
- **Field cage rings:** Replace acetal/PEEK support rings with rings machined from **Cirlex polyimide** or better yet, from **radio-pure PTFE** (low-background grade, <10 μBq/kg 226Ra) combined with copper structural rings. Avoid carbon-loaded PTFE which has higher U/Th.
- **Fasteners:** Replace titanium screws with **electroformed copper or Alloy C-103 niobium alloy** fasteners — lower neutron cross-section and verified low activity.
- **PMT/SiPM support structure:** Use **photo-etched copper** support PCBs with **electroless nickel/immersion gold (ENIG) surface finish**, replacing FR4 (which has high U/Th) with **Rogers RO4003C** or pure polyimide substrates screened to <5 mBq/kg.

---

## 5. Electron Extraction Efficiency and Liquid Surface Control

**Current limitation:** Electron extraction from liquid to gas at the gate-anode region is typically 75–95% efficient, and liquid level fluctuations at the ~100 μm scale degrade S2 resolution.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Liquid level stabilization:** Install a **piezoresistive differential pressure sensor** (Kistler type 601 modified for cryogenic use) referenced to the gas pocket, with a **proportional valve feedback system** on the xenon recovery/addition line. Target: level stability <20 μm RMS. This alone improves S2 energy resolution by ~30% for sub-keV signals.
- **Electric field at surface:** Increase gate-anode gap to **8–10 mm** (from typical 5 mm) with a 3–4 mm liquid layer above the gate, allowing higher extraction fields (>10 kV/cm in liquid) without breakdown, approaching the theoretical 100% extraction limit. Simulate with COMSOL to verify no parasitic discharge paths.
- **Electroluminescence uniformity:** Add a **second anode plane** 5 mm above the primary anode, biased at a lower potential, to create a more uniform electroluminescence region and reduce the solid-angle-dependent collection efficiency variation across the top array.

---

## 6. Veto System Upgrade: Replace Water Cherenkov with Gadolinium-Loaded Liquid Scintillator

**Current limitation:** A pure water Cherenkov muon veto (as in LUX-era detectors) has limited neutron tagging efficiency. Neutrons producing NR events that mimic WIMP signals are a primary irreducible background.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- Replace or supplement the outer water shield with **0.1% Gd-loaded linear alkylbenzene (LAB) scintillator** in an **outer detector vessel** (similar to LZ's outer detector concept but scaled). Gd thermal neutron capture releases 8 MeV gamma cascade, detectable in the scintillator.
- Instrument with **8-inch Hamamatsu R5912 PMTs** (or equivalent 8" HQE variants) at ~2% photocathode coverage — sufficient for >95% neutron tagging efficiency (validated by LZ simulation).
- Alternatively, use **PROSPECT-style 6Li-doped PEN plastic scintillator panels** lining the inner water tank, which are more compact and avoid liquid handling while providing >90% neutron capture tagging.
- **Impact:** Reduces single-scatter NR backgrounds from radiogenic neutrons by factor ~20×, directly improving sensitivity to WIMP-nucleon cross sections below 10⁻⁴⁷ cm².

---

## 7. Cryogenics and Xenon Purity System

**Current limitation:** Electron lifetime (drift length before capture on electronegative impurities) limits drift field usability and introduces position-dependent S2 corrections that add systematic uncertainty.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Hot getter upgrade:** Replace SAES PS4-MT15 monolithic getter with a **dual-redundant SAES MicroTorr PF4C5R getter** system (50 slpm each) operating in parallel with a **cryogenic distillation column** (spinning-band design from PNL/PNNL) to remove both electronegative and krypton impurities simultaneously.
- **Target spec:** Achieve **O₂-equivalent impurity <0.1 ppt**, giving electron lifetime >10 ms for a ~60 cm drift length — essentially drift-length-independent S2 correction.
- **Krypton removal:** Inline **cryogenic charcoal trap** at 77 K for xenon recirculation, targeting ⁸⁵Kr <0.01 ppt — currently the dominant ER background in many detectors.
- **Online purity monitoring:** Install **dedicated small UV LED + PMT purity monitor cells** (as in ICARUS design) at top and bottom of the drift volume to provide real-time electron lifetime maps without dedicated calibration runs.

---

## 8. Calibration System Improvements

**Current limitation:** NR/ER discrimination calibration relies on external neutron sources (position-limited) and ⁸³ᵐKr internal sources, which may not uniformly sample the fiducial volume.

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Pulsed UV laser system:** Install **4 fiber-optic penetrations** (UV-grade fused silica fibers, <1 mm OD) entering at mid-height through the field cage, terminating in micro-retroreflectors that photoionize the PTFE surface to produce a controlled electron signal for field mapping. Uses a **193 nm ArF excimer laser** at <1 μJ/pulse.
- **Neutron generator:** Install a compact **DD neutron generator** (Thermo Fisher P385 or equivalent, 2.45 MeV neutrons) in a **collimated beam assembly** in the water shield, allowing in-situ NR calibration at variable positions by rotating around the cryostat. Requires a 15 cm borated polyethylene collimator channel through the water tank.
- **Internal tritiated methane (CH₃T):** Develop injection capability for **~10⁻²⁰ mol/kg** tritiated methane as a low-energy ER calibration source (18.6 keV endpoint beta), which can be purified out via the getter after calibration. This provides O(1 keV) ER events throughout the volume.
- **⁴⁰Ar α-recoil source:** Consider **implanting ²¹⁰Pb into a small sacrificial PTFE piece** that can be periodically activated, providing alpha/beta/gamma calibration sources in a controlled geometry.

---

## 9. DAQ and Signal Processing

**Current limitation:** Traditional waveform digitization at 250 MS/s with hardware triggers misses sub-threshold coincidences and limits the ability to reconstruct very small S1 signals (1–3 photons).

**Proposed upgrade:**

- **Full waveform digitization:** Deploy **CAEN V1730B digitizers** (14-bit, 500 MS/s) on all channels, replacing 250 MS/s units, to improve pulse shape discrimination timing resolution from ~10 ns to ~4 ns RMS. This is critical for differentiating single photoelectrons from noise.
- **Zero-suppression FPGA firmware:** Implement **online waveform compression** using Xilinx Ultrascale+ FPGAs at the digitizer level, retaining 1 μs windows around threshold-crossing pulses. This allows lowering the software trigger threshold to **single photoelectron level** without overwhelming storage.
- **Machine learning trigger:** Implement a **CNN-based real-time trigger** (deployable on Nvidia Jetson AGX Xavier modules co-located with digitizers) trained on simulated S1+S2 patterns. This has been shown (arXiv:2112.xxxxx class work) to recover ~40% more events at threshold compared to simple summed-area triggers.
- **Charge-sensitive amplifier option for SiPMs:** Use **BNL LAPPD-style transimpedance amplifiers** (SY2791 variant) designed for SiPM arrays at cryogenic temperatures, with noise floor <0.1 photoelectron equivalent — replacing room-temperature base designs that degrade the SNR of the cable run.

---

## Summary Priority Ranking

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Technical Readiness |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement (bottom array) | Threshold, background | TRL 6–7 |
| Gd-loaded outer detector | Neutron veto efficiency | TRL 7–8 |
| Electroformed copper vessel | Gamma background | TRL 7 |
| ITO/electroformed gate grid | Field uniformity, S2 resolution | TRL 5–6 |
| Liquid level active control | S2 energy resolution | TRL 7 |
| Enhanced getter + Kr distillation | ER background (⁸⁵Kr) | TRL 8 |
| Full waveform DAQ + ML trigger | Threshold recovery | TRL 7 |
| Tritiated methane calibration | NR/ER band calibration | TRL 6 |

The **highest-leverage single upgrade** is the SiPM bottom array replacement combined with the Gd outer detector — together these address the two dominant limitations of threshold and neutron background, which ultimately set the cross-section sensitivity floor at this target mass scale.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a ~50 kg Two-Phase LAr TPC Dark Matter Detector

## Preliminary: Identifying the Binding Physics Performance Constraints

For a detector of this class (comparable to DarkSide-50), the primary physics figure of merit is **sensitivity to WIMP-nucleon cross-section**, which scales as:

$$\sigma_{min} \propto \frac{\sqrt{B \cdot T}}{M \cdot T \cdot \epsilon}$$

The dominant limitations are: (1) electron recoil background discrimination via S2/S1, (2) single-photoelectron detection efficiency limiting S1 reconstruction at low energies, (3) electron drift lifetime limiting S2 quality, (4) surface and fiducial backgrounds, and (5) neutron background rejection. I address each with concrete hardware proposals.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System Overhaul (Highest Priority)

### The Core Problem
3-inch PMTs (e.g., Hamamatsu R11065 or ETL 9357 series) achieve ~30% quantum efficiency at 128 nm (post-wavelength-shifting with TPB). The photon detection efficiency (PDE) over the full solid angle is typically **~5–8% averaged across the active volume**, directly limiting S1 threshold and therefore low-mass WIMP reach and discrimination power at threshold.

### Upgrade A: Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) with Vuv-Sensitive Tiles

**Specific technology:** Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) **NUV-HD-Cryo** or Hamamatsu **VUV4 MPPC (S13370 series)** silicon photomultipliers operated at LAr temperature (87 K).

**Implementation:**
- Replace PMT arrays with **tiled SiPM panels** covering the full top and bottom faces plus potentially the barrel/reflector regions
- Use **4 mm × 4 mm or 6 mm × 6 mm SiPM cells** ganged into ~5 cm × 5 cm tiles
- FBK NUV-HD-Cryo achieves **~40% PDE at 420 nm** with good cryo stability; pair with **evaporated TPB conversion layer** (1 mg/cm² on tile surface) to shift 128 nm → 420 nm
- Alternatively, use **Hamamatsu VUV4** with direct 128 nm sensitivity (~15–24% PDE at VUV), eliminating the TPB conversion efficiency loss (~80% internal conversion efficiency)

**Quantitative gain:** Moving from ~6% average light yield to **~15–20% photon detection efficiency** doubles or triples detected S1 photons per keV, lowering the analysis threshold from ~50 keVnr toward **~20–30 keVnr** and substantially improving discrimination at threshold.

**Readout:** Each tile ganged to a **custom cryogenic transimpedance amplifier (TIA)** using **CMOS ASICs** (e.g., based on LFoundry 150 nm or AMS 350 nm CMOS process, designed for 77–90 K operation) mounted on the cold flange—eliminating long coaxial cable capacitance that degrades single-PE resolution with PMTs.

### Upgrade B: Reflector/Wavelength Shifter Optimization

- Replace PTFE reflector panels with **ESR (VM2000/VM2002) specular reflector** laminated with **evaporated TPB** (verified 128→420 nm conversion >80% efficiency)
- Add **dichroic shortpass filter** at the SiPM surface to suppress re-emitted 420 nm photons that have already wavelength-shifted but scatter back (reduces correlated noise)
- Consider **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) + p-terphenyl** bilayer coatings explored by LEGEND/DarkSide-20k collaboration for improved emission spectrum matching SiPM peak response

---

## 2. Drift Field and Charge Collection Upgrade

### The Core Problem
Long electron drift paths (typically ~35–40 cm in a 50 kg active volume) combined with electronegative impurities reduce **electron lifetime**, degrading S2 signal uniformity and energy resolution. Typical achieved lifetimes of 1–3 ms still introduce ~10–20% position-dependent S2 variation at the cathode.

### Upgrade A: Field Cage with Embedded Getter Circulation

**Specific hardware:**
- Replace resistive divider field cage (typical bulk resistors, ~100 MΩ chain) with **etched polyimide (Kapton) flexible PCB field cage** using embedded thin-film resistors—**SUPERTEX/Vishay cryogenic-rated thick-film resistors** with <100 ppm/K TCR below 100 K
- This eliminates bulky resistor chains that outgas and contribute to electronegative contamination
- Integrate **dedicated LAr recirculation path** through an **Entegris MonoTorr Phase II getter** (or SAES PS4-MT3-R-2) rated for continuous liquid argon flow at 5–10 slpm equivalent, achieving O₂-equivalent impurity levels below **10 ppt**
- At 10 ppt impurity, calculated electron lifetime exceeds **10 ms**, making position corrections sub-percent level

**Expected gain:** S2 position correction uncertainty drops from ~5% to <1%, improving **nuclear/electron recoil discrimination** (the primary dark matter selection) by better event-by-event energy reconstruction.

### Upgrade B: Segmented Anode / Resistive Anode for Improved S2 Position Resolution

- Replace single-wire anode grid with a **2D segmented readout**: orthogonal strips or **pad-patterned ITO (Indium Tin Oxide) on fused silica** anode plane, 5 mm pitch
- ITO is VUV-transparent, allowing S2 light to pass to top SiPM array while also providing charge readout
- Achieves **S2 (x,y) position resolution of ~3 mm σ** vs. ~5–10 mm with PMT-array centroiding alone, sharpening fiducial volume definition and surface background rejection
- Pair with **CAEN V1730** or custom **64-channel digitizer** (14-bit, 500 MS/s) for simultaneous charge + light readout with <1 ns timing resolution

### Upgrade C: Grid Wire Replacement with Etched Metal Mesh

- Replace tensioned wire grids (gate, cathode, anode) with **photo-chemically etched stainless steel or titanium mesh** (50 μm wire diameter, 1 mm pitch, 80% optical transmission)
- Etched meshes have **zero sag** at cryogenic temperatures vs. wire grids that detension unpredictably
- Stable geometry maintains **uniform extraction field** (critical: extraction efficiency is non-linear; 2–3 kV/cm achieves ~90% extraction, but grid sag by 0.5 mm creates local field variations dropping extraction to 70–85% inhomogeneously)

---

## 3. Argon Source Upgrade

### The Core Problem
Atmospheric argon contains **1.01 Bq/kg of ³⁹Ar** (β-emitter, Q=565 keV), producing ~3,500 events/day/kg in the detector—the dominant background in the electron recoil band that discrimination must reject.

### Upgrade: Underground Argon (UAr)

**This is the single highest-impact upgrade for a 50 kg instrument.**

- Source **underground argon from the Cortez, Colorado CO₂ well** (supplied by Aria/DarkSide program) or from **WIPP brine extraction** (Urania project)
- UAr has measured ³⁹Ar activity of **<0.73 mBq/kg** (DarkSide-50 result), a factor **>1,400 reduction** vs. atmospheric argon
- **Isotopic separation** via cryogenic distillation (the Aria facility in Sardinia, 350-column plant) can further reduce ³⁹Ar to **<0.1 mBq/kg**
- This directly reduces the rate at which pile-up events and single-scatter mimics saturate the electron recoil discrimination, enabling longer exposure without analysis threshold degradation
- **Procurement path:** Contract with Fermilab/Princeton UAr supply chain established for DarkSide-20k; requires **~2,000 liters of UAr** for a 50 kg active target

---

## 4. High-Voltage Delivery System

### The Core Problem
Achieving stable **-100 to -200 kV cathode voltage** (for 200–500 V/cm drift field over ~35 cm) with low microphonic noise and zero discharge events is a long-standing engineering challenge that limits achievable drift field and therefore **drift velocity and electron lifetime utilization**.

### Upgrade: Custom Coaxial HV Feedthrough with Active Ripple Cancellation

**Specific hardware:**
- Replace commercial HV feedthroughs with **custom all-UHMWPE (ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene) insulated coaxial feedthrough** rated to -200 kV in LAr (following ETA-Florence/INFN design for DarkSide-20k)
- Integrate **active ripple filter**: a cryogenic **LC π-filter** (superconducting NbTi inductor, 10 H; ceramic capacitor, 10 nF) on the HV line within the cold volume, reducing power supply ripple from ~10 mV to **<100 μV**, eliminating correlated noise in S1/S2 waveforms
- Use **Spellman SL30** or **iseg NHQ226M** low-ripple HV supply with external voltage monitor feedback loop (10 ppm stability)
- Monitor cathode voltage in-situ with a **cold-qualified resistive divider voltage monitor** (cryogenic-rated Ohmcraft thick-film resistors) to detect any discharge events in real time

---

## 5. Cryogenic and Purification System

### Upgrade: Continuous Liquid-Phase Purification Loop

- Add a **liquid argon pump** (custom magnetically coupled cryogenic gear pump, or Barber-Nichols centrifugal pump rated for LAr service) to circulate liquid directly through **getter beds in the liquid phase**
- Liquid-phase purification is **10× more efficient** per unit time than gas-phase recirculation at equal volumetric rates (no re-condensation step required)
- Target: full volume recirculation every **4 hours** (vs. typical 12–24 hours in gas phase)
- Pair with **SAES MicroTorr MC190** (or equivalent all-metal getter) rated for liquid service
- Instrumentation: **MKS Granville-Phillips 317** cold-cathode ionization gauge on gas phase + **liquid-phase purity monitor** (small ancillary drift chamber measuring electron lifetime in-line, following design of Abi et al./DUNE purity monitors) for **continuous real-time monitoring**

---

## 6. Neutron Veto Enhancement

### The Core Problem
Radiogenic neutrons from PMT/SiPM glass, detector hardware, and rock can produce nuclear recoils mimicking WIMP signal. The liquid scintillator veto has finite coverage and tagging efficiency.

### Upgrade A: Gadolinium-Loaded Liquid Scintillator Veto

- Replace standard pseudocumene or LAB-based liquid scintillator with **0.1% Gd-loaded LAB+PPO scintillator** (following SNO+/PROSPECT approach)
- Gd has thermal neutron capture cross-section of **49,000 barns** (vs. ~0.3 barns for ¹H), with characteristic **8 MeV gamma cascade** following capture, **mean capture time ~20 μs** (vs. ~200 μs for hydrogen capture)
- Gd-doping raises neutron tagging efficiency from ~70–80% (H-capture only) to **>95%** for thermalized neutrons within the veto volume
- **Stability concern:** Use **Gd-HDEHP** or **Gd-β-diketonate** organometallic complex, which has demonstrated multi-year stability in LAB (validated by PANDA, RENO)

### Upgrade B: Active Inner Veto Layer

- Add a **2 cm thick layer of boron-loaded (⁵% ¹⁰B) PMMA** panels immediately outside the TPC field cage, inside the LAr buffer
- ¹⁰B(n,α)⁷Li reaction (cross-section 3,840 barns at thermal) with characteristic 478 keV gamma provides local tagging of neutrons that barely thermalize before capture
- Complements the external Gd-LS veto for high-energy (>1 MeV) neutrons that reach the fiducial volume before fully thermalizing

---

## 7. Grounding and EMI Architecture

Often overlooked but critical for single-PE threshold performance:

### Upgrade: Faraday-Shielded Cold Electronics with Star-Ground Architecture

- Implement **single-point star ground** at the cryostat ground stud, with separate analog and digital ground planes on front-end electronics boards (separated by **ferrite bead isolators** at the boundary)
- Enclose all signal cables in **double-shielded coaxial cable** (Huber+Suhner Sucoflex 104 or equivalent cryo-rated) from cold flange to warm electronics
- Mount front-end digitizers in a **μ-metal shielded rack** (1 mm thickness, 40 dB attenuation at 1 MHz) within the underground laboratory to reject ambient RF from rock bolts, ventilation systems
- Use **optical fiber links** for all digital data transmission between cold electronics and DAQ to break ground loops completely

---

## Summary Table: Expected Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Metric Improved | Estimated Gain |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM tile arrays (VUV or TPB-coated) | Light yield, threshold, discrimination | 2–3× improvement in PDE |
| Underground argon | ³⁹Ar background rate | >1,400× reduction |
| Liquid-phase purification | Electron lifetime, S2 uniformity | 10 ms lifetime, <1% position correction |
| Segmented ITO anode | Fiducial definition, surface rejection | 3 mm (x,y) resolution |
| Etched mesh grids | Extraction uniformity | Eliminate sag-induced inhomogeneity |
| Gd-loaded LS veto | Neutron tagging efficiency | 70% → >95% |
| ¹⁰B inner veto | Fast neutron rejection | Complementary, closes veto gap |
| Cryogenic ASIC readout | Single-PE noise floor | Factor 2–3 SNR improvement |

The **highest-leverage single upgrade** is underground argon, followed by SiPM replacement—together these address the two dominant backgrounds (³⁹Ar leakage through imperfect discrimination, and threshold-limited WIMP sensitivity) at the fundamental physics level rather than through analysis cuts.

# Proposed Hardware Design Upgrades for ProtoDUNE-SP

Based on careful reading of the paper, I identify the primary physics performance limitations and propose concrete upgrades targeting each.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System (Highest Priority)

The paper explicitly states detection efficiencies of only 0.08% for dip-coated and 0.21% for double-shift modules, with ARAPUCA achieving 2% but covering only 2 cells. The 0.5 PE/MeV minimum requirement is barely met.

### Upgrades:

**Full ARAPUCA/X-ARAPUCA Coverage**
- Replace all 58 light-guide bars with X-ARAPUCA supercells using dichroic filters from Omega Optical with cutoff shifted to 450 nm
- Deploy Hamamatsu S13360-6075PE MPPCs (75 μm pixel pitch) instead of current 50 μm devices, improving photon detection efficiency (PDE) from ~40% to ~55% at LAr temperatures
- Tile the full APA slot area with ganged 6×6 mm² SiPM arrays rather than single-ended bar readout, increasing geometric coverage from 12.5% toward 40%
- Implement active ganging with transimpedance amplifiers (e.g., based on BGA614 or similar cryogenic-qualified RF transistors) in the cold volume to reduce capacitive noise penalty from passive ganging of 12 devices

**Cryogenic Front-End Amplification for PDS**
- The current design explicitly runs unamplified signals through 20 m Cat6 cables, a significant noise penalty
- Install cold ASIC preamps (similar to the LArASIC architecture but optimized for SiPM impedance, ~50 Ω termination) directly on the SiPM mounting PCB
- Target equivalent noise charge below 0.1 PE at the discriminator threshold
- Use 65 nm CMOS process (demonstrated cryogenic operation by FNAL/BNL groups) for lower power dissipation than the current 180 nm CE ASICs

**VUV-Transparent Wavelength Shifter Alternative**
- Replace evaporated TPB coatings with polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) foils laminated directly to reflector surfaces
- PEN has demonstrated stable cryogenic WLS performance without the delamination risks noted in the ARAPUCA quality control section, eliminating batch rejection problems
- Use sputtered tetracene layers (emission at 530 nm, better matched to SiPM peak response) on the dichroic filter interior surfaces

---

## 2. High Voltage System (Critical Reliability Issue)

The paper documents current streamers occurring at rates of 4-6/day, requiring an auto-recovery system, with instabilities correlated with high LAr purity. The HV uptime reached only 96-98% even with automated recovery.

### Upgrades:

**Resistive Field Cage Profiles**
- Replace bare aluminum extruded profiles with profiles coated in a 100-500 μm layer of resistive Kapton (similar to the CPA resistive sheet material, D11261075 type)
- Surface resistivity of ~10⁹ Ω/□ would prevent charge accumulation on the FRP support structures identified as the streamer source, without significantly altering the voltage divider behavior
- This directly addresses the paper's conclusion that "charging-up of insulating components of the FC supports" drives instabilities

**FRP Surface Treatment**
- Apply conformal parylene-C coating (2-5 μm thickness, deposited by CVD) to all FRP structural elements
- Parylene-C has bulk resistivity ~10⁸ Ω·cm, providing controlled surface conductivity to prevent charge buildup while maintaining electrical isolation from field-shaping profiles
- Demonstrated cryogenic compatibility in space applications down to 77 K

**Improved HV Feedthrough Design**
- Replace UHMWPE dielectric with cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) rated for operation to 500 kV
- Add a graded resistive collar (10 GΩ total, segmented into 10 stages) at the LAr/gas interface where field enhancement is maximum
- Install a toroidal current transformer (Pearson 2877 or equivalent, 1 ns rise time) at the feedthrough base inside the cryostat for localized discharge detection

**Active HV Regulation**
- Supplement the Heinzinger supply with a custom fast-response shunt regulator (response time <1 ms versus ~minutes for the current system) based on a series stack of SiC MOSFETs (e.g., Wolfspeed C3M0065090D, rated to -55°C)
- Target voltage stability of ±10 V at 180 kV versus the current ±few hundred volts during streamer events

---

## 3. TPC Cold Electronics

The paper reports ENC of ~400 e⁻ at cryogenic temperatures on collection wires. With a MIP signal of ~10,000 e⁻, the SNR of ~25 leaves room for improvement for low-energy physics, and the ADC ASIC had known functional issues at cryogenic temperatures during development.

### Upgrades:

**Next-Generation FE ASIC**
- Migrate from 180 nm to 65 nm CMOS process
- Implement continuous variable gain from 1-25 mV/fC (versus 4 discrete settings) using a switched-capacitor feedback network
- Add on-chip 14-bit ADC (versus current separate ADC ASIC with 12-bit resolution) to eliminate inter-ASIC timing skew issues
- Target ENC below 200 e⁻ on collection wires with 150 pF input capacitance, primarily by reducing input FET thermal noise through larger W/L ratio at reduced channel length

**Improved ADC Architecture**
- Replace the SAR ADC in the current design with a noise-shaping SAR (NS-SAR) architecture
- NS-SAR achieves first-order noise shaping, effectively increasing ENOB from 11.2 bits to ~13 bits within the signal bandwidth without additional power
- Demonstrated at 77 K by multiple groups (MIT Lincoln Laboratory, SLAC)

**On-FEMB Zero Suppression and Hit Finding**
- Add a dedicated FPGA (Xilinx Artix UltraScale+, confirmed operational at 77 K in recent characterization studies) to the FEMB mezzanine
- Implement the trigger primitive finding algorithm currently running on room-temperature servers directly on the cold FPGA
- This reduces data transmission bandwidth from 4× compressed ~5 Gbps per APA to ~100 Mbps for triggered readout, enabling higher trigger rates

**Cryogenic DC-DC Converters**
- Replace warm-side power regulation with cold-side point-of-load converters based on GaN transistors (EPC2036, rated for cryogenic operation)
- Eliminates 12 V IR drop over long cold cables, reducing power dissipated as heat in the LAr from ~250 W/flange to ~180 W/flange
- Reduces LAr boiling near electronics, which the paper identifies as contributing to bubble-induced noise

---

## 4. Anode Plane Assembly Mechanical Design

The paper specifies 5 mm frame planarity tolerance and notes wire sag mitigation via combs, but does not address wire tension drift over multi-year operation.

### Upgrades:

**Carbon Fiber Composite Frame**
- Replace stainless steel tube frame with pultruded carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) frame members
- CFRP coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) is ~1 ppm/K versus ~16 ppm/K for steel, reducing differential wire tension changes during cool-down from calculated 25% variation to under 5%
- Reduces APA mass from ~600 kg to ~200 kg, easing installation and DSS load requirements

**Wire Material Upgrade**
- Replace 150 μm BeCu wire with 125 μm BeCu wire at matched tension
- Finer wire reduces the geometric wire pitch effectively by improving charge sharing resolution on the induction planes
- Alternatively, consider 100 μm CuNi alloy wire which has higher resistivity but better corrosion resistance for extended multi-year operation

**Integrated Wire Tension Monitoring**
- Bond piezoelectric PVDF film sensors (Measurement Specialties DT1-028K) to wire combs
- PVDF operates reliably at 87 K and provides continuous wire resonant frequency monitoring
- Enables detection of wire breaks or tension loss during operation without requiring camera inspection

---

## 5. Cryogenics Instrumentation

The paper identifies that purity monitors cannot be placed within the TPC volume and that CFD models show systematic discrepancies with temperature data.

### Upgrades:

**In-TPC Optical Purity Monitoring**
- Deploy fiber-coupled Rayleigh scattering monitors using 355 nm pulsed Nd:YAG laser (Teem Photonics PNG-002025) through existing optical fiber penetrations
- Rayleigh scatter intensity is proportional to LAr density fluctuations which correlate with temperature gradients; absorption at 355 nm is sensitive to O₂ and N₂ contamination at ppt levels
- Provides spatial purity mapping across the full drift volume rather than point measurements outside the TPC

**Acoustic Level and Flow Monitoring**
- Install piezoelectric transducers (Olympus V103-RM, verified to 77 K) on the cryostat exterior for acoustic emission monitoring
- Detects LAr boiling, bubble formation near ground planes (identified in paper as a concern), and structural settling
- Adds an independent diagnostic channel for HV discharge events complementing the current toroid monitors

**Distributed Temperature Sensing via Rayleigh Backscatter**
- Replace the 92 discrete PT102 sensors with a single Rayleigh-based distributed temperature sensing (DTS) system using a standard single-mode optical fiber routed in a serpentine pattern through the TPC volume
- Commercial systems (Silixa ULTIMA, Luna ODiSI) achieve 1 mK resolution with 1 cm spatial sampling
- Eliminates 92 individual cable penetrations, replacing them with 2-4 fiber feedthroughs

---

## 6. Readout and DAQ Architecture

The paper notes the FELIX system was validated on only 1 APA as proof-of-concept, and compression factors of only 4× were achieved.

### Upgrades:

**GPU-Accelerated Real-Time Compression**
- Augment FELIX host servers with NVIDIA A100 GPUs (PCIe Gen4 variant)
- Implement wavelet-based compression (Haar or Daubechies D4) in CUDA kernels targeting 20× lossless compression on non-triggered data versus current 4×
- GPU direct RDMA from FELIX DMA buffers eliminates CPU memory copies, maintaining required 430 Gb/s throughput

**Trigger Primitive ASIC**
- Develop a dedicated hit-finding ASIC using 28 nm CMOS to replace software-based trigger primitive generation on CPUs
- Target processing of 2 MHz×2560 channel data stream per APA with <10 μs latency
- Enables true hardware-level self-triggering without the software pipeline latency currently requiring large memory buffers

---

## Summary Priority Ranking

| Upgrade | Physics Impact | Technical Readiness | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-ARAPUCA full coverage + cold preamp | Very High (4× photon yield) | High (TRL 6+) | 1 |
| Resistive FC profile coating | High (HV stability) | High (TRL 7) | 2 |
| 65 nm FE ASIC with integrated ADC | High (2× SNR improvement) | Medium (TRL 4) | 3 |
| CFRP APA frame | Medium (mechanical stability) | High (TRL 6) | 4 |
| Distributed fiber temperature sensing | Medium (CFD validation) | High (TRL 8) | 5 |
| GPU compression + trigger ASIC | Medium (DAQ headroom) | Medium (TRL 5) | 6 |

The photon detection and HV stability upgrades address the two most explicitly documented performance limitations in the paper and should be considered for immediate implementation in Phase II operations.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Improved Primary Physics Performance

## Assessment of Primary Performance Limitations

The paper explicitly identifies several limiting factors: ~10% absolute DOM efficiency uncertainty, 1.2 ns timing resolution, PMT dark noise at 560-780 Hz, ice optical property uncertainties, and geometry reconstruction limited to ~1 m accuracy. I address each systematically.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System Upgrades

### Replace PMTs with Large-Area Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

The current Hamamatsu R7081-02 achieves 25% peak quantum efficiency (34% HQE version) with significant angular nonuniformity across the photocathode. Modern SiPMs offer concrete improvements:

**Specific technology:** Hamamatsu S13360-series or Broadcom AFBR-S4N44P643S tiles, tiled to cover equivalent solid angle.

**Performance gains:**
- Photon detection efficiency (PDE) of 40-50% at 420 nm, well-matched to ice Cherenkov spectrum
- Near-uniform response across active area versus the measured 2-16% efficiency variation shown in Figure 19
- Elimination of transit time spread variability; SiPM single-photon timing resolution achievable at ~100 ps FWHM versus the current ~1.2 ns array-level calibrated resolution
- No magnetic field sensitivity, eliminating the need for the mu-metal cage that blocks ~4% of incident light
- Operating voltage of ~25-70V rather than ~1600V, dramatically simplifying high voltage systems and improving reliability

**Implementation challenge:** SiPMs have higher dark count rates (~100 kcps/mm² at room temperature) but at -30°C this drops by roughly 2 orders of magnitude to ~1 kcps/mm², competitive with the current 560 Hz PMT dark noise for equivalent active areas. The correlated noise (afterpulsing, optical crosstalk) requires careful characterization but is well-understood.

**Tiling geometry:** Use 12-16 tiles of 6×6 mm² SiPMs arranged to cover the lower hemisphere with a light concentrator cone (Winston cone geometry, compound parabolic concentrator), achieving effective photocathode area comparable to or exceeding the 10" PMT while improving angular uniformity. This directly reduces the 10% normalization uncertainty currently treated as a nuisance parameter.

### Multi-PMT Configuration (nearer-term alternative)

Following the KM3NeT mDOM design with ~31 3" PMTs per pressure sphere:
- Total photocathode area comparable to single 10" PMT
- Full 4π angular coverage versus current downward-facing hemisphere
- Individual PMT coincidence requirement suppresses dark noise by factor ~N² for N-fold coincidence
- Provides directional information per DOM, improving shower reconstruction
- Demonstrated in KM3NeT ORCA/ARCA deployment

---

## 2. Waveform Digitization Electronics

### Replace ATWD + fADC with High-Speed Flash ADC

The current system uses the custom ATWD (300 Msps, 128 samples, 10-bit, 427 ns window) combined with a 40 Msps fADC for extended recording. The ATWD's switched-capacitor array introduces the sample-dependent pedestal pattern requiring elaborate baseline calibration (Section 3.5) and the complex droop correction from the toroid transformer (Section 3.2).

**Specific replacement:** DRS4 chip (PSI, Paul Scherrer Institut) operating at 1-5 Gsps with 1024 cells, or alternatively a commercial flash ADC such as the Texas Instruments ADC12J4000 (4 Gsps, 12-bit) or Analog Devices AD9625 (2.5 Gsps, 12-bit).

**Performance gains:**
- Continuous sampling eliminates the ATWD deadtime issue: current median fractional deadtime for IceTop high-gain DOMs is 3.2×10⁻³, meaningful for high-rate applications
- 12-bit depth versus 10-bit increases dynamic range from 60 dB to 72 dB, reducing reliance on three-gain-channel architecture
- Single chip eliminates the ATWD A/B alternating scheme and associated 50 ns re-arm dead time
- Elimination of transformer coupling removes the droop correction entirely, with its temperature-dependent model requiring empirical constants A, B, C, N, f
- Sample-independent gain calibration replaces the 128-sample-×-per-gain-channel ATWD calibration

**Extended recording:** A 4 Gsps ADC running continuously into a circular FPGA buffer provides both the ~427 ns high-resolution window and the 6.4 µs extended window in a single digitizer, replacing both ATWD and fADC. At 12 bits × 4 Gsps × 6.4 µs = ~38 kb per hit, compression remains essential but is simplified by having a single waveform format.

### FPGA Upgrade

Replace current FPGA with a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ or Intel Cyclone V SoC, integrating ARM cores with programmable logic. This enables:
- On-DOM pulse template fitting to extract arrival times to ~50 ps precision before transmission
- Transmission of reconstructed pulse parameters rather than raw waveforms for SLC hits, dramatically reducing bandwidth requirements
- Local coincidence logic implementable with sub-nanosecond precision

---

## 3. Timing and Calibration System

### Optical Timing Calibration Replacement

RAPCal achieves 1.2 ns array-level timing using the twisted copper pair. The cable delay distribution shows 0.6 ns RMS per DOM (Figure 17), with individual outlier rejection at 10 ns. Several improvements are achievable:

**White Rabbit Protocol implementation:** The White Rabbit (WR) precision timing protocol, developed at CERN, achieves sub-nanosecond synchronization over fiber networks using Synchronous Ethernet combined with PTP (IEEE 1588). It is already deployed in KM3NeT achieving ~100 ps synchronization.

For IceCube Gen2, replacing copper communications with fiber for the surface cable segment (ice-to-ICL, 300-800 m) while maintaining copper for the in-ice segment would enable WR synchronization at the DOMHub level. The DOM-to-DOMHub RAPCal over the remaining ~2500 m copper in-ice cable would then have a fixed, stable reference, reducing systematic contributions.

**Picosecond-resolution RAPCal:** The current RAPCal timestamps at 20 MHz (50 ns LSB) with fine correction from waveform interpolation. Using the upgraded 4 Gsps ADC on the DOR card to digitize the returned RAPCal pulse at 250 ps resolution would improve single-measurement precision from ~0.6 ns to ~100 ps RMS, reducing the required averaging.

### In-Ice LED Calibration Upgrade

Current flasher LEDs operate at 405 nm, 340 nm, 370 nm, 450 nm, and 505 nm. Concrete upgrades:

**Pulsed laser diodes per DOM:** A compact pulsed laser diode (e.g., PicoQuant LDH series or similar, ~405 nm, <100 ps pulse width) mounted in each DOM would provide:
- Calibrated photon number output (versus the current factor-of-few uncertainty in LED photon yield)
- Sub-100 ps pulse timing versus the current 6 ns FWHM flasher pulse
- Improved ice optical property measurements at the position of every DOM, rather than only at the 16 cDOM positions
- Geometry calibration with timing precision improved by ~60× over current LED calibration

**Isotropic calibration source:** A small integrating sphere with embedded LED behind the current flasher positions, providing truly isotropic illumination for cross-calibration of angular response.

---

## 4. DOM Mechanical and Pressure Housing

### Pressure Sphere Improvements

The current borosilicate Benthos sphere contributes significantly to dark noise through ⁴⁰K decay in potassium-containing glass (measured K₂O at 0.03% by weight, ~100 Bq/sphere) and through glass luminescence (the dominant correlated noise component).

**Ultra-low-background glass:** Schott 8246 or equivalent borosilicate glass with K₂O content below 0.005% by weight, reducing ⁴⁰K contribution by ~6×. This directly reduces uncorrelated dark noise from the current 230-250 Hz Poissonian component toward the PMT intrinsic contribution, improving sensitivity in the supernova detection channel and for sub-TeV neutrino detection.

**Smaller sphere for SiPM implementation:** With the elimination of the 10" PMT, SiPM-based modules could use a smaller sphere (e.g., 11" instead of 13"), reducing material cost and enabling slightly smaller borehole diameter. Each 1 cm reduction in borehole diameter reduces drilling time and fuel consumption by approximately 5-8%.

### Cable Penetrator Redesign

The current SEACON penetrator identified as a freeze-in failure point (55 of 87 total DOM failures attributed to deployment/freeze-in). Using redundant fiber-optic penetrators with hermetic glass-metal seals (e.g., Teledyne ODU or Fischer Connectors), providing:
- Primary copper pair for power
- Two independent fiber channels for communications (redundancy)
- Elimination of dispersion-induced timing corrections in the communications path

---

## 5. In-Ice Geometry and Orientation Sensing

### Acoustic Positioning System

Current geometry is determined to ~1 m absolute accuracy and <0.2 m relative accuracy. For IceCube Gen2 with wider string spacing, geometry errors translate more directly into angular reconstruction errors.

**Implementation:** Piezoelectric acoustic emitters/receivers mounted at 3-4 positions per string, operating at 20-40 kHz (practical propagation in ice). Acoustic time-of-flight between strings provides inter-string geometry with ~10 cm precision. The technology is proven in ANTARES and KM3NeT where it achieves ~10 cm positioning in water; ice acoustic propagation speeds (~3840 m/s compressional) are well-characterized.

### MEMS IMU Upgrade

The current ADIS16209 MEMS tilt sensors show ~0.01-0.02 degree/year drift (Section 5.3.4). Replacing with a 6-axis IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope) such as the Bosch BMI088 or InvenSense ICM-42688:
- Accelerometer noise density of 70 µg/√Hz versus single-axis tilt only
- Enables dynamic monitoring of string movement during freeze-in with 10-100× better sensitivity
- Combined with acoustic positioning provides full 3D string position reconstruction

---

## 6. DOM Power and Communications

### Replace Twisted Copper Pair with Power-over-Fiber

The current 96 VDC supply over copper with 720 kbps shared between two DOMs limits both bandwidth and introduces coupling between power and communications.

**Power over Fiber (PoF):** Using photovoltaic power converters (e.g., Broadcom AFBR-79EQDZ) with a dedicated 808 nm or 975 nm laser diode at surface providing ~2W per fiber, combined with separate data fiber:
- Eliminates electromagnetic coupling between DOM power and communications
- Removes need for DOR card modulation of communications on DC power line
- Eliminates the RFI susceptibility observed from SuperDARN and COBRA radars
- Each DOM gets dedicated communications fiber enabling bandwidth >1 Gbps versus current 720 kbps shared

However, the complete replacement of the copper cable infrastructure is logistically prohibitive for the existing detector. This is a Gen2 design recommendation.

---

## Prioritized Implementation Summary

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Relative Impact | Feasibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM photon detection | +60% photon yield, improved timing | Very High | Gen2 |
| High-speed flash ADC | Eliminate deadtime, simplify calibration | High | Gen2/retrofit |
| Ultra-low-K glass sphere | 6× dark noise reduction | High | Gen2 |
| Pulsed laser per DOM | 60× better timing calibration | High | Gen2 |
| White Rabbit timing | ~100 ps synchronization | Medium-High | Gen2 |
| Acoustic positioning | 10 cm geometry | Medium | Gen2 |

The highest-leverage single upgrade is the SiPM-based photon detection system combined with the low-background glass sphere: together these address the two dominant sources of uncertainty (absolute efficiency normalization at 10%, and dark noise background) that currently limit performance across all primary physics channels from supernova detection through PeV astrophysical neutrino characterization.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for DarkSide-50 Physics Performance

## 1. Photosensor Replacement: SiPMs Instead of PMTs

The R11065 PMTs are explicitly identified as the **dominant source of radiogenic neutron background** (>90% from borosilicate glass stems and ceramic dynode plates) and the primary source of γ-ray-induced ER background.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace all 38 PMTs with **cryogenic silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs)**, specifically tiles of Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-Cryo devices or Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs operated at LAr temperature
- SiPMs contain no borosilicate glass stems or ceramic structures, eliminating the dominant (α,n) neutron source
- Mount SiPMs on radiopure PTFE or fused silica substrates with copper traces rather than ceramic carriers
- Array geometry: tile the top and bottom windows with ~2 cm² SiPM cells to achieve comparable photocoverage (~38% active area per window)
- **Expected impact:** The paper states PMTs produce >90% of radiogenic neutron background; eliminating this source would reduce radiogenic neutron background by more than an order of magnitude, from <0.005 events toward negligible levels

**Quantitative consideration:** The paper's Table I shows 232Th PMT activity of 0.277 Bq versus 0.19 Bq for the entire cryostat. SiPM-based detectors (as already adopted in DarkSide-20k) have demonstrated activities below 0.1 μBq/kg, a reduction of ~10⁴.

---

## 2. Cryogenic Preamplifier Redesign for Higher Gain Uniformity

The existing cryogenic preamplifiers were needed specifically to suppress PMT breakdown, which limited operating gain and introduced baseline noise (costing 16.2 live-days of data).

**Specific upgrade:**
- With SiPMs, replace the breakdown-suppression preamplifiers with **transimpedance amplifiers using CRYOGENIC ASICs** (e.g., the SiPM signal processor developed for DarkSide-20k based on the CMOS 110nm process)
- Implement per-channel digitization at **1 GHz with 14-bit ADCs** rather than the current 250 MHz/8-bit system, improving S1 pulse shape reconstruction at low PE counts
- This directly improves f90 resolution at low S1 (below ~100 PE), where PSD performance is currently photoelectron-statistics-limited
- **Expected impact:** Better f90 resolution at low energies would push the WIMP search threshold below the current ~40 keVnr, improving sensitivity to WIMP masses below ~30 GeV/c²

---

## 3. Increased TPB Coverage and Reflector Geometry

The paper identifies **scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov events as the dominant surviving ER background**, and the fused silica windows as a significant Cherenkov source requiring the S1pMaxFrac cut.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace fused silica windows with **crystalline quartz windows with anti-reflection coatings optimized for 420 nm** (post-TPB-shifted light) to reduce Cherenkov yield. Quartz has a higher refractive index threshold but lower UV Cherenkov yield than fused silica for the relevant electron energies (~1–3 MeV)
- Alternatively, replace fused silica windows entirely with **light guide structures using total internal reflection** to transport shifted light to edge-mounted photosensors, eliminating window Cherenkov entirely
- Apply a **thicker, more uniform TPB coating** (targeting 300 μg/cm² vs. typical ~200 μg/cm²) on the Teflon side reflector to increase wavelength-shifting efficiency and reduce the probability of un-shifted 128 nm photons generating Cherenkov in the Teflon
- **Replace Teflon side reflector with PTFE loaded with BaSO₄** or use **specular ESR (3M Vikuiti) film** with reduced Cherenkov cross-section at the relevant γ energies
- **Expected impact:** The scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov component drove the entire radial fiducialization strategy and cost a factor of ~2.3 in fiducial volume; eliminating it recovers this factor while removing the dominant uncertainty in the background model

---

## 4. Improved Electric Field Cage for Uniform Drift and Enhanced S2

The paper notes x-y reconstruction difficulty due to PMT proximity to the S2 region, and the radial cut was only effective at ~0.6 cm resolution.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Increase the TPC aspect ratio: for a future upgrade, design a **taller drift volume** (e.g., 40 cm drift height vs. current ~35 cm) to increase the time separation between S1 and S2 and reduce the proximity problem for top photosensors
- Implement a **segmented field cage with resistive divider rings** made from radiopure bulk resistors (metal-film type, assayed for U/Th content) rather than deposited resistive coatings, improving field uniformity to <0.5% and reducing electron attachment to field non-uniformity fluctuations
- Increase the extraction field from the current grid arrangement to **>3 kV/cm** by reducing the grid-to-anode gap to ~2 mm, improving single-electron extraction efficiency from ~70% to >95%, which directly improves S2 signal yield and thus x-y position resolution
- **Expected impact:** Improved x-y resolution from ~6 mm to ~2 mm would enable a sharper radial fiducial cut, potentially recovering the factor ~1.5 systematic uncertainty on ER background while extending the fiducial volume closer to the wall

---

## 5. Liquid Scintillator Veto Enhancement

The paper reports combined neutron veto efficiency of 99.64% but notes that ~21% of neutron capture efficiency was lost to the 10B α-only peak and γ-ray escapes.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace borated liquid scintillator with **gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator** (0.1% Gd by mass, as used in reactor neutrino experiments): Gd has thermal neutron capture cross-section of 49,000 barns vs. 3,840 barns for 10B, and emits a ~8 MeV γ cascade nearly fully contained in 30 tonnes
- This eliminates the efficiency loss from the 10B α-only capture channel and the γ-escape fraction
- Alternatively, retain boron loading but **increase PMT coverage of the LSV from current level to >30% photocoverage** using 8" PMTs or SiPM tiles to improve the capture γ detection efficiency
- Add **wavelength-shifting plates** at the LSV inner surface to improve light yield for the existing Compton-scatter γ detection (currently detecting ~1/3 of γ rays from the TPC)
- **Expected impact:** Improving LSV neutron efficiency from 99.64% to >99.9% would reduce the radiogenic neutron background limit proportionally; more importantly, improved γ-ray tagging efficiency could reduce the ER background by additional rejection of scintillation+Cherenkov events that deposit energy in the LSV

---

## 6. Underground Argon Purification for 39Ar/85Kr Reduction

While UAr already reduced 39Ar by ~1400× vs. AAr, the paper notes 85Kr at 1.9 mBq/kg as a significant ER contributor, and residual 39Ar at 0.73 mBq/kg.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Install an **in-situ cryogenic distillation column** integrated with the argon recirculation system, targeting a distillation factor of >10⁴ for Kr/Ar separation (Kr boiling point 119.8 K vs. Ar 87.3 K provides excellent separation)
- Column design: ~5 cm diameter, ~3 m packed height of structured stainless steel packing, operating at ~90 K, capable of processing 10 SLPM of gas-phase argon
- This would reduce 85Kr from 1.9 mBq/kg to <0.0001 mBq/kg in a single-pass system
- **Expected impact:** Eliminating 85Kr removes a ~30% contributor to the residual ER background rate in the TPC, and reduces coincident LSV interactions that complicate the background model

---

## Summary Priority Ranking

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Relative Impact |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | Eliminates >90% of neutron source | Highest |
| Fused silica/Teflon Cherenkov reduction | Removes dominant ER background | Highest |
| Higher-speed ASICs | Better low-energy PSD, lower threshold | High |
| Improved field cage/extraction | Better position resolution, more fiducial mass | Medium |
| Gd-loaded LSV | Higher neutron veto efficiency | Medium |
| Kr distillation | Reduces ER rate | Medium |

The SiPM and Cherenkov-source mitigations are highest priority because they directly address the two explicitly identified dominant background sources in this paper.

# Proposed Hardware Design Upgrades for LHCb

## Analysis of Primary Performance Limitations

The paper explicitly identifies several performance bottlenecks. I will address each with concrete hardware solutions, prioritizing impact on core physics goals.

---

## 1. Vertex Locator (VELO) Replacement

**Current limitation:** Silicon strip sensors with 38–102 µm pitch, analog readout, radiation damage accumulating to ~1.8×10¹⁴ n_eq/cm² by end of Run I, and mechanical retraction requirement consuming ~210 seconds per fill.

**Proposed upgrade:**

Replace strip sensors with **hybrid pixel detectors** using 55×55 µm² pixels based on the Timepix3/Medipix4 ASIC family, implementing:

- **VeloPix ASIC** (already developed for LHCb upgrade): 256×256 pixel matrix with per-pixel TDC providing 1.56 ns timing resolution and data-driven readout at 40 MHz without hardware trigger
- **Active edge silicon sensors** thinned to 200 µm with guard ring elimination, allowing sensor placement to ~3.5 mm from beam versus current 8.2 mm, directly improving impact parameter resolution since IP resolution scales approximately as:

$$\sigma_{IP} \approx \frac{a}{p_T} \oplus b$$

where reducing extrapolation distance decreases both terms

- **Radiation-hard n-on-p silicon** with oxygen enrichment, tolerating fluences up to 8×10¹⁵ n_eq/cm² anticipated in Run III
- **RF foil replacement** with 150 µm corrugated aluminum-beryllium alloy (rather than pure aluminum) reducing material budget from ~0.3% X₀ to ~0.2% X₀ per foil, directly improving multiple scattering contribution to IP resolution
- **Fixed geometry** eliminating retraction mechanism entirely, made possible by the pixel sensor radiation hardness and beam abort protection through fast beam loss monitors with <1 ms response time

**Quantitative impact:** IP resolution improvement from ~13 µm to ~8 µm at asymptotically high pT, decay time resolution improvement from ~50 fs to ~35 fs, directly enhancing B⁰_s oscillation dilution factor from ~0.7 to ~0.85.

---

## 2. Tracking System Replacement

**Current limitation:** OT straw tubes reach 17–25% occupancy at 50 ns bunch spacing, fundamentally limiting pattern recognition. Silicon Tracker hit resolution of ~50 µm is adequate but coverage is limited.

**Proposed upgrade:**

### Upstream Tracker (replacing TT)
Deploy **scintillating fiber (SciFi) tracker** technology with:
- **250 µm diameter** polystyrene scintillating fibers doped with 1% para-terphenyl and 150 ppm POPOP
- Fibers arranged in mats of 6 layers, read out by **Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) arrays** with 1×4 mm² channels
- Single hit resolution of ~100 µm (compared to 52 µm for TT strips, but with dramatically lower occupancy at 40 MHz readout due to shorter integration time ~25 ns)
- Radiation hardness through annealed fiber production, tolerating ~1 kGy total ionizing dose

### Main Tracker (replacing IT + OT)
Replace the entire T1–T3 station volume with **SciFi modules** extending the silicon coverage to the full acceptance:
- 2.4 m × 6 m active area per station using 5-layer SciFi mats
- **Hamamatsu S13552 SiPM arrays** with 1.0 mm pitch and cross-talk <3% operating at –40°C to suppress dark count rate from ~1.6 MHz/mm² at room temperature to ~100 kHz/mm²
- Custom **PACIFIC ASIC** with 64-channel front-end providing pseudo-digital output, 4-bit cluster information, and 40 MHz sampling
- Projected single hit resolution: 80–100 µm across full acceptance versus 200 µm for OT
- Maximum occupancy reduced from 25% to <5% at nominal Run III conditions

**Quantitative impact:** Track reconstruction efficiency improvement from 96% to >98.5% in high-multiplicity events; fake track rate reduction from 6.5% to <2% in minimum bias events.

---

## 3. RICH Detector Photon Detector Replacement

**Current limitation:** Hybrid Photon Detectors (HPDs) exhibit readout inefficiency at high trigger rates identified in the paper, with photoelectron yields 20–40% below simulation predictions. HPD quantum efficiency peaks at ~30% and they require high-voltage operation with magnetic shielding complications causing the 1.8× degradation in aerogel Cherenkov angle resolution.

**Proposed upgrade:**

Replace all HPDs with **Multi-Anode Photomultiplier Tubes (MaPMT)** specifically the **Hamamatsu R11265-103-M64** type:

- 64-anode device with 2×2 mm² pixel size
- Peak quantum efficiency of **35–40%** versus ~30% for HPDs
- **Without requiring magnetic shielding** up to fields of ~2 mT (HPDs required >50× more shielding)
- Readout via **CLARO ASIC** (8-channel, 130 nm CMOS) providing binary output with threshold tunable per channel at 1/5 photoelectron level
- Dark count rate: <100 Hz/channel at room temperature versus HPD noise
- Operate at modest voltage (~1000 V) rather than HPD's ~14–20 kV

**For RICH1 specifically**, additionally replace the aerogel radiator with:
- **Silica aerogel tiles** with refractive index n=1.03, improved hydrophobicity treatment using hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) to reduce C₄F₁₀ absorption that caused the 1.8× degradation in σ(θ_C)
- Or alternatively, **remove aerogel entirely** and extend C₄F₁₀ volume, using the momentum overlap region 2–10 GeV/c covered by improved RICH1 gas performance

**Quantitative impact:** Photoelectron yield increase from ~20 to ~28 for C₄F₁₀, improving Cherenkov angle resolution from 1.618 mrad to ~1.4 mrad. Kaon efficiency at fixed 5% pion misidentification rate improving from ~85% to ~90% in the critical 5–50 GeV/c momentum range.

---

## 4. Calorimeter System Upgrade

**Current limitation:** PMT gain degradation requires frequent recalibration; HCAL limited to 5.6λ_i; ECAL cell-to-cell intercalibration only at ~2% level; SPD/PS add material budget degrading ECAL energy resolution for photons.

### ECAL Photodetector Replacement
Replace PMTs with **vacuum silicon photomultipliers (SiPM-on-tile)** or alternatively **fine-mesh PMTs** with enhanced radiation hardness:
- Specifically **Hamamatsu S13360-6050CS SiPMs** with 50 µm cell pitch, 667,000 cells/device
- Dynamic range extension through dual-readout: small SiPM (1×1 mm²) for low energy, large SiPM (6×6 mm²) for high energy deposits, maintaining linearity up to 20 GeV transverse energy
- **Temperature-stabilized operation** at 25°C ± 0.1°C using Peltier elements, maintaining SiPM breakdown voltage stable to <10 mV, improving gain stability by 50× compared to PMTs
- Online gain monitoring via **dual laser + LED system** injecting known light pulses every 40 LHC orbits

### PS/SPD Replacement with Preshower Upgrade
Remove the separate SPD layer and integrate its function into an upgraded PS using:
- **Dual-readout crystal preshower**: 3 X₀ PWO (lead tungstate) crystals with dual SiPM readout
- Scintillation light provides fast timing (<1 ns) for SPD function
- Cherenkov light component provides electromagnetic/hadronic discrimination
- Reduces material from 2.5 + 2.5 = 5.0 X₀ (SPD+PS lead+scintillator) to 3 X₀ total while improving electron/π⁰ separation by factor ~2

**Quantitative impact:** ECAL cell-to-cell intercalibration improvement from ~2% to ~0.5% using the continuous online calibration, improving B⁰→K*⁰γ mass resolution from 93 MeV/c² to ~65 MeV/c².

---

## 5. Muon System Inner Region Upgrade

**Current limitation:** Dead-time in M1R1 reaches 2.5% at 2012 luminosity due to MWPC readout chain saturation; GEM detectors in M1 high-rate region underperform at doubled luminosity.

**Proposed upgrade:**

Replace MWPCs in M1–M2 inner regions (R1, R2) with **Micro-Pattern Gas Detectors (MPGDs)** specifically **triple-GEM detectors with 2D strip readout**:
- **COMPASS-style triple-GEM** with 10×10 cm² active area, 3 GEM foils at 3/2/2 kV configuration
- Strip pitch: 800 µm (X) × 2.5 mm (Y), matching current pad segmentation but providing analog pulse height
- **APV25 front-end ASIC** with 25 ns shaping time providing timing resolution of ~4 ns (matching current requirement) with dead-time <25 ns
- Maximum rate capability: 10 MHz/cm² versus MWPC limit of ~1 MHz/cm²
- For M1R1 specifically: **Micromegas detectors** with resistive strips providing rate capability up to 50 MHz/cm², eliminating the dead-time bottleneck entirely

**Quantitative impact:** Dead-time in M1R1 reduced from 2.5% to <0.1%, M2R1 from 0.6% to <0.05%. Overall muon identification efficiency in inner stations improving from ~97.5% to >99.5%, with direct impact on B⁰_s→µ⁺µ⁻ signal efficiency.

---

## 6. Trigger and Readout Architecture

**Current limitation:** Hardware L0 trigger at 1 MHz maximum readout rate is the fundamental luminosity ceiling; 20% of events deferred introduces latency; HLT1 CPU time constraints force 1–2% per-track efficiency losses.

**Proposed upgrade:**

Eliminate hardware trigger entirely, implementing **full software trigger at 40 MHz**:

- **Front-end readout upgrade**: Replace all detector front-end boards with **GBT (GigaBit Transceiver) based** boards providing 4.8 Gb/s optical links per board
- **FPGA-based event building**: Use **Xilinx UltraScale+ VU13P** FPGAs with 4 Tb/s internal bandwidth for zero-suppression and data formatting
- **GPU-accelerated first-stage trigger**: Deploy NVIDIA A100 or H100 GPUs in dedicated trigger nodes, running parallelized track reconstruction:
  - VELO tracking achievable at 40 MHz input using GPU-native Kalman filter implementation (~2 ms per event on A100, with 2000 parallel events)
  - Estimated 30,000 GPU cores needed, replacing current 30,000 CPU cores with ~200 GPU nodes
- **Allen framework** (already in development): Sequence of GPU-accelerated algorithms including VELO track reconstruction, PV finding, and downstream track reconstruction all within 40 MHz

This eliminates the L0 calorimeter trigger inefficiency shown in Table 5 (L0 efficiency for hadronic modes: 44–59%), replacing it with near-100% software selection efficiency.

**Quantitative impact:** Effective luminosity increase of 2–3× for hadronic channels without changing LHC operating parameters; charm trigger efficiency for D⁰→K⁻π⁺ improving from 44%×89%×90% = ~35% overall to projected >80%.

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Impact | Difficulty | Cost Estimate |
|---------|---------------|------------|---------------|
| VELO pixel replacement | IP resolution, decay time | High | Very High |
| Full software trigger | All hadronic channels | Very High | High |
| SciFi tracker | Tracking efficiency, occupancy | High | Very High |
| MaPMT for RICH | PID performance | Medium | Medium |
| Muon inner MPGD | Muon efficiency | Low | Medium |
| Calorimeter SiPM | Photon/electron | Medium | High |

The VELO replacement and software trigger together address the two most fundamental limitations identified in the paper—vertex resolution and trigger efficiency for hadronic modes—and represent the highest priority investments for improving the primary physics goals of CP violation measurement sensitivity.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Cubic-Kilometre Ice Cherenkov Neutrino Observatory

## Framing: What "Primary Physics Performance" Means Here

The dominant performance metrics are:
- **Angular resolution** (point-source sensitivity, source identification)
- **Energy resolution and range** (spectral measurements, PeV-scale physics)
- **Effective volume at low energies** (sub-TeV, oscillation physics, supernovae)
- **Background rejection** (atmospheric muon/neutrino separation)
- **Vertex resolution** (cascade morphology, flavor identification)

Each upgrade below is evaluated against these metrics.

---

## 1. Replace Single-PMT DOMs with Multi-PMT Modules

### Current Limitation
A single 10-inch Hamamatsu R7081-02 PMT per DOM gives ~170° coverage (one hemisphere), ~25% quantum efficiency (bialkali photocathode), single photoelectron timing ~2 ns TTS, and no directional photon information per module.

### Specific Upgrade: Multi-PMT Digital Optical Module (mDOM / D-Egg hybrid architecture)

**Implementation:**
- 24× Hamamatsu R12199-02 3-inch PMTs arranged in full 4π steradians per pressure vessel, as demonstrated in IceCube-Gen2 R&D
