- Alternatively, 2× 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912-100 PMTs facing opposite hemispheres (D-Egg geometry, deployed in IceCube Upgrade)
- Each small PMT: ~25–27% QE bialkali, but aggregate photocathode area per module increases effective collection by ~35% over single large PMT when accounting for angular uniformity
- Critical addition: **GaAsP photocathode PMTs** (Hamamatsu R13111) at 40–45% peak QE for a subset of channels — currently cost-prohibitive at scale but a priority for the densest inner strings

**Physics gain:**
- Per-module directional sensitivity enables photon arrival direction reconstruction, improving angular resolution by ~30–40% for cascade events
- 4π coverage eliminates the geometric dead zone of single-hemisphere DOMs
- Coincidence requirement between PMTs within one module provides ~10× dark noise rejection, critical for sub-GeV neutrino detection and supernova burst detection

---

## 2. Upgrade Photon Detector Quantum Efficiency: SiPM-Based Modules

### Current Limitation
Bialkali PMT QE peaks at ~25% at 390 nm. Ice scintillation and Cherenkov emission peak near 350–400 nm. PMT dark count rates ~1–3 kHz at -40°C degrade low-charge hit detection.

### Specific Upgrade: Large-Area Silicon Photomultiplier Arrays

**Implementation:**
- Tile the pressure vessel optical window with **Hamamatsu S14161-6050HS SiPMs** (6mm × 6mm cells, 50 μm microcell pitch): peak PDE ~50% at 450 nm, ~40% at 350 nm
- Array of 48 tiles per module, total active area ~170 cm² per module (comparable to 10-inch PMT photocathode area of ~490 cm², but with dramatically higher PDE)
- Preferred alternative: **FBK NUV-HD-SF** SiPMs optimized for near-UV (350–420 nm), PDE ~55% at 380 nm, designed for cryogenic operation
- Operating temperature advantage: at -40°C (IceCube ice temperature), SiPM dark count rate drops to **~10–50 Hz/mm²** vs. ~2 kHz total for PMTs — roughly equivalent total noise at this temperature despite higher intrinsic SiPM DCR/area at room temperature
- Correlated noise (optical crosstalk, afterpulsing) mitigated by: (a) trenched cell isolation in modern SiPMs, (b) waveform-level pulse shape discrimination in FPGA firmware

**Engineering challenges requiring specific solutions:**
- SiPM gain temperature coefficient (~2%/°C) compensated by **on-module PT1000 sensors** feeding real-time bias voltage adjustment via a **DAC on the mainboard** (implemented already in prototype modules)
- Capacitive load of large SiPM arrays demands **transimpedance amplifier front-end** (e.g., based on OPA847 or custom ASIC) with >500 MHz bandwidth
- Radiation damage negligible at 1.5–2.5 km depth (cosmogenic flux suppressed)

**Physics gain:**
- Photon yield per event effectively doubles relative to bialkali PMTs, directly improving energy resolution (scales as √N_photons → ~40% improvement)
- Improved sensitivity to dim, low-energy events (3–10 GeV range relevant for atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements)
- Better single-photon timing through elimination of PMT transit time spread variability (SiPM timing jitter ~200–300 ps vs. ~2 ns for 10-inch PMT)

---

## 3. Waveform Digitization and Timing Upgrade

### Current Limitation
IceCube uses custom **ATWD** (Analog Transient Waveform Digitizer) at 300 MSa/s, 10-bit, with 3 gain channels, plus a slower FADC at 40 MSa/s. Dead time during readout is ~6 μs per ATWD launch. GPS-disciplined timing via the **RAPCal** calibration system achieves ~2 ns RMS inter-DOM timing precision.

### Specific Upgrade A: High-Speed Continuous Digitization

**Implementation:**
- Replace ATWD with **continuous-sampling ADC**: Texas Instruments ADC12DJ3200 (3.2 GSa/s, 12-bit, dual-channel) or **e2v EV12AQ600** (6.4 GSa/s, 10-bit)
- Store in circular buffer on **Xilinx Ultrascale+ FPGA** (e.g., XCZU9EG) with 512 MB HBM2 on-package memory
- Trigger on threshold, read out ±500 ns window — eliminates ATWD dead time entirely
- 3.2 GSa/s at 12-bit: Nyquist frequency 1.6 GHz, captures full PMT/SiPM pulse structure and enables deconvolution-based timing at <200 ps precision

**Physics gain:**
- Eliminates event losses during high-rate periods (muon bundles, calibration)
- Enables waveform-level photon counting rather than charge integration, recovering photon arrival time distributions

### Specific Upgrade B: White Rabbit Precision Timing

**Implementation:**
- Replace RAPCal with **White Rabbit PTP** (IEEE 1588 profile): demonstrated sub-ns synchronization across networks
- Deploy **White Rabbit Switch v4** at surface, run optical fiber timing through existing in-ice cable plant
- Each DOM mainboard incorporates **White Rabbit endpoint FPGA IP core** (open-source OHWR implementation on Xilinx Artix-7 or Lattice ECP5)
- Achieves **<100 ps RMS** inter-module synchronization, confirmed in KM3NeT deployment

**Physics gain:**
- Angular resolution for track events is dominated by timing precision: improving from 2 ns to 200 ps timing would reduce median angular error from ~0.4° to ~0.1° for TeV muon tracks — transforming point-source sensitivity by ~10× in solid angle
- Enables correlation with gravitational wave and FRB observations at sub-millisecond precision

---

## 4. Ice Property Enhancement: Wavelength-Shifting Dopants

### Current Limitation
Bulk South Pole ice has scattering length ~25 m and absorption length ~100 m at 400 nm in the cleanest layers. Dust layers at certain depths (e.g., ~2000–2100 m) severely degrade performance. The refreezing column around each string ("hole ice") has poorly characterized and spatially variable optical properties that dominate systematic uncertainties in directional reconstruction.

### Specific Upgrade A: Wavelength-Shifting Module Coatings

**Implementation:**
- Coat pressure vessel exterior with **perylene-based wavelength shifter** (e.g., bis-MSB or BBQ dye in PMMA matrix, 50–100 μm thick layer)
- Shifts 250–350 nm UV Cherenkov photons (where ice absorption length is <10 m) to 430–480 nm (where absorption length exceeds 100 m)
- Technology demonstrated in liquid scintillator detectors; adaptation to solid coating on glass spheres requires UV-stable binder (fluoropolymer matrix, e.g., PVDF-HFP)
- Gain in effective photon collection: roughly 15–20% additional photons recovered from UV component of Cherenkov spectrum

### Specific Upgrade B: Hole Ice Mitigation via Index-Matched Fill

**Implementation:**
- Inject **low-scattering optical fluid** (e.g., **LAB — linear alkylbenzene** used in SNO+, scattering length >20 m, freezing point suppressants added) into the drill hole before refreezing
- LAB refractive index ~1.48 at 400 nm, closer to ice (1.32) than air, reducing interface reflections at DOM glass sphere
- Alternatively: drill with a **hot-water drill profile that minimizes bubble column** in the refreezing zone using controlled slow-freeze thermal management (heater elements on cable)
- Reference: PINGU/IceCube-Upgrade "flasher-based hole ice characterization" programs show hole ice is the dominant DOM-level systematic; controlled fill reduces this uncertainty from ~±30% effective QE variation to ~±5%

---

## 5. String Geometry and Spacing Optimization for the Dense Core

### Current Limitation
IceCube string spacing of 125 m horizontal, 17 m vertical DOM spacing, optimized for TeV–PeV range. DeepCore inner strings at 72 m spacing lower threshold to ~10 GeV. Physics below ~5 GeV is inaccessible.

### Specific Upgrade: Ultra-Dense Low-Energy Core (ULDEC)

**Implementation:**
- **7 additional strings** at 20 m spacing around a central string, DOMs at 3 m vertical spacing, 300 total DOMs
- Instrumented volume: ~100,000 m³ (~0.1 Mt effective for contained neutrinos)
- Use **smaller pressure vessels** (5-inch borosilicate, e.g., Vitrovex 8282.00) with single 3-inch PMT or SiPM tile
- Each DOM at this density: self-veto using surrounding shells, analogous to PINGU design but with SiPM-based inner detector
- Target physics: **atmospheric neutrino oscillations at Δm²₂₃** with statistics competitive with dedicated oscillation detectors; reactor neutrino cross-section measurements if near a source

**Physics gain:**
- Threshold reduction to **1–3 GeV** for contained events
- Enables muon neutrino disappearance measurement to δ(sin²θ₂₃) < 0.01 level with 5 years of data
- Supernova neutrino burst detection: at 10 kpc, ~300,000 signal events vs. ~10,000 in current IceCube (noise-dominated collective rate rise method)

---

## 6. Veto and Background Rejection Hardware

### Current Limitation
Atmospheric muon background exceeds astrophysical neutrino signal by ~10⁶:1 at trigger level. Current rejection relies on software cuts (starting event selection, likelihood vetoes). The surface array (IceTop) provides partial muon veto but has ~100% duty cycle gaps from blizzards and limited lateral extent.

### Specific Upgrade A: Buried Veto Layer

**Implementation:**
- Deploy **2 horizontal planes of scintillator panels** at 1400 m depth (just above the instrumented volume) and at the outer boundary
- Technology: **extruded plastic scintillator strips** (Fermilab-style NOvA cells, 4 cm × 6 cm cross-section, TiO₂-coated walls, wavelength-shifting fiber readout with SiPM)
- 144 panels per layer × 2 layers = ~1500 m² active area at each level
- Timing resolution <5 ns sufficient to tag entering muons before they produce Cherenkov light in the fiducial volume
- Enables **100% rejection of entering muons** for events where the muon crosses a veto panel — extending the starting-event HESE sample by factor ~3 in solid angle

### Specific Upgrade B: Radio-Cherenkov Hybrid Integration

**Implementation:**
- Embed **in-ice dipole radio antennas** (300–600 MHz, Salla-type or bicone, as in RNO-G/ARA) every 5th string, ~50 m below the top of the optical array
- Target: Askaryan radio emission from UHE neutrino cascades above 10 PeV, where optical DOM spacing causes severe undersampling
- Single-string radio + optical coincidence provides improved vertex reconstruction at 1–100 EeV
- Hardware: **custom LNA** (low-noise amplifier, NF < 1 dB, gain 40 dB) at antenna, coaxial transmission to surface, **100 MSa/s 12-bit digitizer** (e.g., CAEN V1724)
- Cross-calibration between radio and optical reduces energy scale uncertainty from ~15% to ~5% in overlap region 1–10 PeV

---

## 7. Calibration Hardware Upgrades

### Current Limitation
LED flashers on DOMs provide in-situ light sources but with limited angular control and single fixed wavelength bands. Ice model systematics (scattering tensor anisotropy, depth-dependent absorption) are the leading systematic in energy and direction reconstruction.

### Specific Upgrade A: Isotropic Calibration Light Sources

**Implementation:**
- **Nitrogen laser + optical fiber diffuser ball**: 337 nm pulsed laser (pulse width <1 ns FWHM, e.g., LTB Lasertechnik MNL100), coupled to 1 mm step-index silica fiber, terminated in **integrating sphere** (Spectralon-coated aluminum, 1 cm diameter) — produces Lambertian emission with <2% angular uniformity variation
- Deploy 1 per string, fixed to cable at mid-array depth
- Enables precise measurement of scattering length tensor components (bulk ice is birefringent/anisotropic) by using azimuthal DOM pattern in hit timing

### Specific Upgrade B: Acoustic Positioning System Upgrade

**Implementation:**
- Current taut-wire + compass tilt sensor positioning achieves ~1 m module position accuracy
- Replace with **piezoelectric transducer network**: 1 transmitter per string, 3 receivers per string, Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) positioning
- Technology: **Benthowave BII-7530 transducers** (calibrated, 10 kHz–100 kHz), operated at 20 kHz to avoid absorption
- Achieves **<10 cm** position reconstruction per DOM, reducing from ~1 m
- Impact: for TeV muon angular resolution, ~1 m position error contributes ~(1 m / 25 m propagation distance) × (c_ice) ≈ 0.5 ns timing equivalent error — reducing to 10 cm gives 0.05 ns equivalent, below the White Rabbit timing floor

# Hardware Design Upgrades for LUX: Specific Proposals

## 1. PMT Array Replacement with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

The R8778 PMTs are the dominant background source (Table 3 shows PMTs contribute 0.4 ER events vs. <0.02 for cryostats). The radioactivity stems from the PMT construction materials: Fe/Ni/Co in steel bodies, glass windows, and the aluminum ring flagged by XMASS.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace the 122 R8778 PMTs with arrays of Hamamatsu MPPC S10362-series or SensL MicroFC-series SiPMs mounted on low-radioactivity substrates (fused silica or sapphire carrier boards)
- SiPM die themselves are pure silicon with negligible U/Th/K content compared to the 9.8 mBq/PMT U measured at SOLO
- Use Cirlex or PTFE circuit boards rather than standard PCB to avoid FR4 fiberglass radioactivity
- Wire-bond directly to reduce solder mass containing Pb-210
- Expected radioactivity reduction: greater than factor 10 in U/Th activity based on material composition alone

**Tradeoff to manage:** SiPMs have higher dark count rates at room temperature, but at 170K the thermal dark rate drops by several orders of magnitude. The 33% QE of the R8778 is comparable to or exceeded by available SiPMs at 175nm with appropriate anti-reflection coatings, though VUV response requires specific window-free or coated designs using wavelength shifters like TPB (tetraphenyl butadiene) deposited at approximately 0.2 mg/cm².

---

## 2. Cathode High Voltage System Redesign

The current system routes the HV cable through a 55 cm path inside the xenon with the ground shield removed at 25 cm depth, creating a known discharge risk and requiring a 0.1 SLPM xenon purge specifically to remove cable outgassing. This is a direct electron-lifetime threat.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace the Heinzinger HVC100 cable with a custom coaxial line using ultra-high-purity PTFE dielectric and copper-beryllium inner conductor, eliminating plasticizers that outgas electronegative species
- Alternatively, implement a graded-field feedthrough design using a series of titanium or OFHC copper rings embedded in UHMWPE, allowing the full 100 kV to be maintained with the ground shield intact all the way to the cathode connection point
- Add a second independent cold-trap electron-lifetime monitor on the HV umbilical purge return line to separately quantify cable outgassing contribution versus bulk xenon contamination
- Replace the PMX-561 transformer oil on the warm side with a silicone-free fluid (e.g., Galden HT-135 perfluoropolyether) to eliminate any possibility of silicone vapor transport into the xenon system

---

## 3. Upgraded Anode Grid and Electron Extraction Region

The current anode uses a 30-micron wire mesh with 88% optical transparency and measured 130-micron deflection at operating fields. This non-planarity creates position-dependent S2 width variation that degrades z-resolution and fiducial volume definition.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace the woven mesh anode with a photolithographically etched electroformed nickel or copper grid on a PTFE-tensioning frame, achievable at 95%+ optical transparency with 25-micron features
- Electroformed grids have intrinsic planarity at the micron level versus the 130-micron sag measured on the current design
- Use a segmented anode with four to eight independently biased sectors to allow active correction of liquid surface tilt, replacing the passive mechanical leveling rods (currently achieving only ±250 micron horizontal)
- This directly improves the uniformity of the 5 kV/cm extraction field, reducing the position-dependent S2 width variation that currently limits low-energy position reconstruction

---

## 4. Internal Circulation and Heat Exchanger Enhancement

The paper reports circulation was limited to 300 kg/day during surface running due to suboptimal path, with the system designed for 420 kg/day. Electron lifetime is directly tied to purification throughput.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Replace the single SAES MonoTorr getter with two parallel units on independently valved legs, allowing one getter to be regenerated while the other maintains purification flow, eliminating downtime-driven purity degradation
- Add a second diaphragm pump in parallel with the primary to achieve the full 50 SLPM design throughput reliably, with automatic switchover on pump failure
- Install a continuous electron-lifetime monitor (pulsed electron gun with drift time measurement, similar to the EL monitor used in XENON10) directly on the xenon return line to provide real-time feedback to the circulation PID loop rather than relying on periodic source calibrations
- Replace the stainless steel concentric-tube heat exchanger sections with OFHC copper tube-in-tube design to reduce the thermal gradient along the return path, minimizing condensation before the getter which reduces getter efficiency

---

## 5. Enhanced Fiducial Volume Definition: Position Reconstruction

The paper projects ~1 cm x-y position reconstruction accuracy based on XENON10 likelihood methods. The bottom array sits below the cathode in liquid with limited S2 signal access, while the top array does the primary S2 imaging.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Add a thin (3mm) secondary PTFE light guide ring at the level of the gate grid, instrumented with 8 to 12 small-format VUV photodiodes (e.g., Hamamatsu S1227 series adapted for VUV with MgF2 windows), to provide an independent annular S2 position estimator at the extraction plane itself
- This ring-detector provides a redundant radial fiducial cut independent of the top PMT array pattern recognition, directly reducing the uncertainty on the fiducial boundary
- For z-reconstruction, add a second electron-drift velocity calibration system using a pulsed UV laser (157nm F2 excimer) directed through a fused silica fiber to photoionize trace impurities at a precisely known z-position, providing absolute drift velocity as a function of field and temperature without relying on the 83mKr decay chain timing

---

## 6. Water Shield Muon Veto Upgrade

The paper describes 20 ten-inch PMTs achieving greater than 90% muon rejection efficiency. With only 20 PMTs in a 7.6m × 6.1m tank, the photocoverage is sparse.

**Specific upgrade:**
- Increase from 20 to 48 Hamamatsu R7081 PMTs, tripling photocoverage to approximately 0.8% of tank surface area, sufficient to tag muons producing fewer than 50 photoelectrons (currently the threshold is ~200 phe per the paper's estimate)
- Replace the Tyvek liner with ESR (enhanced specular reflector) film from 3M, which has measured reflectivity greater than 98% compared to approximately 90% for Tyvek at visible wavelengths, increasing Cherenkov light collection by 20 to 30%
- Add 4 PMTs on the tank floor oriented upward specifically to tag upward-going muons and horizontal muons that produce hadronic showers primarily in the lower water volume, which are undersampled by the current vertical-string geometry
- This directly addresses the 1 event per 3 years single-scatter NR background from muon-generated neutrons quoted in Section 2, pushing the veto efficiency toward the Super-Kamiokande benchmark of greater than 99.99%

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Addresses Paper's Stated Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | Factor 10+ background reduction | PMTs dominate Table 3 |
| Electroformed anode grid | Improved S2 uniformity and z-resolution | 130 µm sag explicitly measured |
| Dual getter system | Higher and continuous electron lifetime | 300 kg/day limitation explicitly noted |
| Cathode HV redesign | Eliminate outgassing, reduce discharge risk | 0.1 SLPM purge explicitly required |
| Enhanced muon veto | Improved NR veto efficiency | 90% efficiency explicitly cited as target |
| Secondary position reconstruction | Sharper fiducial boundary | Fiducial volume uncertainty limits sensitivity |

The SiPM replacement and anode grid redesign offer the largest primary physics returns because they directly attack the dominant background source and the primary position-reconstruction limitation respectively, both of which set the ultimate WIMP sensitivity floor.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for SNO: Concrete Proposals

## Preamble on Constraints

I will reason strictly from what the paper describes as actual limitations, bottlenecks, and design compromises, proposing upgrades using technologies plausibly available or in development by 2000.

---

## 1. Photomultiplier Tubes and Light Collection

### Current Limitations Identified in the Paper
- Hamamatsu R1408 with 31% bare photocathode coverage, improved to ~54% effective coverage with reflectors
- Single photoelectron timing resolution of 1.7 ns RMS (specification was <1.70 ns — barely met)
- Dark noise rate of ~500 Hz at operating temperature
- 9-dynode design with mean operating voltage of 1875 V
- 850 g glass envelope dominates radioactivity: ~40 ppb Th and U in Schott 8246 borosilicate

### Proposed Upgrades

**Replace R1408 with a purpose-designed low-radioactivity PMT using synthetic fused silica envelopes**

The paper notes that Schott 8246 borosilicate was already a custom low-radioactivity glass developed for SNO, but achieves only <40 ppb Th/U and weighs 850 g. Synthetic fused silica (as used for the NCD insulators — Heraeus-Amersil Suprasil T-21 is explicitly mentioned in the paper) has dramatically lower intrinsic radioactivity, typically at or below the ppt level, and superior UV transmission down to ~160 nm. The mass of the envelope could also be reduced.

Concretely: commission Hamamatsu to produce a variant of the R1408 (or its successor R5912 lineage) with:
- Synthetic fused silica bulb instead of Schott 8246, targeting <1 ppb Th/U
- Reduced wall thickness feasible with fused silica's higher mechanical homogeneity, lowering total radioactive mass by roughly an order of magnitude per tube
- This directly reduces the dominant source of internal background neutrons from photodisintegration of deuterium

**Improve photocathode quantum efficiency**

The paper does not state the QE of the R1408 explicitly, but circa 1999 bialkali photocathodes peaked at roughly 20-25% at 420 nm. The Cherenkov spectrum in water peaks in the blue-UV. Replacing with a high-QE bialkali or a multialkali photocathode optimized for the 300-450 nm range, targeting >28% peak QE, would increase photoelectron yield per event, directly improving energy resolution (which scales as 1/√Npe) and vertex resolution.

**Increase timing resolution**

The 1.7 ns RMS timing is the dominant contribution to vertex reconstruction uncertainty, which in turn affects fiducial volume definition and background rejection. A redesigned dynode chain with fewer, faster dynodes (8 rather than 9, or a mesh/metal channel dynode structure as was entering commercial production circa 1998-2000) could reduce transit time spread to ~1.0 ns RMS. This would tighten event vertex resolution from roughly 20-30 cm toward ~15 cm, meaningfully increasing the effective fiducial mass.

---

## 2. Light Concentrators

### Current Limitation
The paper describes 18-piece aluminum concentrators with mean effective reflectance of 82 ± 3% in water, using a multilayer dielectric coating (Al + MgF₂ + mixed TiO₂/Pr₂O₃ oxides). The 3D critical acceptance angle is 56.4°, giving a 7 m viewing radius. Approximately 15% of isotropically generated photons are absorbed by the NCD array.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Replace dielectric-coated aluminum with total-internal-reflection (TIR) acrylic light guides**

A Winston cone geometry machined or injection-molded from the same UVT acrylic already qualified for SNO (with demonstrated optical absorption coefficient of 0.01 cm⁻¹ at 400 nm) would rely on TIR rather than metallic reflection. TIR efficiency is >99% per bounce for wavelengths above the acrylic cutoff (~300 nm), compared to 82% per bounce for the current metallic reflectors. Given that a typical photon undergoes 1-3 bounces in the concentrator, this represents a meaningful gain in collected photons.

The acrylic material is already radiochemically qualified at <1.1 pg/g Th and U. Molding rather than multi-piece assembly would eliminate the 18-piece construction complexity and potential gaps between pieces.

Caveat: TIR cones require the entrance aperture medium (water) to have lower refractive index than the cone material (acrylic has n≈1.49, water n≈1.34), which is satisfied. The acceptance angle would need to be re-optimized for the new geometry, but the fundamental optical efficiency gain is straightforward.

---

## 3. Front-End Electronics and Dynamic Range

### Current Limitation
The paper describes the SNOINT chip providing dual-gain channels giving >14 bits effective dynamic range, with 12-bit ADCs running at 2 µs conversion time. The SNOD discriminator chip was fabricated in AT&T's CBICU-2 bipolar process. The timing resolution is described as "significantly better than minimum requirements" but the charge linearity and timing performance are already good.

The most significant electronics limitation identified is the per-channel deadtime of ~400 ns (set to accommodate light reflections across the 17 m detector). At the ~500 Hz per-channel noise rate this is manageable, but for supernova burst events at >1 MHz aggregate rate, and for any future higher-rate running, this is a bottleneck.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Replace CBICU-2 bipolar ASICs with deep-submicron CMOS equivalents**

By 1999-2000, 0.25 µm CMOS processes were available (e.g., through TSMC or IBM) offering:
- Lower power per channel (reducing heat load in the underground electronics racks, which the paper notes must be cooled)
- Ability to integrate the SNOD, SNOINT, and QUSN7 functions into a single chip, reducing inter-chip timing jitter
- On-chip 12-bit ADC integration at faster conversion rates (~200 ns rather than 2 µs), reducing the per-channel digitization deadtime
- Multiple-hit buffering deeper than 16 cells per channel, critical for supernova bursts

**Shorten the per-channel deadtime window**

The 400 ns deadtime is set by the maximum light travel time across the detector (66 ns direct + reflections). The paper acknowledges reflected photons may arrive later, but a smarter approach would be a two-window system: a 100 ns primary window for direct Cherenkov photons plus a secondary 300 ns window triggered only if the primary window fires above a threshold. This requires the discriminator to support conditional re-arming, which is implementable in a redesigned ASIC.

**Replace the 50 MHz quartz oscillator with a GPS-disciplined oscillator underground**

The paper describes using a surface GPS receiver with a 4 km fiber delay that must be continuously monitored. A rubidium oscillator disciplined by GPS signals processed on the surface but with the Rb local oscillator underground would provide 10⁻¹¹ stability without sensitivity to fiber propagation variations, improving absolute timing for supernova correlation from ~100 ns to ~20 ns.

---

## 4. Neutral Current Detector Array

### Current Limitation
The paper describes 96 strings of 3He proportional counters with 50 µm copper anode wire, operating at 2.5 atm 85% ³He / 15% CF₄, giving ~37% neutron capture efficiency (taken as 25% effective efficiency after alpha discrimination). The dominant background concern is alpha particles from the nickel tube walls producing signals overlapping the ³He(n,p)T peak.

The bottom termination uses a 415 Ω delay line for position readout by pulse-reflection timing, with signals read out on a single 91 Ω coaxial cable per string.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Increase ³He pressure to 3.5-4.0 atm with thicker CVD nickel walls**

The paper notes that higher pressure would increase gas gain requirements and complicate microdischarge management, but also that lower pressure would require thicker walls for collapse resistance. At 3.5 atm of ³He (maintaining 15% CF₄), the neutron capture efficiency per unit length increases, allowing a sparser array that intercepts less Cherenkov light while maintaining the same total neutron detection efficiency. The wall eﬀect (proton or triton range vs. counter radius) is mitigated at higher pressure since ranges decrease.

The CVD nickel fabrication process at Mirotech is already demonstrated; qualifying it at higher wall thickness (0.05 cm vs. 0.036 cm nominal) is incremental.

**Implement waveform digitization rather than charge integration for pulse shape discrimination**

The paper describes pulse-shape discrimination as a technique to distinguish alpha backgrounds from neutron events, but the existing readout uses a single coaxial cable carrying an analog signal. Replacing the cable-end resistive coupler with a low-power waveform digitizer (e.g., a switched-capacitor array such as the Domino Ring Sampler chip being developed at PSI circa 1999, sampling at ~1 GSa/s with ~1024 samples) would capture the full ion-current profile of each event. The alpha/neutron discrimination figure of merit improves substantially when the full risetime and pulse shape are available rather than integrated charge alone.

This requires redesigning the cable endcap electronics and the above-water readout electronics for the NCD strings, but the mechanical design of the strings themselves is unchanged.

**Improve delay-line position readout by replacing the open-ended delay line with a matched termination plus digitized timing**

The paper uses a 30 ns open-ended 415 Ω delay line at the bottom of each string for position readout by reflection timing. Replacing this with a precision-timed digitizer at both ends of each string (enabled by the waveform digitization upgrade above) would give position resolution of ~5 cm rather than the ~10-15 cm achievable with the existing scheme, improving the ability to localize alpha backgrounds near the endcaps where radioactivity is concentrated.

---

## 5. Water Purification — Radon Reduction

### Current Limitation
The paper states the Process Degasser reduces radon by a factor of ~50 in water, and the cover gas system uses boiloff nitrogen with <10⁻⁵ pCi/L radon. Laboratory air contains radon at 3 pCi/L. Radon in the D₂O is identified as a serious concern because ²¹⁴Bi produces 2.445 MeV gammas capable of photodisintegrating deuterium.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Add a secondary electrodialysis stage to the D₂O recirculation loop**

The current D₂O purification relies on RO membranes for ionic removal and the process degasser for radon. Electrodialysis using ion-exchange membranes (which by 1999 were commercially available in laboratory-scale configurations from manufacturers such as Ionics Inc.) selectively removes Ra²⁺ and Pb²⁺ ions — the long-lived precursors in the ²²⁶Ra→²²²Rn and ²¹⁰Pb→²¹⁰Bi chains — with high efficiency even at the ultrapure water conductivities relevant to SNO. Removing Ra and Pb from the D₂O before they can decay to radon addresses the problem at the source rather than relying solely on degassing of already-produced radon.

The membranes themselves must be radiochemically qualified (the paper already describes such procedures for all wetted materials), and the electrodialysis cell must be constructed from materials compatible with ultrapure D₂O.

---

## 6. Magnetic Field Compensation

### Current Limitation
The paper describes 14 horizontal coils embedded in the cavity walls that cancel only the vertical component of the Earth's field (approximately 55 µT at 15° from vertical). The residual maximum field in the PMT region is 19 µT, causing ~2.5% photon detection efficiency loss. The full uncorrected field would cause ~18% efficiency loss.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Add a three-axis compensation coil system**

The existing system cancels only the dominant vertical component. Adding a second set of coils oriented to cancel the horizontal component (~55 µT × sin15° ≈ 14 µT horizontal) would reduce the total residual field from 19 µT to below 5 µT. At 5 µT, the R1408's efficiency loss is below 0.5% based on the scaling described in the paper (<3% at 20 µT, so roughly linear in this regime, giving ~0.75% at 5 µT).

This requires two additional sets of large-radius coils (the cavity is 22 m diameter), powered by the existing CMA-monitored electrical system. The coil design is straightforward; the challenge is routing current through the sealed cavity without introducing contamination paths, addressed by using sealed cable penetrations of the same type already used for the 14 existing coils.

The improvement is modest (recovering ~2% of PMT efficiency) but is essentially free in terms of added radioactivity or mechanical complexity, and improves uniformity of PMT response across the array, reducing systematic uncertainties in energy reconstruction.

---

## Summary Table of Expected Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Estimated Quantitative Gain |
|---|---|---|
| Fused silica PMT envelopes | Reduced photodisintegration background | ~10× reduction in PMT-origin neutron background |
| Higher QE photocathode | Energy and vertex resolution | ~10-15% more photoelectrons → ~5-7% better energy resolution |
| Faster dynode timing | Vertex reconstruction | ~1.0 ns RMS timing → ~15 cm vertex resolution vs ~25 cm |
| TIR acrylic concentrators | Light collection | ~10-15% more photons collected per event |
| NCD waveform digitization | Alpha/neutron discrimination | Effective NCD efficiency closer to 37% than 25% |
| Electrodialysis Ra/Pb removal | Radon background reduction | Reduction in ²¹⁴Bi photodisintegration neutrons |
| Three-axis B-field compensation | PMT efficiency uniformity | Recovery of ~2% average efficiency, reduced systematic error |

The highest-priority single upgrade is the fused silica PMT envelope, as the PMT glass is identified in the paper as the dominant radioactivity contributor to the detector, and photodisintegration neutrons are the principal irreducible background for the neutral-current measurement that is the core physics goal of SNO.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for XENON1T

## 1. Photosensor System

### Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)
The R11410-21 PMTs achieve only 12.5% photon detection efficiency (PDE) in the detector configuration, limited by the 34.5% quantum efficiency, geometric packing, and reflection losses. A SiPM-based readout could improve this substantially:

**Specific implementation:**
- Deploy Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) VUV4 or Hamamatsu VUV-sensitive MPPC arrays (e.g., S13371-6050CQ series) directly tiled on the top and bottom arrays
- These achieve ~24% PDE at 178 nm in cryogenic LXe conditions versus the effective ~12.5% currently achieved
- Tile the bottom array at near-100% geometric coverage using 6mm × 6mm SiPM cells versus the current circular PMT packing with dead regions
- Estimated improvement: factor ~2-3 in light collection, reducing S1 threshold from ~4 PE to ~1-2 PE, directly extending sensitivity to lower WIMP masses

**Radioactivity concern mitigation:**
- SiPMs have demonstrated lower specific radioactivity than PMTs (~0.1 mBq/kg vs ~1 mBq/kg for U/Th chains in R11410)
- Use ceramic rather than PCB substrates for mounting to reduce Rn emanation
- Operate in a ganged configuration (e.g., 9-pad groups summed) to reduce channel count and cabling radioactivity contribution

### Improved Top Array Position Reconstruction
Replace the current radially-oriented PMT arrangement with a **dual-layer crossed-strip SiPM architecture**:
- Two planes of 5 mm strip SiPMs at different heights within the gas phase
- Provides direct XY charge centroid measurement complementing the current likelihood reconstruction
- Reduces position reconstruction uncertainty from ΔR < 2 cm toward sub-centimeter, improving fiducialization and background rejection near the PTFE walls

---

## 2. Field Cage and Electrode System

### Higher Transparency Electrodes
The current gate electrode at 92.7% transparency and cathode at 97.2% impose measurable S1 light losses. The bottom screen at 97.2% sits only 12 mm from the bottom PMTs:

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace etched-mesh electrodes with hexagonal photolithographically etched electrodes in 50 µm tungsten wire, achievable at 3.5 mm pitch with >97% transparency
- Replace the parallel-wire cathode and bottom screen with fine-pitch (3 mm) hexagonal gold-plated meshes at >98.5% transparency
- Estimated S1 improvement: ~3-5% additional light collection at cathode depth

### Higher Drift Field Operation
The science run 0 operated at only 0.125 kV/cm due to instabilities, well below the design. This suppresses the charge/light yield ratio beneficial for ER/NR discrimination:

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace the Heinzinger PNC 150000-1 supply with a more stable Iseg NHQ 226M series with active ripple suppression (<5 mV ripple vs ~50 mV currently)
- Redesign the cathode HV feedthrough using PTFE-encapsulated coaxial geometry rather than the current rod-in-polyethylene design, rated to stable −100 kV operation in LXe (tested to −80 kV demonstrated by EXO-200 coaxial feedthroughs)
- Install resistive field-shaping rings using 1 GΩ thin-film resistors on PTFE frames rather than discrete resistor chains, eliminating chain failure modes
- Target: 1.0 kV/cm drift field, increasing electron/photon yield ratio and improving NR/ER discrimination from >99.5% to potentially >99.9% at 50% NR acceptance

### Charge Loss Reduction at Liquid Surface
The current extraction efficiency is 96% but degrades at field nonuniformities near the liquid surface:

**Specific implementation:**
- Add a fine-pitch (2 mm) stainless steel grid 1 mm below the liquid surface as an "extraction assist" electrode biased to ~−0.5 kV
- This homogenizes the field in the critical extraction region and suppresses liquid surface waves that cause S2 width broadening
- Benchmarked from the RED-100 and DarkSide-50 surface grid designs

---

## 3. Radon Mitigation Hardware

Radon at 10 µBq/kg is the dominant background (620 events/(t·y) before ER rejection), and reducing it by a factor of 10 would transform the experiment.

### Radon-Trapping Cold Trap on Purification Loop
**Specific implementation:**
- Install a dedicated electrostatic radon trap (activated charcoal at −40°C in a stainless steel vessel, similar to BOREXINO's design) on each purification loop branch
- The trap consists of a 50 cm column of Carboact 0.5 mm activated charcoal maintained at precisely −40°C by a Peltier element
- At this temperature, the adsorption coefficient for Rn on charcoal is ~30,000 s, providing effective delay/removal without significant Xe loss (Xe adsorption coefficient ~3 s at −40°C)
- This would intercept Rn from the getter and pump components before returning xenon to the TPC
- Expected reduction: factor 5-10 in Rn contribution from purification system

### Electropolished Inner Surfaces with Radon Barrier Coating
- Apply 100 nm Al₂O₃ atomic layer deposition (ALD) coating to all inner cryostat and TPC copper surfaces
- ALD Al₂O₃ has demonstrated Rn emanation suppression factors of 10-50 in MPIk Heidelberg measurements, by blocking Rn diffusion from bulk material through surface layers
- Specifically target the PTFE panels (known Rn emanators) with a 50 nm silicon oxide ALD barrier

### Online Radon Distillation Column Upgrade
The current demonstration showed >27× reduction but used only a shortened column on XENON100:

**Specific implementation:**
- Install a dedicated second distillation column in series specifically for Rn removal, using 2 m of Sulzer EX packing operating in reverse mode (Rn removed from bottom)
- Increase the Rn-dedicated flow to 20% of total purification flow (vs 7% in SR0) enabled by upgrading to CHART QDrive Series III pumps rated for 100 slpm
- Expected Rn reduction from online distillation: factor >50 at full flow

---

## 4. Xenon Purification System

### Upgrade to Liquid-Phase Circulation
Current gas-phase purification at 50 slpm through heated getters limits electron lifetime:

**Specific implementation:**
- Install a cryogenic liquid-phase purification system using heated SAES PS4-MT50 getters in a LXe-compatible enclosure, based on the LUX/LZ liquid circulation design
- Liquid pumps (Barber-Nichols cryogenic centrifugal pumps, model BNCP-32) operating at 500 slpm LXe equivalent throughput
- This reduces the impurity attachment time constant by 10× without the heat load penalty of evaporation/recondensation
- Target: electron lifetime >3 ms (vs 450 µs in SR0), allowing full drift field utilization

---

## 5. Neutron Veto System

The paper notes 0.55 events/(t·y) from radiogenic neutrons with no dedicated neutron veto beyond fiducialization and multiple scatter rejection. Adding a dedicated system addresses this irreducible background:

**Specific implementation:**
- Instrument the water shield with gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator (0.1% Gd by mass, GdCl₃ dissolved in linear alkylbenzene) replacing or supplementing the current pure water in a cylindrical annulus 50 cm thick around the cryostat
- Deploy 40 additional 8-inch Hamamatsu R5912 PMTs in this region
- Gd has a 49,000 barn thermal neutron capture cross section, capturing neutrons within ~20 µs and emitting ~8 MeV in gamma cascades detectable in coincidence with TPC events
- This approach is established in SNO+ and EGADS programs
- Expected neutron veto efficiency: >90% for single-scatter NR events from radiogenic neutrons, reducing this background from 0.55 to <0.05 events/(t·y)

---

## 6. Data Acquisition System

### Upgrade ADC Resolution and Sampling Rate
Current 14-bit, 100 MHz CAEN V1724 digitizers limit pulse shape discrimination at low energies:

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace with CAEN V1730 16-bit, 500 MHz digitizers currently commercially available
- Higher sampling rate resolves S1 triplet/singlet lifetime components (45 ns vs 22 ns for NR/ER) enabling additional pulse-shape based ER/NR discrimination beyond S2/S1 ratio
- This is particularly powerful at low energies where S2/S1 discrimination degrades
- The 16-bit dynamic range eliminates the need for the ×10 Phillips amplifiers, removing a noise source and reducing the minimum detectable S1 threshold

### FPGA-Based Online Position Reconstruction for Triggering
Current trigger at 200 PE (≈7 electrons) misses the lowest energy NR events:

**Specific implementation:**
- Implement a Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA-based real-time position reconstruction running the likelihood maximizer algorithm in hardware at 40 MHz clock rate
- Use reconstructed position to apply fiducial volume selection at trigger level, enabling threshold reduction to ~50 PE (≈2 electrons) in the fiducial volume without unmanageable trigger rates from surface backgrounds
- This extends NR sensitivity to ~1 keV (from ~3 keV currently), improving sensitivity to low-mass WIMPs below 10 GeV/c²

---

## Summary of Expected Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Metric Improved | Expected Gain |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM photosensors | S1 threshold, light yield | Factor 2-3 lower WIMP mass reach |
| Higher drift field | ER/NR discrimination | 99.9% vs 99.5% ER rejection |
| Rn trapping + distillation | ER background rate | Factor 5-10 reduction |
| Liquid-phase purification | Electron lifetime/charge yield | Factor 6 improvement |
| Gd-loaded neutron veto | NR background | Factor 10 reduction |
| 500 MHz 16-bit DAQ | Energy threshold | Factor 2 lower in energy reach |

The highest-priority single upgrade is the **Rn mitigation hardware**, as Rn dominates the background budget at 88% of total ER events, and the hardware solutions are well-demonstrated at prototype scale. The **SiPM photosensor replacement** provides the broadest physics improvement by simultaneously lowering threshold, improving position reconstruction, and reducing intrinsic radioactivity.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for LHCb Performance Improvement

## Identification of Primary Performance Limitations

Before proposing upgrades, the binding constraints from the paper must be identified:

1. **L0 hardware trigger limits readout to 1 MHz**, creating the dominant efficiency loss for hadronic channels (~40-53% L0 efficiency for hadronic b-decays)
2. **VELO mechanical retraction** introduces 210-second dead time per fill
3. **OT straw tube occupancy** reaches 17-25% at 50ns spacing, degrading pattern recognition
4. **RICH photoelectron yield** falls below simulation predictions, reducing PID separation power
5. **Calorimeter PMT aging** requires frequent recalibration interventions

---

## Proposed Upgrades in Priority Order

### 1. Full Software Trigger via 40 MHz Readout (Highest Impact)

**The core problem:** The L0 hardware trigger causes 47-60% efficiency loss for hadronic charm and beauty decays because calorimeter and muon hardware decisions cannot apply vertex displacement criteria, which is the most powerful discriminant for heavy flavor.

**Specific hardware changes:**

**VELO replacement with hybrid pixel detector:**
- Replace silicon microstrip sensors with **55 µm pitch hybrid pixel detectors** using VeloPix ASICs derived from Timepix3 architecture
- Timepix3 provides **time-over-threshold and arrival time simultaneously** with 1.56 ns resolution, enabling per-hit timing for pile-up rejection
- Reduce sensor thickness from 300 µm to **200 µm n-on-p sensors** to decrease radiation length from ~0.4% X₀ per sensor to ~0.25% X₀, directly improving IP resolution
- Eliminate the mechanical retraction requirement by implementing a **radio-frequency foil** between beam and detector at 5 mm radius rather than the current 8.2 mm, achieved by replacing the aluminium foil with a 100 µm corrugated aluminum RF shield supported by a carbon fiber structure
- Expected impact: IP resolution improvement from 13 µm to ~8 µm at high pT based on reduced material and closer approach

**Upstream Tracker (UT) replacing TT:**
- Replace 500 µm thick TT sensors with **250 µm silicon pixel sensors** arranged in four layers
- Increase channel count from ~143k to ~750k channels using **SALT ASICs** with 40 MHz readout capability
- The finer segmentation reduces occupancy in the innermost regions from 1.9% to below 0.5%, critical for pattern recognition at higher luminosity
- Readout bandwidth: each SALT chip serializes data at 320 Mb/s over a single fiber, aggregated via GBT links

**Scintillating Fiber Tracker (SciFi) replacing IT/OT:**
- Replace both the Inner Tracker silicon and Outer Tracker straws with **250 µm diameter scintillating fibers** (polystyrene core, PMMA cladding)
- Fibers read out by **Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPM)** with 4 µm² cell size operating at -40°C to reduce dark count rate from ~10 MHz/mm² at room temperature to ~150 kHz/mm²
- This architecture provides **40 MHz hit readout** without the 3-bunch-crossing integration window that currently adds ghost hits from adjacent crossings, which is the primary driver of 17-25% OT occupancy
- Single hit resolution target: 100 µm versus the current 200 µm OT resolution, achievable through the smaller fiber pitch
- Dark count suppression via coincidence between two staggered fiber layers within a 1 ns window
- Eliminates the magnetic field sensitivity that caused 5 mm IT box movements during field ramping

**Readout electronics architecture:**
- Replace selective L0 readout with **full 40 MHz detector readout** across all subsystems
- Front-end boards aggregate data via **GBT (Gigabit Transceiver) ASICs** at 4.8 Gb/s per link
- Event builder farm receives ~40 Tb/s raw data, requiring ~1000 FPGA-based PCIe40 readout boards
- Allen GPU-based first-pass trigger running on ~500 NVIDIA GPU nodes performs track and vertex reconstruction in real time, replacing the L0 hardware decision with a software primary vertex and displaced track selection

**Quantified benefit:** For B⁰→K⁺π⁻, L0 efficiency rises from 53% to effectively 100% since the hardware bottleneck is removed. The full trigger chain efficiency for hadronic modes approaches the HLT2 efficiency ceiling (~80%), representing a factor ~1.5 improvement in effective yield per unit luminosity.

---

### 2. RICH Detector Upgrade for Higher Luminosity PID

**The core problem:** The paper reports photoelectron yield deficits of 28% (C₄F₁₀) and 30% (CF₄) relative to simulation, and Cherenkov angle resolution for C₄F₁₀ of 1.618 mrad versus simulated 1.52 mrad. Both trace to the Hybrid Photon Detector (HPD) performance and residual magnetic field distortions.

**Specific hardware changes:**

**Replace HPDs with Multi-Anode Photomultiplier Tubes (MaPMTs):**
- Hamamatsu R11265 MaPMT with **64 pixels per tube** in 8×8 arrangement, 2×2 mm² pixel size
- Quantum efficiency of MaPMTs (~35% peak at 350 nm) exceeds HPD quantum efficiency (~23%), directly recovering the Nₚₑ deficit
- MaPMTs are not sensitive to magnetic fields below 1 mT, eliminating the field distortion corrections that contribute the 0.1 mrad excess resolution in RICH1
- No requirement for high-voltage ion-feedback suppression that limits HPD rate capability
- **Elementary Cell architecture**: group 4 MaPMTs with a single MAROC3 frontend ASIC per group, each ASIC handling 64 channels with 40 MHz zero-suppressed readout
- Pixel occupancy per MaPMT: estimated 1-2% at nominal luminosity, well within digitization capability

**RICH1 geometry modification:**
- Increase RICH1 mirror radius of curvature from current value to reduce spherical aberration contribution to σ(θ_C)
- Replace current flat mirror arrangement with **tilted spherical mirror geometry** that moves photon detectors outside the spectrometer acceptance, reducing the material budget seen by signal tracks by eliminating the HPD window material (~0.5% X₀ per crossing)

**Quantified benefit:** Nₚₑ recovery to simulation levels increases kaon identification efficiency at ∆logL(K-π)>0 from ~95% to ~97% while reducing pion misidentification from ~10% to ~7% based on Cherenkov ring fit quality improvement with additional photons.

---

### 3. Calorimeter System: SiPM Replacement of PMTs

**The core problem:** PMT dynode degradation causes progressive gain loss requiring bi-monthly recalibration shutdowns for HCAL (using ¹³⁷Cs sources) and continuous monitoring corrections for ECAL. The paper explicitly shows this in Figure 29, with the L0-hadron rate drifting by ~40% between calibrations.

**Specific hardware changes:**

**ECAL readout replacement:**
- Replace PMTs with **SiPMs mounted directly on WLS fiber bundles** exiting each shashlik module
- Use Hamamatsu S13360 series SiPMs with 3×3 mm² active area, 50 µm cell pitch (3600 cells), operating at ~-10°C via Peltier cooling integrated into the connector board
- SiPM gain stability: <0.5% variation per degree Celsius after voltage compensation, versus PMT gain variation of ~2-3% per degree
- Each SiPM read out by a **custom 12-bit ADC ASIC** sampling at 40 MHz with digital baseline subtraction, replacing the current analog pipeline
- Eliminates need for high-voltage distribution system, replacing with low-voltage (+30V) bias supply with per-channel digital-to-analog voltage trim for gain equalization

**HCAL modification:**
- Same SiPM replacement eliminates the requirement for ¹³⁷Cs source calibration runs, recovering ~12 hours of running time per 2-month period
- Integrate **blue LED calibration pulser** into each tile for continuous gain monitoring at nanosecond timing precision, calibrated against known test-pulse injection

**SPD/PS upgrade:**
- Replace single-bit SPD with a **2-bit charge measurement** (0, 0.5 MIP, 1 MIP, >1 MIP) using SiPM readout, providing shower multiplicity information that improves the electron/hadron separation used in L0Electron trigger lines
- Expected improvement: electron identification efficiency in calorimeter rises from (91.9±1.3)% to ~95% based on the additional longitudinal shower shape information

---

### 4. Muon System Rate Capability Enhancement

**The core problem:** The paper reports dead-time of 2.5% in M1R1 and 0.6% in M2R1 at 2×10³² cm⁻²s⁻¹, exceeding the 99% efficiency design requirement in inner regions. The front-end chip dead time of 50-100 ns is intrinsic to the current CARIOCA architecture.

**Specific hardware changes:**

**GEM detector extension to M2:**
- Extend **triple-GEM technology** from M1 to the R1 region of M2, where occupancy is highest
- GEM detectors with 2 mm drift gap and 100 µm amplification gap achieve <10 ns signal collection time versus 50-100 ns for MWPC, reducing dead time by factor ~7
- Use **TIGER ASIC** with 6-bit charge measurement and 200 ps time resolution, replacing CARIOCA binary output
- The time resolution improvement allows tighter 10 ns coincidence windows, reducing accidental hit rate that contributes to M5 back-scattering contamination noted in the paper

**Readout segmentation increase in R1:**
- Double the number of readout pads in M1R1 and M2R1 by implementing **stereo strip readout** with 5 mm pitch in place of current pad geometry
- This halves occupancy per channel without changing detector active area, directly reducing the dead time from OR-of-channels architecture

---

### 5. VELO Radiation Hardness Extension

**The core problem:** The paper reports sensors reaching 1.8×10¹⁴ neq/cm² by end of Run I with effective depletion voltage of ~100V, approaching the 500V operational limit projected for Run II end.

**Specific hardware changes:**

**Replace n-on-n sensors with n-on-p (p-type bulk) sensors:**
- p-type bulk sensors do **not undergo type inversion** under irradiation, meaning the depletion voltage increases monotonically but more slowly for equivalent fluence
- Use **Czochralski silicon** rather than float-zone material: oxygen-enriched bulk suppresses radiation-induced effective doping change by factor ~2 based on CERN RD50 results
- Implement **active edge technology**: sensors diced by laser with 50 µm dead edge rather than current 450 µm mechanical guard ring, allowing closer approach to beam while maintaining coverage
- Thin sensors to 150 µm: reduces charge collection path, allowing operation at lower bias voltage (200V rather than 500V) at equivalent fluence, while maintaining signal-to-noise >10:1 with VA_LHCb ASIC

**Sensor geometry modification:**
- Transition from R/Φ strip geometry to **tilted pixel geometry** with 55×300 µm² pixels
- Pixel geometry eliminates the need for separate R and Φ sensor pairs, halving the material per station from ~0.8% X₀ to ~0.4% X₀
- 3D sensor option for innermost stations: silicon pillars etched through substrate provide charge collection perpendicular to particle trajectory, reducing trapping effects at high fluence by factor ~3

---

## Summary Table of Expected Performance Gains

| Upgrade | Key Metric | Current | Projected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 40 MHz readout + SciFi | Hadronic trigger efficiency | 40-53% | ~80% |
| VELO pixel + RF foil | IP resolution at high pT | 13 µm | ~8 µm |
| MaPMT RICH | Nₚₑ (C₄F₁₀) | 20.4 | ~27 |
| SiPM calorimeter | Gain stability | ±40% drift | <1% drift |
| GEM M1-M2 inner | M1R1 dead time | 2.5% | <0.3% |
| p-type VELO sensors | Max fluence tolerance | 1.8×10¹⁴ neq/cm² | ~5×10¹⁴ neq/cm² |

The dominant single improvement is the **40 MHz full readout with software trigger**, as it converts the hardware trigger efficiency floor into a software-accessible problem where vertex and impact parameter information can be applied at the first decision stage, recovering the factor ~1.5-2.0 in hadronic channel yield that the calorimeter-threshold L0 trigger currently discards.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Single-Phase LArTPC Neutrino Detector

## Preamble: Identifying the Primary Physics Bottlenecks

For a single-phase LArTPC of this class (clearly ProtoDUNE-SP / DUNE FD heritage), primary physics performance is governed by:
1. **Signal-to-noise ratio** on the wire planes
2. **Light yield and timing resolution** from the photon detection system
3. **Space-charge effect mitigation**
4. **Argon purity** (electron lifetime)
5. **Low-energy threshold** (supernova neutrinos, solar neutrinos, proton decay)

---

## Upgrade 1: Wire Readout → Pixelated Charge Readout (LArPix ASIC Array)

### Current Limitation
The CPA/APA wire-based readout suffers from:
- Inherent left-right ambiguity in 3D reconstruction requiring multi-plane coincidence
- Wire capacitance (~200 pF/m) increasing intrinsic noise (~1000 e⁻ ENC)
- Track ghosting in high-multiplicity events (e.g., atmospheric ν, beam ν interactions)

### Proposed Upgrade
Replace the wire planes with **LArPix v2b tile arrays** — a fully pixelated 3D charge readout system developed at LBNL.

**Specific components:**
- **LArPix ASIC** (65 nm CMOS, ~100 e⁻ ENC, self-triggering): each chip reads 64 pixels on a 4.4 mm pitch
- **Pixel tiles** (~10 cm × 10 cm PCB modules, 100 channels/tile) mounted on the anode plane frame in place of wire boards
- **Data/power routing** via cold differential signaling through the existing flange penetrations using CRYO-grade flex cables
- **COLDATA-compatible serialization** to interface with existing WIB/FELIX DAQ infrastructure

**Physics gain:**
- Eliminates track ambiguity entirely → unambiguous 3D hit positions at 4.4 mm resolution
- ~3× improvement in vertex resolution for NC/CC discrimination
- Critical for supernova neutrino burst reconstruction where high track multiplicity is extreme
- Threshold reduction to ~5 ke⁻ per pixel vs. ~15 ke⁻ per wire channel

**Engineering caveat:** Power density requires careful thermal management (~1 mW/channel cold); bump-bonding yield at cryogenic temperatures needs validation at scale beyond the 2×2 module currently deployed at NuMI.

---

## Upgrade 2: Photon Detection — Replace Light-Guide Bars with VUV-Sensitive SiPM Arrays (DAPHNE-X / X-ARAPUCA)

### Current Limitation
The dip-coated light-guide bar design (using TPB wavelength shifter) suffers from:
- Light collection efficiency of **~0.1–0.3%** detected photons per scintillation photon
- Non-uniform spatial coverage (bars embedded only at anode plane edges)
- TPB coating degradation over multi-year operation
- Timing resolution limited by bar propagation time dispersion (~10–50 ns spread)

### Proposed Upgrade: X-ARAPUCA Modules with NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs

**Specific components:**
- **X-ARAPUCA dichroic filter trap cells**: each ~10 cm × 10 cm window uses a PTP+TPB bilayer on a dichroic filter to shift 128 nm VUV → 430 nm, trapping photons toward a central SiPM cluster
- **NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs** (FBK/Hamamatsu S13360 or SiPM-on-tile): 6 mm × 6 mm devices with PDE >35% at 430 nm at 87 K, dark rate <0.1 Hz/mm² at 77 K
- **DAPHNE v2 readout board** (64-channel cold analog front-end at 14-bit, 125 MSPS) — replace existing readout electronics
- **Deployment geometry**: Install X-ARAPUCA supercells (10 cells/module, ~50 cm × 10 cm footprint) on both cathode plane faces AND frame-mounted arrays on field cage walls at 1 m longitudinal pitch

**Physics gain:**
- Light yield improvement from ~2 PE/MeV → **~20–50 PE/MeV** (demonstrated in ProtoDUNE-HD design)
- Enables **absolute t₀ tagging at <1 ns** for all interactions (critical for space-charge correction)
- Supernova burst detection efficiency: at 10 kpc, threshold drops from ~30 MeV to **<5 MeV** (individual burst neutrino visibility)
- Calorimetric energy resolution improves ~15% from light+charge combined reconstruction (NEST-calibrated)
- Michel electron detection efficiency: improves from ~60% → >90% above 5 MeV

**Specific SiPM choice justification:** FBK NUV-HD-Cryo has been characterized to maintain Geiger efficiency and controlled afterpulsing (<2%) down to 40 K, unlike standard Hamamatsu VUV4 devices which show excessive afterpulsing below 77 K in single-phase operation.

---

## Upgrade 3: Front-End Electronics — Cold ADC Replacement (COLDATA + ColdADC v2)

### Current Limitation
The existing cold electronics (LArASIC + COLDADC in 180 nm TSMC) show:
- ADC differential nonlinearity (DNL) artifacts at ~1 LSB causing spurious hit rate at low threshold
- Noise floor of ~600 e⁻ ENC on collection wires but ~900 e⁻ on induction (after full signal processing)
- Limited dynamic range (12-bit effective) creating saturation on stopping proton tracks near vertex

### Proposed Upgrade
**Swap ColdADC v1 for ColdADC v2 (65 nm process)** with concurrent LARASIC8 preamplifier:

**Specific components:**
- **ColdADC v2**: 16-channel, 12-bit SAR ADC with on-chip calibration DAC; DNL < 0.3 LSB demonstrated at 77 K; 2 MSPS per channel; power: 1.5 mW/channel (vs. 3 mW for v1)
- **LArASIC8** (65 nm): programmable gain (4.7/7.8/14/25 mV/fC), peaking time 0.5–3 µs, ENC <400 e⁻ on 150 pF load — addresses induction plane noise
- **WIB3 (Warm Interface Board, gen. 3)**: full 10 GbE FELIX interface, on-board Kintex UltraScale+ FPGA for real-time hit compression (zero-suppression at 10 Hz noise threshold)
- **Cold power regulators**: replace LDOs with switched-mode cold regulators (LTC3388 characterized at 77 K) to reduce heat load in LAr by 40%

**Physics gain:**
- ENC reduction to ~350 e⁻ → threshold of **~1 ke⁻ per channel** → detection of dE/dx from slow, low-energy recoils
- Critical for **solar neutrino** (<15 MeV electron recoil) detection in DUNE far detector extrapolation
- Eliminates DNL-induced fake tracks that currently corrupt automated reconstruction at ~3% rate

---

## Upgrade 4: High-Voltage System — Modular Resistive Cathode + Active HV Compensation

### Current Limitation
The single-cathode HV design using a resistive divider field cage:
- Space-charge buildup from cosmic muons in surface prototype creates **~10% local E-field distortion** at 500 V/cm nominal
- Any HV trip causes total detector dead time (~10 min recovery)
- Single CPA failure is catastrophic for entire drift volume

### Proposed Upgrade: Segmented Resistive Cathode + Active Field Compensation

**Specific components:**
- **Resistive cathode panels** (graphite-loaded fiberglass, resistivity ~10⁹ Ω/□): Replace metallic CPA with a resistive surface that self-quenches streamer discharges — eliminates breakdown-induced HV trips. Design derived from ALICE TPC and validated for LAr in the 2×2 prototype
- **Active field cage monitoring**: embed **50 µm diameter cold-rated resistance temperature detectors (RTDs)** and **miniature E-field probes** (Pockels cells using LiNbO₃ crystals, operated at 87 K — validated by ETH Zürich group) at 20 cm longitudinal intervals along field cage profiles
- **Piezo-electric HV modulators** on each of 4 independent drift volume segments: allow ±5% active E-field correction at 100 Hz bandwidth to compensate space-charge in real time
- **SHV feedthroughs → custom ultra-low-outgassing CF-flange HV feedthroughs** (LEMO coaxial, PTFE-free, rated to -150 kV) to eliminate gassing from PTFE insulators currently contributing ~1 ppb N₂ equivalent contamination

**Physics gain:**
- Reduces track position distortion from space charge: **∆r from ~1.5 cm → <2 mm** at maximum drift distance
- Directly improves angular resolution for beam νµ charged-current quasi-elastic events by ~factor 3 in distorted region
- Eliminates ~8% detector dead time from HV trips (current measured value in ProtoDUNE-SP operations)

---

## Upgrade 5: Argon Purification — In-vessel Getter Cartridges + Online Purity Monitoring

### Current Limitation
External purification loop (pump + hot getter) achieves ~5 ms electron lifetime in bulk, but:
- Diffusion-limited impurity re-introduction from detector materials limits lifetime plateau
- Purity measurement latency (~hours for extracted samples) prevents rapid feedback
- Outgassing from wire insulation (polyimide), field cage G10, and APA frames contributes O₂ equivalent ~10 ppt/day

### Proposed Upgrade

**Specific components:**
- **In-vessel SAES MonoTorr PS4-MT50-R-2** getter cartridges (cold-rated, validated to 77 K operation): mount 4 cartridges on LAr recirculation risers inside cryostat — eliminates warm-loop pressure drop, increases effective purification throughput by 3×
- **UV laser-based purity monitors** (337 nm N₂ laser + gold photocathode purity monitor tubes, Bromberg-Rameika design): deploy 3 units at different drift distances; measure attenuation length in real time with 5-minute time constant
- **Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) on argon gas recirculation line**: Stanford Research Systems RGA 200, with custom cold-trap interface — identifies specific outgassing species (H₂O, O₂, N₂, Ar₂) at <0.01 ppb sensitivity
- **Low-outgassing material substitution for APA frames**: replace G10/FR4 with **Stesalit 4411W** (measured outgassing rate 2 orders lower than standard G10 at 87 K per CERN-EDMS measurements)

**Physics gain:**
- Extend electron lifetime from ~5 ms → **>15 ms**: reduces recombination correction uncertainty from ~3% → <0.5% at full 3.6 m drift
- Directly reduces systematic uncertainty on **proton decay** branching ratio measurements (dominant systematic in p→K⁺ν̄ channel is calorimetric energy scale)
- Required to fully exploit pixelated readout upgrade — pixel threshold advantage is negated by attachment loss at <5 ms lifetime

---

## Upgrade 6: Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) System — Full Enclosure with Timing-Upgraded Scintillator Panels

### Current Limitation
Partial CRT coverage (top + sides only) leaves **~30% solid angle untagged**, particularly for near-horizontal cosmic muons that mimic neutrino interaction topologies and are the dominant background for surface operation.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Specific components:**
- **Full 4π CRT enclosure**: Add bottom and downstream-face panels using **Fermilab-design extruded plastic scintillator strips** (3.2 cm × 1.8 cm × 400 cm, EJ-200) with wavelength-shifting fiber readout (Y-11 Kuraray, 1 mm diameter)
- **SiPM upgrade on all CRT channels**: Replace existing PMT readout with **Hamamatsu S14160-3050HS SiPMs** (3 mm × 3 mm, 50 µm cell pitch, 74% PDE at 450 nm) — improves timing resolution from ~5 ns → **<1 ns** per panel
- **White-rabbit timing distribution** (CERN WR-LEN nodes): synchronize all CRT panels to the photon detection system with <100 ps jitter — enables absolute drift-time measurement for every muon track crossing any two panels
- **CRT-TPC matching algorithm hardware accelerator**: Xilinx Alveo U250 FPGA card in DAQ farm running real-time track-matching at full 2 MHz CRT trigger rate

**Physics gain:**
- Full tagging efficiency for cosmogenic backgrounds: reduces untagged muon contamination from ~15% → **<1%** in fiducial volume
- Enables **in-situ E-field mapping** via tagged muon straight-track comparison (Δposition vs. drift time) — provides independent space-charge measurement with mm-level precision
- Critical for **low-energy physics program**: reduces Michel electron background mis-ID by ~factor 5

---

## Summary Priority Matrix

| Upgrade | Primary Physics Driver | Estimated Performance Gain | Technical Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pixelated readout (LArPix) | ν reconstruction fidelity | 3× vertex resolution | TRL 5 (2×2 demonstrated) |
| X-ARAPUCA + NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs | Light yield / low-E threshold | 10–50× light yield | TRL 7 (ProtoDUNE-HD) |
| ColdADC v2 + LArASIC8 | S/N, dynamic range | ~2× ENC reduction | TRL 6 |
| Resistive cathode + active HV | Track position accuracy | 10× distortion reduction | TRL 6 |
| In-vessel getters + purity monitors | Calorimetry systematics | 3× lifetime improvement | TRL 8 |
