### 6.1 Balanced Homodyne Detection

**Current:** RF heterodyne readout (Pound-Drever-Hall with RF sidebands).

**Upgrade:**
- **DC balanced homodyne detection** with a bright local oscillator picked off at the beam splitter (or from a dedicated local oscillator cavity): eliminates RF oscillator phase noise from the readout, reduces LO RIN coupling
- **Requires:** Interferometer operating at dark fringe to < 1 ppm contrast defect; active phase control of output Faraday isolator and beam splitter at

# Hardware Design Upgrades for SNO

## Assessment of Primary Physics Limitations

The core physics goal is distinguishing CC/NC/ES rates with maximum statistical and systematic precision. The binding constraints are: photon detection efficiency (~54% effective coverage), energy threshold (~5 MeV imposed by radioactive backgrounds), and neutron detection efficiency (~37% with NCDs). I'll address each systematically.

---

## 1. Photomultiplier System Replacement

### Current Limitation
The Hamamatsu R1408 provides 31% bare photocathode coverage, boosted to ~54% effective coverage with aluminum reflector concentrators. The 1.7 ns RMS timing resolution and ~20% quantum efficiency at 420 nm directly limit vertex reconstruction accuracy and energy resolution.

### Proposed Upgrade: Large-Area Picosecond Photodetectors (LAPPDs)

Replace the 9438 R1408 tubes with **Incom LAPPD Gen-II microchannel plate detectors** (20×20 cm active area):

- **Quantum efficiency**: 30-35% bialkali at 390 nm versus ~20% for R1408, with potential for GaAs photocathodes reaching 40-45% in the 300-500 nm SNO-relevant window
- **Timing resolution**: 50-100 ps single photon transit time spread versus 1.7 ns RMS, enabling substantially improved vertex reconstruction from Cherenkov cone geometry
- **Spatial resolution**: ~1 mm position resolution within each tile permits photon direction reconstruction at the detector face, providing additional handle on event topology without concentrators
- **Pressure rating**: Hermetic ceramic/glass construction handles 200 kPa easily; internal MCP structure is insensitive to the ~55 µT magnetic field without compensation coils

**Implementation specifics:**
- Replace concentrator+PMT assemblies with flat LAPPD tile panels tessellating the PSUP hexagonal cells directly
- Each 20×20 cm tile covers approximately the same solid angle as one hexagonal concentrator unit
- Remove the 14 magnetic compensation coils since LAPPDs are field-insensitive, eliminating associated infrastructure and potential contamination sources
- Replace single RG59 coaxial cable per PMT with **stripline readout boards** carrying differential LVDS signals; 4 striplines per tile recover 2D position, reducing cable plant mass and associated U/Th contamination
- Estimated photocathode coverage increase to ~65% geometric without concentrators; with modest 1.3× light guide coupling tiles to curved PSUP surface, approach 75%

**Radiological impact**: LAPPDs use borosilicate glass with demonstrated <5 ppb U/Th in Gen-II production runs, versus ~40 ppb in Schott 8246. With 9438 units at reduced glass mass per unit (~400g versus 850g), total PMT U/Th contribution drops by factor ~8.

---

## 2. Improved Neutral-Current Neutron Detection

### Current Limitation
The 3He NCD array captures ~37% of neutrons with 16 ms mean capture time, creating substantial accidental coincidence backgrounds. The 15 cm dead zone at string ends, ~15% optical obscuration, and pulse-shape discrimination efficiency limit the effective NC detection efficiency to ~25% usable events.

### Proposed Upgrade A: Gadolinium-Loaded Water Phase

Rather than NCD strings (which obscure Cherenkov light), dissolve **gadolinium sulfate Gd2(SO4)3** at 0.1% concentration in the D2O:

- **Neutron capture**: Natural Gd has thermal neutron cross-section of 49,000 barns (versus 5330 b for 3He and ~0.5 mb for deuterium), capturing >90% of thermalized neutrons within ~30 µs at 0.1% loading
- **Capture signal**: Gd(n,γ) releases 8.0 MeV in a cascade of 3-4 gamma rays (versus 6.25 MeV single gamma on deuterium), producing a distinctive high-multiplicity PMT hit pattern easily distinguished from CC electrons
- **Capture time**: Mean capture time ~30 µs versus 16 ms for pure D2O with NCDs, dramatically reducing accidental backgrounds from radioactivity
- **No optical obscuration**: Eliminates the 15% photon absorption from NCD strings entirely

**Implementation specifics:**
- Gd2(SO4)3 must be purified to <10 ppt U/Th; this is achievable with ion-exchange chromatography using Chelex-100 resin followed by electrodeposition assay, as demonstrated by SK-Gd R&D
- Modify the existing D2O RO recirculation system with an additional **Gd-selective ion exchange column** (DOWEX 50W-X8 cation resin) to remove Gd during desalination phase without full water replacement
- Add a **dedicated Gd assay system** using ICP-MS for concentration monitoring at ±1% accuracy
- The 8.0 MeV gamma cascade requires no threshold change and is detectable above the 5 MeV analysis threshold with high efficiency

### Proposed Upgrade B: Enhanced NCD Readout (if strings retained)

If Gd loading is deferred, replace the analog delay-line position readout in each NCD string with **distributed flash ADC readout**:

- Install **Texas Instruments ADS5400 12-bit 1 GSPS ADCs** at each string preamplifier, digitizing the full ionization current waveform
- Implement FPGA-based (Xilinx Kintex-7) pulse shape analysis discriminating n-capture events from alpha particles using 2D PSD parameter space (rise time versus integrated charge), improving the usable efficiency from 25% toward the nominal 45% capture efficiency
- Replace the single 91Ω South Bay Cable coax per string with **low-mass twisted pair** for digital readout, reducing U/Th cable contribution

---

## 3. Water Purification Enhancement for Lower Energy Threshold

### Current Limitation
The analysis threshold is ~5 MeV, set by radioactive backgrounds particularly from 214Bi (2.45 MeV gamma, photodisintegration) and Cherenkov light from beta decays. The D2O target requires <3×10⁻¹⁵ g/g Th and <4.5×10⁻¹⁴ g/g U.

### Proposed Upgrade: Electrodeposition Assay + Continuous Radium Removal

- Replace batch SUF (seeded ultrafiltration) assay with **continuous-flow MnO2-coated fiber ultrafiltration** using Membralox ceramic membranes (0.2 µm pore, alumina substrate with MnO2 coating), operating at 50 L/min continuously rather than batch 100-tonne campaigns
- Add a **second-pass electrodeposition Ra/Pb removal column** using bismuth phosphate co-precipitation followed by electrodeposition on stainless steel electrodes, achieving Ra removal efficiency >99% per pass
- Install **online ICP-MS** (Thermo Fisher iCAP-RQ) with direct water injection at 0.1 mL/min for continuous U/Th/Ra monitoring at 10⁻¹⁶ g/g sensitivity, replacing the current delayed radiochemical assay methods
- Upgrade the Process Degasser with an additional **membrane contactactor stage** (Liqui-Cel 10×28 Extra-Flow) to reduce dissolved Rn from ~50-fold to ~5000-fold reduction, targeting <0.01 pCi/L Rn in D2O

These improvements would lower the effective analysis threshold from 5 MeV toward 3.5 MeV, opening sensitivity to the pep and CNO solar neutrino fluxes.

---

## 4. Electronics and Data Acquisition Modernization

### Current Limitation
The three-ASIC chipset (SNOD/SNOINT/QUSN7) provides 12-bit ADC resolution, 16-deep analog memory, and ~400 ns per-channel deadtime. The 19-crate VME architecture with 8 MB/s XL1/XL2 links becomes a bottleneck for high-rate calibration and supernova burst scenarios.

### Proposed Upgrade: Waveform Digitizer Architecture

Replace the three-chip ASIC set with **DRS4-based waveform sampling boards** (Paul Scherrer Institute DRS4 chip, 5 GSPS, 1024 cells deep):

- **Timing resolution**: 20 ps RMS per channel versus 1.7 ns, enabling photon-by-photon Cherenkov ring reconstruction rather than hit-counting triggers
- **Dynamic range**: 11.5 effective bits over 1V range; dual-range input (1:16 split retained) gives >17 effective bits
- **Dead time**: DRS4 operates in cascaded mode with <2% deadtime at 10 kHz per channel versus 400 ns fixed window
- **Waveform capture**: Full 200 ns capture window at 5 GSPS resolves prepulses, late pulses, and after-pulses in situ without separate characterization runs

**Backend upgrade:**
- Replace VME/68040 eCPU architecture with **ATCA shelf hosting Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs** (VU9P) for trigger formation, providing 32×100 GbE links to surface DAQ
- Implement **trigger-less readout**: stream all PMT waveforms above 0.1 pe threshold continuously at ~40 GB/s aggregate, performing online event building in a GPU farm (NVIDIA A100 cluster, 8 cards) using real-time Cherenkov ring fitting for trigger decisions
- This eliminates the global trigger deadtime entirely and enables sub-threshold analysis for supernova relic neutrinos

---

## 5. Acrylic Vessel and Structural Improvements

### Current Limitation
The 5.5 cm thick UVT acrylic panels have bulk absorption coefficient of 0.01 cm⁻¹ at 400 nm and 0.18 cm⁻¹ at 320 nm, significantly attenuating the near-UV portion of the Cherenkov spectrum where PMT response is reasonable.

### Proposed Upgrade: Low-Absorption Acrylic Reformulation

- Specify **Mitsubishi Rayon DELAGLAS HT acrylic** with <0.003 cm⁻¹ bulk absorption at 400 nm and <0.05 cm⁻¹ at 350 nm, representing factor 3-4 improvement in UV transmission
- This is achievable with reduced UV-absorbing monomer impurities and careful polymerization; the same 5.5 cm nominal thickness would transmit ~15% more 350-nm photons
- For the rope groove equatorial panels (11.4 cm thick), use **borosilicate glass panels** with silicone gel coupling to acrylic, achieving near-zero bulk absorption; structural bonding via room-temperature vulcanizing silicone adhesive qualified to the same 27.5 MPa bond strength standard

---

## Summary of Expected Performance Improvements

| Parameter | Current SNO | Upgraded SNO |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|
| Effective photocathode coverage | 54% | ~75% |
| Single photon timing resolution | 1.7 ns RMS | ~100 ps RMS |
| NC neutron detection efficiency | ~25% usable | >80% (Gd) |
| Neutron capture time | 16 ms | ~30 µs |
| Analysis energy threshold | ~5 MeV | ~3.5 MeV |
| PMT U/Th contribution | ~100 µg/PMT | ~10 µg/PMT |
| Electronics deadtime | ~400 ns/channel | <10 ns effective |

The most impactful single upgrade is Gd-loading combined with LAPPD deployment, as these jointly address the two primary statistical limitations: NC detection efficiency and photon collection efficiency.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Improved Physics Performance

## 1. Liquid Argon Scintillation Veto (Highest Priority)

The paper explicitly states this was deferred to Phase II after LArGe demonstrated its effectiveness. Concrete implementation:

**Wavelength Shifter Deployment**
- Coat the existing radon shroud and mini-shrouds with tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) at ~1 mg/cm² deposition density
- Replace the plain 30 µm copper foil radon shroud with a composite: copper structural layer plus evaporated TPB on inner surface facing detectors
- The existing VM2000 foil in the water tank already demonstrates the collaboration's competence with wavelength-shifting reflectors; apply analogous technology inside the LAr volume

**Photosensor Selection**
- Deploy Hamamatsu R11065 3-inch PMTs or SensL/onsemi MicroFC-60035 silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) arranged on the radon shroud structure
- SiPMs are preferred over PMTs here specifically because: they operate stably at 87K LAr temperature, have no 40K background from borosilicate glass, and their compact form factor minimizes material near detectors
- Target ~50 SiPMs of 6×6 mm² active area distributed around the radon shroud cylinder, providing roughly 3% optical coverage of the inner volume
- Expected signal rejection: the paper cites ~80% background suppression demonstrated in LArGe; full implementation should reduce BI by factor ~5 in the ROI

**Readout Electronics for SiPMs**
- Custom cryogenic transimpedance amplifiers using Cremat CR-110 or equivalent JFET-input designs tested at 77K
- Requires additional feedthroughs through the manifold; use existing DN200 ports where possible

---

## 2. Replacement of Phase I Coaxial Detectors with BEGe or ICPC Detectors

The paper notes Phase II BEGe detectors achieve 1.7 keV FWHM versus 4.2-5.3 keV for Phase I coaxial detectors, and have demonstrated pulse shape discrimination (PSD) capability.

**Inverted Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC) Geometry**
- Beyond BEGe, ICPC detectors (developed at UNC/Majorana) combine the mass of coaxial detectors (~2 kg per crystal) with the single-channel point-contact readout enabling PSD
- Target: deploy 35 ICPC detectors of ~2 kg each for 70 kg total active mass in Phase II configuration
- Key specification: achieve A/E (current amplitude to energy ratio) discrimination parameter separating single-site (0νββ signal-like) from multi-site (gamma background) events with >90% signal acceptance at >90% background rejection

**Improved Dead Layer Characterization**
- The paper notes active mass assessed at ~87% with uncertainty; deploy each detector with a dedicated low-activity 241Am collimated source scan in the GDL test stand before insertion
- Use the existing LAr test bench to map dead layer thickness to <50 µm precision using the 59.5 keV gamma line

**Improved Electrical Contact Design**
- The paper reports ANG1, ANG3, RG3 required additional reprocessing due to high leakage currents; the Chinese hat p+ contact pressed by silicon spring is mechanically adequate but electrically marginal
- Replace silicon spring with a custom-machined PTFE-backed gold-plated beryllium-copper spring finger contact, providing more consistent pressure distribution and lower contact resistance variability
- Eliminate the copper strip HV contact pressed by disc/screw assembly; replace with a gold wire ball-bonded contact to the n+ surface, as used in commercial point-contact detector production

---

## 3. Active 42Ar/42K Background Suppression

This was identified as the dominant unexpected background source. The mini-shroud addresses ion drift but not the underlying 42Ar activity.

**Nitrogen-Flushed Mini-Shroud Interior**
- Modify mini-shroud design to be fully hermetic with a top cap sealing the LAr volume inside from the bulk LAr
- Fill the interior volume with ultra-pure liquid nitrogen rather than LAr, eliminating 42Ar entirely from the detector-proximate volume
- The existing LN2 cooling infrastructure (280 L/day consumption noted) provides a natural supply; route a dedicated LN2 fill line through the cable chain
- Engineering challenge: thermal interface between LN2-filled mini-shroud (~77K) and surrounding LAr (~87K) requires a thin-walled low-conductivity shroud; use 50 µm titanium foil (lower thermal conductivity than copper, radiopurity verified by the collaboration for similar applications)

**Alternatively: LAr Purification for 42Ar Removal**
- 42Ar (half-life 32.9 yr) cannot be removed by activated charcoal (unlike 222Rn)
- Implement continuous LAr recirculation through a cryogenic distillation column to exploit the slight mass difference; this is technically demonstrated at the DEAP-3600 and DarkSide experiments
- Required throughput: ~64 m³ LAr volume; target one full volume exchange per 6 months through a 1 L/min distillation system

---

## 4. Upgraded Front-End Electronics (CC3 Preamplifier)

The CC2 preamplifier uses commercial IC packages (BF862 JFET, AD8651 op-amp) not optimized for LAr temperatures.

**Custom Cryogenic ASIC**
- Design a custom CMOS ASIC in 130nm or 65nm technology (demonstrated stable at 77K by multiple groups including ATLAS and CMS upgrade programs)
- Target specifications based on CC2 limitations identified in the paper:
  - Noise: reduce from 0.8 keV baseline to <0.3 keV FWHM contribution at Qββ
  - Power: reduce from 45 mW/channel to <10 mW/channel, reducing heat load and microphonics-inducing boiling
  - Rise time: improve from 55 ns to <20 ns, improving PSD figure of merit
- The Cuﬂon PCB substrate should be retained for radiopurity; ASIC die can be directly wirebonded

**Feedback Resistor Replacement**
- Current CC2 uses 500 MΩ feedback resistor (RF in Fig. 15); at LAr temperature resistance values shift unpredictably
- Replace with pulsed-reset circuit using a JFET reset switch, eliminating the feedback resistor entirely and its associated Johnson noise contribution; this is standard practice in bolometer readout

**Differential Signal Transmission**
- Current scheme uses single-ended 50Ω coaxial lines (Habia SM50); over 20m cable length this accumulates noise
- Implement fully differential output stage at the CC2, transmit on twisted-pair within the cable chain, convert back to single-ended at the FADC input
- Expected noise improvement: ~3 dB reduction in picked-up interference, particularly relevant for the microphonics observed in the LAr environment

---

## 5. Enhanced Muon Veto Coverage

The paper reports 97.2% minimum detection efficiency with the current system; the neck region is identified as a coverage gap.

**Water Cherenkov PMT Upgrade**
- Replace ETL 9350KB/9354KB tubes with Hamamatsu R7081 high-quantum-efficiency variants (35% QE vs ~25% for ETL tubes at 420 nm)
- Increase PMT count from 66 to 90 by utilizing currently empty mounting positions; the skirt provides 6 mounts, the paper implies additional mounting capacity exists
- Install 6 additional PMTs on the underside of the cryostat balcony structure facing downward into the volume between cryostat skirt and water tank floor

**Neck Region Coverage**
- Current plastic scintillator array covers 4×3 m² but the paper identifies muons entering the cryostat neck as a specific gap
- Add a dedicated annular scintillator ring of 12 panels arranged in a circle matching the 800mm inner neck diameter, installed immediately above the manifold on the clean room floor
- Use Saint-Gobain BC-408 scintillator (faster decay time: 2.1 ns vs UPS-923A's ~3 ns) with SiPM readout rather than PMTs to fit the constrained geometry
- Trigger requirement: 2-of-12 coincidence within 10 ns, providing >99.5% efficiency for muons passing through the neck

## 6. Radon Mitigation Improvements

The measured 54.7 mBq cryostat emanation rate is the dominant identified radon source.

**Electropolishing of Inner Copper Shield**
- The current copper shield consists of 16 tonnes of OFRP copper plates; the paper reports radon increased by ~20 mBq after copper installation
- Electropolish the copper surfaces to remove the outermost ~10 µm layer where radium daughters are implanted from prior cosmic ray exposure; demonstrated to reduce 222Rn emanation by factor 3-5 in Borexino copper components
- This is feasible in-situ using a portable electropolishing rig through the existing access neck

**Radon Shroud Improvement**
- Current 30 µm copper foil radon shroud provides up to factor 7 suppression
- Replace with a hermetically welded stainless steel cylinder with CF-flange top and bottom connections, eliminating the current open-top design implied by the description
- Add a LN2-cooled copper cold trap immediately above the liquid surface inside the radon shroud to freeze out 222Rn before it can reach detectors

|---------|---------------|------------------------|
| LAr scintillation veto | Multi-site gamma rejection | Factor 5-10 |
| ICPC detector geometry | PSD capability + energy resolution | Factor 2-3 via PSD |

The LAr scintillation veto combined with ICPC PSD represents the highest-leverage combination, as both provide event-by-event discrimination rather than passive shielding, and their background rejection is largely independent and therefore multiplicative.

# Hardware Design Upgrade Proposals for the ProtoDUNE-SP Detector

Based on careful reading of the technical details presented in the paper, I identify the primary performance limitations and propose concrete hardware upgrades targeting each.

---

## 1. High Voltage System Stabilization

### Identified Problem
The paper describes persistent "current streamers" originating from a single ground plane (GP#6), with rates of 4-6 per day under auto-recovery, tied to charging of insulating FC support materials. The effect is enhanced by high LAr purity—meaning the best physics conditions exacerbate the instability.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Resistive Field Cage Profiles**
Replace extruded aluminum profiles with carbon-loaded UHMWPE or resistive glass profiles (surface resistivity ~10⁹–10¹¹ Ω/sq). This bleeds accumulated surface charge continuously rather than allowing buildup to discharge threshold. Similar approach was validated in EXO-200 and nEXO R&D. The profile cross-section geometry need not change, preserving field uniformity calculations.

**Segmented Ground Planes with Individual Current Monitoring**
Replace monolithic perforated stainless steel GP sheets with 4×4 segmented panels, each with an independent 100 MΩ monitoring resistor to a common bus. This provides spatial resolution on discharge location at ~20 cm scale rather than knowing only which of 12 GPs is involved, enabling targeted diagnosis. Current sensitivity of ~10 nA per segment is achievable with standard instrumentation amplifiers operating at room temperature on the warm side.

**Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) Coating on FRP Supports**
Apply 50–100 nm Al₂O₃ via ALD on all fiberglass-reinforced plastic structural components before assembly. ALD coatings are conformal, pinhole-free, and have been demonstrated to reduce surface charge accumulation on insulators in liquid noble detectors (demonstrated in XENON1T SiPM mounting structures). This directly addresses the charging mechanism identified in the paper without requiring structural redesign.

**RC Filter Upgrade at HV Feedthrough**
Add a third filter stage with a 10 GΩ / 10 nF RC combination between the existing two stages and the feedthrough. This extends the time constant for energy delivery during a discharge event from ~milliseconds to ~100 ms, reducing peak discharge current by roughly two orders of magnitude and limiting damage potential to wire planes. Filter resistors should use the same cylindrical coaxial geometry described in the paper, rated to 300 kV.

---

## 2. Anode Plane Assembly Wire Readout

### Identified Problem
The paper reports ENC of ~400 e⁻ at cryogenic temperatures for collection wires with 150 pF input capacitance, yielding SNR of 13–16 for MIPs. Induction plane signals are inherently bipolar and smaller. Wire breakage risk exists during cool-down despite 5 N tension design margin.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Replacement of Beryllium Copper Wire with Stainless Steel Clad Copper Wire**
Move from 150 μm CuBe (resistivity 7.68 μΩ-cm) to 125 μm Cu-clad stainless steel wire with ~4 μΩ-cm effective resistivity at the signal frequencies of interest. The stainless core provides higher yield strength (~800 MPa vs ~600 MPa for CuBe), reducing breakage risk. The copper cladding (20–30% by cross-section) carries the RF signal via skin effect at operating frequencies. Critically, this eliminates beryllium toxicity hazards during production, which are a significant practical limitation on wire handling and quality control procedures described extensively in the paper.

**LArASIC Next-Generation FE ASIC with Improved Input Stage**
The current FE ASIC uses a p-channel input MOSFET with L/W = 0.27 μm/10 μm. Redesign the input transistor in 65 nm CMOS (which has demonstrated cryogenic operation in multiple groups) with L/W optimized for the 150 pF wire capacitance load: target W ~50 μm, L ~65 nm, operating at 4 mA drain current. Simulation studies at Brookhaven and SLAC suggest this can reduce ENC to below 200 e⁻ at 2 μs peaking time for equivalent capacitance, improving MIP SNR from ~15 to ~30. The 65 nm node also reduces power per channel from 6 mW to approximately 2.5 mW, reducing LAr boiling near the electronics.

**Integrated ADC+FE Single-Chip Architecture**
The current design uses separate FE ASICs and ADC ASICs (16,000 vs 320,000 transistors respectively), requiring inter-chip connections that introduce noise. A monolithic 128-channel ADC+FE chip in 65 nm CMOS eliminates this interface. The ADC can be upgraded from 12-bit to 14-bit at the same 2 MSPS rate, improving dynamic range from 72 dB to 84 dB. This directly benefits reconstruction of highly ionizing tracks (protons, pions near stopping) which currently saturate the 300 fC full-scale range at 25 mV/fC gain.

**Cold FPGA Mezzanine Replacement with SiGe ASIC**
Replace the warm-temperature-rated FPGA mezzanine with a custom SiGe BiCMOS serializer/MUX ASIC that operates reliably at 87 K. The current FPGA operates at room temperature on a board that sits in the LAr, introducing thermal gradients and reliability concerns from repeated thermal cycling. A SiGe ASIC (IBM 8HP process, demonstrated to 4 K operation) implementing the 4:1 MUX and 1.28 Gbps serial driver would eliminate this vulnerability and reduce the thermal load from the FEMB by approximately 30%.

---

## 3. Photon Detection System

### Identified Problem
The paper reports photon detection efficiencies of 0.08% (dip-coated), 0.21% (double-shift), and 2% (ARAPUCA) per module, with the full system yielding ~1.9 photons/MeV at 3.3 m only if entirely ARAPUCA-equipped. The 100 ns timing resolution requirement is met but marginally. The 128 nm VUV scintillation light must be wavelength-shifted before detection.

### Proposed Upgrades

**X-ARAPUCA with Expanded Active Area**
The paper's ARAPUCA cells use a single dichroic filter window. Upgrade to the X-ARAPUCA geometry (developed after the construction period described) using two parallel filter windows facing opposite sides of a reflective cavity, doubling the acceptance solid angle per unit bar volume. Replace the PTP external coating (200 μg/cm²) with evaporated TPB at 400 μg/cm², which has ~30% higher VUV conversion efficiency at 128 nm. Use the same bar form factor (209.7 cm × 11.8 cm × 2.3 cm) to maintain APA compatibility. Replace the 12-MPPC array with 24 FBK-NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs (3×3 mm², 30 μm cell pitch), which have demonstrated 50% photon detection efficiency at 87 K for 430 nm light vs approximately 25% for the SensL devices used in the original design.

**VUV-Sensitive SiPM Direct Detection Strips**
For modules not using the ARAPUCA geometry, replace the WLS light guide approach entirely with VUV-sensitive SiPMs arranged along the bar edges. Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) has developed SiPM variants with SiO₂ window removal and specialized anti-reflection coating that achieve ~15% PDE at 128 nm at 77 K. An array of 48 such 6×6 mm² devices per bar, placed along both long edges, eliminates the two-step WLS efficiency losses (each step is ~80% efficient at best) that limit the dip-coated and double-shift designs. Estimated module efficiency improvement: factor of 5–8 over the dip-coated baseline.

**Cryogenic SiPM Signal Amplification at the APA**
The current design transmits unamplified SiPM signals over 20 m Cat6 cables, relying on the SSP's differential amplifier at room temperature. The paper notes SNR of 6 for ARAPUCA channels. Add a cryogenic transimpedance amplifier (TIA) per SiPM group using a GaAs PHEMT (ATF-34143 or equivalent, characterized to operate at 77 K) providing 20 dB of gain with less than 0.5 pF input capacitance and 2 nW power dissipation. Locate the TIA on the SiPM mounting PCB within the APA slot. This reduces the impact of 20 m cable capacitance (~200 pF) on signal rise time from ~10 ns to ~2 ns, improving timing resolution from ~100 ns to an achievable ~10 ns, enabling better t₀ determination and spatial event localization.

**Polarization-Preserving Fiber for LCM Calibration System**
Replace the existing quartz fiber-optic delivery for the UV LED calibration system with polarization-maintaining fiber and add a Glan-Thompson polarizer at each diffuser. This enables measurement of SiPM angular response and cross-talk as a function of polarization state, providing additional calibration handles. More importantly, adding 4 diffuser positions per CPA face (from the current 5 total to 20 total) with optical multiplexing via a MEMS fiber switch improves spatial uniformity of the calibration measurement across the APA surface from ~30 cm to ~10 cm granularity.

---

## 4. Cryogenics Instrumentation

### Identified Problem
The paper reports purity monitor charge ratio uncertainties of 1.9–3.9% and a temperature measurement accuracy of 2.6 mK. The dynamic T-gradient monitor's stepper motor uses a ferrofluidic seal identified as a reliability concern. CFD model comparison shows unexplained features (bump at 6.2 m, temperature deviations at the bottom).

### Proposed Upgrades

**Ionic Liquid-Based Purity Monitor with Extended Dynamic Range**
The current purity monitors saturate at electron lifetimes above ~70 ms (top monitor) because Q_A/Q_C approaches 1 and the relative lifetime uncertainty diverges. Replace the photocathode UV illumination with a pulsed 193 nm ArF laser source (Coherent COMPex series) delivering 10× more photoelectrons per pulse via the existing 8-fiber feedthrough. This reduces the fractional statistical uncertainty in Q_A/Q_C by a factor of √10, extending reliable lifetime measurement to >300 ms. Additionally, add a second electrode pair at 7 cm drift distance within the same monitor body to provide a short-drift reference measurement simultaneously with the long-drift measurement, enabling real-time normalization for light source fluctuations and reducing systematic uncertainty from 3.9% to below 1%.

**Resistance Temperature Detectors Replacement with Johnson Noise Thermometry**
Replace the Lake Shore PT102 platinum RTDs with Johnson Noise Thermometry (JNT) sensors using NIST-traceable absolute accuracy of 0.1 mK without calibration drift over the multi-year operational period. The JNT approach measures the thermal noise voltage across a known resistor (100 Ω precision wirewound) using a cross-correlation technique that rejects amplifier noise. Commercial JNT modules (Measurements International Model 6010B) achieve 1 mK precision at 87 K in a 100-second measurement. This eliminates the 2.6 mK calibration uncertainty and removes dependence on the "pumps-off" calibration method as a cross-check.

**Bellows-Sealed Linear Actuator for Dynamic T-Gradient Monitor**
Replace the ferrofluidic dynamic seal on the stepper motor with a stainless steel edge-welded bellows actuator (150 mm stroke, Servometer or equivalent). Metal bellows seals have zero leak rate by design and have demonstrated >10⁷ cycles at cryogenic temperatures in space applications. The external linear actuator (piezoelectric or ball-screw) can be decoupled from the internal rod via a magnetic coupling through the bellows wall, eliminating any shaft penetration of the LAr boundary entirely. This removes the most mechanically complex reliability concern in the instrumentation system.

**Distributed Fiber Optic Temperature Sensing**
Add a Rayleigh-scattering distributed temperature sensor (Luna ODiSI or OFS BL-SENSOR equivalent) using a single 50 μm GRIN multimode fiber routed through the detector volume in a serpentine pattern, providing temperature measurements at 1 cm spatial resolution along the full 8 m vertical extent of the cryostat. At 87 K, Rayleigh backscatter thermometry achieves 0.1 K precision at 1 cm resolution with commercial interrogators. This provides 800 temperature measurement points per fiber pass compared to the current 92 discrete sensors, enabling full 3D temperature field reconstruction for CFD validation and identification of localized convection cells responsible for the unexplained temperature features noted in the paper.

---

## 5. Data Acquisition and Trigger

### Identified Problem
The paper describes 430 Gb/s raw TPC data rate requiring factor-of-4 compression, 25 Hz trigger rate limited by 20 Gb/s transfer bandwidth, and ongoing development of self-triggering capability on a single server per APA. The FELIX system reads one APA as proof-of-concept.

### Proposed Upgrades

**FPGA-Based Hit Finding on FELIX Server with Intel Stratix 10 MX**
Replace the current Intel QAT compression acceleration with Intel Stratix 10 MX FPGAs integrated directly on the FELIX PCIe card (via CXL or direct PCIe attachment). Implement the hit-finding algorithm in FPGA fabric rather than CPU software, reducing latency from ~10 ms to ~50 μs and reducing server count from one per APA to one per four APAs. The Stratix 10 MX has 32 GB HBM2 memory on-package providing 500 GB/s memory bandwidth sufficient to buffer 2 APAs at full rate simultaneously. This directly enables the DUNE-SP self-triggering architecture described as a goal in the paper.

**Waveform Compression Using Machine Learning Inference at WIB**
Upgrade the WIB FPGA from Altera Arria V to Xilinx Versal AI Core series, which integrates AI Engine processors alongside programmable logic. Implement a trained autoencoder network (16:1 compression demonstrated on LArTPC data by the Deep Underground group at Fermilab) directly in the WIB AI engines. This performs lossy-but-physics-preserving compression before data even leaves the cryostat flange, reducing the 430 Gb/s to approximately 27 Gb/s and eliminating the 20 Gb/s transfer bottleneck that constrains trigger rate to 25 Hz. Trigger rate could increase to ~200 Hz, proportionally increasing physics dataset size.

**White Rabbit Timing with Sub-Nanosecond Synchronization**
Replace the GPS-disciplined oscillator and custom encoded timing stream with a White Rabbit PTP implementation (CERN/GSI standard, hardware available from Seven Solutions). White Rabbit achieves <1 ns synchronization accuracy across fiber networks versus the current system's implied ~10 ns accuracy (inferred from the 20 ns CRT timing resolution and 60 ns CRT hit resolution). Sub-nanosecond timing directly benefits proton decay search sensitivity through improved vertex reconstruction and reduces the coincidence window for CRT-TPC matching from 80 ns to ~5 ns, reducing accidental coincidence backgrounds by a factor of 16.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for ProtoDUNE-SP / DUNE-SP

## 1. Anode Plane Assembly Improvements

### Wire Replacement with Pixel or Strip Readout
The current 150 μm CuBe wire geometry with ±35.7° induction angles creates intrinsic ambiguities in 3D reconstruction. Replacing with **pixelated charge readout (LArPix)** would eliminate these ambiguities entirely.

- **Specific technology**: LArPix ASIC tiles (already demonstrated at 0.16 cm² pixel pitch by LBNL) mounted on tiled PCB panels replacing wire frames
- **Quantitative benefit**: Eliminates ~15% of events with reconstruction ambiguity in multi-track topologies, particularly critical for νe appearance signal
- **Trade-off**: Power dissipation increases to ~1 μW/channel, requiring revised thermal management; channel count increases from 2,560 to ~50,000 per APA panel

### Improved Wire Tension Monitoring
Current system has no in-situ continuous wire tension monitoring. Embedding **piezoelectric resonance sensors** at wire termination boards would detect wire breaks and tension drift during cool-down.

- **Specific component**: Murata PKGS series piezo elements at each wire board stack
- **Implementation**: Monitor resonant frequency shift; 5 N nominal tension has ~15% variation tolerance before reconstruction impact

---

## 2. Cold Electronics Upgrades

### FE ASIC Replacement with Lower-Noise Architecture
The current LArASIC achieves ~400 e⁻ ENC at 77K with 150 pF load, adequate but not optimal. The dominant noise source is the input MOSFET thermal noise.

- **Specific upgrade**: Replace with **COLDATA/COLDADC successor ASICs** using 65 nm CMOS (vs. current 180 nm), reducing channel power from 6 mW to ~1.5 mW and ENC to ~150 e⁻
- **65 nm process advantage**: Lower threshold voltage reduces flicker noise corner frequency from ~10 kHz to ~1 kHz, directly improving signal-to-noise on slow induction signals
- **Practical impact**: SNR improvement from ~16:1 to ~45:1 on collection wires enables detection of sub-MIP ionization, improving low-energy neutrino reconstruction below 100 MeV threshold

### ADC Sampling Rate Increase
Current 2 MHz maximum sampling (500 ns) limits transverse diffusion measurement and thus z-position resolution.

- **Upgrade**: Implement **4 MHz sampling** with 12-bit resolution in new ADC ASIC
- **Physics benefit**: Reduces drift coordinate uncertainty from ~1.5 mm to ~0.8 mm RMS, approaching wire pitch resolution
- **Required change**: WIB bandwidth increases from ~5 Gbps to ~10 Gbps per FEMB group, requiring upgraded optical transceivers (already near FELIX bandwidth limits)

### On-FEMB Zero Suppression
Currently all data streamed continuously at 430 Gb/s total. Adding **on-FPGA real-time zero suppression** with configurable hit-finding thresholds would:

- Reduce continuous data rate by factor ~50× during non-beam periods
- Enable self-triggered supernova detection mode without DAQ bottleneck
- **Specific implementation**: Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC replacing current Spartan-6 equivalent, providing ~4× FPGA logic resources for hit-finding firmware

---

## 3. Photon Detection System Overhaul

### Full ARAPUCA Coverage Replacing Light Guides
The paper explicitly reports photon detection efficiency of only **0.08% for dip-coated and 0.21% for double-shift bars**, versus **2% for ARAPUCA cells**. The efficiency gap is ~25×.

- **Upgrade**: Replace all 58 light guide modules with **X-ARAPUCA supercells** (the evolved design adopted for DUNE FD)
- **X-ARAPUCA specific design**: Dichroic filter plates (Omega Optical 400 nm cutoff) with both faces coated via resistive evaporation — external PTP at 200 μg/cm², internal TPB at 300 μg/cm² — inside VIKUITI ESR reflector cavity
- **Photosensor upgrade**: Replace current SensL 35 μm pixel SiPMs with **Hamamatsu S14160-6050HS** (50 μm pixel, 74% PDE at 450 nm at room temperature, improved at 87K) or **FBK NUV-HD-Cryo** optimized for 87K operation with ~55% PDE at 420 nm
- **Quantitative impact**: Extrapolated full ARAPUCA coverage yields 1.9 PE/MeV at 3.3 m; full X-ARAPUCA with improved SiPMs projects to ~8-10 PE/MeV, enabling calorimetric reconstruction of supernova neutrinos at 5-15 MeV

### SiPM Cold Amplification Stage
Currently signals travel 20 m on Cat6 cable with no cold amplification, degrading SNR particularly for single-PE detection.

- **Add cold transimpedance amplifier**: Single-stage **BF862 JFET-based TIA** at the SiPM array output, power budget ~5 mW per module at 87K (verified stable)
- **Benefit**: Reduces effective cable noise contribution by ~10 dB, improving single-PE resolution from current SNR ~6 (ARAPUCA) to ~20+
- **Critical for**: Supernova burst detection where single-PE counting statistics matter

### Timing Resolution Improvement
Current 100 ns timing resolution requirement is met marginally. Upgrading SSP readout:

- Replace current 150 MHz 14-bit ADC with **1 GHz sampling PSEC4A ASIC** (developed at University of Chicago) achieving ~10 ps timing resolution
- **Physics impact**: Enables t₀ determination to ~2 cm position resolution vs. current ~15 cm, critical for non-beam events (nucleon decay, atmospheric neutrinos)

---

## 4. High Voltage System Redesign

### Resistive Field Cage Profiles
The paper describes persistent HV instabilities attributed to charging of insulating FRP support structures, with current streamers occurring on a regular cycle.

- **Replace extruded aluminum profiles with resistive-material profiles**: Use **carbon-loaded UHMWPE** profiles with bulk resistivity ~10⁹ Ω·cm, similar to approach in MicroBooNE upgrade studies
- **Mechanism**: Resistive surfaces prevent charge accumulation that drives the streamer instability, eliminating the charging-up process described in Section 4.1.4
- **Specific material**: Ensinger TECAFINE PC ELS (electrostatic dissipative polycarbonate) or equivalent, processable by extrusion into the existing profile geometry
- **Expected improvement**: Eliminate current streamers entirely rather than managing with auto-recovery, increasing HV uptime from 96-98% to >99.5%

### Segmented Cathode with Modular HV
Current single −180 kV supply means any instability drops entire drift field.

- **Upgrade**: Divide CPA into three independent horizontal segments, each with dedicated **iseg SHQ series 300 kV supply** with 10 nA current resolution
- **Benefit**: Localize HV faults to one-third of detector; maintain 67% data-taking efficiency during discharge events
- **Added feature**: Enable differential drift field studies (E-field mapping) using independent segment voltages

## 5. Cryogenics Instrumentation Upgrades

### Inline Purity Monitoring
Current purity monitors are outside the TPC volume and measure only three vertical positions.

- **Add fiber-coupled Rayleigh scattering monitors**: Deploy **4 UV laser paths** at 266 nm crossing the drift volume at different heights using existing penetrations
- **Technology**: Quantel Ultra CFR Nd:YAG laser, 4th harmonic, with in-vacuum fiber injection; scattered light detected by 16-channel PMT array
- **Benefit**: 3D purity map with 10 cm spatial resolution vs. three-point measurement; enables detection of localized contamination pockets near outgassing components

### Acoustic Discharge Detection
HV streamers are currently detected only via current monitors with ~1 second latency.

- **Add piezoelectric acoustic sensors**: Mount **5× Physik Instrumente P-876 DuraAct** patch transducers on cryostat outer wall
- **Detection**: Acoustic emission from discharges propagates through LAr and steel with characteristic frequency ~100 kHz; enables <1 ms localization of discharge position
- **Implementation cost**: Minimal — sensors operate at room temperature on outer vessel

### FPGA-Based Trigger Primitive Generation
Currently trigger primitives are generated in software on CPUs, limiting real-time performance.

- **Upgrade**: Implement **trigger primitive generation in FPGA firmware within FELIX cards** using Xilinx Alveo U250 (replacing current BNL-711 PCIe cards)

Current WIB-to-FELIX links at 10.3 Gbps are near saturation with 4 MHz sampling upgrade.
