# Hardware Design Upgrades for SNO

## Assessment of Primary Physics Limitations

The core physics goal is distinguishing CC, NC, and ES reactions with maximum statistical power and minimal systematic uncertainty. The binding constraints from the paper are: photocathode coverage (54% effective after reflector losses), PMT timing resolution (1.7 ns RMS), neutron detection efficiency (37% with NCD array), and radioactive backgrounds requiring stringent material purity. I'll address each with concrete upgrade proposals.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System

### Replace Hamamatsu R1408 with Large-Area SiPM Tiles

The R1408 tubes provide ~10% single-photon quantum efficiency in the Cherenkov-relevant 300-500 nm range. Modern silicon photomultipliers offer substantially better performance.

**Specific implementation:**
- Deploy **Hamamatsu S13361-6075 SiPM tiles** (6×6 mm² cells, 75 µm microcell pitch) or equivalent FBK NUV-HD-SF devices arranged in panels behind the existing Winston cone concentrators
- Peak photon detection efficiency of **50-55% at 420 nm** versus ~10% for the R1408 photocathode
- These devices are intrinsically rated for operation in cold, high-purity water environments when encapsulated in optical-grade silicone (Shin-Etsu KE-103 or equivalent with measured U/Th < 1 pg/g)
- The 9438 PMT positions would be retrofitted with **20×20 cm² SiPM tile assemblies**, each comprising approximately 16 individual 5×5 cm² tiles read out in groups, maintaining the existing mechanical mounting geometry on the ABS hexagonal cells
- Dark count rate at 10°C drops to approximately **50-100 kcps/cm²**, manageable with coincidence gating already implemented in the QUSN7 trigger logic

**Physics impact:** Effective photocathode coverage increases from 54% to approximately 85% of the geometric acceptance, yielding roughly 1.6× more detected photons per event. This directly improves energy resolution from the nominal ~15% at 10 MeV toward ~8%, tightening the reconstructed electron energy spectrum for CC/ES separation and lowering the effective energy threshold by approximately 0.5 MeV.

**Radioactivity consideration:** SiPM silicon substrate has intrinsic U/Th at sub-ppt levels, far below the 120 ng/g U specification for PMT glass. The dominant radioactivity concern shifts to readout circuit boards, which should use **Rogers 4350B PTFE laminates** with measured Th < 5 ng/g rather than standard Kapton.

---

## 2. PMT/SiPM Readout Electronics

### Replace SNOD/SNOINT/QUSN7 ASIC Chain with Modern FADC-Based Readout

The existing custom bipolar ASIC chain provides 12-bit ADC sampling with ~400 ns per-channel deadtime and analog memory. This architecture was state-of-art in the early 1990s but is now substantially superseded.

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace the three-chip set (SNOD + SNOINT + QUSN7) with **Texas Instruments ADC32RF45 dual-channel 14-bit ADCs** running at 3 GSPS per channel
- At 3 GSPS, full waveform digitization captures the complete PMT/SiPM pulse profile, enabling offline pulse-shape discrimination without analog shaping
- Each **custom ATCA blade** handles 64 channels using a **Xilinx Ultrascale+ XCVU9P FPGA** for real-time processing: baseline subtraction, leading-edge timing extraction to <100 ps precision, charge integration over selectable windows, and pulse-shape parameter extraction
- The 19-crate architecture maps naturally to 19 ATCA shelves, each with 8 blades handling 512 channels, maintaining the existing logical partitioning
- Eliminate the per-channel 400 ns deadtime entirely; the FPGA pipeline processes continuously with zero deadtime up to the sustained trigger rate
- **100 GbE optical links** per blade replace the RS485 XL1/XL2 translator chain, providing >100× bandwidth improvement to the event builder

**Timing improvement:** The existing TAC-based timing achieves ~1.7 ns RMS. Waveform digitization at 3 GSPS with interpolation yields timing resolution of **~100-150 ps RMS**, improving vertex reconstruction accuracy from approximately 25 cm to better than 10 cm. This is critical for fiducial volume definition and for rejecting PMT-face backgrounds.

**Pulse shape discrimination:** Full waveform capture enables rejection of the late-pulsing and afterpulsing fractions (specified at <1.5%) offline, and more importantly enables **Cherenkov/scintillation separation** if any wavelength-shifting additive is later introduced.

---

## 3. Neutral-Current Detector Array Enhancement

### Replace Ni-body 3He Proportional Counters with Lithium-Loaded Scintillator Strings

The NCD array as described achieves 37% neutron capture efficiency with 25% analysis efficiency after alpha discrimination, and backgrounds require subtraction. The 3He supply is also a long-term constraint given global shortages.

**Specific implementation:**
- Deploy **6Li-loaded liquid scintillator capture segments** in the same 96-string geometry, using **0.1% natural LiCl dissolved in linear alkylbenzene (LAB) scintillator** with wavelength shifter PPO at 2 g/L
- The 6Li(n,t)α reaction has Q = 4.78 MeV with no gamma emission, providing clean neutron capture signal entirely contained within the scintillator volume - this eliminates the dominant alpha/neutron confusion present in gas proportional counters
- String bodies fabricated from **electroformed copper** (achievable at <0.01 ppt Th/U by established electrodeposition techniques at SNO+ and Borexino) rather than nickel CVD, reducing string radioactivity by approximately 10×
- Each string segment (200/250/300 cm active length matching existing NCD geometry) contains a **30 mm diameter acrylic tube** filled with Li-loaded LAB, read out at each end by **3 mm diameter Kuraray Y-11 wavelength-shifting fiber** routed to a **2-inch Hamamatsu R7600-300 metal channel PMT** at the string top
- The n-capture signal (4.78 MeV, ~47,000 photons in LAB at 10,000 photons/MeV) provides >99% neutron/gamma discrimination via both energy deposition topology and pulse shape in the scintillator
- Capture efficiency improves to approximately **60% at natural 6Li abundance** (7.5% 6Li) given the 940 b thermal cross section, compared to 37% for the 3He system

**Alpha background rejection:** The 6Li(n,t)α topology is fully contained and monoenergetic. Alpha particles from U/Th chain decays in the copper walls have ranges of ~30 µm in LAB, depositing energy at the string periphery with distinct pulse shape (Birks quenching reduces light yield by ~5× relative to electrons), providing >99.9% alpha/neutron discrimination versus the ~50% achieved via track length analysis in the 3He counters.

---

## 4. Water Cherenkov Target Enhancement

### Add Perylene-Bis-Dicarboximide (PBD) Wavelength Shifter to D₂O at Sub-ppb Level

The existing detector detects Cherenkov photons with peak emission around 300-400 nm, where acrylic absorption (0.04 cm⁻¹ at 360 nm, 0.18 cm⁻¹ at 320 nm per Table 2) and PMT quantum efficiency losses are significant.

**Specific implementation:**
- Dissolve **bis-MSB (1,4-bis(2-methylstyryl)benzene) at 0.5 µg/L** in the D₂O - this concentration has been demonstrated by the SNO+ collaboration to have negligible impact on D₂O optical scattering and is compatible with the existing RO/ion-exchange water purification system
- Bis-MSB absorbs at 345-375 nm (peak Cherenkov emission) and re-emits at 420-440 nm where acrylic transmission is high (>95%) and PMT/SiPM response is near peak
- The wavelength shift increases the mean photon detection probability per Cherenkov photon from approximately 12% to approximately 22%, equivalent to a further 1.8× improvement in detected photons
- Radiological impact: bis-MSB at 0.5 µg/L in 1000 tonnes contributes 0.5 g total. At commercially available purities (>99.99%), U/Th content is below 1 pg/g, contributing <0.5 µg total Th to the D₂O volume - three orders of magnitude below the 3×10⁻¹⁵ g/g limit

**Compatibility:** The existing MnOx assay columns and RO membranes pass sub-ppb organic molecules; periodic replacement of the ion exchange resins (already part of normal operation) handles the small organic load. The wavelength-shifted photon timing distribution broadens by approximately 1 ns due to fluorescence lifetime, which is acceptable given the improved timing electronics above.

---

## 5. Radon Suppression in D₂O Recirculation

### Replace Process Degasser with Membrane Contactors Plus Online Radon Monitor

The existing process degasser (81 cm diameter, 6 m vessel at 20 torr) removes radon by factors of ~50 but introduces significant dead volume and maintenance requirements underground.

**Specific implementation:**
- Install a **Membrana Liqui-Cel 14×28 membrane contactor** using nitrogen sweep gas, which achieves radon removal factors of >1000 in a compact (35 cm diameter, 90 cm long) inline unit rated for the required 150 L/min flow rate
- Operate with **ultra-pure N₂ sweep** from the existing liquid nitrogen boil-off system (already demonstrated at <10⁻⁵ pCi/L radon)
- Add a dedicated **Lucas cell radon monitor** (ZnS scintillation detector with electrostatic collection) inline on the D₂O return stream, sampling continuously at 1 L/min with sensitivity of <0.01 mBq/m³, providing real-time feedback to the membrane contactor sweep flow control
- The compact form factor (versus the existing 6 m vessel) eliminates the large dead volume that created low-pressure conditions damaging PMT connectors - this failure mode drove the N₂ regassing requirement and its associated complexity

---

## 6. Magnetic Field Compensation

### Upgrade from 14 Fixed Coils to Active 3D Helmholtz Array

The existing system cancels only the vertical component of the 55 µT geomagnetic field using 14 fixed coils, leaving a residual field of up to 19 µT and 2.5% PMT efficiency loss.

**Specific implementation:**
- Install **48 saddle coils** in three orthogonal Helmholtz configurations on the cavity walls, using the existing Urylon liner as the substrate
- Wind coils from **electroformed copper ribbon** (0.5 mm × 5 mm cross section) measured at <1 ppt U/Th
- Drive with **16-bit DAC-controlled current sources** (Kepco BOP 20-20M or equivalent) with 1 mA resolution out of 10 A maximum, providing field control to better than 0.1 µT
- Monitor residual field with a **3D fluxgate magnetometer array** (Bartington Mag-03 sensors) at 12 positions within the PSUP volume, feeding a real-time PID feedback loop running on the existing CMA system
- Achievable residual field uniformity: <1 µT throughout the PMT array, reducing efficiency variation to <0.1% - effectively eliminating this systematic

---

## Prioritized Implementation Summary

| Upgrade | Physics Gain | Technical Complexity | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| FADC waveform readout | Vertex resolution 25→10 cm; zero deadtime | Medium - well-established technology | 1 |
| SiPM tile replacement | 1.6× photon yield; improved energy resolution | High - sealing/radioactivity qualification | 2 |
| 6Li scintillator NCDs | 60% vs 25% effective neutron efficiency | Medium - benefits from SNO+ LiCl work | 3 |
| Bis-MSB wavelength shift | Additional 1.8× effective photon yield | Low - compatible with existing systems | 4 |
| Membrane radon removal | Factor 20× improvement on Rn backgrounds | Low - proven commercial technology | 5 |
| Active field compensation | Eliminate 2.5% efficiency systematic | Low - straightforward coil engineering | 6 |

The combination of upgrades 1 and 2 alone would reduce the statistical uncertainty on the CC/NC flux ratio by approximately 40% for equivalent running time, and improve the systematic uncertainty on vertex reconstruction sufficiently to reduce fiducial volume uncertainty from ~1.5% toward ~0.4%.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Dual-Phase Xenon TPC Dark Matter Detector

## Prioritization Framework

I'll rank upgrades by their impact on the **primary physics figure of merit**: sensitivity to WIMP-nucleon cross-sections, particularly in the few-GeV to few-TeV mass range, which requires maximizing signal efficiency, minimizing backgrounds, and lowering energy thresholds.

---

## 1. Photosensor Replacement: PMTs → Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**The single highest-impact upgrade.**

### Current Limitation
Standard 3" Hamamatsu R11410 PMTs (the industry standard for this class of detector) have:
- Quantum efficiency ~35% at 175 nm VUV
- Non-negligible radioactive contamination (~0.5–2 mBq/PMT from U/Th chains in the glass/dynode stack)
- With ~500 PMTs in a 2-tonne detector, this contributes **~500–1000 mBq total**, setting a hard floor on electromagnetic backgrounds
- Limited ability to operate at very high fields without electron emission artifacts

### Specific Upgrade
Replace with **VUV-sensitive SiPMs**, specifically:
- **Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs (S13370-6050CN)** or **FBK VUV-HD3** devices, 6×6 mm² cells, operated at ~57 V bias at LXe temperature (−108°C)
- Tile arrays of ~4×4 devices on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)-backed PCBs using low-radioactivity electroless-plated copper traces
- Target coverage: match or exceed existing PMT photocoverage (~50–60%) using tiled arrays on both top and bottom faces

### Physics Benefits
- **Photon detection efficiency (PDE) ~24–28%** at 175 nm (VUV4), vs ~35% QE × ~70% collection efficiency for PMTs — roughly comparable or better at the photocathode level, but **vastly better specific radioactivity**
- Radioactivity budget: well-selected SiPM tiles can reach **<0.01 mBq/device**, reducing photosensor background contribution by **1–2 orders of magnitude**
- No PMT glass (major source of ²⁰⁸Tl and ²²⁶Ra)
- Enables **sub-keV energy threshold** by improving S1 light yield at low energies
- Eliminates PMT afterpulsing artifacts that mimic S1/S2 signals

### Key Engineering Challenges
- Cryogenic PCB design for thermal cycling without delamination — use Rogers 4350B or ceramic substrates
- SiPM dark count rate (~100 kcps/mm² at 77 K, falling to ~10 kcps at LXe temperature) manageable with coincidence requirements
- Correlated avalanche noise requires careful digitization firmware

---

## 2. Electroluminescence Grid Upgrade: Improved Gate/Anode Electrode Design

### Current Limitation
Standard electroformed or photo-etched stainless steel wire grids (50–100 μm diameter wires, ~5 mm pitch) suffer from:
- Wire sag and vibration causing non-uniform electric field at the liquid surface
- Surface roughness creating localized high-field regions → electron emission backgrounds
- Limited transparency (~90%) creating optical shadowing that distorts S2 position reconstruction

### Specific Upgrade
Replace wire grids with **micro-patterned mesh electrodes** fabricated from:
- **Photochemically etched titanium or copper-beryllium** (for elasticity and radioactive cleanliness) with hexagonal aperture patterns
- **Optical transparency >97%** to minimize S2 light anisotropy
- Tensioned frames using Invar (Fe-64Ni) rings to match xenon's thermal contraction coefficient (~2×10⁻⁶/K), preventing sag to <50 μm planarity over a 1-meter diameter
- Electropolished to Ra <0.1 μm surface roughness to suppress electron emission

Alternatively, adopt **indium tin oxide (ITO)-coated fused silica plates** as transparent electrodes (as prototyped by the nEXO collaboration) — near-perfect optical transmission with conductive surface.

### Physics Benefits
- Uniform drift field reduces position-dependent S2 yield variation from ~5% to <1%, dramatically improving **fiducialization accuracy** and **ER/NR discrimination**
- Reduced electron emission background (a dominant low-energy background source) by eliminating field hotspots
- Better S2 width uniformity improves **z-coordinate reconstruction** precision from ~3 mm to <1 mm

---

## 3. Low-Radioactivity PTFE Inner Vessel and Structural Components

### Current Limitation
PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) reflectors are essential for light collection but standard commercial PTFE contains:
- **²³⁸U and ²³²Th** at levels of 0.1–1 ppb, contributing Compton scattering backgrounds
- Surface radon emanation from ²²⁶Ra decay daughters

### Specific Upgrade
- Source **radio-assayed ultra-pure PTFE** from dedicated clean synthesis runs (as developed for nEXO/PandaX-xT programs), achieving <0.1 ppt U/Th
- Replace solid PTFE panels with **microporous PTFE (ePTFE, e.g., Gore-Tex membrane laminate)** which has lower density (0.3–0.5 g/cm³ vs 2.2 g/cm³) → proportionally reduced radioactive mass while maintaining >97% VUV reflectivity
- Combine with **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) wavelength shifter** applied by vacuum evaporation to exactly 200 nm thickness for optimal 175→420 nm conversion where SiPD sensitivity peaks

### Physics Benefits
- Reduces γ-ray background rate in fiducial volume by ~30–50%
- Lower mass reduces neutron scattering contribution from PTFE hydrogen content (relevant for nuclear recoil backgrounds)

---

## 4. Charge Readout Upgrade: Pixel or Strip Segmentation of Anode

### Current Limitation
Current detectors reconstruct (x,y) position from the **S2 light pattern** on the top PMT/SiPM array — a photon-statistics-limited process giving ~1–3 cm resolution for small S2 signals. This limits:
- Fiducial volume definition near walls
- Multi-scatter rejection near threshold (where S2 size is small)
- Background discrimination for surface events

### Specific Upgrade
Implement **direct charge readout** at the anode plane using:
- **Segmented anode tiles**: 1 cm² copper pads on low-radioactivity PCB, read out individually — analogous to the LArPix chip developed for LArTPC (directly applicable)
- Or **CMOS charge-sensing pixels** using **ATLAS/CMS-heritage silicon strip detectors** adapted for cryogenic operation — strip pitch 1–2 mm
- Readout ASIC: **SLAC's LArPix v2a** or custom **cold CMOS** (e.g., SKY130 process rad-hard design) — the key is <1 electron equivalent noise at LXe temperature

### Physics Benefits
- x,y resolution improved to **<1 mm** even for single-electron S2 signals — fundamental improvement for low-mass WIMP search
- Enables detection of **single ionization electrons** with known position → opens sensitivity to **sub-GeV dark matter** via the Migdal effect and Bremsstrahlung channels
- Dramatically improved wall-event rejection: fiducial boundary sharpness from ~5 mm to <2 mm adds ~10–15% effective fiducial mass

---

## 5. Neutron Veto Upgrade: Gadolinium-Loaded Liquid Scintillator Shell

### Current Limitation
A pure water Cherenkov muon veto efficiently tags **muons** but is nearly transparent to **fast neutrons** from:
- Detector construction materials (U/Th (α,n) reactions in stainless steel, PMT glass)
- Muon-induced neutrons that scatter before reaching water volume

Neutrons producing single nuclear recoils are the **irreducible background** mimicking WIMPs, currently at ~0.1–1 event/tonne/year levels.

### Specific Upgrade
Add an **intermediate gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator (Gd-LS) layer** between the cryostat and water tank:
- **0.1% Gd-loaded linear alkylbenzene (LAB) + PPO scintillator** (as used in SNO+, JUNO) in a 30–50 cm thick shell surrounding the cryostat
- Gd has a **thermal neutron capture cross-section of 49,000 barns**, capturing neutrons after thermalization with ~8 MeV gamma cascade — easily detected in LS
- Instrumented with **8" Hamamatsu R5912** PMTs (or equivalent) at ~20% photocoverage
- Gadolinium complex: use **Gd(dpm)₃** (dipivaloylmethanate) chelate for chemical stability — same formulation validated in Super-K Gd

### Physics Benefits
- Neutron tagging efficiency: **>90%** for neutrons reaching the LS layer (vs ~10–20% detection probability in pure water)
- Reduces neutron background by a factor of **5–10×**
- Combined with TPC fiducialization and multiple scatter rejection, drives neutron background **below the neutrino floor** for most WIMP masses
- Scintillation signal also provides redundant muon veto with lower threshold than Cherenkov

---

## 6. Cryogenics: Closed-Loop Krypton Removal System with Online Distillation

### Current Limitation
**Krypton-85** (a β-emitter, Q=687 keV) from atmospheric krypton dissolved in xenon produces a flat ER background indistinguishable from low-energy WIMPs at the ~1 events/tonne/day level even at ppt-level Kr concentrations. Radon-222 (from ²²⁶Ra in materials) similarly contributes.

### Specific Upgrade
Integrate a **continuous online cryogenic distillation column** into the xenon circulation loop:
- **Packed column** with 2" diameter, ~3 m height, using Sulzer DX stainless steel structured packing (validated by XENON collaboration)
- Flow rate: 5–10 slpm gaseous Xe through column continuously during detector operation
- **Separation factor** for Kr/Xe: ~10 per theoretical plate; achievable reduction to **<0.01 ppt Kr/Xe** (vs ~0.1 ppt from single pre-purification)
- Add a **⁲²²Rn emanation monitoring system**: electrostatic radon concentration detector (sensitivity ~1 mBq/m³) on the gas return line with <1 hour response time, enabling **source identification and isolation** via automated valve sequencing

### Physics Benefits
- Reduces ⁸⁵Kr background by **factor 10–100×** — moves ER background below detector sensitivity floor
- Online operation means **no xenon transfer downtime** vs. batch distillation
- Radon monitoring enables rapid identification of leaking components (a critical operational capability)

---

## 7. High-Voltage System: Resistive Field Cage with Carbon-Loaded PEEK

### Current Limitation
Conventional field cages use copper rings on PTFE support rods with discrete resistors — creating:
- Localized field distortions at each ring gap
- Potential for discharges in LXe from imperfect resistor mounting
- Radioactive contribution from resistor ceramic bodies (containing U/Th)

### Specific Upgrade
Replace with **continuously graded resistive field cage** using:
- **Carbon-loaded PEEK (polyether ether ketone)** cylindrical shell machined to specific bulk resistivity (10⁸–10¹⁰ Ω·cm tunable by carbon black loading fraction)
- Single monolithic cylinder replaces ~100 discrete rings — eliminates all field discontinuities
- PEEK is LXe-compatible, has low outgassing, and can be radio-assayed to <0.1 ppt U/Th
- Couple to HV feedthrough using **zero-halide alumina ceramic** insulators brazed to stainless steel flanges (rather than conventional Kapton cables which fail at high fields)

### Physics Benefits
- Electric field uniformity improved to **<0.1%** variation across drift volume — reduces position-dependent electron lifetime corrections and enables more aggressive fiducialization
- No discharge risk from resistor failures — critical for stable long-term operation at 1–2 kV/cm drift fields
- Reduced radioactivity from elimination of ceramic resistors

## 8. Data Acquisition: Full Waveform Digitization with FPGA-Based Online Trigger

### Current Limitation
Many current implementations use hardware discriminators with fixed thresholds, meaning:
- Sub-threshold S1 signals (for low-mass WIMPs) are permanently lost
- Pile-up rejection is conservative, vetoing valid events near accidental coincidences
- Position reconstruction relies on offline processing of saved waveforms

### Specific Upgrade
- Deploy **250 MHz, 14-bit FADCs** (e.g., CAEN V1725 or custom ATCA boards) on every channel simultaneously — full waveform recording
- **Xilinx Ultrascale+ FPGAs** performing real-time pulse finding, S1/S2 pairing, and online position reconstruction at <10 μs latency
- Implement **triggerless streaming readout** to disk, with online processing flagging events of interest — no hardware threshold applied at data taking
- **Machine learning inference on FPGA** (BDT or small CNN quantized to INT8, implemented in firmware using HLS4ML framework) for real-time ER/NR classification — reduce trigger rate while retaining efficiency

### Physics Benefits
- Recovers **sub-threshold S1 signals**, extending sensitivity to **<1 GeV WIMP** mass
- Enables offline re-analysis with improved algorithms on preserved raw data
- Reduces systematic uncertainty from trigger efficiency corrections

# Hardware Design Upgrades for DarkSide-50 Physics Performance

## 1. Photomultiplier Tube Replacement with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**Current limitation:** The 3" Hamamatsu R11065 PMTs are the dominant source of radioactive background (Table I shows ~0.277 Bq of ²³²Th, ~0.84 Bq of ²³⁸U lower chain per PMT array). The paper explicitly states PMTs are the source of >90% of radiogenic neutron background and dominant Cherenkov background. PMT proximity to the S2 emission region also limits x-y position reconstruction.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace PMT arrays with tile arrays of **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD SiPMs** or equivalent cryogenic-rated devices
- SiPMs have intrinsically lower radioactivity per unit photosensitive area (no borosilicate glass stem, no ceramic dynode supports, no Kovar casing - the specific PMT components identified as radioactivity hosts)
- Mount SiPMs on low-background **fused silica or PTFE substrates** with copper traces rather than standard PCB
- Operate at ~87K with custom ASIC-based cryogenic front-end electronics integrated directly on the SiPM tiles, replacing the current discrete cryogenic preamplifiers

**Expected physics impact:**
- Reduction of radiogenic neutron background by >90% (directly stated fraction from PMTs)
- Reduction of Cherenkov background by removing dominant source (PMT borosilicate glass)
- SiPMs placed flush against active volume walls enable finer S2 position granularity, improving x-y reconstruction resolution from the current ~0.6 cm toward ~1-2 mm, enabling tighter radial fiducialization
- Higher photon detection efficiency (~50-60% PDE vs ~30% QE for R11065) increases photoelectron yield, improving PSD (f90) discrimination at low energies where it is currently statistics-limited

---

## 2. Replacement of Fused Silica Windows with Alternative Optical Coupling

**Current limitation:** The paper identifies fused-silica PMT and TPC windows as a significant Cherenkov background source. The S1pMaxFrac cut was specifically developed to reject this, but at cost of WIMP acceptance. The paper states this is eliminated as primary background only by that cut, leaving Teflon Cherenkov as dominant.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Eliminate discrete fused silica TPC windows entirely by transitioning to a **windowless SiPM-on-PTFE design** where photosensors are embedded directly in the reflector panels
- For any remaining optical interfaces, replace fused silica with **crystalline sapphire (Al₂O₃)** windows: sapphire has a Cherenkov threshold of ~0.75 MeV for electrons (higher than fused silica's ~0.18 MeV), drastically reducing Cherenkov yield from Compton electrons in the relevant energy range
- Alternatively, use **UV-transparent acrylic (PMMA)** which has lower Cherenkov yield due to lower refractive index and can be produced at higher radiopurity than borosilicate glass

**Expected physics impact:**
- Elimination of the entire fused-silica Cherenkov background class that required the S1pMaxFrac cut (~0.948 acceptance factor recovered)
- Removes need for S1pMaxFrac cut, recovering ~5% WIMP acceptance
- Directly addresses what the paper identifies as the category of events driving box design at high f90

---

## 3. Upgraded Teflon Reflector System to Suppress Dominant Cherenkov Background

**Current limitation:** The paper explicitly concludes that scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov is the *dominant remaining ER background* after all cuts, driving the final box design and limiting sensitivity. The S1NLL and RadialFid cuts were specifically developed to combat it, but only achieved rejection factors of ~2.3.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace PTFE reflectors with **tetraphenylbutadiene (TPB)-doped deuterated polyethylene** panels: deuterated materials have significantly reduced Cherenkov yield because the higher effective mass of deuterium raises threshold momenta for Cherenkov emission
- Alternatively, coat inner PTFE surfaces with a **thin layer of evaporated lithium fluoride (LiF)**, which has a Cherenkov threshold of ~3 MeV for electrons due to its very low refractive index (n≈1.39 at 420 nm), compared to PTFE's n≈1.35 which allows Cherenkov from electrons above ~0.18 MeV
- More practically: use **specular rather than diffuse reflector geometry** (e.g., aluminized foil on low-radioactivity substrate) - specular reflectors produce anisotropic Cherenkov emission patterns that are geometrically distinguishable from isotropic scintillation in the S1 PMT hit pattern, making the S1NLL cut dramatically more powerful
- Segment the reflector with **independent SiPM readout panels** to provide spatial information about where Cherenkov light is generated, enabling direct vetoing

**Expected physics impact:**
- Reduction of dominant ER background by an estimated factor of 5-10 beyond current cuts
- Would allow tighter WIMP search box lower boundary, improving sensitivity at lower WIMP masses
- More powerful S1NLL discrimination could replace the computationally expensive radial fiducialization

---

## 4. Upgraded Liquid Scintillator Veto with Gadolinium Loading

**Current limitation:** The LSV uses borated liquid scintillator achieving 99.64% neutron veto efficiency (Table II). The residual inefficiency limits radiogenic neutron background to <0.005 events. The delayed cut's 22 µs capture lifetime requires a 189.5 µs search window, increasing accidental veto rate.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace boron-loaded scintillator with **gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator** (e.g., 0.1% Gd by mass in linear alkylbenzene)
- Gadolinium has a thermal neutron capture cross section of ~49,000 barns vs. ~767 barns for ¹⁰B, and captures produce a ~8 MeV γ cascade (highly distinctive) vs. ¹⁰B's 2.3 MeV (α+γ) or 0.48 MeV (α-only) signals
- The Gd capture lifetime of ~20-30 µs is comparable to B, but the much higher energy release improves capture detection efficiency, particularly for the α-only channel that currently has low efficiency
- Add a **segmented inner acrylic vessel** containing Gd-LS closest to the TPC cryostat to maximize neutron capture probability before thermalization reaches the outer scintillator

**Expected physics impact:**
- Improved neutron capture signal-to-noise ratio due to higher-energy γ cascade, enabling lower threshold on delayed cut
- Potential reduction of the LSVdelayed search window from 189.5 µs, reducing accidental veto rate (currently 0.835 acceptance for LSVdelayed is the single largest acceptance loss in Table V)
- Recovery of ~2% WIMP acceptance currently lost to accidental LSV vetoing
- Veto efficiency potentially improvable to >99.9% for radiogenic neutrons

---

## 5. Enhanced Inner Electrode and Grid System

**Current limitation:** The current grid 4.7 mm below the liquid-gas interface creates a 200 V/cm drift field. The paper notes significant surface background from the cathode and grid (requiring z fiducialization removing 40 µs from top and bottom). The x-y position resolution limitation is partly attributed to S2 proximity effects.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace the single extraction grid with a **multi-wire proportional structure** using electroformed copper wires on a low-radioactivity fused silica frame, increasing wire density from current design to ~1 mm pitch
- Implement a **four-grid system** (cathode, two field-shaping grids, anode) similar to designs used in noble liquid TPCs for particle physics, providing better-defined and more uniform extraction field
- Use **electron-transparent mesh electrodes** made from etched copper-clad Kapton with >85% optical transparency to reduce S2 optical shadowing effects that currently complicate position reconstruction
- Increase drift field to **500 V/cm** by upgrading the high-voltage feedthroughs to custom PTFE-insulated designs rated to >100 kV

**Expected physics impact:**
- Higher drift field improves electron lifetime sensitivity and S2 yield, enhancing x-y position reconstruction
- Better-defined extraction region reduces the "Type 2" surface background (S1-only + uncorrelated S2 pileup) by improving S2 signal uniformity
- Reduced z dead layer from improved field uniformity, potentially recovering 2-3% of fiducial mass
- Finer mesh pitch improves S2 position resolution toward the ~1 mm scale needed for aggressive radial fiducialization in a scaled-up detector

---

## 6. Active Inner Cryostat Veto Layer

**Current limitation:** The paper identifies that γ rays from the cryostat steel are a significant background source, and that only ~1/3 of γ rays producing ER in TPC are detected by the LSV. The cryostat activities are fixed in the background model and cannot be reduced post-construction.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Install a **thin (5 mm) active liquid scintillator layer** between the inner TPC cryostat wall and the LSV, instrumented with **2" cryogenic SiPM panels** on a copper support structure
- Use **EJ-301 or similar fast scintillator** doped with wavelength shifter for operation near LAr temperatures
- This layer provides a 4π veto specifically targeting γ rays from the cryostat that currently escape the LSV detection, acting as an "inner veto"
- Alternatively, instrument the existing LAr blanket surrounding the TPC inner cryostat with **wavelength-shifting plates and SiPMs** to detect Cherenkov light from Compton electrons in the LAr surrounding the TPC

**Expected physics impact:**
- Improvement in γ-ray veto efficiency from ~33% to potentially >80% for cryostat-sourced γ rays
- Reduction of the dominant Compton scatter ER background component
- Reduced rate of scintillation+Cherenkov events since fewer high-energy γ rays reach the TPC reflector
- Most impactful for the multi-tonne successor detector where cryostat surface-to-volume ratio is reduced but absolute cryostat activity may increase

---

## Priority Ranking and Summary

| Upgrade | Primary Background Addressed | Estimated Impact |
|---------|------------------------------|-----------------|
| SiPM replacement | Radiogenic neutrons + Cherenkov (PMT glass) | Highest: eliminates >90% of neutron background |
| Gd-loaded LSV | Accidental veto acceptance | High: recovers ~2% acceptance, improves neutron veto |
| Specular reflector + segmented readout | Teflon Cherenkov (dominant ER background) | High: directly targets rate-limiting background |

The SiPM replacement is the single highest-priority upgrade because it simultaneously addresses the dominant radiogenic neutron source, the dominant Cherenkov source, and the x-y reconstruction limitation identified as a major analysis challenge throughout the paper.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for EXO-200

## Preamble on Performance Constraints

The paper explicitly identifies the binding limitations: energy resolution (σE/E = 1.6% target at Qββ), high voltage instability above 8-14 kV limiting drift field to 8 kV rather than the design 75 kV, LAAPD noise setting the scintillation threshold, and backgrounds from internal components. I address each concretely.

---

## 1. Replace LAAPDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

### Problem Being Solved
The paper states LAAPDs have "lower gain and higher noise" as explicit disadvantages, and that "noise in the LAAPDs limits the scintillation threshold." At 1400 V bias with 125 pF capacitance per device and ganging of 5-7 units, the effective capacitance per readout channel reaches roughly 875 pF, severely degrading noise performance. The measured noise is 2 e⁻/pF for LAAPD channels versus 1 e⁻/pF for wire channels.

### Proposed Upgrade
Replace the 468 LAAPDs with cryogenic-qualified SiPMs, specifically devices in the Hamamatsu MPPC series (e.g., S10931-050P or S10362-33 variants) or Photonique SSPM devices, which by 2012 had demonstrated operation at liquid nitrogen temperatures with acceptable dark count rates.

**Specific design changes:**

- **Device geometry:** Use 3×3 mm² or 6×6 mm² SiPM tiles arranged in the same hexagonal packing pattern on the existing copper platters, replacing the 16 mm diameter LAAPD dies. The smaller individual device capacitance (roughly 35 pF for a 3×3 mm² device at 50 µm pitch) compared to 125 pF per LAAPD dramatically reduces the dominant noise source.

- **Gain advantage:** SiPMs operate at gains of 10⁵–10⁶, compared to LAAPD gains of order 10²–10³ at LXe temperature, reducing the relative importance of downstream electronic noise.

- **Reduced bias voltage:** SiPMs operate at 25–75 V overvoltage rather than 1380–1400 V, eliminating the complex trim voltage distribution network described in Section 3.1 and reducing the risk of electrical breakdown near the readout plane.

- **Ganging modification:** Because SiPM capacitance per unit area is lower, gangs can be kept smaller (3-4 devices) without sacrificing channel count, improving position reconstruction of scintillation light and enabling crude z-position reconstruction from light asymmetry between the two end planes.

- **VUV sensitivity:** The 178 nm scintillation wavelength requires either direct VUV-sensitive SiPMs or deposition of a wavelength-shifting layer (p-terphenyl or tetraphenyl butadiene, TPB) on the SiPM face. TPB evaporated at 50–100 nm thickness onto the SiPM surface converts 178 nm photons to ~430 nm where SiPM photon detection efficiency exceeds 25%. This same coating should be applied to the PTFE reflector tiles, replacing the uncoated TE-6472 surface whose 70% reflectance at 178 nm in Ar gas (noted as expected to be higher in LXe but unmeasured in situ) would be supplemented by diffuse re-emission at visible wavelengths where PTFE reflectance exceeds 98%.

- **Radioactivity:** SiPM bulk silicon has intrinsically lower U and Th content than the LAAPD structure, which includes gold-coated contacts, polyimide edge coating, and bonded ring structures. The paper notes the LAAPD contribution is < 0.13 mBq for K and < 0.09 mBq for Th across 518 units; SiPMs with simpler construction and no ceramic encapsulation should achieve comparable or better specific activity.

---

## 2. Redesign the High Voltage Feedthrough and Field Cage to Recover Drift Field

### Problem Being Solved
Section 3.2.4 explicitly states the detector operates at 8 kV instead of the design 75 kV due to "~mV-scale glitches" attributed to corona discharge on sharp photoetched edges. At 8 kV across the 38.4 cm half-drift length, the drift field is approximately 0.21 kV/cm, far below the design 3.7 kV/cm. This has severe consequences: electron lifetime requirements become more stringent, diffusion broadens charge clusters degrading position and single-site/multi-site discrimination, and recombination at lower fields reduces the charge yield, worsening energy resolution from the combined charge+light estimator.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Cathode and field cage electrode redesign:**

- Replace all photoetched phosphor bronze components in the high-field region with **electropolished stainless steel or titanium machined parts**. Photoetching produces rough edges with radii of curvature of order micrometers, which concentrate electric fields and initiate corona. Precision machining followed by electropolishing achieves edge radii exceeding 0.5 mm, raising the corona onset voltage by an order of magnitude.

- The cathode grid, currently photoetched with 90% optical transparency, should be redesigned as **stretched wire grid** using 50 µm diameter electropolished stainless steel wires at 0.5 mm pitch, achieving similar optical transparency while eliminating sharp photoetched edges entirely. Wire ends terminate in precision-machined copper clamps with generous radii.

- Field shaping rings should be machined from the same low-background copper stock currently used, but with all edges receiving a minimum 3 mm radius of curvature and electropolishing to surface roughness Ra < 0.1 µm. The current ring geometry (0.97 cm long, 10 rings per half-TPC) can be retained but with this surface treatment.

**HV feedthrough redesign:**

- Replace the RG217 coaxial cable and Swagelok compression seal with a **custom coaxial feedthrough using a solid PTFE dielectric rod** machined to tight tolerances, with the center conductor being a continuous electropolished copper rod rather than a stranded or solid cable with connectors. The current design relies on the polyethylene extrusion providing a He-leak-tight seal, acknowledged in the paper as relying on an empirical observation rather than a designed seal.

- The spring-loaded receptacle contact in the PTFE block (Figure 12) introduces a mechanical interface at high field. Replace this with a **brazed or welded continuous conductor** from the feedthrough to the cathode connection point, eliminating the contact interface where corona initiates.

- Add a **field grading electrode** at the room-temperature end of the HV conduit where the cable transitions from gas to vacuum phase, a region not addressed in the current design.

---

## 3. Upgrade Wire Readout to Reduce Diffusion and Improve Position Resolution

### Problem Being Solved
At the operating drift field of ~0.21 kV/cm, transverse diffusion in LXe over the 19.2 cm half-drift length is approximately σT ≈ √(2DT·t) where DT/µ (the characteristic diffusion coefficient) is roughly 55 cm²/s / (cm/µs per kV/cm) at this field. The result is transverse diffusion of several millimeters, comparable to the 9 mm readout pitch. Single-site versus multi-site discrimination, critical for rejecting Compton background, is therefore severely compromised. Recovering the design drift field via the HV upgrade above is the primary fix, but the wire planes themselves can also be improved.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Reduced wire pitch with ASIC readout:**

- Reduce readout pitch from 9 mm to **3 mm** (the field optimization pitch already implemented for wire triplets but currently summed into groups). This requires increasing the channel count from 38 to 114 channels per U or V plane, totaling approximately 456 wire channels rather than 152.

- At this channel count, custom **ASIC front-end chips** become justified and beneficial. A charge-sensitive amplifier ASIC in 0.35 µm CMOS, similar to designs used in the ATLAS liquid argon calorimeter or ALICE TPC, can be designed with input noise of 500 e⁻ ENC at 50 pF input capacitance, adequate for the 0.51 pF/cm × 3 cm ≈ 1.5 pF wire capacitance. The ASIC can be located on the warm side of the feedthrough as currently, or at intermediate temperature in the HFE-7000 volume where component count and radioactivity screening become more manageable given the shielding already provided by the HFE.

- The wire triplet mechanical design is elegant and should be retained, but individual wire readout within each triplet should be restored by breaking the electrical bridges, with each wire carrying its signal independently to the ASIC.

**Cathode segmentation for improved z-reconstruction:**

- The current z-position reconstruction relies entirely on the drift time measured as the difference between scintillation detection and charge arrival. Add **resistive cathode segmentation** by replacing the single cathode grid with a grid having 5 MΩ inter-strip resistors connecting strips at 3 cm pitch in one direction, enabling cathode-induced signal reconstruction to provide a redundant z-coordinate measurement independent of the scintillation signal. This technique, proven in gaseous TPCs, works in liquid xenon given sufficiently fast shaping.

---

## 4. Barium Ion Tagging Infrastructure

### Problem Being Solved
The paper explicitly notes (Section 2.3): "The double beta decay of ¹³⁶Xe produces a barium ion (¹³⁶Ba²⁺) that can in principle be tagged, drastically reducing backgrounds. The techniques for Ba tagging are being developed by the EXO-collaboration but are not part of the design of EXO-200."

This is the single most impactful potential upgrade since successful Ba tagging would reduce backgrounds by several orders of magnitude, converting EXO-200 from a background-limited to a signal-limited experiment at current exposure.

### Proposed Upgrade

The paper notes the enriched xenon is at 80.6% ¹³⁶Xe with the remainder predominantly ¹³⁴Xe. The Ba²⁺ ion produced in ββ decay must be extracted and identified.

**Gas-flow extraction probe:**

- Install a **thin-walled stainless steel capillary probe** (0.5 mm outer diameter) that can be inserted through the existing calibration source guide tube (Figure 21) to within a few centimeters of the reconstructed event vertex. Following a candidate ββ event identified by energy and position reconstruction, the probe tip is positioned at the reconstructed vertex coordinates.

- A controlled flow of xenon gas through the probe, combined with electrostatic focusing using a **biased extraction electrode** at the probe tip (approximately +100 V to attract Ba²⁺), draws the ion toward the probe entrance. Ion mobility in LXe at the operating conditions is sufficient for micron-scale drift over milliseconds.

- The extracted ion in xenon carrier gas is then **laser-tagged** in a small buffer volume immediately outside the cryostat using the resonance fluorescence technique: Ba⁺ (after charge exchange from Ba²⁺) has a strong optical transition at 493 nm (6S₁/₂ → 6P₁/₂) accessible with a frequency-doubled diode laser system. A repump laser at 650 nm prevents shelving in the 5D₃/₂ metastable state. Single-ion detection via photon counting with a cooled CCD or avalanche photodiode in photon-counting mode achieves essentially zero background.

**Required hardware additions:**

- One additional feedthrough port in the copper vessel and inner cryostat hatch, rated for the LXe operating pressure, accommodating the 0.5 mm capillary with sufficient mechanical rigidity for positioning. The port can share the existing calibration tube penetration.

- A small external ion optics chamber (approximately 5 cm³ volume) constructed from electropolished stainless steel with a fused silica optical window, pumped to 10⁻⁶ torr base pressure with a small turbomolecular pump. Laser access via two orthogonal ports for excitation and fluorescence collection.

- A 493 nm laser system: a 986 nm external-cavity diode laser (Toptica DL100 or equivalent) frequency-doubled in a periodically-poled KTP crystal, delivering ~1 mW to the ion region. A 650 nm diode laser for repumping. Both lasers stabilized to a reference cavity.

---

## 5. Improved Radon Exclusion System

### Problem Being Solved
Section 5.3 states the measured radon concentration inside the lead shielding is approximately 6 mBq/L, three times the 2 mBq/L limit that produces 0.3 counts/yr in the 0νββ window. The paper notes "this favors, for the future, the purging of the volume inside the lead shield with reduced radon air" but this system is not implemented.

### Proposed Upgrade

- The 0.8 mm stainless steel enclosure around the lead shielding already exists (Section 4.3). Upgrade it to a **hermetic enclosure** by replacing sheet metal overlaps with welded or gasketed joints (silicone or Viton O-ring compression seals at all penetrations) and installing:

- A **radon-scrubbing recirculation system** using a charcoal trap cooled to -40°C (achievable with a Peltier-cooled cold trap or a small mechanical refrigerator), which adsorbs radon with a partition coefficient sufficient to reduce radon to below 0.1 mBq/L in the enclosed volume. The system recirculates the enclosed air volume at approximately 10 volume changes per hour using a small oil-free diaphragm pump.

- Alternatively, supply the enclosure with radon-reduced air from a **membrane separation unit** or a compressed nitrogen boil-off supply. Membrane separators commercially available by 2012 (e.g., Parker domnick hunter units) achieve radon reduction factors of 100-1000 relative to ambient air with modest flow rates.

- Monitor radon continuously inside the enclosure using one of the existing seven electrostatic counters (described in Section 4.1) repositioned inside the lead enclosure, providing real-time feedback to the recirculation system controls.

---

## 6. Front-End Electronics Relocation and Upgrade

### Problem Being Solved
Section 3.3 states the electronics choice "trades some increased noise for the simplicity and accessibility of room temperature, conventional construction electronics." The polyimide cables from detector to electronics traverse approximately 1 m, with measured capacitance of 30 pF between signal and guard traces and total trace resistance of ~5 Ω per channel. This cable capacitance dominates the input capacitance for wire channels (60-80 pF total versus ~1.5 pF wire capacitance), increasing noise by a factor of roughly 7 relative to electronics placed at the wire plane.

### Proposed Upgrade

- Relocate the first amplification stage to the **HFE-7000 volume** at approximately 170 K. At this temperature, JFET noise performance improves due to reduced thermal noise current, and the cable capacitance contribution is eliminated. The first-stage preamplifier, consisting of the JFET and feedback components only (no power-hungry opamp stages), dissipates approximately 5-10 mW per channel. For 228 wire channels and 78 LAAPD channels, total dissipation is approximately 3 W, manageable by the existing cryogenic system.

- Use **2SK932 JFETs** (already specified in the paper, reference [74]) mounted on small Rogers 4350B PCBs (low loss, low outgassing, cryogenic-compatible) attached to the existing copper support structure. The PCBs must be screened for radioactivity before installation; at the HFE-7000 location outside the TPC vessel they contribute to backgrounds only at the level of the existing HFE shielding layer.

- The remaining shaping and digitization electronics remain at room temperature, connected by the existing polyimide cable infrastructure now carrying lower-impedance voltage signals rather than high-impedance charge signals, greatly reducing microphonic susceptibility.
