2. VELO silicon sensors approaching radiation damage limits, with effective depletion voltage reaching ~100V at Run I end
3. RICH photoelectron yields 20-35% below simulation predictions
4. Calorimeter PMT aging causing gain drift requiring frequent recalibration
5. OT occupancy reaching 25% at 25 ns bunch spacing, limiting tracking performance

---

## Upgrade 1: Full Software Trigger via 40 MHz Readout

### Motivation
The paper explicitly identifies the hardware L0 trigger as the dominant efficiency limitation. The L0 hadron trigger achieves only 40-53% TOS efficiency for two-body B decays and as low as 22% for four-body charm modes. These losses are irreversible. The 1 MHz readout ceiling is the root constraint.

### Proposed Implementation

**Front-end electronics replacement across all subsystems:**

- Replace all existing front-end ASICs with zero-suppression capable chips reading out at 40 MHz bunch crossing rate
- Implement on-detector data compression using time-over-threshold encoding for silicon detectors, reducing raw data volume by approximately a factor of 5
- Install high-bandwidth optical links (minimum 4.8 Gb/s per link, using radiation-hard GBTX-style serializers) on all subdetector front-ends to handle the factor-40 increase in data bandwidth

**Data acquisition network:**

- Replace current readout network with a fully switched 10-40 GbE fabric capable of sustaining approximately 40 Tb/s aggregate throughput from the detector
- Deploy dedicated readout boards with on-FPGA first-stage event building to reduce CPU load in the software trigger farm

**Software trigger farm expansion:**

- Scale EFF from ~30,000 to approximately 50,000-60,000 processing cores
- Implement GPU-based track reconstruction as a first filter stage, exploiting the parallelism of pattern recognition; GPU implementations of Hough-transform-based VELO tracking can achieve throughputs of order 10^5 events/second per GPU board
- First software trigger stage runs fast VELO reconstruction and IP-based selection, replacing the L0 hardware function entirely

### Expected Performance Gain

Eliminating the hardware trigger removes the 40-60% efficiency loss for hadronic modes. For D0→Kπ the effective retained sample more than doubles. The calorimeter SPD multiplicity veto, which currently discards high-multiplicity events, is also eliminated.

---

## Upgrade 2: VELO Replacement with Silicon Pixel Detector

### Motivation
The strip-based VELO faces several documented limitations:
- Radiation damage reaching ~100V depletion voltage at Run I end; at higher luminosities this becomes unmanageable with strip geometry
- Best achievable single-hit resolution of ~4 μm only at optimal projected angle; at normal incidence resolution degrades significantly
- The 29 mm retraction requirement and 210-second closing procedure introduce operational dead time
- Strip geometry limits 3D hit information, constraining pattern recognition in high-multiplicity environments

### Proposed Implementation

**Sensor technology: hybrid pixel detectors with 55×55 μm² pixel pitch**

- Replace R and Φ strip sensors with planar n-in-p silicon pixel sensors, 200 μm thick to reduce material budget
- Target pixel pitch of 55 μm × 55 μm, providing genuinely 2D hit information per layer and eliminating ambiguities inherent to strip detectors
- Use p-spray isolation between pixels rather than p-stop to improve radiation tolerance
- Bias voltage capability to 1000V to maintain charge collection efficiency at fluences of order 10^15 n_eq/cm², a factor ~5 beyond Run I maximum

**Readout ASIC:**

- Custom pixel readout chip with per-pixel time-over-threshold digitization providing both hit position and charge information
- Implement 40 MHz readout with data-driven (triggerless) architecture, buffering hits in on-chip memory
- Target power dissipation below 400 mW/cm² to allow CO2 evaporative cooling with thinner cooling structures

**Mechanical and vacuum interface:**

- Reduce RF foil thickness from current aluminum to 150 μm thick corrugated aluminum or replace with 100 μm thick carbon fiber composite, reducing material per foil by ~40%
- Redesign retraction mechanism to reduce retraction distance from 29 mm to 5 mm by implementing a thinner RF foil profile, reducing closing time from 210 seconds to under 30 seconds
- Implement a secondary vacuum system allowing module exchange without full detector removal

**Material budget:**

- Target total material budget of 0.5% X₀ per station (compared to approximately 0.8% X₀ for current strip modules including support and cooling)

### Expected Performance Gain

- IP resolution at high pT improves from ~13 μm to approximately 8-10 μm based on reduced material and improved single-hit resolution
- Pattern recognition ghost rate in high-multiplicity events reduces due to 2D hit disambiguation
- Primary vertex resolution improves approximately proportional to IP improvement
- Radiation tolerance extended to support operation at luminosities of 2×10^33 cm^-2 s^-1

---

## Upgrade 3: RICH Detector Modifications

### Motivation
The paper documents that:
- C4F10 Cherenkov angle resolution in data (1.618 mrad) exceeds simulation (1.52 mrad) by ~6%, attributed to magnetic field distortions on HPD images
- Photoelectron yields are 20-35% below simulation for all three radiators
- Aerogel Npe has large uncertainty and the radiator absorbs C4F10, degrading performance
- HPD read-out inefficiency identified at high trigger rates

### Proposed Implementation

**Replace Hybrid Photon Detectors with Multianode Photomultiplier Tubes (MaPMTs):**

- HPDs are known to suffer performance degradation from residual magnetic fields and have demonstrated read-out inefficiency at high rates
- Replace with multianode PMTs (e.g., 64-channel devices with 2×2 mm² pixel size), which are inherently insensitive to magnetic fields up to ~1 mT without external shielding
- MaPMTs have single-photon detection efficiency comparable to HPDs but with simpler, more robust front-end electronics
- Implement new front-end ASIC with 40 MHz readout capability, time-over-threshold encoding, and on-chip zero suppression

**Remove aerogel radiator from RICH1:**

- The paper explicitly notes aerogel absorbs C4F10 gas, degrading both components
- The aerogel Npe is only 4-5 detected photons with large uncertainty, providing minimal PID discrimination
- Removing aerogel eliminates the contamination effect on C4F10 performance and simplifies the radiator geometry
- The momentum range previously covered by aerogel (below ~5 GeV/c near threshold) must be compensated; extend C4F10 path length by approximately 15% by repositioning the radiator entry window

**Magnetic shielding improvement for RICH1:**

- Install additional mu-metal shielding panels around the RICH1 photon detector planes
- Current residual field causes documented image distortions; target residual field below 0.5 mT at detector plane (down from current ~2 mT)
- This directly addresses the identified discrepancy between data and simulation Cherenkov angle resolution

**Improved mirror alignment monitoring:**

- Implement laser-based continuous alignment monitoring system with position sensitive detectors at mirror edges
- Currently mirror alignment is performed offline; online monitoring allows correction within fills rather than between fills

### Expected Performance Gain

- Cherenkov angle resolution for C4F10 improving from 1.618 mrad toward simulation value of 1.52 mrad, approximately 6% improvement
- Photoelectron yield for C4F10 and CF4 improving by 10-20% through better read-out efficiency
- Kaon identification efficiency at fixed 5% pion misidentification rate improves by approximately 3-5 percentage points across the 10-60 GeV/c momentum range

---

## Upgrade 4: Scintillating Fibre Tracker Replacing OT and IT

### Motivation
The paper documents OT straw occupancy reaching 17-25% at 50 ns and 25 ns bunch spacing respectively. At higher luminosity this becomes the dominant tracking inefficiency source. The OT drift time of up to 35 ns means three bunch crossings must be read out, inherently creating spillover and occupancy problems at short bunch spacing. The IT silicon strips function well but have limited coverage. Having two distinct technologies (OT straws + IT silicon) in the same station complicates alignment and calibration.

### Proposed Implementation

**Scintillating fibre (SciFi) tracker with SiPM readout:**

- Replace all three T1-T3 stations with scintillating fibre mats, using fibres of 250 μm diameter
- Fibres are arranged in mats of 6 layers glued together, providing sufficient light yield even with short fibre segments
- Read out by silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) at the fibre ends; SiPMs provide single-photon sensitivity, operate at room temperature, and are insensitive to magnetic fields
- Crucially, SiPM response time is below 1 ns, enabling time measurements that allow bunch crossing identification without multi-crossing readout windows

**Segmentation and channel count:**

- Target pitch of 250 μm per channel provides spatial resolution of approximately 70 μm (better than current OT 200 μm but utilizing 2D cluster shape)
- Full station coverage from beam pipe to outer acceptance using single technology, eliminating IT/OT boundary
- Approximately 500,000 channels for three stations, manageable with modern SiPM array packaging

**Cooling:**

- SiPMs require operation at approximately -40°C to suppress dark count rate to acceptable levels (~100 kHz per mm²)
- Implement CO2 bi-phase cooling system on the SiPM carrier boards; fibres themselves operate at room temperature
- Cooling structure contributes <0.3% X₀ per station

**Front-end electronics:**

- Custom ASIC with 40 MHz readout, integrating charge over 25 ns window, with threshold comparison and time-over-threshold encoding
- On-chip clustering to reduce output bandwidth

### Expected Performance Gain

- Occupancy per channel at 25 ns bunch spacing and luminosity 2×10^33 cm^-2 s^-1 remains below 5% (compared to 25% in OT at Run I conditions) due to smaller channel size
- Spatial resolution of ~70 μm uniformly across full station area compared to 200 μm OT and 50 μm IT with discontinuity at boundary
- Eliminates multi-bunch-crossing readout issue entirely, removing spillover hits that increase OT occupancy

---

## Upgrade 5: Calorimeter Photodetector Replacement

### Motivation
The paper documents ongoing PMT gain degradation due to dynode aging at high integrated anode current, requiring frequent voltage adjustments and creating gaps between absolute calibrations. The HCAL calibration can only be performed bi-monthly using cesium sources, too infrequent to track rapid gain changes. The consequence is systematic uncertainty in energy scale that propagates into photon and electron PID performance.

### Proposed Implementation

**Replace PMTs in highest-rate ECAL inner region with silicon photomultipliers:**

- The inner ECAL region (smallest cell size, 4.04 cm, highest rate) drives most of the aging problem
- Replace PMTs in inner 20% of ECAL area with SiPMs of active area matched to existing fibre bundle diameter
- SiPMs do not suffer dynode aging and maintain stable gain over the full operational period
- Requires new front-end shaping electronics matched to SiPM capacitance and fast recovery time
- For outer and middle ECAL regions, retain existing PMTs but install metal channel dynode replacements which have demonstrated factor ~3 longer lifetime at same anode current

**Continuous calibration system upgrade:**

- Install LED-based calibration system with absolute light output stabilization using reference photodiodes
- Current LED system monitors relative changes well but does not provide absolute calibration
- Add laser-based calibration injection via optical fibre to each PMT/SiPM, enabling absolute gain calibration between physics fills without dedicated calibration runs
- For HCAL, supplement the bimonthly cesium source procedure with continuous monitoring using isolated single-hadron events reconstructed online, providing weekly inter-calibration corrections

**SPD and PS readout modernization:**

- Replace existing MAPM (multi-anode PMT) devices in SPD and PS with SiPM arrays, eliminating the high-voltage supply complexity and magnetic field sensitivity issues
- New SiPM-based readout provides improved single-MIP resolution, reducing SPD threshold uncertainty

### Expected Performance Gain

- ECAL energy resolution stability improves; cell-to-cell intercalibration maintained at 1% level continuously versus current 2% achieved only after dedicated calibration campaigns
- Photon energy resolution for B→K*γ mass reconstruction improves from current 93 MeV/c² toward approximately 75 MeV/c²
- Electron identification efficiency improves by 2-3 percentage points at fixed misidentification rate due to better energy resolution in E/pc matching

---

## Summary of Priority Ordering

| Upgrade | Primary Gain | Complexity | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full software trigger | Factor 2+ in hadronic charm yield | Very high | Highest |
| Pixel VELO | IP resolution, radiation tolerance | High | Highest |
| SciFi tracker | Occupancy, uniformity | High | High |
| RICH MaPMT | PID efficiency 3-5% | Medium | Medium |
| Calorimeter photodetectors | Energy scale stability | Medium | Medium |

The software trigger and pixel VELO upgrades are interdependent and synergistic: the pixel VELO's 2D hit information and faster readout are prerequisites for running pattern recognition at 40 MHz within the software trigger latency budget. These two upgrades together represent the highest-leverage investment for physics performance improvement at higher luminosity running.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for XENON1T

## 1. Photosensor Upgrades

### Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)
The R11410-21 PMTs represent the single largest radioactivity contribution per unit photosensitive area. Specific implementation:

- **Device**: VUV-sensitive SiPMs such as Hamamatsu VUV4 or FBK VUV-HD series, optimized for 178 nm with photon detection efficiency (PDE) >20% versus the effective ~12.5% photon detection efficiency achieved in science run 0
- **Geometry**: Tile the entire top and bottom faces with 6×6 mm² SiPM cells in modular arrays, eliminating dead space between circular PMT windows
- **Radioactivity**: SiPMs contain negligible amounts of U/Th compared to the ~1 mBq/PMT level measured for R11410-21 tubes; with 248 PMTs this is a dominant materials background contribution
- **Gain stability**: SiPMs eliminate the vacuum integrity problem that disabled 27 PMTs (11% channel loss) during science run 0, caused by xenon leaking into the PMT vacuum
- **Critical challenge to address**: SiPM readout electronics must be located outside the cryostat to avoid radioactivity contribution; use long low-capacitance coaxial lines with cryogenic preamplifiers based on JFET or HEMT transistors mounted at an intermediate temperature stage (~150K) to preserve signal-to-noise ratio

### Wavelength-Shifting Reflector Panels
- Replace bare PTFE panels with tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) or polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) wavelength-shifting coatings on PTFE
- TPB converts 178 nm VUV photons to ~430 nm where SiPD PDE is substantially higher (~50%)
- Estimated light yield improvement: factor 2-3× increase in g1 from the measured 0.144 PE/γ
- Implementation: vacuum-deposited TPB at 0.2 mg/cm² on all 24 PTFE panels and reflector plates, verified for stability at −96°C

---

## 2. Field Cage and Electrode Redesign

### Higher Voltage Operation
Science run 0 operated at only 0.125 kV/cm drift field versus the design goal of ~1 kV/cm, severely compromising ER/NR discrimination and electron lifetime:

- **Root cause**: The Heinzinger PNC 150000-1 supply and feedthrough limited reliable operation to −12 kV cathode bias
- **Upgrade**: Redesign the UHMW polyethylene feedthrough with a graded-field structure using resistive dividers along the 1.5 m length, targeting reliable operation at −100 kV (corresponding to ~1 kV/cm across the 97 cm drift gap)
- **Electrode modification**: At higher fields the anode voltage must increase proportionally; replace the Kapton-insulated CAEN A1526P supply and cable with a dedicated high-voltage system rated to +10 kV for the extraction field, targeting >10 kV/cm extraction efficiency to improve the measured 96% electron extraction efficiency toward theoretical maximum
- **Field shaper resistors**: Replace the 5 GΩ resistor chain with lower-value 500 MΩ resistors to reduce voltage drop sensitivity to small leakage currents at high voltage, improving field uniformity; use custom bulk metal foil resistors (Vishay) screened for radioactivity

### Improved Electrode Meshes
- The hexagonal etched meshes showed sagging (evidenced by the S2 response increase toward center visible in figure 22)
- Replace with woven wire electrodes using 50 µm diameter Au-plated tungsten wire at 2 mm pitch, pre-tensioned to 200 MPa, achieving <100 µm sag across the 96 cm diameter
- Gate electrode wire diameter reduction from 127 µm to 50 µm increases optical transparency from 92.7% to ~98%, directly improving S1 light collection below the gate

---

## 3. Radon Mitigation Hardware

Radon at 10 µBq/kg is the dominant background (620 events/(t·y)), dwarfing all other sources.

### Online Radon Distillation Column Integration
- The existing distillation column demonstrated Rn reduction >27× on XENON100 but requires diverting purification flow
- Install a **dedicated second distillation column** optimized specifically for online Rn removal operating in parallel with the existing Kr column, using 2 m of Sulzer MellapakPlus 252.Y structured packing operating at higher reflux ratio than the Kr column
- Design the Rn column to handle the full 50 slpm purification flow rather than the 7% fraction used in science run 0
- Expected reduction: from 10 µBq/kg to <1 µBq/kg, reducing the dominant background by 10×

### Electropolishing and Radon-Emanation-Suppressed Surfaces
- The inner cryostat surface is identified as a significant Rn emanation source
- Apply **atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Al₂O₃** (20 nm thickness) to all inner stainless steel surfaces including the cryostat interior, purification system components, and getter housings; ALD coatings reduce Rn emanation by factors of 10-100 by blocking Ra recoil implantation sites
- Replace SAES PS4-MT50-R getters with custom cold-trap-based purification using activated charcoal at −40°C, which removes electronegative impurities without the Rn emanation associated with the zirconium getter beds

---

## 4. Purification System Upgrades

### Higher Flow Rate Pumps
Science run 0 electron lifetime was limited to ~450 µs by outgassing at the maximum reliable pump flow of 50 slpm:

- Replace CHART QDrive pumps with **magnetically-coupled centrifugal cryogenic pumps** (e.g., Barber-Nichols BNCP series adapted for xenon service) capable of 200 slpm flow rates
- At 200 slpm the purification turnover time drops from ~8 days to ~2 days, projecting electron lifetime improvement to >2 ms based on the outgassing model fit shown in figure 19
- An electron lifetime of 2 ms versus 452 µs reduces the S2 correction uncertainty at the cathode from ~50% to ~12%, significantly improving position reconstruction accuracy and fiducial volume definition

### Liquid-Phase Purification
- Complement gas-phase purification with **liquid-phase filtration** using a submerged getter cartridge (SAES MonoTorr PS4 adapted for LXe immersion) installed directly in the LXe volume below the cathode
- Eliminates the heat exchanger evaporation/condensation cycle thermal load of 0.39 W/slpm × 50 slpm = 19.5 W currently imposed on the cryogenic system

---

## 5. Cryogenic System Improvements

### Active Vibration Isolation
- Pulse-tube refrigerators introduce 1.4 Hz mechanical oscillations that couple to the liquid-gas interface position; the diving bell capacitive levelmeters show ~30 µm precision but the interface stability is likely worse due to PTR vibrations
- Install **vibration decoupling bellows** with active pneumatic damping on the cold finger connections, targeting interface stability <10 µm, which directly reduces S2 width variations and improves z-position reconstruction

### Improved Liquid Level Control
- Replace the vertically-adjustable gas-exhaust tube with a **piezoelectric actuated micro-valve** on the diving bell pressurization line, enabling sub-millimeter liquid level control with <1 ms response time
- This stabilizes the extraction field geometry and reduces event-by-event variation in S2 pulse shape

---

## 6. Data Acquisition Upgrades

### Higher Resolution Digitizers
- Current CAEN V1724 digitizers operate at 100 MHz with 14-bit resolution, providing 10 ns time bins
- Replace with **250 MHz, 16-bit digitizers** (e.g., CAEN V1730 or custom ATCA-based system) reducing timing uncertainty from 10 ns to 4 ns
- The transit time spread of R11410-21 PMTs is (9.1 ± 1.3) ns; current digitizer timing is comparable to this, so improvement yields better S1 rise-time discrimination between S1 and S2, improving the minimum 3-PMT-in-50ns S1 classification threshold
- Improved S1 timing enables extension of the analysis threshold below the current 200 PE S2 trigger (≈7 electrons), potentially reaching single-electron S2 sensitivity

### FPGA-Based Online Position Reconstruction
- Implement the likelihood-based XY position reconstruction algorithm in **Xilinx Ultrascale+ FPGAs** co-located with the digitizer crates
- Enables real-time fiducial volume cuts in the trigger logic, reducing the data rate from calibration sources by ~10× and enabling higher calibration source activities without DAQ saturation

---

## Prioritized Impact Summary

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Estimated Background Reduction |
|---|---|---|
| Dedicated Rn distillation column | Dominant ER background | 10× reduction in Rn contribution |
| ALD surface coatings | Rn emanation at source | Factor 5-10× Rn reduction |
| High-flow purification pumps | Electron lifetime, S2 resolution | Improves charge signal by ~4× at cathode |
| SiPM photosensors | Light yield, radioactivity, reliability | 2-3× increase in g1, eliminates PMT vacuum failures |
| High-voltage feedthrough redesign | ER/NR discrimination at design field | Restores design-goal discrimination efficiency |

The radon mitigation and purification upgrades offer the largest immediate physics return given that the 622 events/(t·y) Rn background dominates all other sources combined, while the photosensor upgrade represents the most transformative long-term improvement for the successor XENONnT instrument.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Advanced LIGO: Prioritized Proposals

## 1. Quantum Noise Reduction via Squeezed Light Injection

The paper explicitly identifies quantum noise as a fundamental limit across most of the detection band, and notes compatibility with squeezed light as a design goal.

### Specific Implementation
- **Inject frequency-dependent squeezed vacuum** from an optical parametric oscillator (OPO) based on periodically-poled potassium titanyl phosphate (PPKTP) crystal into the signal recycling cavity via the output Faraday isolator
- **Filter cavity network**: Two 16-meter triangular filter cavities in series, each with finesse ~5000, to rotate squeezing angle from phase squeezing at high frequencies to amplitude squeezing at low frequencies. The rotation frequency crossover targets ~50 Hz, addressing both shot noise and radiation pressure noise simultaneously
- **Target**: 10 dB of injected squeezing, realistically yielding 6 dB improvement after losses, corresponding to roughly a factor of 2 in strain sensitivity across the band
- **Critical enabling component**: Reduce output chain losses from the current ~10% to below 5% by replacing the output Faraday isolator with a polarizing beam splitter-based circulator, and improving output mode cleaner throughput

The paper acknowledges this directly as a planned future capability; the technology has since been demonstrated at GEO600 and is the clearest near-term gain available.

---

## 2. Test Mass Mirror Coating Replacement

The paper identifies coating Brownian noise as the **dominant thermal noise source** in the most sensitive frequency band around 100 Hz, arising from mechanical loss in the Ta₂O₅-based dielectric coatings with loss angle ~2.3×10⁻⁴.

### Specific Implementation
- **Replace Ta₂O₅/SiO₂ multilayer coatings with amorphous silicon (a-Si) / silicon nitride (Si₃N₄) coatings** deposited by ion beam sputtering at elevated substrate temperatures (~300°C during deposition)
- **Alternative: crystalline AlGaAs coatings** grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs substrates and transfer-bonded to fused silica test masses. These have demonstrated mechanical loss angles of ~5×10⁻⁵, approximately 4× lower than current titanium-doped tantala
- **Layer architecture**: Maintain the current quarter-wave optical thickness design but optimize thicknesses using numerical algorithms minimizing total mechanical energy weighted by optical field intensity profile
- **Expected gain**: Factor of 2 reduction in coating thermal noise power spectral density, directly improving strain sensitivity in the 30–300 Hz band where coating Brownian noise dominates
- **Metrology requirement**: Coating uniformity better than 0.3 nm rms over the central 160 mm diameter must be maintained; interferometric surface profilometry validation required before installation

The paper explicitly states this is the limiting noise source at 100 Hz; even modest improvements here dominate gains in the most astrophysically important band.

---

## 3. Increased Test Mass Size and Substrate Material

The paper establishes that beam size on test masses is constrained to 6.2 cm (1/e²) on the ETMs to limit aperture losses, and that thermal noise scales inversely with beam radius.

### Specific Implementation
- **Increase test mass diameter from 34 cm to 45 cm and mass from 40 kg to 100 kg**, maintaining fused silica substrate material (Heraeus Suprasil 3001 equivalent)
- **Redesign arm cavity geometry**: Adjust ITM radius of curvature to 2450 m and ETM to 2750 m to support beam radii of 7.5 cm / 8.5 cm on ITM/ETM respectively, while keeping g₁g₂ product at 0.83 to maintain the near-concentric configuration
- **Suspension redesign**: Quadruple pendulum must be scaled to accommodate 100 kg bottom mass. Fused silica fiber diameter increases from 400 µm to approximately 600 µm, recalculated to maintain 9 Hz bounce mode; fiber length increases proportionally to maintain 510 Hz violin mode frequency above the sensitive band
- **Vacuum chamber modification**: BSC chamber inner diameter currently limits this; the beam tube bore (1.2 m diameter) sets the ultimate constraint. Larger HAM tanks would need to house expanded recycling cavity optics
- **Thermal noise gain**: Coating Brownian noise scales as 1/r for beam radius r, so moving from 6.2 cm to 8.5 cm ETM beam radius yields ~27% reduction in coating thermal noise amplitude

---

## 4. Cryogenic Test Mass Operation

The paper identifies suspension thermal noise from fused silica fibers and coating thermal noise from mirror surfaces as fundamental limits. Both scale as √T, making cryogenic operation directly beneficial.

### Specific Implementation
- **Cool test masses to 20 K** using a silicon test mass and suspension system (fused silica becomes brittle and loses its favorable mechanical properties below ~100 K, but crystalline silicon has a mechanical loss angle of ~10⁻⁸ at 20 K and a thermal expansion zero-crossing near 18 K)
- **Test mass material**: Switch from fused silica to **100 kg monocrystalline silicon** (34 cm × 20 cm cylinders), which requires changing the laser wavelength to **1550 nm or 2 µm** since silicon is opaque at 1064 nm. Nd:YAG laser must be replaced with an erbium-doped fiber laser (1550 nm) or thulium-doped fiber laser (2 µm)
- **Heat extraction**: Six heat links per test mass using **high-purity aluminum or sapphire crystal ribbons** connecting the test mass to a cold stage, designed to have high thermal conductance at DC while providing mechanical isolation at acoustic frequencies. Calculated heat extraction: ~500 mW per test mass at full power operation
- **Suspension fibers**: Replace fused silica fibers with **silicon ribbon fibers** of rectangular cross-section (2 mm × 0.3 mm), which have substantially lower thermoelastic noise at silicon's thermal expansion zero crossing
- **Cryostat integration**: Each BSC vacuum chamber requires an inner radiation shield at 80 K (liquid nitrogen or cryocooler) and an inner cold stage at 20 K (pulse tube cryocoolers), totaling approximately 200 W cooling capacity per chamber
- **Combined gain**: Factor of ~5–10 in suspension thermal noise, factor of ~3 in coating thermal noise if crystalline coatings are also used at cryogenic temperatures

This is the most transformative upgrade and represents the core design principle of next-generation detectors (Einstein Telescope, KAGRA partially). It requires replacing all downstream infrastructure.

---

## 5. Higher Laser Power with Improved Thermal Compensation

The paper notes that 125 W input power yields 750 kW circulating in the arms, and that parametric instabilities may limit power scaling. Quantum noise decreases as 1/√P.

### Specific Implementation
- **Upgrade laser to 500 W output** using a master oscillator power amplifier (MOPA) architecture with a Yb:YAG thin-disk laser as the high-power stage, replacing the current injection-locked ring oscillator. The thin-disk geometry provides better thermal management at high power with measured M² < 1.1
- **Improved intensity stabilization**: Current specification is 2×10⁻⁹ Hz⁻¹/² at 10 Hz. At 4× higher power, radiation pressure coupling becomes more severe. Add a third in-vacuum intensity sensing stage using a low-noise balanced homodyne detector after the power recycling cavity pickoff, with an AOM as the fast actuator (bandwidth 1 MHz)
- **Parametric instability mitigation**: Install **ring-dampers** on all four test masses — thin lossy rings (aluminum with epoxy coating) bonded to the barrel of each test mass using hydroxide-catalysis bonding. Target: Q-factor reduction of acoustic modes to ~10⁶ while not adding measurable thermal noise from the small added mass
- **Enhanced thermal compensation**: Upgrade CO₂ laser projectors from 15 W to 60 W capacity, with adaptive optic correction using a **deformable mirror** (ALPAO DM97, 97 actuators) in the CO₂ beam path, enabling spatial frequency correction beyond the current central/annular pattern capability
- **Expected gain**: Factor of 2 in laser power yields factor √2 ≈ 1.4 improvement in shot noise-limited sensitivity above ~200 Hz

---

## 6. Improved Seismic Isolation Below 20 Hz

The paper shows gravity gradient noise (Newtonian noise) emerging as a fundamental limit below ~20 Hz, and seismic noise as the limit below 11 Hz.

### Specific Implementation
- **Active Newtonian noise cancellation**: Deploy a network of **72 broadband seismometers** (Nanometrics Trillium Compact 120s, or equivalent) in two horizontal arrays within 10 m of each test mass, arranged in two concentric rings at radii of 2 m and 8 m. Use adaptive Wiener filtering to subtract inferred gravitational gradient noise from the gravitational wave readout signal. Expected subtraction factor: 3–5 in the 5–15 Hz band, based on simulations with realistic seismic field models
- **Underground seismometer boreholes**: Drill four boreholes to 5 m depth adjacent to each test mass chamber, housing vertical seismometers (STS-2 or equivalent). Vertical component provides additional constraint on compressional wave field
- **Improved ISI active isolation**: Replace current L4C geophones (sensitivity floor ~10⁻⁹ m/√Hz above 1 Hz) with **custom inertial sensors using optical readout** (Michelson interferometer displacement sensing of a ~100 g proof mass suspended on a 0.5 Hz pendulum), achieving ~10⁻¹¹ m/√Hz noise floor from 0.1–10 Hz. This directly improves ISI subtraction performance and reduces test mass motion
- **Tilt seismometers**: Install two horizontal rotation seismometers (AIS tiltmeter design, sensitivity 10⁻¹⁰ rad/√Hz) at each BSC chamber stage 1 to decouple tilt from horizontal acceleration, which currently contaminates the T240 seismometer signals below 30 mHz as noted in the paper

---

## 7. Output Mode Cleaner and Readout Chain Improvements

The paper assumes 90% detection efficiency; improving this directly reduces quantum noise equivalently to increasing laser power.

### Specific Implementation
- **Replace current 4-mirror bowtie OMC** with a **6-mirror ring cavity** (round trip length 1.5 m, finesse 600) fabricated from ultra-low expansion glass (Zerodur), with mirror substrates bonded directly using optical contact bonding rather than epoxy. This increases mechanical stability and reduces thermally driven length fluctuations
- **Replace InGaAs photodiodes** with **quantum-dot-based photodiodes** optimized for 1064 nm with demonstrated quantum efficiency >99% (compared to typical 95% for standard InGaAs). Current 90% total efficiency with 95% QE diodes losing ~5% in the diode itself
- **Balanced homodyne detection replacement for DC readout**: Implement a proper **balanced homodyne detector** using a 50/50 beamsplitter and two matched photodiodes, eliminating the current DC offset readout scheme. This removes the need to operate the interferometer slightly off the dark fringe, recovering ~1% of lost contrast and reducing classical laser noise coupling by the common mode rejection ratio of the balanced detector (~40 dB)
- **Output squeezing path loss reduction**: Add an in-vacuum Faraday isolator with improved TGG crystal aperture (12 mm diameter versus current design) to reduce clipping losses from ~2% to <0.5%

---

## Priority Ranking by Impact

| Upgrade | Frequency Band Improved | Strain Sensitivity Gain | Implementation Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Squeezed light injection | 50 Hz – 5 kHz | Factor 2 amplitude | Medium – near term |
| Crystalline/low-loss coatings | 30 – 300 Hz | Factor 2 amplitude | High – material R&D |
| Cryogenic silicon test masses | 10 – 300 Hz | Factor 3–5 amplitude | Very high – requires full redesign |
| Larger test masses | 30 – 300 Hz | Factor 1.3 amplitude | High |
| Higher laser power | 100 Hz – 5 kHz | Factor 1.4 amplitude | Medium |
| Newtonian noise cancellation | 5 – 20 Hz | Factor 3–5 amplitude | Medium |
| Readout chain improvement | All frequencies | Factor 1.1 amplitude | Low – near term |

The squeezed light injection and improved coatings offer the best near-term returns within the existing infrastructure. The cryogenic silicon upgrade represents the necessary long-term architectural evolution, as reflected in the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer design studies.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Improved 0νββ Physics Performance

## 1. Liquid Argon Scintillation Veto (Highest Priority)

The paper explicitly states this was deferred to Phase II based on LArGe results. Concrete implementation:

**Wavelength Shifter System**
- Replace the existing radon shroud with a **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) coated nylon or VM2000 reflector cylinder** at ~1 mm thickness, achieving ~80% photon collection efficiency from the 128 nm LAr scintillation re-emitted at ~420 nm
- Deploy **Hamamatsu R11065 3" low-background PMTs** or **SensL MicroFC-60035 SiPMs** on the inner surface of the mini-shroud cylinder; SiPMs are preferable given their negligible radioactivity (~μBq/kg range) versus PMT glass (~mBq/kg)
- Target 50 photoelectrons/MeV to discriminate alpha/beta/gamma event topologies via LAr scintillation pulse shape (τ_slow = 1.6 μs for singlet/triplet ratio discrimination)
- Expected background reduction: **factor 3-5** on BI from 2×10⁻² toward 5×10⁻³ cts/(keV·kg·yr)

## 2. Transition to BEGe Detectors Universally

The paper notes Phase II BEGe detectors achieve **1.7 keV FWHM vs 4.5 keV** for coaxial detectors at 1332 keV.

**Specific improvements:**
- Full replacement with **Canberra BEGe or ORTEC PROFILE Series** p-type point-contact detectors, 700-900g mass per unit
- Point contact geometry provides A/E (current amplitude to energy ratio) pulse shape discrimination with **~90% signal acceptance at ~99.9% alpha/multi-site rejection** based on single-site vs multi-site event topology
- Energy resolution improvement from 4.5 keV → ~2.5 keV FWHM at Qββ reduces ROI width proportionally, directly cutting background by factor ~1.8 for same BI
- **Inverted Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC)** geometry (demonstrated by MJD collaboration) allows larger masses (>1 kg) while retaining PSD capability; evaluate **RD-ICPC detectors from Mirion/Canberra** with demonstrated 2.0 keV FWHM at 2615 keV

## 3. Front-End Electronics Replacement

Current CC2 preamplifier operates at LAr temperature but uses commercial BF862 JFET in standard packaging.

**Upgrade path:**
- Implement **custom ASIC-based charge sensitive amplifier** (e.g., similar to CUBE ASIC developed for CDEX or FADC-coupled designs from LBNL) designed specifically for 88 K operation
- Replace BF862 discrete JFET with **bare-die silicon JFET** (Interfet NJ132L or equivalent) with direct cold bonding, reducing input capacitance from ~5 pF to ~1-2 pF
- This reduces electronic noise contribution from **0.8 keV + 0.024 keV/pF** baseline; for 300 pF detector capacitance, gain of ~1.5 keV FWHM improvement is achievable
- Implement **on-board 14-bit ADC at LAr temperature** (evaluate Analog Devices AD9649 characterized at cryogenic temperatures) to eliminate 10 m analog cable transmission noise currently degrading resolution from ~2.2 keV (manufacturer spec) to 4.5 keV operational

## 4. Mini-Shroud and Electric Field Shielding Redesign

The 42K problem required post-hoc mini-shroud implementation. A redesigned system should:

**Hermetic Faraday enclosure:**
- Replace 60 μm Cu foil mini-shroud with **electroformed copper cylinders** (10 μm wall, <0.1 μBq/kg ²²⁸Th demonstrated for Majorana) providing complete electrostatic shielding with minimal mass (~5g per detector vs current ~15g)
- Integrate **TPB-coated inner surface** for combined ion shielding + LAr photon collection in single component
- Add **getter rings of activated charcoal** (Carbo-Act International, as already qualified) at top/bottom of mini-shroud to capture ²²²Rn before it reaches detector surface
- Seal mini-shroud to string structure with **indium wire gaskets** rather than overlapping foil, eliminating convective exchange with bulk LAr

## 5. Calibration System Enhancement

Current ²²⁸Th wire sources deployed vertically have non-uniform illumination.

**Upgrades:**
- Replace movable source design with **permanently installed ⁸³ᵐKr injection system** (as used in XENON experiments): krypton dissolved in LAr provides spatially uniform calibration at 41.5 keV without mechanical reliability issues; purge with activated charcoal after calibration
- Add **²⁰⁸Tl needle sources** on retractable fibers positioned at detector mid-plane for direct 2615 keV line calibration (closer to Qββ = 2039 keV than current geometry)
- Implement **LED-based charge injection system** directly on CC2 board with improved stability: replace current test pulse capacitor CT with **laser diode + fiber** to p+ contact window for absolute efficiency monitoring at <0.1% systematic

## 6. Water Cherenkov Veto Upgrade

Current 0.5% PMT coverage with 66 × 8" PMTs is marginal.

**Upgrades:**
- Replace ETL 9350KB PMTs with **Hamamatsu R7081HQE** (35% quantum efficiency vs ~25% for ETL) or **R12860** ultra-low background high-QE tubes
- Increase coverage to **~2%** by adding 120 additional PMTs on existing mount rings; at current photon yield this raises MDE from 97.2% toward >99.5%
- Add **gadolinium sulfate (Gd₂(SO₄)₃) at 0.1% concentration** to water: neutron capture on ¹⁵⁷Gd releases 8 MeV gamma cascade with ~30 μs delayed coincidence, enabling neutron-muon coincidence tagging to suppress cosmogenic ⇒ reduces indirect muon background by estimated factor 10

## 7. Radon Suppression Infrastructure

Current emanation of 54.7 mBq from cryostat remains significant.

**Hardware additions:**
- Install **cryogenic radon trap** on LAr recirculation line: 2 kg activated charcoal column at 77 K (LN₂ cooled) with demonstrated >10³ reduction factor for Rn in gas phase; integrate into existing triaxial pipe system
- Replace stainless steel manifold flanges (currently dominant Rn source at ~20 mBq post-copper-shield installation) with **electropolished OFHC copper manifold** with Helicoflex metal seals throughout, targeting <5 mBq total emanation
- Line radon shroud interior with **thin evaporated gold film** (10 nm on copper foil) to reduce Rn diffusion through grain boundaries by factor ~5

## Summary Impact Assessment

| Upgrade | BI Reduction Factor | Implementation Complexity |
|---------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| LAr scintillation veto | 3-5× | High |
| Universal BEGe + PSD | 5-10× (combined) | Medium |
| Improved FEE/resolution | 1.5-2× (via ROI narrowing) | Medium |
| Hermetic mini-shroud + getter | 2-3× (42K suppression) | Low |
| Gd-loaded water | 2-3× (neutron background) | Low |
| Radon trap upgrade | 2× | Low |

Combined, these upgrades could plausibly push the BI from the current **2×10⁻² toward 10⁻³ cts/(keV·kg·yr)**, the stated Phase II target, while improving energy resolution sufficiently to reduce the effective ROI background by an additional factor of ~2.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Forward Heavy-Flavour Spectrometer

## Framing the Problem

The primary physics performance metrics for such an instrument (essentially LHCb-like) are: **proper-time resolution** (driven by vertex/tracking), **mass resolution** (momentum resolution), **particle identification**, **trigger efficiency and latency**, and **luminosity reach**. I'll address each with concrete technology choices.

---

## 1. Silicon Vertex Detector: The Highest-Leverage Upgrade

### 1.1 Pixel Sensor Technology

**Replace strip/hybrid-pixel sensors with Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors (MAPS) based on 65 nm or 28 nm CMOS imaging process.**

- **Technology**: Tower Semiconductor / TSMC 65 nm with deep p-well (enabling full CMOS in-pixel). Examples: ALICE ITS3 concept, or next-generation descendants of ALPIDE.
- **Pixel pitch**: Reduce from ~55 μm (Timepix3/Velopix era) to **10–20 μm pitch**, improving single-hit resolution from ~14 μm to ~3–5 μm.
- **Impact on IP resolution**: Proper-time resolution scales as σ_t ∝ σ_IP/p_T. Halving σ_IP from ~35 μm to ~15 μm at 1 GeV/c directly doubles effective tagging significance.
- **Thinning**: MAPS can be thinned to **50 μm active layer** (vs. ~200–300 μm for hybrids), reducing multiple Coulomb scattering (MCS) contribution to IP resolution by ~√4 = factor 2 in the MCS-dominated regime.

### 1.2 Sensor Geometry: Curved/Cylindrical Wafer-Scale

**Implement bent, wafer-scale MAPS modules (ITS3-style) wrapping around the beampipe.**

- Eliminate module overlaps, support structures, and inter-module material.
- First layer at **r ≈ 25 mm** from beam axis (or closer with retractable mechanics), moving from ~30 mm typical.
- **Material budget target**: < 0.1% X₀ per layer (vs. 1–2% X₀ for current hybrid systems).
- Use **stitched reticles** (multi-reticle sensors) to cover full azimuth in one monolithic piece.

### 1.3 Radiation-Hard Design

- For HL-LHC-era luminosities, innermost layer must sustain **10¹⁶ neq/cm²**.
- Use **p-type substrate with n-type collection electrode** (better radiation hardness in MAPS), combined with **active edge** processing to minimize dead regions.
- Implement **in-pixel signal amplification with discriminator** to maintain time resolution < 2 ns at end-of-life.

### 1.4 Timing Layer Addition

**Add a dedicated fast-timing silicon layer (AC-LGAD / RSD technology) at intermediate radius (~100–150 mm).**

- **AC-LGAD (AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Detector)**: provides ~30 ps time resolution per hit with ~50 μm spatial resolution, 80–100 μm pitch.
- Manufacturer path: BNL/UFSD consortium; HPK production.
- Resolves **vertex-position ambiguity** in high-pileup (μ > 50) by 4D tracking: associate hits by both position and time, suppressing fake-vertex rate by O(10).
- Place before the RF-foil / beampipe to preserve pointing resolution.

---

## 2. Upstream Tracking: Replacing Low-Density Tracker Planes

### 2.1 Scintillating Fibre Tracker → Fine-Pitch Silicon Strip

**Replace the upstream scintillating fibre stations with large-area thin silicon microstrip detectors in AC-coupled strip geometry.**

- **Strip pitch**: 100 μm (X-view) / 200 μm (stereo at 5°), sensor thickness 200 μm.
- **Technology**: Float-zone n-in-p sensors (Hamamatsu S series or similar), similar to CMS Phase-2 outer tracker but optimized for single-sided readout.
- Momentum resolution improvement: reduces the downstream lever arm contribution; combined with better IP from vertex detector, gives δp/p improvement of ~30% at 10 GeV/c.
- Readout ASIC: **SALT2 or FASER-style readout** adapted to 40 MHz bunch crossing.

### 2.2 Add a Silicon Telescope Station Immediately Downstream of Vertex Detector

Four stereo-angle planes at z = 200–500 mm:
- **Hybrid pixels** (50 μm × 50 μm, Timepix4 ASIC) for high-rate capability (> 1 GHz/cm²).
- Provides **ghost-hit rejection** and seed tracks for pattern recognition before the full downstream tracker.

---

## 3. Particle Identification: Critical for Flavour Tagging and Background Rejection

### 3.1 RICH Detector: Replace Flat Mirrors with SiPM-Based Photon Detectors

**Upgrade photon detectors from Multiwire Proportional Chambers + HPDs (Hybrid Photon Detectors) to Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs).**

- **Device**: Hamamatsu S13360-series or FBK/INFN SiPMs, 50 μm microcell pitch, PDE > 50% at 450 nm, dark count rate < 100 kHz/mm² at –30°C.
- **Configuration**: Tile array of 3 mm × 3 mm SiPMs with ~3 mm spatial resolution (sufficient for ring imaging), operated at ≈ –20°C with CO₂ cooling.
- **Advantage over HPDs**: No high-voltage divider chains, factor ~3 better PDE, much smaller dead area, radiation-hard up to 10¹² neutron-eq/cm².
- Cherenkov angle resolution improvement: from ~0.4 mrad (HPD) to **~0.25 mrad** per track, extending π/K separation above 5σ to **~80 GeV/c** (vs. ~60 GeV/c currently).

### 3.2 Introduce Time-of-Flight Layer with Picosecond Resolution

**Install a Focusing DIRC (Detection of Internally Reflected Cherenkov) or Fast TOF wall at ~12 m.**

- **Focusing DIRC**: Synthetic fused silica bars (Heraeus Suprasil 3002), coupled to SiPM array with focusing lens system.
- σ_t per track: ~15 ps, giving π/K separation up to **10–12 GeV/c** (currently absent in this spectrometer).
- Covers the rapidity gap where RICH has insufficient angle resolution at low momentum.
- Alternative: **AC-LGAD wall** at 12 m, 1.3 m × 1.3 m active area, 1.3 mm pitch, 30 ps resolution per hit.

### 3.3 Muon System: Add GEM Pre-Shower before Iron Absorbers

- Replace first muon station cathode-strip chambers with **Triple-GEM detectors** (10 cm × 10 cm readout boards, 250 μm pitch).
- Spatial resolution: < 100 μm (vs. ~6 mm for existing CSCs), enabling precise muon–track matching and improving punch-through rejection.
- Add **thin electromagnetic pre-shower** (2 X₀ Pb + scintillator) before first absorber to distinguish muons from pions at 3–10 GeV/c.

---

## 4. Calorimetry: Upgrade for Better Photon and Neutral Pion Resolution

### 4.1 Replace Shashlik ECAL with Tungsten Powder/Scintillator or PbWO₄

**Option A – Tungsten sampling calorimeter with SiPM readout (preferred for forward geometry):**
- **W-Si sampling**: alternating 2.5 mm W plates and 300 μm silicon sensors (HGCal-derivative technology from CMS).
- Position resolution: ~1 mm at 10 GeV (vs. ~6 mm shashlik), enabling π⁰ reconstruction up to 50 GeV.
- Energy resolution: σ_E/E ~ 10%/√E ⊕ 0.5%, improvement from ~10%/√E ⊕ 1.5%.
- This dramatically improves **B → ψ(2S)X, B → η_c X** modes and radiative decay modes.

**Option B – PbWO₄ crystals with SiPM readout:**
- Already radiation-hard; readout with large-area SiPMs (6 mm × 6 mm, low-noise operation at –25°C).
- Better energy resolution (σ/E ~ 2%/√E ⊕ 0.5%) but higher cost and mass production complexity.

---

## 5. Trigger and DAQ: Full Software Trigger Architecture

### 5.1 Eliminate Hardware Level-0 Trigger Entirely

**Move to a fully triggerless, continuous readout architecture (Allen/GPU-based, successor to LHCb Upgrade I).**

- **Front-end**: All detector elements read out at **40 MHz** (or 160 MHz with time-interleaved readout), zero-suppressed on-chip.
- **Data links**: lpGBT (Low-Power GigaBit Transceiver, 10.24 Gbps) × N per module, optical fibres via VCSEL arrays.
- **FPGA concentrators**: Xilinx Versal / Intel Agilex with HBM2e for event buffering.

### 5.2 GPU Farm as First Trigger Stage

**Deploy GPU-based real-time reconstruction as primary trigger (Allen algorithm successor):**

- **Hardware**: NVIDIA H100/H200 SXM5 GPUs (80 GB HBM3, ~3000 TFLOPS FP16), deployed in ~200-GPU farm.
- **Algorithm**: Hough-transform seeded Kalman filter for track reconstruction, executed in < **1 ms latency** per bunch-crossing readout window.
- **IP significance cut**: σ_IP > 3 applied in real time selects displaced vertices with > 95% efficiency for B-hadrons while rejecting > 99.9% of prompt background.
- Throughput: 40 Tbit/s aggregate input, ~100 kHz physics output after GPU stage.

### 5.3 FPGA-Based Fast Vertex Reconstruction

**Insert a dedicated FPGA stage for 2D-vertex seed finding before GPU farm:**

- **Device**: AMD/Xilinx Alveo U280 (100 Gbps bandwidth, HBM2).
- Perform **2D Hough accumulation in r-φ** within 200 ns of hit arrival.
- Pre-cluster hits and pass to GPU, reducing GPU input by factor 5, enabling lower thresholds.

### 5.4 Timing Distribution and Synchronization

**Replace TTC system with White Rabbit (WR) timing network:**
- Sub-nanosecond synchronization across all front-ends, critical for 4D tracking and AC-LGAD hits.
- **WR switch** (CERN wr-switch v3) with PPS distribution, jitter < 50 ps RMS.

---

## 6. Beampipe and Mechanical Integration

**Replace Be beampipe section near IP with lower-Z alternative:**

- **Carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP) beampipe**, 0.8 mm wall thickness, r = 20 mm.
- Material budget: ~0.15% X₀ (vs. ~0.4% X₀ for 1 mm Be).
- Combined with thin MAPS first layer, MCS contribution to σ_IP reduced by factor ~1.7.
- Coat inner surface with **Non-Evaporable Getter (NEG)** for distributed pumping, maintaining UHV (< 10⁻⁹ mbar) without pump obstructions.

---

## Quantified Summary of Expected Gains

| Subsystem Upgrade | Primary Metric | Expected Improvement |
|---|---|---|
| MAPS vertex detector (20 μm pixel, 50 μm thick) | IP resolution at 1 GeV/c | 35 μm → ~12–15 μm |
| AC-LGAD timing layer (30 ps) | Fake vertex rate at μ=50 | Factor 5–10 reduction |
| SiPM-RICH photon detectors | π/K separation reach | 60 → ~80 GeV/c |
| Focusing DIRC / TOF | Low-p PID gap filling | π/K > 3σ up to 12 GeV/c |
| W-Si ECAL | π⁰ position resolution | 6 mm → ~1 mm at 10 GeV |
| Full software trigger (GPU) | Trigger efficiency, B → hh | ~60% → ~90% for hadronic modes |
| CFRP beampipe + MAPS | Combined σ_t (proper time) | ~45 fs → ~25 fs for B⁰ |

---

## Priority Ordering (by physics return per cost)

1. **MAPS vertex detector with thinned sensors** — largest single impact on all heavy-flavour observables
2. **Full software trigger / GPU farm** — unlocks hadronic modes entirely inaccessible with hardware L0
3. **AC-LGAD timing layer** — essential for high-luminosity pileup rejection
4. **SiPM RICH upgrade** — necessary to maintain PID quality at higher rates
5. **W-Si ECAL** — opens new decay modes; highest cost, phased implementation practical

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a ~2-tonne Dual-Phase Xenon TPC

## Framing: What "Primary Physics Performance" Means Here

The figure of merit is **sensitivity to WIMP-nucleon cross-section**, which scales as:

$$\sigma_{\min} \propto \frac{\sqrt{B \cdot M \cdot t}}{M \cdot t \cdot \epsilon}$$

So upgrades must target: **(1) background reduction, (2) signal efficiency, (3) fiducial mass, (4) energy threshold, (5) position resolution.** I address each with concrete hardware proposals.

---

## 1. Photosensor Replacement: PMTs → Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

### The Problem with Current PMTs
- **Radioactivity**: A typical 3-inch Hamamatsu R11410-23 contributes ~0.5–1 mBq/PMT in ²³⁸U/²³²Th chains. With ~120 PMTs per array, this is the **dominant ER background source** for most analyses.
- **Single photoelectron resolution** is ~30% (PDE ~35%), limiting low-energy threshold.
- **Dead area** on the bottom array reduces S1 light collection efficiency.

### Proposed Upgrade
**Replace both PMT arrays with tiled VUV-sensitive SiPM arrays** (e.g., Hamamatsu VUV4 series S13371 or FBK NUV-HD-Cryo tiles operated at LXe temperature ~165 K).

**Specific implementation:**
- Tile the bottom array with **~3,000 × 6mm × 6mm SiPM pixels** on low-radioactivity PCBs (ENIG-free, polyimide substrate with electrodeposited copper traced to minimize U/Th)
- Use **Vikuiti ESR reflector** backing between tiles to maintain >95% active area coverage
- Front-end: **cryogenic JFET-based transimpedance amplifiers** (e.g., BF862 or custom ASIC like the ABCD3TA derivative) mounted on the flange feedthrough to minimize cable capacitance
- Target **PDE >50% at 175 nm** (vacuum ultraviolet), achievable with anti-reflection SiO₂ coatings matched to LXe

**Quantitative impact:**
- Radioactivity reduction: SiPMs + substrate can achieve **<0.1 mBq total** per array vs. ~60 mBq for PMT arrays → factor ~10–30 reduction in photosensor-induced ER background
- PDE improvement raises S1 yield from ~8 to ~15 photons/keV detected → **lower energy threshold** (~1 keVee vs. ~2 keVee), accessing sub-GeV DM and improving nuclear recoil acceptance at low energy
- Near-unity fill factor eliminates geometric inefficiency

---

## 2. Anode/Gate/Cathode Electrode Redesign for Improved Field Uniformity

### The Problem
- Conventional wire grids (SS or Be-Cu, ~100 μm diameter) suffer from **electrostatic sagging** over 1-meter diameter spans at high voltage, distorting the drift field
- Wire grids create **localized high-field regions** causing spurious electron emission (the primary source of "grid leak" ER background)
- Field non-uniformity → position reconstruction bias → fiducial volume uncertainty of ~5–10%

### Proposed Upgrade
**Replace wire grids with photolithographically patterned, etched metal mesh electrodes on fused silica frames**

**Specifics:**
- **Anode**: 50 μm-thick electroformed stainless steel mesh, hexagonal cell geometry, 500 μm pitch, 85% optical transparency, laser-welded to a PTFE-free titanium frame (titanium chosen for low U/Th and matched thermal contraction to fused silica)
- **Gate**: Same mesh spec, tensioned to <50 μm planarity tolerance using spring-loaded radial tensioning ring similar to CMS pixel detector support techniques
- **Cathode**: Thicker (200 μm) mesh on Kovar frame to handle higher HV (~50 kV for 1 kV/cm drift field across 1.2 m)
- **Field shaper**: Replace stacked ring resistor chain with **flexible printed circuit field shapers** (polyimide + Au traces, <0.1 mm pitch) laminated to the inner PTFE walls — eliminates resistor radioactivity entirely

**Quantitative impact:**
- Field uniformity improvement to <0.5% RMS → fiducial volume boundary uncertainty <1% → effectively increases usable fiducial mass by ~5–8%
- Reduced grid-induced electron emission → factor ~3 reduction in "mystery" ER background seen in all current-generation experiments near the gate region

---

## 3. Xenon Purification: Continuous Online Distillation Column

### The Problem
- **Krypton-85** (β-emitter, 687 keV endpoint) is the dominant low-energy ER background; achieving <0.01 ppt ⁸⁵Kr/Xe requires **sub-ppt natKr/Xe** levels
- Current getter-based purification removes electronegative impurities but **cannot remove noble gas contaminants** (Kr, Ar)
- Single pre-fill distillation is insufficient as Kr out-gasses from detector components over years

### Proposed Upgrade
**Integrate a continuous cryogenic distillation column into the xenon recirculation loop**

**Specifics:**
- **Spinning-band distillation column**: 2-meter tall, 50 mm diameter, with PTFE Sulzer-type packing, operating at ~180 K (LXe at slightly elevated pressure), achieving **theoretical plate count >100**
- Flow rate: 3–5 SLPM (compatible with standard getter recirculation), allowing full xenon mass processing in ~2 weeks continuously
- **Online radon trap in series**: activated charcoal trap at 200 K (Jacobi trap design) with 10 kg charcoal, replacing periodically — targets ²²²Rn reduction to <0.1 μBq/kg
- Monitor with **residual gas analyzer (Pfeiffer PrismaPlus)** on the gas return line for real-time Kr/Xe monitoring at ppt level

**Quantitative impact:**
- Achieve **<0.01 ppt Kr/Xe** continuously → ⁸⁵Kr event rate <0.01 events/(tonne·year·keVee) in the WIMP signal region → essentially negligible
- Radon reduction to <0.1 μBq/kg → <0.1 ER events/(tonne·year) from ²¹⁴Pb chain → factor ~5–10 over current state-of-art

---

## 4. Cathode High-Voltage Feedthrough: Eliminating Radioactive Cables

### The Problem
- Standard HV cables (coaxial, mineral-insulated) routing through the cryostat introduce **bulk radioactivity** and are prone to **micro-discharges** that generate spurious UV/VUV photons mimicking S1 signals
- Existing feedthroughs are failure points for Rn emanation

### Proposed Upgrade
**Custom cold-to-warm HV feedthrough using graded silicon carbide (SiC) field graders**

**Specifics:**
- **Feedthrough body**: Alumina ceramic with matched metal seal (Kovar), electropolished, baked at 400°C under vacuum
- **Graded resistivity SiC rings** (following ATLAS IBL feedthrough heritage) distribute the HV gradient eliminating triple-point discharge
- **HV cable inside cryostat**: Replace coaxial cable with a single-conductor **PTFE-clad Cu rod** supported by ultra-low-background PTFE standoffs — minimizes total material budget
- **Filtered power supply**: Add **PI-section LC filter** at room temperature with cutoff at 10 Hz to eliminate power supply noise coupling into the drift field

---

## 5. Outer Detector Upgrade: Gadolinium-Loaded Water Cherenkov + Neutron Capture

### The Problem
- The water Cherenkov muon veto identifies **muon-induced neutrons** but has poor efficiency for **radiogenic neutrons** (from U/Th fission/α-n reactions in detector materials) because these neutrons don't produce associated muon signals
- Radiogenic neutrons causing single-scatter NR events in the fiducial volume are **irreducible** with the current outer detector design — this is the dominant NR background

### Proposed Upgrade
**Load the water shield with 0.1% Gd₂(SO₄)₃ (gadolinium sulfate) by mass**

**Specifics:**
- Gd has the highest thermal neutron capture cross section of any stable element (49,000 barns for ¹⁵⁷Gd), emitting an 8 MeV gamma cascade detectable in the water Cherenkov
- **Gd-doped water handling**: Closed-loop filtration system with Gd concentration monitor (ICP-MS at monthly calibration points); Gd sulfate chosen for chemical stability and low corrosivity vs. GdCl₃
- Replace inner surface of water tank with **ESR or Lumirror reflective liner** to improve Cherenkov photon collection efficiency for low-energy gamma cascades
- **Add 20–40 additional 8-inch PMTs** (Hamamatsu R5912) to the outer detector to achieve >30% photocathode coverage, enabling tagging of 8 MeV cascades with >90% efficiency even for neutrons thermalizing far from the capture point
- **Liquid scintillator layer option**: Add a **2-tonne acrylic-enclosed liquid scintillator (LAB+PPO) shell** between xenon cryostat and water — provides ~4π gamma/neutron veto with ~500 keVee threshold, similar to LZ outer detector design but with improved coverage

**Quantitative impact:**
- Gd loading increases radiogenic neutron capture tagging efficiency from ~20% (pure water) to **>90%** — reduces NR background from neutrons by ~factor 5
- Combined with LS layer: NR background from single-scatter neutrons reduced to **<0.1 events/(tonne·year)** in the WIMP signal region

---

## 6. Cryostat and Internal Surface Radon Mitigation

### The Problem
- ²²²Rn emanating from PTFE reflectors, copper field shapers, and cryostat welds produces **²¹⁴Pb** (β, 1 MeV endpoint) and **²¹⁰Pb** daughters that plate out on inner surfaces and generate ER and NR backgrounds

### Proposed Upgrade
**Electropolished, passivated copper inner vessel + PTFE surface coating**

**Specifics:**
- **Inner cryostat vessel**: Switch from 316L SS to **oxygen-free high-conductivity (OFHC) copper** with electropolishing (Ra < 0.1 μm) — copper has lower Rn emanation rate and lower U/Th than steel
- **PTFE reflectors**: Switch to **sputtered PTFE-on-copper panels** rather than bulk PTFE extrusions — bulk PTFE dominates Rn emanation; thin sputtered layers reduce surface-to-volume ratio by ~100×
- **Getter-based Rn trap upstream of LXe return**: SAES MonoTorr PS4-MT50 getter operated at room temperature + cold charcoal trap in series, targeting Rn activity <1 μBq/kg

---

## 7. Data Acquisition and Trigger: Zero-Suppression ASIC Readout

### The Problem
- Current DAQ systems based on **CAEN V1724 digitizers** (14-bit, 100 MS/s) with software-level zero-suppression create **deadtime** and **threshold effects** that limit detection of very small S1 signals
- Low-energy NR events (sub-keV) produce S1 signals of **1–3 photons** total, requiring single-photon sensitive, low-threshold triggering

### Proposed Upgrade
**Custom ASIC-based readout with hardware waveform processing**

**Specifics:**
- Deploy **ATLAS HGTD ASIC derivative** or custom 65 nm CMOS ASIC with:
  - 12-bit ADC at 250 MS/s per channel
  - On-chip digital pulse finder with **2 ns timing resolution** for S1/S2 discrimination
  - Hardware coincidence trigger requiring ≥2 SiPM channels with >0.3 PE within 100 ns window (eliminates dark current triggers)
- **Trigger-less streaming readout**: Continuously stream waveforms at reduced bit-depth to GPU farm for offline trigger — eliminates hardware threshold bias entirely
- **GPU-accelerated online position reconstruction** (boosted regression trees on NVIDIA A100s) for real-time fiducial volume cuts, enabling **trigger on fiducial position** rather than energy alone — critical for sub-GeV DM searches

---

## Priority Ranking and Expected Combined Impact

| Upgrade | Background Reduction | Threshold Improvement | Relative Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM arrays | 10–30× ER from photosensors | 2× (lower threshold) | **Highest** |
| Online Rn/Kr distillation | 5–10× ER | Modest | **Highest** |
| Gd-loaded water + LS | 5× NR | None | **High** |
| Mesh electrodes | 2–3× ER (grid emission) | 5–10% FV gain | **High** |
| SiC HV feedthrough | Reliability/Rn | None | Medium |
| Electropolished Cu vessel | 2–3× Rn | None | Medium |
| Streaming DAQ/ASIC | Efficiency gain | Factor ~2 | Medium |

**Combined projected sensitivity improvement**: approximately **1–2 orders of magnitude** in cross-section at 40 GeV/c² WIMP mass over a baseline 2-tonne instrument with conventional components, largely driven by the SiPM + distillation + Gd-water combination.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Bare HPGe Array in Liquid Argon (GERDA/LEGEND-style)

## Framing the Problem

The primary physics performance metric is **sensitivity to neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ)**, which scales as:

$$S_{1/2}^{0\nu} \propto a \cdot \eta \cdot \sqrt{\frac{M \cdot T}{B \cdot \Delta E}}$$

So upgrades must attack: **background index B** (counts/keV/kg/yr), **energy resolution ΔE** (FWHM at Q_ββ = 2039 keV), **active mass M**, and **signal efficiency η**.

---

## 1. Detector Crystal Upgrades

### 1.1 Inverted Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC) Geometry — Push Further
**Current state:** LEGEND-200 uses ICPCs (~1-2 kg each). **Proposed upgrade:** Grow **larger-diameter ICPCs (≥100 mm diameter, ≥2.5 kg per crystal)** using improved Czochralski pullers with active diameter control feedback.

- **Why:** Larger crystals → higher surface-to-volume ratio improves, fewer contact surfaces per kg, fewer detector interfaces with potential radioactive contamination
- **Concrete technology:** Upgrade zone-refinement and Czochralski furnaces with laser interferometric diameter control (Siltec/PVA TePla-style) to reduce crystal defect density and enable reproducible large-boule growth
- **Impact:** ~30-40% reduction in detector module count for same mass → fewer components in radiopure zone

### 1.2 Improved Ge-76 Enrichment
**Current state:** ~88% enrichment via centrifuge cascade (Russia/URENCO).

**Proposed upgrade:** Implement **laser isotope separation (LIS) of germanium** using SILEX-derived or atomic vapor laser isotope separation (AVLIS) approaches post-centrifuge, pushing enrichment to **>95%**.

- **Concrete technology:** Pulsed CO₂ laser (wavelength-tuned to Ge isotopologue-specific vibrational bands in GeF₄) combined with cryogenic aerodynamic separation
- **Impact:** At 95% vs 88% enrichment, effective Q_ββ signal rate increases ~8%; more critically, background from non-76 isotopes (e.g., cosmogenic activation of ⁷²Ge, ⁷⁴Ge producing ⁶⁸Ge→⁶⁸Ga) is suppressed

### 1.3 Detector Surface Passivation and Groove Geometry
**Current state:** Lithium-diffused n+ surface, boron-implanted p+ point contact, with amorphous Ge or SiO passivation of groove region.

**Proposed upgrade:** Replace amorphous Ge passivation with **hydrogen-plasma-treated crystalline Ge surface termination** combined with **atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Al₂O₃ (~5 nm)**.

- **Why:** Amorphous Ge passivation creates near-surface charge trapping that degrades pulse shape discrimination (PSD) and causes slow-pulse tails in the spectrum
- **Concrete technology:** Remote H₂ plasma passivation system (similar to solar cell manufacturing) + Oxford Instruments FlexAL ALD reactor, process temperature <150°C to avoid lithium diffusion
- **Impact:** Reduces surface alpha/beta events leaking into ROI; improves A/E (current-to-energy ratio) PSD cut efficiency from ~90% to potentially >95% with lower dead layer contribution

---

## 2. Electronics and Signal Readout Upgrades

### 2.1 Cryo-ASIC Front-End at Detector Stage
**Current state:** GERDA/LEGEND use bare copper J-FETs (IF1320 or custom) at ~120K near the detector, with room-temperature shaping electronics.

**Proposed upgrade:** Replace discrete J-FET + resistive feedback with a **custom cryo-ASIC** (Application-Specific Integrated Circuit) operating at LAr temperature (87K).

- **Concrete technology:** Design in **SiGe BiCMOS process (e.g., IHP SG13G2, 130nm)** or **GaAs HEMT** technology — both have demonstrated low-noise operation at 77-87K
  - Input transistor: SiGe HBT with fT >200 GHz at 87K
  - On-chip: charge-sensitive amplifier, pole-zero cancellation, pile-up rejection logic, and **first-stage digitization** (8-bit flash ADC at 250 MS/s on-chip)
  - Power dissipation target: <200 μW/channel to avoid LAr boil-off increase
- **Why:** Eliminates cable capacitance between detector and first amplifier stage — a 50 pF cable adds ~3-5 eV equivalent noise charge (ENC) per pF
- **Impact:** Reduce ENC from ~50e⁻ to ~15-20e⁻ RMS, improving FWHM at 2039 keV from ~2.5 keV toward **1.5 keV** (approaching theoretical phonon/charge fluctuation limit for HPGe)

### 2.2 Multi-Channel Correlated Signal Readout
**Current upgrade:** Instrument **every detector segment** (for segmented variants) with independent cryo-ASIC channels plus **inter-crystal timing** with <10 ns resolution.

- **Concrete technology:** White Rabbit timing protocol over optical fiber (already used in LEGEND infrastructure) extended to individual detector timestamps; synchronization to <1 ns
- **Impact:** Enables rejection of multi-site Compton events across crystals at the coincidence level (vs. purely relying on single-crystal A/E PSD)

### 2.3 Digital Signal Processing: FPGA-Based Online PSD
**Current state:** Waveforms digitized at 25 MS/s and processed offline.

**Proposed upgrade:** Deploy **Xilinx Ultrascale+ or Intel Agilex FPGAs** for online waveform processing at **250 MS/s, 14-bit ADC** (e.g., CAEN V1725S or custom).

- Implement online **neural network inference** (shallow CNN) on FPGA fabric for real-time PSD
- Store only flagged waveforms + summary parameters, reducing data volume by 100×
- Implement **online muon veto** correlation within 10 μs window
- **Impact:** Faster analysis cycles, ability to adjust PSD thresholds dynamically, elimination of digitization-induced dead time

---

## 3. Liquid Argon Veto System Upgrades

### 3.1 Wavelength Shifter Quality and Coverage
**Current state:** LEGEND uses a **wavelength-shifting fiber curtain** (TPB-coated Tetratex fibers) + SiPM readout.

**Proposed upgrade:** Replace with **large-area monolithic TPB-coated acrylic panels** with embedded wavelength-shifting optical fibers, read out by **VUV-sensitive SiPMs without wavelength shifting on the SiPM face**.

- **Concrete technology:** 
  - Hamamatsu VUV4 SiPMs (50 μm cell pitch, PDE >20% at 128 nm) arranged in tiled panels
  - Acrylic panels with embedded Y-11 WLS fibers (emission at 490 nm), read out at panel edges
  - Alternatively: **Vikuiti ESR mirror foil** backing to improve photon collection efficiency
- **Why:** Current fiber curtain has ~15-20% geometric coverage gaps and TPB coating uniformity issues
- **Impact:** Improve LAr veto efficiency from ~80% to >95% for events depositing >100 keV in LAr → directly reduces ²⁰⁸Tl and ⁴²K backgrounds

### 3.2 LAr Purification for Extended Scintillation Mean Free Path
**Current state:** LAr purity is maintained but triplet lifetime (~1.5 μs) is limited by N₂, O₂ contamination at ppb level.

**Proposed upgrade:** Install a **continuous LAr recirculation and purification system** with:
- **Oxysorb/Hydrosorb getter cartridges** (SAES MonoTorr or Entegris) in a bypass loop at ~5-10 L/min flow rate
- **Inline photosensor monitoring** to measure Ar scintillation lifetime in real-time as a purity proxy
- Target: **O₂ equivalent contamination <0.1 ppb** (triplet lifetime >1.55 μs)

- **Additional upgrade:** Dope LAr with **small quantities of xenon (10-50 ppm)** — Xe shifts 128 nm Ar scintillation to 178 nm (Xe emission), extending attenuation length from ~1 m to >10 m in the detector volume and enabling more uniform light collection
- **Concrete technology:** Xe injection system with mass flow controller (MKS Instruments); validated at DarkSide-20k
- **Impact:** 20-30% improvement in LAr veto efficiency; enables timing-based discrimination of surface events

### 3.3 LAr Instrumentation: Charge+Light Coincidence
**Proposed new addition:** Instrument the LAr volume with **charge-sensitive electrodes** (wire planes or thick-GEM-style structures) to detect ionization electrons drifting under a weak electric field (~100 V/cm).

- **Concrete technology:** Induction-wire LAr TPC readout borrowed from DUNE/MicroBooNE, using **cold ADC ASICs (COLDATA/COLDADC)** already designed for LAr temperature
- Provides **3D spatial localization** of LAr background events to within ~1 mm
- **Impact:** Topology-based background rejection of multi-site events in LAr; particularly effective against ²⁰⁸Tl gamma backgrounds

---

## 4. Radiopurity and Materials Upgrades

### 4.1 Underground Electroforming of Copper Components
**Current state:** Detector holders use electroformed copper (OFHC or EF copper) with some underground production.

**Proposed upgrade:** Establish a **dedicated underground electroforming facility** (1500+ mwe) using:
- **High-purity copper sulfate bath** with online elemental analysis (ICP-MS sampling loop)
- Target: **<0.1 μBq/kg ²²⁶Ra, <0.1 μBq/kg ²²⁸Th** — an order of magnitude below surface-electroformed copper
- Electroform all LAr-facing structural components underground, never exposing to surface cosmic rays
- **Concrete technology:** Similar to Majorana Demonstrator underground EF facility at SURF; scale up to 10 kg/month production rate

### 4.2 Low-Mass Detector Mounting Structures
**Current state:** Copper or PTFE contact holders and spring clips.

**Proposed upgrade:** Replace copper springs/holders with **ultra-thin amorphous carbon (a-C) fiber structures** or **silicon carbide ceramic springs**.

- **Concrete technology:** CVD-grown a-C films (<10 μm thick) on Kapton mandrel, released and formed into spring clips; SiC machined from Norstel or Cree SiC wafers (ultra-low U/Th from semiconductor-grade precursors)
- Radiopurity of semiconductor-grade SiC: **<1 μBq/kg** for all gamma-emitting backgrounds
- **Impact:** Reduce near-detector material mass by 50-70% → reduce surface-proximity background by comparable factor

### 4.3 Improved Bond Wire and Electrical Contact Specification
**Current state:** Thin gold or aluminum bond wires from detector to PCB.

**Proposed upgrade:** Replace with **electroformed copper micro-ribbon contacts** and screen all PCB materials to **<0.01 mBq/kg ²²⁶Ra**.

- Screen every component lot with **ICP-MS and gamma spectroscopy** at dedicated underground counting facility (GeMPI/Gator-class HPGe screening detectors)
- Implement **materials database tracking** (chain of custody from mine to detector)

---

## 5. Water Shield and Muon Veto Upgrades

### 5.1 Upgrade Water Cherenkov Muon Veto PMTs to SiPMs
**Current state:** PMTs in water tank (GERDA) or pure water Cherenkov detector.

**Proposed upgrade:** Replace 8-inch PMTs with **tiled 6×6 mm SiPM arrays** (FBK NUV-HD or Hamamatsu S15779) on **ultra-low background acrylic support panels**.

- **Why:** SiPMs have no radioactive glass envelope (PMT glass is typically ~10 Bq/kg ²²⁶Ra), higher PDE at Cherenkov wavelengths (>400 nm), no high-voltage feed-through
- **Impact:** Muon veto efficiency >99.99% with improved timing resolution (SiPM transit time spread <100 ps vs PMT ~1 ns) → better muon shower reconstruction and rejection of cosmogenic neutron-induced backgrounds

### 5.2 Active Water Cherenkov + Gadolinium Loading
**Proposed upgrade:** Load the water shield with **gadolinium sulfate (Gd₂(SO₄)₃)** at **0.1% by mass**.

- Gd has a thermal neutron capture cross section of 49,000 barns, capturing in ~2 μs, followed by 8 MeV gamma cascade (vs. 2.2 MeV for hydrogen capture)
- **Concrete technology:** Gd loading established by Super-Kamiokande (SK-Gd), use their validated water purification + Gd sulfate dissolution protocol; install Gd-compatible water recirculation with Eichrom/Tulsion ion exchange resins to maintain Gd while removing U/Th/Ra
- **Impact:** Reduce cosmogenic neutron background by >50%; neutrons from (α,n) reactions and muon spallation captured with near-100% efficiency vs ~10% in pure water

---

## 6. Data Acquisition and Analysis Hardware

### 6.1 Transition to Fully Streaming DAQ with Hardware Trigger
**Proposed upgrade:** Eliminate hardware trigger thresholds entirely — implement **zero-suppression streaming DAQ** where all channels stream continuously at 250 MS/s, with online FPGA-based zero suppression and feature extraction.

- **Concrete technology:** ATCA-based DAQ (as in ATLAS Phase-II upgrade) with custom FPGA blades (Xilinx Ultrascale+ VU13P, 4M logic cells) per 64-channel readout crate
- Enables **sub-threshold coincidence analysis** — detecting events below individual crystal threshold by requiring correlated sub-threshold signals in multiple detectors
- **Impact:** Recovers ~5-10% of signal efficiency lost to threshold effects in current triggered system
