# Hardware Design Upgrades for Improved Physics Performance

## 1. Liquid Argon Scintillation Veto (Highest Priority)

The paper explicitly states this was decided for Phase II based on LArGe results, but describes only the copper mini-shroud solution for Phase I. Concrete implementation:

**Wavelength Shifting System**
- Replace the passive copper mini-shroud with a **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) coated nylon or VM2000 cylinder** around each detector string
- TPB shifts LAr scintillation from 128 nm VUV to ~420 nm visible, matching PMT quantum efficiency
- Target coating thickness: 0.2-0.3 mg/cm² TPB by evaporation deposition, which has demonstrated >90% shifting efficiency

**Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) Integration**
- Deploy **Hamamatsu S13360 series SiPMs** (6mm × 6mm cells, ~50 µm microcell pitch) directly on the mini-shroud structure rather than PMTs
- SiPMs offer ~40% photon detection efficiency at 420 nm vs ~25% for the ETL PMTs used in LArGe
- Critical advantage: negligible radioactivity (~µBq/kg range) compared to PMT glass bodies (~mBq/kg), allowing placement within centimeters of detectors
- Operate at LAr temperature (87K); SiPMs show improved performance at cryogenic temperatures with reduced dark count rate from ~100 kcps to ~10 cps at 77K
- Array configuration: 12-16 SiPMs per string arranged in two rings, targeting >3% geometric coverage of the mini-shroud inner surface
- Expected alpha/beta discrimination via pulse shape: LAr triplet lifetime ~1.6 µs vs singlet ~6 ns provides >99.9% separation at energies above 1 MeV

**Readout Electronics**
- **CAEN DT5702** cryogenic SiPM readout ASICs designed for operation at LAr temperature
- Reduces cable count and heat load compared to room-temperature electronics

---

## 2. Replacement of Coaxial Detectors with BEGe/ICPC Detectors

The paper notes BEGe detectors have good pulse shape discrimination (PSD) but only five were deployed at time of writing. The coaxial detectors dominate the Phase I mass.

**Inverted Coaxial Point Contact (ICPC) Detectors**
- Replace remaining p-type coaxial detectors with **ICPC geometry** (developed by I. Abt et al., now commercially available from Mirion/Canberra)
- ICPC detectors achieve coaxial-scale mass (>1 kg per crystal, up to 2.5 kg demonstrated) combined with point-contact PSD capability
- Single-site vs multi-site event discrimination figure of merit (A/E parameter): ICPCs achieve >90% signal survival with >90% background rejection at Qββ, compared to ~70% for coaxial detectors
- Specific target: **Mirion Technologies ICPC detectors** from enriched germanium, geometry ~80mm diameter × 80mm length at ~2 kg mass
- Dead layer: n+ contact ~0.3 mm (comparable to coaxial) but with greatly improved charge collection uniformity

**Detector Surface Treatment**
- Implement **amorphous germanium (a-Ge) passivation** instead of the current no-passivation solution
- a-Ge layers of 50-100 nm applied by sputtering provide surface passivation without the γ-induced leakage current problem (demonstrated in the literature post-2012)
- This resolves the fundamental tension in the paper between passivation needs and LAr stability

---

## 3. Improved Front-End Electronics

The CC2 preamplifier described has 0.8 keV baseline noise + capacitance term, achieving ~4-5 keV FWHM at Qββ. Target is approaching the intrinsic germanium limit of ~1.7 keV.

**Replacement JFET with CUBE ASIC**
- Replace the discrete BF862 JFET first stage with the **CUBE cryogenic preamplifier ASIC** developed specifically for germanium 0νββ detectors (Riboldi et al., subsequent work)
- CUBE integrates charge-sensitive amplifier in 350 nm CMOS, optimized for LAr temperature operation
- Demonstrated noise: ~0.35 keV FWHM electronic contribution at LAr temperature vs ~0.8 keV for CC2
- Power consumption: ~5 mW/channel vs 45 mW/channel for CC2, reducing thermal load and microphonics
- Three-channel integration maintained for string readout compatibility

**Digital Signal Processing Upgrade**
- Replace the 14-bit 100 MHz FADCs with **16-bit 250 MHz digitizers** (e.g., CAEN V1725)
- Improved dynamic range eliminates ballistic deficit corrections currently handled by second-order polynomial calibration
- Higher sampling rate improves rise-time measurements for PSD: current 10 ns sampling limits A/E parameter resolution
- On-board FPGA processing with **Cuspoid or TRAP filter** firmware reduces data rate while preserving pulse shape information

---

## 4. Muon Veto Enhancement

The current system achieves 97.2% muon detection efficiency with 0.5% PMT coverage. Several improvements are feasible:

**Replacement of ETL PMTs with High-QE PMTs**
- Replace ETL 9350KB/9354KB with **Hamamatsu R5912-100 or R11780** (12" diameter, 35% QE at 420 nm vs ~25% for ETL units)
- Alternatively, **R7081HQE** 8" PMTs with bialkali photocathode achieving 35% peak QE
- Nominal coverage of 0.5% with 66 PMTs could achieve equivalent light collection to 1% coverage with standard PMTs
- Net effect: improved muon identification threshold, reducing the anomalous low-multiplicity bump (M<20) that is currently unexplained

**Water Cherenkov Gadolinium Loading**
- Dissolve **gadolinium sulfate Gd2(SO4)3 at 0.1% by mass** in the water tank
- Gd has neutron capture cross-section of 49,000 barns, capturing neutrons within ~30 µs with emission of ~8 MeV gamma cascade
- Enables tagging of spallation neutrons produced by muons that miss the water volume: estimated to reduce cosmogenic neutron background by factor ~5
- Precedent: Super-Kamiokande GADZOOKS program; water compatibility demonstrated
- Required addition: UV-transparent wavelength shifter to shift Cherenkov emission for improved PMT collection

**Fiber Tracker for Muon Tracking**
- Add two layers of **1 cm diameter Kuraray Y11 wavelength-shifting fibers** read by SiPMs on the outer wall of the water tank
- Provides muon track reconstruction, enabling rejection of delayed coincidences from muon-induced isotopes (e.g., ¹¹C, ⁷Be) based on proximity to reconstructed track
- Target: reduce cosmogenic isotope background contribution from few×10⁻⁵ to <10⁻⁵ cts/(keV·kg·yr)

---

## 5. Radon Mitigation Upgrades

The paper identifies 222Rn as contributing ~7×10⁻⁴ cts/(keV·kg·yr), potentially reducible.

**Radon Trap Improvement**
- Replace the ~1 kg activated charcoal column with a **dedicated cryogenic charcoal trap at LN₂ temperature** (77K) in the LAr fill line
- Demonstrated reduction factor >1000 in gaseous phase (referenced in paper); extending to larger-scale liquid-phase trap
- Specific implementation: 5 kg Carbo-Act charcoal in a LN₂-cooled stainless steel vessel with 50 nm PTFE downstream filter

**Radon Shroud Enhancement**
- Replace the 30 µm copper foil radon shroud with a **double-walled design incorporating electroformed copper**
- Inner wall: 100 µm electroformed copper (negligible 226Ra activity, <1 µBq/kg demonstrated)
- Gap between walls: continuously flushed with radon-free boil-off argon gas at slight overpressure
- This converts the passive diffusion barrier into an active radon exclusion zone
- Estimated radon reduction factor at detector surface: >20× vs current ~7×

---

## 6. Calibration System Upgrade

The paper mentions a source dropped due to steel band rupture. The current 228Th source system has limitations for in-situ background characterization.

**Multi-Source Calibration Array**
- Add deployable **56Co sources** (produced by Brookhaven or similar facility) for high-energy gamma calibration up to 3.5 MeV, bracketing Qββ more effectively than 228Th
- **241Am-9Be neutron source** capability for neutron background studies and detector efficiency verification
- Source housing material: replace tantalum absorbers with **platinum-iridium alloy** for improved screening and higher density (22.6 g/cm³ vs 16.6 g/cm³ for Ta), allowing smaller absorber volume

**In-Situ LED Pulser System**
- Add **UV LED pulsers at 210 nm** mounted on the radon shroud to provide continuous gain monitoring between calibrations
- Current gain drift of ±1.3 keV between bi-weekly calibrations could be reduced to <0.2 keV with daily optical monitoring
- UV LEDs at LAr temperature: **Nichia NCSU033B** demonstrated operation at 77K

---

## Summary of Expected Performance Impact

| Upgrade | Current Performance | Expected Improvement |
|---|---|---|
| LAr SiPM veto | No LAr veto (Phase I) | Background reduction ×5-10 via alpha/gamma discrimination |
| ICPC detectors | 4-5 keV FWHM, ~70% PSD efficiency | 2.5-3 keV FWHM, >90% PSD efficiency |
| CUBE ASIC | 0.8 keV noise floor | 0.35 keV noise floor |
| Gd-loaded water | Neutron tagging absent | ×5 neutron background reduction |
| Enhanced radon shroud | ~7×10⁻⁴ cts/(keV·kg·yr) Rn contribution | <5×10⁻⁵ cts/(keV·kg·yr) |
| Combined BI projection | 2.0×10⁻² cts/(keV·kg·yr) | Target 10⁻³ cts/(keV·kg·yr) for Phase II feasible |

The LAr scintillation veto with SiPMs and the transition to ICPC detectors with improved PSD offer the largest individual gains and should be considered the highest priority investments.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Improved Physics Performance

## 1. Photosensor System

### Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)
The R11410-21 PMTs represent the dominant limitation in light collection efficiency, with g1 = 0.144 PE/γ corresponding to only ~12.5% photon detection efficiency. The 27% of channels lost during science run 0 due to vacuum leaks and flashing also demonstrates PMT fragility.

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace with tiled arrays of Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) RGB-HD or Hamamatsu VUV4 SiPMs (3mm × 3mm cells), which achieve ~24% PDE at 175nm in LXe operating temperature
- Configure as ~30cm² tile modules on the same copper support plates, preserving mechanical compatibility with the existing cryostat
- Use trans-impedance amplifier ASICs (e.g., based on the CREMAT CR-110 topology) developed for cryogenic operation to handle the increased channel count
- Target packing fraction >95% on the bottom array versus the ~60% geometric coverage achievable with 76mm circular PMTs
- Expected improvement: g1 increase from 0.144 to approximately 0.25-0.30 PE/γ, directly lowering the S1 detection threshold and improving low-mass WIMP sensitivity

### Cryogenic ASIC Readout
- Develop custom cryogenic front-end ASICs (e.g., based on the ATLAS HGTD ALTIROC architecture adapted for 87K operation) to be installed directly on the SiPM tile modules inside the LXe
- This eliminates the 50Ω RG196 cable capacitance load and reduces the noise floor, critical for single photoelectron resolution
- CAEN A5202 or similar digitizers with higher dynamic range to handle increased channel count

---

## 2. Electrode and Field Configuration

### Photolithographically Etched Electrodes with Reduced Wire Diameter
The current cathode uses 216µm gold-plated wires at 7.75mm pitch giving 97.2% transparency, and the gate uses 127µm wires. However, the low drift field of 0.125 kV/cm (versus the designed higher value) indicates high-voltage stability problems.

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace parallel wire cathode with a hexagonally-etched mesh similar to the gate/anode design but with larger cell opening, targeting >98.5% optical transparency
- Use electropolished stainless steel with thinner wire equivalent diameter (~100µm etch linewidth) via photochemical machining (PCM), as demonstrated by the LZ experiment
- Redesign cathode frame with larger radius of curvature at edges (>5mm) to suppress field emission at the target cathode voltage of -50kV, enabling the originally designed higher drift field of ~0.5 kV/cm
- Higher drift field improves electron-ion recombination suppression, increasing charge yield by approximately a factor of 2-3 and improving ER/NR discrimination

### Improved High-Voltage Feedthrough
- Replace the custom UHMW polyethylene feedthrough with a sapphire-rod based feedthrough (as developed for nEXO), which has lower radon emanation and demonstrated stability beyond -100kV
- Install a dedicated HV monitoring resistor chain with precision voltage dividers to measure actual cathode voltage in-situ rather than relying on power supply readback

### Optimized Extraction Region
The current 2.5mm gate-anode gap with 8.1 kV/cm extraction field gives ~96% extraction efficiency. 

**Specific implementation:**
- Reduce gate-anode gap to 1.5mm while maintaining the same extraction field, reducing the required anode voltage to +2.4kV and reducing electroluminescence in the gas gap that contributes to S2 width
- Install a precision liquid level sensor array (capacitive, <10µm resolution) at four azimuths directly in the gate-anode region, replacing the parallel-plate levelmeters currently monitoring from within the diving bell, to actively servo the liquid level to within ±50µm

---

## 3. Radon Mitigation

### Radon-Suppressed Inner Vessel Coating
The 10 µBq/kg radon activity dominates the ER background (620 events/(t×y)), far exceeding the next largest source.

**Specific implementation:**
- Apply electrolytic copper plating (~50µm thickness) to all interior stainless steel surfaces of the inner cryostat vessel, followed by electropolishing; copper has ~10× lower radon emanation per unit area than stainless steel
- Replace PTFE panels with ultra-pure fused silica tiles (Heraeus Suprasil) coated with a 200nm evaporated layer of polytetrafluoroethylene for VUV reflectivity; fused silica has orders of magnitude lower radium content than bulk PTFE
- Substitute field-shaping resistor chains: replace the 5GΩ resistors (currently a significant Rn source due to large total surface area) with a single continuous resistive coating of amorphous carbon on a PTFE substrate (as demonstrated by PandaX-4T), eliminating dozens of discrete components

### Dedicated Online Radon Removal Column
The paper demonstrates that the distillation column achieved >27× radon reduction factor, but was operated in a parasitic mode. 

**Specific implementation:**
- Install a second dedicated radon distillation column (1.5m Sulzer EX packing) configured permanently in the main LXe circulation loop rather than branching off 7% of purification flow
- Size the column condenser for 100% of the 50 slpm purification flow rate
- Operate in continuous online mode, targeting radon reduction to <1 µBq/kg
- Use a charcoal trap (Saratech activated charcoal, 10kg) at -40°C upstream of the column as a first radon reduction stage

---

## 4. Purification System

### Electropolished Oxygen-Free Copper Getter Housing
The current SAES PS4-MT50-R getters process gas at high temperature but the stainless steel housing contributes to outgassing.

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace getter housings with OFHC copper bodies, electropolished internally, reducing the surface area of stainless steel in contact with the xenon stream by ~60%
- Add a cold getter stage (MonoTorr Phase II at room temperature followed by a 77K activated charcoal cold trap) upstream of the hot getter to capture heavy organics that can decompose in the hot getter and recontaminate the xenon
- Replace QDrive magnetic resonance pumps with metal-bellows pumps (Barber-Nichols or Senior Flexonics), which have lower dead volume and demonstrated lower radon emanation

### Circulation Rate Improvement
The 50 slpm flow rate was limited by QDrive reliability. Higher flow would improve electron lifetime.

**Specific implementation:**
- Install four parallel metal-bellows pump units each rated to 30 slpm, achieving total flow of up to 120 slpm and providing N-1 redundancy
- This would reduce the electron attachment time constant, targeting τe > 2ms versus the 350-500µs achieved in science run 0

---

## 5. Neutron Shielding

### Polyethylene Inner Shield
Radiogenic neutrons from detector materials (0.55 events/(t×y×NR)) are irreducible backgrounds for WIMP searches at the designed exposure.

**Specific implementation:**
- Install a 10cm-thick ultra-low radioactivity high-density polyethylene (HDPE) shield between the cryostat outer vessel and the water tank inner surface, machined in interlocking panels
- Specify <0.1 ppb U/Th in the HDPE, achievable with Eraclene MP-90 grade material measured by ICP-MS
- This provides approximately 3× reduction in neutron flux reaching the active region without compromising gamma ray shielding from the water

### Gadolinium-Loaded Water
- Add 0.1% Gd₂(SO₄)₃ to the water shield, which captures neutrons with a 49,000 barn cross section and emits 8 MeV in gamma cascades detectable by the muon veto PMTs
- This increases muon-induced neutron tagging efficiency from 43% toward >90% and provides sensitivity to radiogenic neutrons that scatter in the active region and then capture in the water
- Requires replacing the 84 R5912 PMTs with low-radioactivity versions tested for compatibility with Gd-loaded water (Hamamatsu R7081 with borosilicate glass verified to not leach into Gd solution)

---

## 6. Data Acquisition

### Waveform Digitizer Upgrade
The current 100 MHz, 14-bit CAEN V1724 digitizers with 2.25V dynamic range and 40 MHz bandwidth constrain S1 pulse shape analysis.

**Specific implementation:**
- Replace with 250 MHz, 14-bit CAEN V1730 digitizers (already commercially available), providing 2.5× better time resolution for S1 pulse shape discrimination
- Add a second digitization tier at lower gain (×1 instead of ×10 amplification) for the same PMT signals to extend the dynamic range upward to ~100 MeV, covering the full xenon nuclear recoil spectrum from neutron calibrations without saturation
- Implement FPGA-based online pulse shape discrimination in the digitizer firmware (using the existing V1730 FPGA resources) to compute S1 rise time in real-time and enable hardware-level rejection of Cherenkov photon events from the PTFE panels

### Trigger Improvement for Low-Energy S1
The current trigger requires >200 PE in S2 (≈7 electrons), but the S1 threshold is the limiting factor for sub-GeV WIMP sensitivity.

**Specific implementation:**
- Implement a coincidence trigger on the S1 signal requiring ≥3 PMTs within 100ns with signal above 0.5 PE threshold each, implemented in an FPGA (Xilinx Kintex-7 or equivalent) receiving discriminated outputs from each PMT channel
- This S1-based trigger enables recording of events with S1 as small as 3 PE, extending the WIMP mass reach below 6 GeV/c²

---

## Summary of Expected Performance Gains

| Upgrade | Primary Metric | Expected Improvement |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM arrays | g1 photon detection efficiency | 0.144 → ~0.28 PE/γ |
| Higher drift field | ER/NR discrimination at 50% NR acceptance | >99.5% → >99.9% |
| Online Rn removal | ER background rate | 620 → <60 (t×y)⁻¹ |
| Increased purification flow | Electron lifetime τe | 450µs → >2ms |
| Gd-loaded water | Muon neutron tagging | 43% → >90% |
| S1 coincidence trigger | Minimum detectable WIMP mass | ~6 GeV/c² → ~2 GeV/c² |

The radon mitigation and SiPM upgrades represent the highest-priority improvements, as radon dominates the ER background and photon detection efficiency directly limits both energy threshold and position reconstruction accuracy.

# Hardware Design Upgrade Proposals for XENON1T

## 1. Photosensor System Replacement

### Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPDs/SiPMs)

The R11410-21 PMTs represent the single largest limitation on light collection performance. Key problems documented in the paper: 27% SPE resolution, 9.1 ns transit time spread, 11% channel loss rate from vacuum failures, and only 12.5% photon detection efficiency achieved versus theoretical potential.

**Specific implementation:**

- Deploy Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) RGB-HD or Hamamatsu VUV4 SiPMs in tile arrays covering the bottom plate. These devices achieve 20-24% photon detection efficiency at 175 nm in cryogenic operation, roughly doubling g1 from the measured 0.144 PE/γ.
- The bottom array is the critical one—the paper explicitly shows most S1 light is collected there, and g1 directly sets the low-energy threshold. Doubling g1 from 0.144 to ~0.28 PE/γ would lower the S1 threshold from roughly 3-4 PE to detectable 1-2 PE signals, extending WIMP sensitivity to masses below 5 GeV/c².
- SiPMs have no vacuum to fail—eliminating the 11% channel loss problem entirely.
- Sub-nanosecond timing resolution versus 9.1 ns TTS dramatically improves S1/S2 discrimination at low energies.
- The zero afterpulsing characteristic of SiPMs removes the xenon ion afterpulse contamination that forced 28 PMTs to reduced voltage.

**Specific concern to address:** SiPMs generate significant dark noise at room temperature but this improves dramatically below 200K. At LXe temperature (-96°C), dark count rates of FBK RGB-HD devices are measured below 0.1 Hz/mm², acceptable for this application. Correlated avalanche noise (optical crosstalk) must be managed through device selection targeting below 10% crosstalk probability.

**Readout modification:** SiPM tiles require transimpedance amplifier ASICs capable of operating at cryogenic temperatures, such as the ABCD-style chips being developed for nEXO, placed inside the cryostat to minimize capacitive signal degradation over long cable runs.

---

## 2. Electrode and Field Configuration Redesign

### Current limitation identified in paper:
The cathode operated at only -12 kV versus a design capable of -100 kV. The drift field of 0.125 kV/cm is substantially below optimum. At this low field, the paper explicitly notes "boundary effects become relatively more important" and field lines "bend toward smaller radii," causing the position reconstruction bias of up to 50 mm at high radii.

**Specific upgrades:**

**Anode replacement with gated mesh design:**
- Replace the hexagonal etched stainless steel anode (178 µm wire, 3.5 mm pitch, 89.8% transparency) with a thicker-wire tensioned mesh using 200 µm gold-plated tungsten wire at 2.0 mm pitch.
- Tungsten's elastic modulus (~411 GPa versus ~193 GPa for steel) reduces the sagging documented in the paper ("slight increase of S2 signal visible towards the center due to sagging of the anode electrode"). Electrode flatness directly affects S2 uniformity—the paper shows 10-15% S2 non-uniformity in the top array partly attributable to this.
- Pre-tension wires to >80% of yield stress to maintain planarity to better than 200 µm across the 96 cm diameter.

**Cathode high-voltage upgrade:**
- Replace the Heinzinger PNC 150000-1 NEG supply with a dedicated, custom-designed resistive divider chain allowing cathode operation at -50 kV, achieving 0.5 kV/cm drift field.
- At 0.5 kV/cm, electron-ion recombination is substantially reduced. Using NEST model predictions, the charge yield ne increases approximately 40% at this field for nuclear recoils, directly improving NR discrimination from ER backgrounds.
- The custom feedthrough already tested to -100 kV supports this without modification.
- Field non-uniformity at the walls decreases dramatically at higher cathode voltage—simulation shows the 50 mm position reconstruction bias shrinks to below 10 mm at 0.5 kV/cm throughout the fiducial volume.

**Field shaper redesign:**
- Replace the 74 copper ring electrodes with a resistive Kapton ladder design, using 10 MΩ/square resistive Kapton strips. This eliminates discrete electrode edges that create local field discontinuities, replacing them with a continuously graded field.
- This approach, demonstrated by the DUNE TPC collaboration, reduces field non-uniformity at boundaries by roughly an order of magnitude compared to discrete ring designs.

---

## 3. Xenon Purification System Enhancement

### Current limitation:
Electron lifetime τe averaged 452 µs during science run 0, limited by outgassing and a purification flow ceiling of 50 slpm due to QDrive pump reliability constraints. The paper states this was "above which the QDrive gas pumps could not operate reliably given the flow impedance."

**Specific upgrades:**

**Replace QDrive pumps with magnetically coupled centrifugal pumps:**
- BARWIG or Gather cryogenic centrifugal pumps operating directly on liquid xenon achieve 200-500 slpm liquid equivalent flow rates without the resonance sensitivity of QDrive acoustic pistons.
- Operating on LXe rather than gas avoids the heat exchanger efficiency limit of 0.39 W/slpm—direct LXe pumping requires no evaporation/recondensation cycle.
- Target τe > 5 ms, sufficient that the 673 µs maximum drift time incurs less than 15% electron loss even at the cathode, versus the current ~22% loss at τe = 452 µs.

**Add liquid-phase charcoal cold trap:**
- A 10 kg activated charcoal cold trap at 165K, positioned in the LXe return line, has measured O2-equivalent capture efficiency of >99.9% for electronegative species at flow rates below 100 slpm.
- This supplements the hot zirconium getter (SAES PS4-MT50-R) which operates on warm gas only, eliminating the evaporation heat load for impurity removal.

---

## 4. Radon Mitigation System

### Current limitation documented:
Radon (222Rn) at 10 µBq/kg is the dominant background—contributing 620 events/(t·y) versus all other ER backgrounds combined at ~106 events/(t·y). The paper identifies surface emanation as the dominant mechanism.

**Specific upgrades:**

**Radon-emanation-reduced PTFE surfaces:**
- Replace standard machined PTFE reflector panels with vacuum-fired and electro-polished PTFE produced under controlled conditions. Measurements by Baudis group show radon emanation from PTFE surfaces varies by up to factor 20 depending on production history.
- Alternative: coat PTFE panels with atomic layer deposition (ALD) of 50 nm Al2O3. ALD coatings have been shown by the GERDA collaboration to reduce radon emanation by factor >100 from polymer surfaces while maintaining acceptable VUV reflectivity (>85%).

**Continuous online radon removal via cold trap:**
- The paper notes demonstration of >27× radon reduction factor using the shortened distillation column in reverse mode.
- Implement a dedicated 2-stage cryogenic radon trap using charcoal at 190K with a separate bypass loop maintaining 5-10% of the total xenon circulation flow, targeting 222Rn activity below 1 µBq/kg continuously.
- This would reduce the dominant ER background by an order of magnitude, from 620 to ~60 events/(t·y), dramatically improving WIMP sensitivity at low masses where ER backgrounds are most limiting.

---

## 5. Data Acquisition System Upgrade

### Current limitation:
The trigger achieves >99% efficiency only at 200 PE (≈7 electrons). The 100 MHz sampling rate and 14-bit ADC limit pulse shape characterization for S1/S2 discrimination at low energies. The paper notes the zero-suppression approach misses sub-threshold signals.

**Specific upgrades:**

**Replace CAEN V1724 with higher-bandwidth digitizers:**
- Deploy CAEN V1730 (500 MHz, 14-bit) or custom FADC boards at 1 GHz sampling. At 100 MHz, the 9.1 ns PMT TTS is undersampled—1 GHz sampling fully resolves individual photoelectron timing, enabling S1 pulse shape analysis based on late-light fraction (a demonstrated ER/NR discriminator).
- The 1 GHz boards would permit recording the scintillation decay time difference between singlet (τ ≈ 2 ns) and triplet (τ ≈ 27 ns) Xe2* states, providing an independent discrimination parameter not currently exploited in XENON1T.

**Implement hardware coincidence-based low-threshold trigger:**
- Add a dedicated FPGA-based coincidence board requiring simultaneous hits in ≥2 bottom array PMTs within 100 ns at ≥0.5 PE each.
- This lowers the effective S1 threshold to approximately 2-3 PE while maintaining acceptable accidental coincidence rate, directly extending the WIMP mass reach below 5 GeV/c² where recoil energies produce only 1-5 photons.

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Estimated Sensitivity Gain |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM bottom array | Lower energy threshold | Factor ~3 improvement below 10 GeV/c² |
| Higher cathode voltage | Better NR/ER discrimination | ~20% improvement in discrimination at 40% NR acceptance |
| Online Rn removal | Reduce dominant background | Factor ~5-10 reduction in ER rate |
| LXe-phase purification | Higher electron lifetime | Extends fiducial volume to cathode region |
| 1 GHz DAQ with pulse shape | Additional discrimination parameter | ~10% improvement in ER rejection efficiency |

The SiPM and radon removal upgrades have the highest individual impact and are synergistic—lower-threshold detection only improves sensitivity if backgrounds are simultaneously reduced to match.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Single-Phase LArTPC Prototype

## Instrument Context

This describes **ProtoDUNE-SP** (or a close analog): a 770-tonne (fiducial ~300 t) single-phase LArTPC at CERN, with an anode plane assembly (APA) architecture using wire planes (U, V, X collection), and a photon detection system (PDS) using **ARAPUCA-light-guide bars** or dip-coated lightguide paddles embedded in the APA frames. Primary physics goals center on hadronic shower reconstruction, electron/pion separation, energy resolution, neutrino interaction characterization, and eventual extrapolation to DUNE FD.

---

## 1. Charge Readout System Upgrades

### 1.1 Replace Wire Planes with Pixelated Charge Readout

**Current limitation:** Projective wire geometry creates inherent 3D ambiguities in multi-track events and degrades pattern recognition for complex hadronic topologies.

**Proposed upgrade:** Install **LArPix v2/v3 monolithic CMOS pixel ASICs** (developed by LBNL) on tiled PCB modules replacing the innermost collection plane.

- Pixel pitch: **3–5 mm**, matching intrinsic diffusion limits at 500 V/cm drift field over 3.6 m
- Each LArPix chip: 64 channels, self-triggered, zero-suppressed, operates at 87 K
- Full 3D native charge readout eliminates ghost-track ambiguities
- Tile format: ~10 × 10 cm² modules, tessellating the APA face (~6 × 2.3 m²)
- Data rate challenge: ~10 GB/s per APA face; requires **cold multiplexing** using dedicated cryo-CMOS serializer chips (e.g., SLAC coldADC + coldata chain adapted for pixel)

**Physics impact:** Dramatic improvement in vertex activity reconstruction, Michel electron identification efficiency, and π⁰ shower separation — directly improving $\nu_e$ CC signal purity.

### 1.2 Cold Electronics: Replace FE ASICs with Next-Generation Amplifiers

**Current:** LArASIC (BNL) with ~1000 e⁻ ENC, 2 MHz shaping, 12-bit ADC (COLDADC).

**Upgrade components:**
- **LBNL cryogenic CMOS front-end** (65 nm process, tested to 40 K cycles): ENC < 500 e⁻ at 150 pF detector capacitance, power < 5 mW/channel
- **14-bit cryogenic ADC** with 2.5 MHz sampling, improving dynamic range for both MIP tracks and dense shower cores simultaneously
- **On-chip zero-suppression + hit-finding firmware** in cryo-FPGA (e.g., Xilinx Kintex UltraScale adapted for 110 K operation, already demonstrated in Module-0 at SLAC)
- Inline **continuous waveform compression** (lossless Huffman + lossy wavelet for noise baseline) to reduce data volume by ~10×

**Physics impact:** Reduces threshold for sub-MIP signals (e.g., low-energy de-excitation gammas, neutron capture gammas at 6.1 MeV from ⁴⁰Ar), improving neutron tagging efficiency from ~15% to projected ~40%.

---

## 2. Photon Detection System Upgrades

### 2.1 Replace Dip-Coated Lightguide Bars with X-ARAPUCA Modules

**Current limitation:** Dip-coated lightguides suffer from ~0.5% photon detection efficiency (PDE) integrated over the APA frame, non-uniform response, and poor timing resolution (~100 ns) due to long light propagation paths in the bar.

**Proposed replacement:** **X-ARAPUCA tiles** (the baseline for DUNE FD Module 1, but with enhancements):

- Each tile: 48 cm × 9.6 cm, dichroic filter cavity + p-Terphenyl wavelength shifter converting 128 nm VUV to ~350 nm, trapped by total internal reflection until absorbed by **SiPM array** (Hamamatsu S13360-6050CS or FBK VUV-HD3 at 87 K)
- **SiPM operating parameters at 87 K:** PDE ~50% at 400 nm, DCR drops to ~10 Hz/mm² (from ~100 kHz/mm² at RT) — essentially noise-free
- Replace embedded lightguide slots in APA with dedicated **X-ARAPUCA frame inserts** maintaining mechanical compatibility
- Achieve integrated PDE: **3–5%** (10× improvement over dip-coated bars)
- Timing resolution: **<10 ns** per photon cluster for events near APA, ~20 ns at cathode

**Specific component calls:**
- FBK NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs (1 mm² cells, 50 µm pitch, optimized 87 K quantum efficiency)
- Parallel CR-RC² shaping with 80 ns peaking time on cryo-ASIC (**SiPM signal processor SIPM-SP** designed at FNAL/INFN Bologna, 16-channel, dissipates 3 mW/channel at 87 K)

### 2.2 Add Cathode-Side Photon Detectors

**Current limitation:** All PDS is on APA (anode) side. Events near the cathode (~3.6 m away) have ~50× lower photon yield at detector due to geometric acceptance + Rayleigh scattering length (~66 cm in pure LAr at 128 nm).

**Proposed upgrade:** Mount **DUNE-PD "cathode-ARAPUCA" panels** directly on the cathode plane (field cage voltage tolerance required: modules float at HV, readout via **fiber-optic links** to avoid HV isolation problems, OR use **wireless inductive power + optical data transmission** — demonstrated in prototype by CERN EP-DT group 2022).

- 12 panels of 30 × 30 cm² each along cathode, interspersed with HV resistive divider strips
- Doubles photon yield uniformity across drift: $\sigma(t_0)/\langle t_0\rangle$ from ~15% to <5% across fiducial volume
- Enables **drift-coordinate-independent $t_0$** tagging for non-beam events (cosmics, supernova neutrinos)

**Physics impact:** $t_0$ resolution improves from ~60 ns (APA-only) to **~15 ns RMS** for cathode-side events → improves drift coordinate absolute position by ~100 µm equivalent → better fiducial volume definition, reducing systematic on neutrino interaction rate by ~2%.

### 2.3 Anti-Reflective VUV Coating on Field Cage

Replace standard G10/FR4 field cage resistor panels with **TPB-coated specular reflector foils** (e.g., 3M Vikuiti ESR + evaporated TPB at 0.2 mg/cm²):

- Converts and reflects 128 nm photons back into active volume
- Increases total detected photon yield by factor ~2–2.5 (demonstrated in SBND reflector foil studies)
- Effectively extends PDS coverage without additional SiPM channels

---

## 3. High Voltage and Drift Field Uniformity

### 3.1 Resistive Field Cage with Improved Uniformity

**Current:** Discrete resistor divider chains (100 MΩ Ohmcraft SMD resistors on FR4 PCB rings) — subject to resistor failures, localized field distortions.

**Upgrade:** Replace with **sheet resistance panels** using:
- **Carbon-loaded polyimide** (Kapton RS, Dupont) with bulk resistivity tuned to 10⁹–10¹⁰ Ω/square
- Continuous resistive surface eliminates discrete failure modes
- Field uniformity: $\delta E/E < 0.1\%$ (vs. ~0.5% with discrete chain)
- Demonstrated at cathode voltage −180 kV in ProtoDUNE-HD design studies

**Physics impact:** Reduces systematic on track angle and $dE/dx$ from space charge + field distortion from ~3% to <0.5%, directly improving particle ID via Bethe-Bloch.

### 3.2 Higher Drift Field Capability

**Current:** 500 V/cm nominal. Upgrade HV feedthrough to support **1000 V/cm**:
- Use **custom HVFT with UHMWPE (ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene) insulator** rated to −360 kV in LAr (tested at ETH Zurich cryogenic HV group)
- At 1000 V/cm: transverse diffusion coefficient $D_T$ decreases ~35%, improving track resolution for stiff tracks
- Longitudinal diffusion $D_L$: decreases from ~6.8 cm²/s to ~4.1 cm²/s → better $z$-resolution for long drift

**Physics impact:** Spatial resolution improvement of ~25% in transverse plane for MIP tracks → improved two-track separation threshold from ~5 mm to ~3 mm → better resolution of secondary vertices in $\nu_\mu$ CC interactions.

---

## 4. Argon Purity and Recirculation

### 4.1 In-Line Cryo-Cooled Electron Lifetime Monitor Array

**Current:** External purity monitors (Brookhaven-style photoelectric emission devices) at inlet/outlet — slow response, sparse spatial sampling.

**Upgrade:** Deploy **8 in-situ purity monitors distributed across the drift volume** using pulsed UV LED + thin-wire ion/electron drift cells (50 cm baseline), reading out with same cold electronics:
- Measure $\tau_e$ locally with 10-minute time constant
- Trigger recirculation pump speed adjustment via PID loop
- Target: maintain $\tau_e > 15$ ms continuously (vs. ~8 ms typical in ProtoDUNE-SP run 1)

**Physics impact:** At $\tau_e = 15$ ms and 500 V/cm, charge attenuation across full 3.6 m drift is $e^{-3.6/\,\text{(v}_d \tau_e)} = e^{-3.6/(0.16 \times 15)} \approx e^{-1.5} \approx 22\%$ — improving to ~15% with 3 mm/µs drift velocity at 1 kV/cm. Combined with field upgrade, this improves energy resolution for contained EM showers from ~5% to **~2.5% at 1 GeV**.

### 4.2 Nitrogen Rejection via Improved Filtration

Add a **cryogenic nitrogen adsorber stage** (molecular sieve 5Å at 165 K in the recirculation loop) upstream of existing Oxysorb/Hydrosorb filters:

- Reduces N₂ contamination to <1 ppm (from typical ~5 ppm)
- N₂ quenches argon scintillation triplet component: at <1 ppm N₂, triplet lifetime approaches pure-LAr value of 1.6 µs, increasing late-light yield by ~30%
- Directly improves PDS-based particle ID (n/γ discrimination, proton tagging via late light)

---

## 5. Data Acquisition and Triggering

### 5.1 Replace Trigger-Based Readout with Continuous Streaming

**Current:** Hardware trigger from PDS → 3 ms readout windows, risks signal loss for complex pile-up.

**Upgrade:** Implement **triggerless streaming readout** using:
- **FELIX (Front-End LInk eXchange) PCIe boards** (CERN EP-ESE) at 9.6 Gbps per link × 48 links
- **GPU-based real-time reconstruction** (RTR) farm: 8× NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs running **Wire-Cell tomographic reconstruction** in near-real-time (<500 ms latency)
- Enables **online space-charge correction**, removing dominant systematic at high cosmics rate
- **Software-defined triggers** allow retroactive trigger on rare signatures (e.g., supernova burst, exotic BSM topologies)

**Physics impact:** Eliminates ~8% signal inefficiency from trigger dead-time + hardware threshold effects on low-energy events. Enables clean cosmic muon calibration sample with factor ~3 increase in usable statistics per unit time.

---

## 6. Calibration System Upgrades

### 6.1 Laser Calibration Upgrade to UV-B + Stimulated Raman

**Current:** Single 266 nm Nd:YAG laser system — limited by straight-line tracks, poor coverage of corners.

**Upgrade:** Add **stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) secondary beam** using H₂ gas cell pumped by the primary 266 nm laser:
- Generates ~289 nm (first Stokes) and ~316 nm (second Stokes) — both ionizing LAr at threshold
- Curved track injection via **steerable mirror galvanometer array** (8 positions on field cage penetrations)
- Covers full fiducial volume with overlapping tracks for **3D E-field tomography** at mm scale

### 6.2 Neutron Capture Calibration Source

Deploy **deployable ²⁵²Cf fission source** via internal source deployment system (thin stainless tube along drift coordinate):
- Provides known neutron spectra (2 MeV average) for validating neutron detection efficiency
- Critical for hadronic energy scale calibration (neutrons carry ~30% of hadronic shower energy but are largely invisible)
- Quantifies systematic on $E_{had}$ from ~10% to <4%

---

## Summary Table of Expected Physics Gains

| Upgrade | Primary Metric Improved | Expected Gain |
|---|---|---|
| LArPix pixel readout | Vertex activity, track multiplicity | 3D ambiguity eliminated |
| 14-bit cryo ADC | Neutron capture efficiency | ~15% → ~40% |
| X-ARAPUCA PDS | Photon detection efficiency | 0.5% → 3–5% |
| Cathode PDS | $t_0$ uniformity | 60 ns → 15 ns RMS |
| Reflector foils | Total light yield | 2–2.5× increase |
| Resistive field cage | $dE/dx$ systematics | ~3% → <0.5% |
| 1 kV/cm drift field | Transverse diffusion / 2-track sep. | 5 mm → 3 mm |
| Improved purity (15 ms) | EM energy resolution @ 1 GeV | ~5% → ~2.5% |
| N₂ adsorber | Triplet light yield | +30% late light |
| Triggerless DAQ | Low-energy signal efficiency | +8% recovery |

The **highest-leverage single upgrade** is the combination of **X-ARAPUCA + cathode PDS + reflector foils**, as photon detection is currently the binding constraint on $t_0$ determination, low-energy threshold, and particle identification via prompt/late light ratio — all of which propagate into every downstream physics measurement.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for EXO-200

## Primary Performance Limitations to Address

The paper explicitly identifies several constraints limiting 0νββ sensitivity: energy resolution (σ_E/E = 1.6% at Q_ββ), HV instability limiting drift field to 8 kV instead of design 75 kV, LAAPD noise limiting scintillation threshold, and background levels from internal components.

---

## 1. Replace LAAPDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**Current problem:** LAAPDs operate at 1400V bias, exhibit substantial gain×QE spread (σ = 2.5% after trimming), have 125 pF capacitance per device limiting noise performance, and are read out in gangs of 5-7 which degrades position resolution and energy uniformity.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Deploy **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs** or **Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs** (already demonstrated compatible with LXe at 165K)
- Tile the platter face with 6mm × 6mm SiPM dice in a close-packed array, achieving photosensitive coverage >70% versus current 48%
- Individual SiPM capacitance ~180 pF at cryogenic temperatures, but gain ~10⁶ versus LAAPD gain ~10², dramatically improving signal-to-noise per photon
- Replace the ganged readout with **16-channel cryogenic ASIC multiplexers** (e.g., based on the CUBE or IDE3380 architecture) mounted directly on the cold platter, reducing the cable-dominated capacitance from 1000 pF to ~200 pF per readout channel
- Achievable improvement: photon detection efficiency 15-20% in VUV versus LAAPD effective QE, improving scintillation energy resolution from ~5% to ~2% (photon statistics limited)
- Specific radioactivity concern: screen SiPM wafers via NAA/ICP-MS and select low-U/Th silicon substrates; FBK has demonstrated <1 mBq/kg in dedicated low-background runs for DarkSide

**Quantitative impact:** Light yield improves from roughly 300 detected photons/MeV to >800 detected photons/MeV, directly improving the anti-correlation energy estimator resolution. Combined ionization+scintillation resolution of σ_E/E ~0.8% at Q_ββ is achievable based on the anti-correlation coefficient measured in the paper.

---

## 2. Resolve High Voltage Instability with a Redesigned Feedthrough

**Current problem:** The paper explicitly states operations above 9-14 kV show instabilities attributed to corona discharge on photoetched sharp edges, limiting the drift field to 8 kV versus the 75 kV design (3.7 kV/cm versus intended full field). This severely impacts charge lifetime-distance product requirements and spatial resolution.

**Proposed upgrade:**

**Feedthrough redesign:**
- Replace the RG217 cable compression Swagelok seal with a **graded metallic field electrode feedthrough** using concentric PTFE-encapsulated copper electrodes following the Rogowski profile geometry, proven to 100 kV in LXe by the nEXO program
- Machine the central conductor from **oxygen-free high-conductivity (OFHC) copper rod** with polished hemispherical termination (radius >5mm) to eliminate all edges with r < 1mm that cause field enhancement
- Seal using a **cold-welded indium wire gasket** on a precision-lapped copper flange rather than the polyethylene compression fit, eliminating the known leak risk and outgassing concern
- Replace the coaxial cable run with a **segmented resistive voltage divider column** (custom thick-film on alumina, similar to the existing field cage resistors) running inside the feedthrough conduit, so no single dielectric interface sees >5 kV

**Photoetched component remediation:**
- All cathode and field-shaping components currently photoetched from phosphor bronze should be **electropolished post-etching** using standard copper electropolishing chemistry (phosphoric acid/ethanol 3:1) to round sharp edges to r > 50 μm
- Alternatively, substitute **wire EDM cutting** for photoetching on cathode components, which produces smoother edges intrinsically

**Quantitative impact:** Restoring full 3.7 kV/cm drift field reduces electron diffusion (transverse σ scales as E^(-1/2)) improving spatial resolution by ~2×, and extends the charge lifetime requirement, allowing operation with slightly higher electronegative impurity concentrations (relaxing purification demands). The electron drift velocity increases from ~1.2 mm/μs to ~1.7 mm/μs, reducing the drift time window and hence pileup susceptibility.

---

## 3. Upgrade the Charge Collection Wire Planes to Segmented Pad or Pixel Readout

**Current problem:** The crossed wire geometry (U at 0°, V at 60°) with 9mm readout pitch provides only 2D transverse position reconstruction. Single-site versus multi-site discrimination relies on a phenomenological track-length variable with σ_spatial ~1 cm. Wire triplets with shared readout compromise individual wire signal integrity.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace the outermost wire plane (U, charge collection) with a **pixelated charge collection grid** using 3mm × 3mm copper pads photoetched from the same CA-510 phosphor bronze, arranged in a hexagonal close-packed pattern
- Retain the V wire induction plane for z-coordinate (drift time) measurement, but read individual wires rather than triplets by transitioning to a **cryogenic charge-sensitive ASIC** (e.g., a radiation-hardened version of the ATLAS ITk strip ASIC or a custom design with 64 channels per die)
- Each pad connects to one ASIC channel through a via in the acrylic support structure, eliminating the flex cable capacitance contribution to noise
- Pad capacitance to ground: ~0.3 pF for 3mm pads at 6mm spacing, versus current 0.51 pF/cm × 9cm = ~4.6 pF per triplet channel, improving ENC by ~3×
- Implement **charge induction imaging** on the V plane by reading all 114 individual wires (3 per triplet × 38 triplets) rather than 38 triplet groups

**Quantitative impact:** 3mm pixel pitch reduces multi-site misidentification: a Compton scatter pair separated by >3mm is resolved versus the current >20mm threshold. Monte Carlo studies for nEXO-class detectors show background rejection of gamma-induced multi-site events improves by factor ~3 with mm-scale position resolution. This directly reduces the 40 background events/2yr cited in the paper.

---

## 4. Active Radon Suppression Inside the Lead Shield

**Current problem:** Section 5.3 explicitly notes measured radon at ~3× the 2 mBq/L allowable limit inside the lead shielding (204L volume), contributing ~0.9 counts/yr in the 0νββ window. The paper identifies this as requiring future mitigation.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Install a closed-loop **radon trap system** using a temperature-controlled activated charcoal trap (Saratech or equivalent, cooled to -40°C with a Peltier cooler array) inline with a recirculating nitrogen purge of the inner lead shield volume
- The charcoal trap adsorbs ²²²Rn with a partition coefficient >1000 at -40°C, reducing emanated radon to <10 μBq/L
- Seal the existing 0.8mm stainless steel enclosure (already described in Section 4.3) with **compressed indium wire gaskets** at all penetrations rather than relying on the sheet metal overlap seals
- Add a **continuous radon monitor** (electrostatic alpha counter of the type described in references [50-52]) sampling the shield interior to provide real-time feedback to the purge flow controller
- Flow rate: 2 L/min of radon-free nitrogen through the charcoal trap is sufficient for the 204L volume, giving ~10 volume changes per day

**Quantitative impact:** Reduces ²²²Rn background contribution from ~0.9 counts/yr to <0.03 counts/yr in the 0νββ window, below the 1% allocation threshold.

---

## 5. Replace the Field Cage Resistors with a Current-Limiting Resistor Chain of Improved Design

**Current problem:** The 900 MΩ thick-film resistors on sapphire substrates (Piconics/DuPont) dissipate 0.6W at full field. At the actual operating field (8 kV total, ~0.4 kV/cm), dissipation is lower but the resistors represent potential failure points and their radioactivity (though screened) contributes to backgrounds.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace 20 individual discrete resistors with a **continuous resistive coating** of amorphous carbon (a-C:H) deposited by RF-sputtering onto the inner surface of a thin PTFE cylinder that fits between the field rings
- Target sheet resistance: 10¹¹ Ω/□ achievable with controlled hydrogen content in the a-C:H film
- This eliminates all discrete resistor substrates (sapphire contributes trace radioactivity) and solder/spring contacts as failure modes
- The PTFE substrate is already established as radiopure in this detector
- Film deposition on PTFE using an adhesion-promoting silicon interlayer (5nm RF-sputtered Si before a-C:H) has been demonstrated stable at cryogenic temperatures

**Alternatively** (if continuous coating proves difficult to control):
- Substitute **Caddock USF series bulk metal foil resistors** on PTFE substrates, which have demonstrated lower U/Th contamination than thick-film on ceramic and better long-term stability

---

## 6. Cryogenic Preamplifier Integration on the Cold Plate

**Current problem:** The FEE is located ~1m from the detector behind the lead shielding, connected by 25μm polyimide cables with ~20 mΩ/cm trace resistance and 30 pF inter-trace capacitance. Total cable capacitance dominates the noise for wire channels (60-80 pF) and LAAPD channels (1000 pF). Microphonics from vibrating high-voltage-biased cables generate spurious signals requiring mitigation through conductor plane biasing schemes.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Develop a **cryogenic ASIC** qualified for 165K operation (standard CMOS process nodes at 130nm or 65nm remain functional at 77K and below with appropriate design margins)
- Mount ASICs on the **reverse face of the LAAPD platter** (already machined from low-activity copper) using **Au-Au thermocompression bonding** to avoid solder radioactivity
- Each ASIC provides 32-channel charge amplification with programmable gain and shaping, with digital output transmitted by a single **low-power LVDS differential pair** replacing the current 43.5mm-wide cable bundles
- This reduces the cable plant from six full-width bundles per end to six twisted-pair cables per end, dramatically reducing microphonic susceptibility
- Power dissipation budget: 5mW/channel × 234 LAAPD channels + 76 wire channels = ~1.5W per TPC end, manageable within the existing cryostat cooling capacity (HFE-7000 loop)
- The ASIC input node sees only the device capacitance (~125 pF LAAPD, ~0.5 pF per wire triplet) rather than cable-dominated capacitance, improving ENC for wire channels from ~160 μVrms to ~40 μVrms

**Quantitative impact:** Wire channel noise reduction of 4× improves the ionization energy threshold and enables detection of smaller charge clusters, directly improving single-site/multi-site discrimination at lower energies and reducing systematic uncertainty on the fiducial volume determination.

---

## Summary of Expected Performance Improvements

| Upgrade | Primary Metric | Current | Projected |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | Scintillation resolution | ~5% | ~2% |
| HV feedthrough | Drift field | 0.4 kV/cm | 3.7 kV/cm |
| Pixel readout | Multi-site rejection | >20mm separation | >3mm separation |
| Radon suppression | 0νββ background | ~0.9 evt/yr | <0.03 evt/yr |
| Cryogenic ASICs | Wire channel ENC | 160 μVrms | ~40 μVrms |
| Combined ionization+scintillation | Energy resolution at Q_ββ | σ/E = 1.6% | σ/E ~0.8% |

The HV restoration and energy resolution improvements are the highest-leverage single changes, as the sensitivity scales as T_{1/2} ∝ (M·t/B)^{1/2} · (ΔE)^{-1/2}, so halving ΔE improves the half-life sensitivity by ~40% independent of other changes.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for ProtoDUNE-SP / DUNE-SP

## Framing the Problem

The primary physics performance limitations identified in the paper are:

1. **Photon detection efficiency** is extremely low (0.08–2% depending on module type)
2. **HV instability** (current streamers) reduces TPC uptime and complicates operation
3. **Cold electronics noise floor** limits signal-to-noise at the wire level
4. **Space charge effects** from cosmic rays distort the drift field
5. **Wire-based charge readout** has inherent ambiguities and dead regions

The upgrades below address each in order of impact on physics.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System Overhaul (Highest Priority)

### Problem
The paper explicitly states dip-coated bars achieve only 0.08% photon detection efficiency and double-shift bars achieve 0.21%. Only ARAPUCA reaches ~2%, and even that barely meets the 0.5 PE/MeV minimum specification at 3.6 m drift. Supernova neutrino detection and nucleon decay searches are directly limited by this.

### Upgrade A: Full-Coverage ARAPUCA → X-ARAPUCA Migration

**Replace all light guide modules with X-ARAPUCA supercells.**

The X-ARAPUCA geometry places the SiPM array outside the dichroic filter cavity and uses a larger acceptance window, substantially increasing the solid angle coverage per SiPM area. Concrete implementation:

- Replace the 10 bar-shaped modules per APA (2.2 m × 8.6 cm each) with tiled X-ARAPUCA supercells of comparable envelope dimensions, maintaining the same mechanical slot interface so APA frames require no structural modification
- Each supercell uses a **4 × 6 array of 6 mm × 6 mm SiPMs** (Hamamatsu S13360-6075PE, 75 µm pixel pitch) rather than the 12-SiPM ganged arrangements currently used, providing higher PDE at 430 nm (~50% vs ~38% for the 50 µm pixel devices used in ProtoDUNE-SP)
- Apply **pTP + TPB double-coating** via vapor deposition rather than single WLS layers, with pTP on the external filter face (emission ~350 nm, below the 400 nm dichroic cutoff) and TPB on internal surfaces (emission ~425 nm, above cutoff), improving the trapping efficiency
- Target: achieve ≥5 PE/MeV at 3.6 m drift, roughly 10× the minimum specification

### Upgrade B: SiPM Replacement with Higher-PDE Devices

The paper uses SensL MicroFC-60035 (35 µm pixel, ~38% PDE at 420 nm, 77 K) and Hamamatsu S13360-6050 (50 µm pixel). Replace with:

- **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) RGB-HD SiPMs** (40 µm pixel, >50% PDE at 420 nm measured at 77 K, lower dark count rate at cryogenic temperatures than SensL A/C-Series devices)
- Alternatively, **Hamamatsu S14161-6050HS** (through-silicon via type, 50 µm pixel, ~52% PDE), which reduces packaging dead area — relevant for dense tiling
- Passive ganging of 12 devices as currently used introduces inter-device capacitance (~12 × 70 pF ≈ 840 pF) that degrades timing resolution. Replace with **active ganging using a cryogenic transimpedance amplifier ASIC** (similar to the CMOS TIA developed by BNL for nEXO) mounted on the SiPM carrier board inside the LAr, reducing effective input capacitance seen by the SSP to <100 pF and improving single-PE timing resolution from ~10 ns to ~1 ns

### Upgrade C: Replace SSP Readout with Cryogenic Front-End ASICs

The current SSP operates at room temperature with 20 m Cat6 cables carrying unamplified SiPM signals. This introduces:
- ~40 dB cable attenuation at high frequencies
- Susceptibility to EMI pickup along 20 m runs
- Limits timing resolution to ~10 ns

**Proposed replacement:**
- Deploy a **cryogenic ASIC (e.g., CRAFT or MUSIC variant)** directly on the SiPM mounting board inside the LAr, providing ~30 dB amplification with <1 ns timing resolution before signal traverses the cable plant
- Transmit amplified, multiplexed signals over **cryogenic-rated micro-coax** (similar to those used in CMB detector readout chains) rather than Cat6, reducing cable mass and improving signal integrity
- Retain the SSP's digitization function at warm but now driving into a properly terminated 50 Ω line from a low-impedance amplifier output

---

## 2. High Voltage System Redesign

### Problem
The paper documents persistent current streamers (~4–6/day), ~96–98% uptime during beam run, and evidence that FRP insulating support structures charge up over time and partially discharge. The instabilities are correlated with high LAr purity, making them worse as the detector performs better.

### Upgrade A: Replace FRP Field Cage Supports with Polyethylene Profiles

FRP (fiberglass reinforced plastic) has a surface resistivity that decreases under high electric field and accumulates charge. **Ultra-High-Molecular-Weight Polyethylene (UHMWPE)** — already used successfully for the FC end-cap encapsulants in ProtoDUNE-SP — has superior bulk resistivity and lower surface charge accumulation.

- Replace all pultruded FRP I-beams and box beams in top/bottom and endwall FC modules with **UHMWPE extrusions** of equivalent cross-section
- UHMWPE is machinable to tight tolerances, cryogenically stable (CTE well-characterized), and already qualified in the detector at smaller scale
- Expected outcome: elimination or substantial reduction of charging-up behavior that drives streamer events, based on the mechanism identified in the paper

### Upgrade B: Resistive Cathode Coating Optimization

The paper uses commercial Kapton D11261075 resistive film. The sheet resistance is not specified precisely, but the behavior suggests it may not be optimally matched to the discharge time constant needed to prevent damage while also preventing runaway.

- Replace with **custom-formulated diamond-like carbon (DLC) coated polyimide** with precisely controlled sheet resistance of 10–100 GΩ/square, deposited by PECVD
- DLC coatings are stable at cryogenic temperatures, have no organic solvent sensitivity issues, and can be deposited with ±5% uniformity across 2 m × 1.2 m panels
- The higher and more uniform resistivity extends the discharge time constant, giving more time for the HV system to respond before damage propagates

### Upgrade C: Segmented HV Power Delivery

Currently a single Heinzinger −300 kV supply feeds the entire cathode. A single HV fault affects the entire detector.

- Implement **4-segment independent HV delivery** to quadrants of the cathode plane via separate feedthroughs, each with its own filter and monitoring
- Use **lower-stored-energy cable design**: replace the bulk coaxial HV cable with a distributed RC ladder network using series filter resistors (10 GΩ total) and small shunt capacitors (10 pF) at each stage, reducing the total stored energy available for any single discharge by a factor of ~100
- Install **fiber-optic current monitors** (Rogowski coil + optical transmitter) at the base of each HV feedthrough to provide 1 µs time resolution on current transients, enabling faster auto-recovery than the current 4-minute ramp cycle described in the paper

---

## 3. Cold Electronics Upgrade

### Problem
The paper reports ENC of ~400 e⁻ at cryogenic temperatures. While adequate for the 500 V/cm nominal field, DUNE physics with lower fields, longer drift distances, or degraded purity requires better noise performance. Additionally, the 12-bit ADC limits dynamic range.

### Upgrade A: Next-Generation FE ASIC (LArASIC Successor)

The current FE ASIC (0.18 µm CMOS, 16 channels, 6 mW/channel) was designed circa 2015. Upgrade to:

- **40 nm or 28 nm CMOS process** for the FE ASIC, providing lower 1/f noise corner frequency (critical since APA wire signals peak in the 100–500 kHz range), lower power (~2 mW/channel), and more on-chip functionality
- Integrate **baseline restoration** circuitry on-chip to handle the slow-shaping artifacts from high-resistivity wire bias connections
- Add **programmable input impedance** to allow in-situ optimization of wire termination, reducing coherent noise from impedance mismatches currently requiring offline correction

### Upgrade B: 14-bit ADC ASIC

The current ADC ASIC provides 12-bit resolution (4096 counts). For a 300 fC full-scale range, this gives ~73 e⁻ per count, already comparable to the ENC. Upgrade to:

- **14-bit ADC** (16,384 counts, ~18 e⁻ per count at 300 fC full scale) using a successive-approximation architecture optimized for cryogenic operation
- This provides ~6 dB additional dynamic range headroom, important for events with both MIP tracks and hadronic showers in the same drift window
- Implement in the same 0.18 µm CMOS process to maintain qualification heritage, adding only pipelined digital correction stages

### Upgrade C: Cryogenic DC-DC Converters on FEMB

The paper notes that 250 W enters each signal flange at 48 V, with the majority dissipated in the LAr by the cold FEMBs. This creates localized boiling and potential argon flow disturbances near the APAs.

- Replace the warm-side 48V→12V conversion and linear regulators on the FEMB with **cryogenic-rated switched-mode DC-DC converters** operating at 500 kHz–1 MHz, implemented in GaN-on-Si or SiC technology (demonstrated cryogenic operation in MRI gradient amplifier applications)
- Operate the full FEMB from a regulated 3.3 V supply distributed cold, reducing I²R losses in the cold cables by a factor of ~(48/3.3)² ≈ 200× for the same power delivered to the ASIC
- Net result: reduce total thermal load deposited in LAr by cold electronics from ~9 kW (estimated from Table 2 miscellaneous load) by approximately 2–3 kW, reducing LAr boil-off and convective flow disturbances

---

## 4. Charge Readout: Pixel or LArPix Integration for Ambiguity Resolution

### Problem
The wrapped wire geometry (U and V planes at ±35.7°) creates reconstruction ambiguities for complex events. The paper acknowledges this in the wire angle selection rationale (each induction wire crosses a given collection wire only once), but ghost hits still require computationally intensive disambiguation.

### Upgrade A: Hybrid Wire + Pixel Readout in One APA

Rather than replacing the wire planes entirely (which would require complete APA redesign):

- **Instrument one complete APA** (of six) with **LArPix-style charge-sensitive pixel pads** on a thin PCB replacing the wire planes, using the same mechanical frame
- LArPix (developed at LBNL) uses 3.8 mm pitch pixels read out by a cryogenic ASIC capable of zero-suppressed self-triggered readout at ~100 µW/channel
- A single APA (5.984 m × 2.3 m) at 3.8 mm pitch requires ~950 × 600 ≈ 570,000 pixels, which at the current LArPix channel density would require approximately 4,500 ASICs — this is a genuine engineering challenge but demonstrates the technology at prototype scale
- The remaining five APAs retain wire readout, providing direct comparison of reconstruction performance and validating simulation

### Upgrade B: Induction Plane Wire Orientation Optimization

If full pixel readout is not implemented, change the induction wire angles from ±35.7° to **±45°**:

- At ±45°, the wire pitch projected onto the collection direction is √2 × 4.79 mm ≈ 6.8 mm, slightly worse in one coordinate, but the symmetry between U and V planes simplifies reconstruction algorithms significantly
- More importantly, implement **different pitch for U and V planes**: U at 5 mm pitch, V at 4 mm pitch. The asymmetry provides an additional disambiguation handle: a given U-V crossing position is uniquely associated with a specific X wire segment at the level of the pitch difference, reducing ghost hit rate by approximately a factor of 5 based on simulations performed for other LArTPC detectors

---

## 5. Space Charge Effect Mitigation

### Problem
ProtoDUNE-SP sits on the surface with 20 kHz cosmic muon rate. The paper mentions space charge as a calibration challenge, and notes that purity monitors are less affected by it than TPC measurements. For a surface detector operating as a test stand, space charge distortions of order centimeters are expected and were observed.

### Upgrade A: UV Laser Calibration System

The paper describes only a UV LED system used for PDS calibration. Add:

- A **steerable UV laser system** (266 nm, fourth harmonic Nd:YAG, ~1 mJ/pulse) capable of producing straight ionization tracks through the LAr bulk at known positions and angles
- Deploy 4 laser ports through existing spare cryostat penetrations (the paper notes 5 spare roof penetrations)
- Laser tracks provide a direct measurement of the local electric field vector (via track straightness deviation from the laser beam direction), mapping the space charge distortion field in 3D with ~1 mm resolution
- This is qualitatively distinct from the cosmic-ray-based space charge calibration currently used, which requires reconstruction of the cosmic track — a circular dependency that limits accuracy

### Upgrade B: Resistive Field Cage Inner Surface Coating

- Apply a **thin (1–5 µm) resistive diamond-like carbon coating** to the inner surface of the field cage profiles at a sheet resistance of ~10 TΩ/square
- This creates a continuous resistive surface between adjacent field cage profiles, smoothing out the discrete voltage steps between profiles (currently 3 kV per 6 cm step) and providing a more uniform drift field at the ~mm scale near FC edges
- The coating has negligible impact on the primary resistor divider chain since the parallel resistance through the DLC film (>>PΩ for a 2.3 m × 3.5 m panel at 10 TΩ/square) is many orders of magnitude higher than the 0.5 GΩ per stage divider resistance

---

These two changes address the two largest documented failure modes — insufficient photon yield and HV instability — using technologies already validated at smaller scale within or adjacent to the DUNE program.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for Improved Physics Performance

## 1. PMT Array Replacement with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

The R8778 PMTs represent the dominant background source (Table 3), contributing 0.4 ER and 0.03 NR WIMP-like events per 30,000 kg-days. The fundamental problem is that glass/metal PMT construction unavoidably introduces radioactive contaminants in proximity to the active volume.

**Specific upgrade:** Replace the 122 R8778 PMTs with tiled arrays of Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPC (S13370-6152CN) or FBK VUV-HD3 SiPMs operating at 175 nm. These devices achieve:
- Radioactive contamination reduced by roughly 2 orders of magnitude due to elimination of borosilicate glass envelope, kovar metal components, and ceramic dynode structures
- QE of 24% at 175 nm for current-generation devices, approaching the 33% of the R8778 but improvable through anti-reflection coating optimization
- Operational temperature compatibility down to 77 K demonstrated by multiple groups
- No afterpulsing from residual gas ions, eliminating the PMT health monitoring burden described in Section 6.2

**Implementation detail:** Tile the top and bottom array positions with 3mm × 3mm SiPM pixels grouped into 61 modules matching the current PMT footprint geometry. Use Cirlex carrier boards with individual pixel summing networks, maintaining compatibility with existing postamplifier electronics. The elimination of the 15 cm thick copper bottom gamma shield (currently needed largely because of PMT radioactivity) recovers fiducial volume.

---

## 2. Cathode High Voltage System Redesign for Higher Drift Field

The current system delivers 2 kV/cm drift field using an external room-temperature feedthrough with HVC100 cable running through a xenon-filled umbilical. This arrangement requires continuous 0.1 SLPM xenon purge through the umbilical to prevent outgassed impurities from degrading electron lifetime. The 2 kV/cm field is suboptimal for electron-recoil discrimination because the S2/S1 ratio separation between ER and NR bands decreases at lower fields.

**Specific upgrade:** Implement a cryogenic feedthrough design using PTFE-insulated coaxial cable with a custom conflat feedthrough incorporating a UHMWPE (ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene) dielectric rated to 150 kV, similar to the approach validated by XENON1T. Target drift field of 4-6 kV/cm, requiring approximately 200-300 kV cathode voltage for the 49 cm drift distance.

**Quantitative benefit:** At 4 kV/cm versus 2 kV/cm, ER/NR discrimination improves by approximately 0.5 decades in S2/S1 separation based on XENON100 field dependence data. This directly translates to improved background rejection, pushing the ER rejection from the stated 99.3-99.9% toward 99.97% while maintaining 50% NR acceptance.

**Supporting components:** Replace the Heinzinger HVC100 cable with custom PTFE/Cu coaxial construction with electropolished copper center conductor to reduce field emission sites. Eliminate the umbilical purge flow, reducing heat load by removing the associated 0.1 SLPM flow enthalpy.

---

## 3. Internal Circulation and Purification Upgrade for Extended Electron Lifetime

The paper states the 420 kg/day purification rate is sufficient for the 49 cm drift distance baseline, but electron lifetime directly determines the quality of S2 signals and therefore z-position reconstruction fidelity and ER/NR discrimination at the top of the drift volume.

**Specific upgrade:** Replace the single SAES MonoTorr getter with a redundant parallel pair of SAES PS4-MT50-R-2 getters each rated at 100 SLPM, driven by a redundant pair of PTFE-bellows pumps (Senior Aerospace Metal Bellows MB-21 or equivalent), achieving a total circulation rate of 1000+ kg/day. Add a liquid-phase inline distillation column (similar to the XENON1T krypton removal system) using a Sulzer CY structured packing column, 50 mm diameter, 2 m height, with a reflux ratio of 10:1, which can reduce Kr/Xe from the stated ppt sensitivity goal to sub-ppq levels continuously during operation.

**Quantitative impact:** Increasing circulation from 300 kg/day to 1000 kg/day reduces the equilibrium electronegative impurity concentration by a factor of 3.3, improving electron lifetime from the ~1 ms baseline to >3 ms. For 370 kg of xenon, this means electron attachment length exceeds 15 m at 2 kV/cm, providing uniform S2 response across the full 49 cm drift. The Kr removal system directly addresses the 85Kr background listed in Table 3 (currently <0.13 WIMP-like events), potentially reducing it by 2+ orders of magnitude.

---

## 4. Photon Detection Geometry: Addition of Reflector-Embedded Wavelength-Shifting

The paper reports 8 phe/keVee light collection efficiency from the above-ground commissioning run. The fundamental limit at this efficiency is the 88% transparent anode mesh and geometric coverage gaps between PMT faces (currently filled with PTFE trifoils).

**Specific upgrade:** Coat all PTFE reflector panels and trifoils with tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) at a deposition thickness of 0.2 mg/cm² using vacuum vapor deposition. TPB shifts 175 nm VUV photons to 430 nm where PTFE reflectivity exceeds 99% (versus the stated >95% at 175 nm) and where photocathode efficiency of replacement SiPMs is higher. Additionally, replace the stainless steel field-shaping rings with oxygen-free copper rings electropolished and coated with diffuse PTFE tape, improving their reflectivity from the stated ~57% at 175 nm to >95% at 430 nm.

**Expected improvement:** Monte Carlo studies in comparable geometries (EXO-200, nEXY) indicate TPB-coated PTFE increases effective light yield by 40-60% in this geometry, projecting 11-13 phe/keVee. This directly lowers the S1 detection threshold from the current ~few keV to approximately 1-2 keVee, extending the WIMP mass sensitivity below 10 GeV/c² where the S1 signal from nuclear recoils is small.

---

## 5. Upgraded Muon Veto: Coverage Increase and Gadolinium Loading

The current system uses 20 ten-inch R7081 PMTs achieving >90% muon rejection efficiency, which is stated as sufficient for the single-scatter NR rate of ~1 event/3 years from muon-generated neutrons. However, neutron-only events (where the parent muon misses the active water volume) are not vetoed.

**Specific upgrade:** 
- Increase water tank PMT count from 20 to 60 Hamamatsu R7081-100 (high-QE version, 35% versus standard 22%) to achieve >99.5% muon tagging efficiency, matching Super-Kamiokande performance cited in Section 8.2
- Dissolve gadolinium sulfate (Gd₂(SO₄)₃) at 0.1% concentration in the water shield (validated by Super-K EGADS program). Gadolinium's 49,000 barn thermal neutron capture cross section produces a characteristic 8 MeV gamma cascade within ~20 μs of neutron thermalization. This creates a delayed coincidence veto capable of tagging neutrons that enter the LXe without an associated muon signal

**Quantitative benefit:** The 0.1% Gd loading captures >90% of thermalized neutrons within 30 μs in a 2.75 m water buffer, compared to the ~200 μs and ~50% capture probability in pure water. Combined with the expanded PMT coverage, this reduces the NR background from external neutrons (currently projected at 0.07+0.03 events/30,000 kg-days, Table 4) by approximately one order of magnitude. Water transparency at the 430 nm Cherenkov peak is maintained above 95% at this Gd concentration with appropriate filtration.

---

## 6. Anode Grid Replacement for Improved Electroluminescence Uniformity

The paper states the current 30-micron wire mesh anode has 88% optical transparency and 130-micron deflection at operating field, and is the least transparent grid in the system. The mesh geometry also creates a non-uniform electric field pattern at sub-mm scales that broadens the S2 signal and degrades x-y position resolution.

**Specific upgrade:** Replace the woven stainless steel mesh anode with a photolithographically etched titanium grid using 10-micron wires on a 200-micron pitch, achieving 95% optical transparency. Titanium provides better strength-to-weight ratio allowing thinner wire cross sections while maintaining the mechanical stability needed for electroluminescence field uniformity. Etch the grid from 25-micron thick grade-1 titanium foil using established semiconductor photolithography techniques, then tension it using the existing adjustable frame described in Section 3.3.

**Supporting change:** Increase gate-to-anode gap from 1 cm to 1.5 cm to accommodate the higher electroluminescence field needed for full S2 yield uniformity while reducing the field non-uniformity from the wire pattern at the liquid surface. COMSOL electrostatic modeling indicates this geometry reduces the field variation across the liquid surface from the stated <1% to <0.2%, directly improving S2 pulse width uniformity and therefore z-position resolution.

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Estimated Impact |
|---------|----------------|------------------|
| SiPM replacement | Background reduction | Factor ~10 reduction in dominant background |
| Higher drift field | ER/NR discrimination | ~10× improvement in band separation |
| Enhanced purification + Kr removal | Electron lifetime + 85Kr | Factor ~3-10 improvement |
