# Hardware Design Upgrades for the DarkSide-50 LAr TPC

## 1. Photomultiplier Tube Replacement with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**The core problem:** The R11065 Hamamatsu PMTs are the dominant source of radioactive background. The paper explicitly states PMTs contribute >90% of radiogenic neutron background and are the primary source of Cherenkov background events, which proved to be the **dominant surviving background** in the analysis.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace 38 × 3" PMTs with tiled arrays of **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD SiPMs** or similar cryogenic-grade devices, operated at 87K
- Target: tile the top and bottom windows with ~24 cm diameter arrays using ~6mm × 6mm SiPM cells in a hexagonal close-pack geometry achieving ~65-70% coverage
- SiPMs have radiopurity roughly **3-4 orders of magnitude better** than borosilicate PMTs, eliminating the dominant neutron and Cherenkov background sources simultaneously
- SiPMs also eliminate the PMT ceramic dynode plates explicitly identified as the dominant neutron source
- Correlated avalanche noise (optical crosstalk) requires mitigation via **trenched cell isolation** designs already available commercially

**Quantified benefit:** The paper identifies scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov as the limiting background, driven by high-energy gammas from 232Th and 238U in PMT components. Removing the PMT radioactivity would reduce the predicted ER background from 0.08 events to well below 0.01 events per equivalent exposure, enabling a factor ~10 larger search box or equivalently much greater sensitivity.

---

## 2. Replacement of Teflon Reflector with Higher-Radiopurity, Lower-Cherenkov Alternative

**The core problem:** The paper identifies scintillation+**Teflon Cherenkov** as the single most important surviving background after all cuts. The S1pMaxFrac cut eliminates fused-silica Cherenkov effectively, but no analogous cut exists for Teflon because the Cherenkov photons originate distributed along the cylindrical wall, making the PMT light pattern diffuse and hard to distinguish.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace PTFE reflector panels with **deuterated polyethylene (d-PE) panels coated with evaporated aluminum** plus a TPB overcoat
  - d-PE has negligible Cherenkov yield in the optical range relevant to TPB emission (~420 nm) because deuterium substitution shifts the refractive index dispersion
  - Aluminum reflectance at 420 nm exceeds 90%, comparable to PTFE
- Alternative: **Spectralon UHMW-PE** has lower refractive index (n~1.35 vs PTFE n~1.38) reducing Cherenkov threshold, but more practically it can be machined to tighter tolerances enabling better surface contact sealing
- More aggressive option: **Crystalline quartz panels with anti-reflection coating** would eliminate polymer Cherenkov entirely, though cryogenic compatibility requires careful thermal expansion matching

**Quantified benefit:** The analysis required a radial fiducial cut removing ~15% of the active mass and an NLL cut specifically to reject Teflon Cherenkov events. Eliminating this background source recovers that fiducial volume and eliminates the need for the computationally expensive 90-live-year Monte Carlo simulation required to model it.

---

## 3. Upgraded Charge Readout for Improved S2 Position Reconstruction

**The core problem:** The paper states explicitly that x-y reconstruction "proved to be very difficult" due to proximity of top PMTs to the S2 emission region limiting charge sharing. The position resolution of ~0.6 cm was achieved only with iterative Monte Carlo corrections, with no reliable absolute position calibration. This forced conservative radial fiducial cuts and introduced the largest systematic uncertainty in fiducial mass determination.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Install a **segmented anode readout** above the liquid-gas interface using a 2D crossed-wire or pixel pad structure
  - Specifically: **two orthogonal wire planes** (pitch ~3-4 mm) at the anode position, read out with charge-sensitive amplifiers operating at 87K
  - Wire planes replace or supplement the ITO-coated window as the charge collection electrode
  - Crossed wire geometry provides ~2mm position resolution from charge centroiding without relying on optical S2 pattern reconstruction
- Alternatively, a **segmented light guide + SiPM array** placed immediately above the liquid surface in the gas gap provides direct S2 position readout with ~1mm resolution from the much larger solid angle subtended

**Quantified benefit:** The paper reports the RadialFid cut acceptance was 0.848, meaning ~15% of WIMP events are rejected. Better position reconstruction would tighten this to <5% loss. More importantly, absolute position calibration would reduce the fiducial mass uncertainty from the current ~1.6% to below 0.5%, and would allow sharper radial cuts providing factor ~3 more background rejection with less signal loss.

---

## 4. Upgraded Liquid Scintillator Veto with Gadolinium Loading

**The core problem:** The current boron-loaded LSV achieves 99.64% neutron veto efficiency, which is excellent. However, the prompt veto window integration is only [-50, 250] ns, and the delayed capture lifetime is 22 µs on 10B. The paper notes that the 10B α-only capture peak (~1.47 MeV) and escaped γ events reduce the modified delayed veto efficiency to ~79% for neutron counting purposes.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Add **gadolinium (Gd) at ~0.1% by mass** to the existing borated liquid scintillator
  - Natural Gd has thermal neutron capture cross section of ~49,000 barns vs. 3,840 barns for 10B
  - Gd capture releases **8 MeV γ cascade** in multiple γ rays vs. the 10B Q-value of 2.79 MeV
  - The high γ multiplicity and energy make Gd captures far easier to detect with high efficiency
  - Gd capture lifetime is ~20 µs at 0.1% loading, comparable to B, maintaining the same DAQ window requirements
- The combination Gd+B would push veto efficiency above 99.9% for all neutron energies
- **Specific formulation:** Use **Gd-THFA (gadolinium trifluoroacetylacetonate)** which has demonstrated stability in liquid scintillator at cryogenic-adjacent temperatures and in aromatic solvents compatible with the existing pseudocumene/TMB mixture

**Quantified benefit:** The radiogenic neutron background is already below 0.005 events, so the benefit here is primarily in **reducing systematic uncertainty** on neutron background estimation and enabling smaller neutron veto windows that reduce accidental WIMP veto rate from the current ~0.5% per cut.

---

## 5. Improved High-Voltage and Electric Field Design

**The core problem:** The paper notes a 1 cm gas pocket above a grid 4.7 mm beneath the liquid-gas interface, with 200 V/cm drift field. The analysis uses S2/S1 as a discriminant but explicitly notes it is "not effective at low S1 where further rejection is most needed." Higher drift fields improve electron lifetime and S2 yield, improving position reconstruction and S2-based discrimination at low energies.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace the single grid geometry with a **double-grid extraction system**:
  - Lower grid at the original position (4.7 mm below interface) defines the drift region boundary
  - Upper grid 2-3 mm above the lower grid creates a well-defined, uniform extraction field of **3-4 kV/cm** in the inter-grid gap
  - This geometry is standard in modern xenon TPCs (LZ, XENONnT) and provides near-100% electron extraction efficiency vs. the ~50% typical at 200 V/cm in single-grid LAr systems
- Use **electroformed copper grids** with 100 µm wire diameter and 5 mm pitch for minimal radioactivity contribution and minimal light absorption
- Increase drift field to **500 V/cm** minimum to reduce electron-ion recombination, increasing S2 signal and improving S2/S1 discrimination particularly at low energies (below 50 keVnr)

**Quantified benefit:** At 200 V/cm, argon has ~50% extraction efficiency. Moving to 500 V/cm drift + 3.5 kV/cm extraction roughly doubles the S2 signal at the same S1, pushing the MinS2uncorr threshold from 200 PE to an effective energy threshold ~30% lower. This directly expands the low-mass WIMP search sensitivity where the current analysis is limited by S2 detection threshold.

---

## Priority Ranking

| Upgrade | Background Reduction | Complexity | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | Eliminates dominant background source | High (cryogenic electronics) | Critical |
| Teflon replacement | Eliminates limiting Cherenkov background | Medium | High |
| Segmented anode | Improves fiducialization | Medium | High |
| Gd-loaded LSV | Reduces neutron systematics | Low | Moderate |
| HV/field upgrade | Improves low-energy threshold | Medium | Moderate |

The SiPM upgrade and Teflon reflector replacement address the two backgrounds that the paper explicitly identifies as limiting the analysis, and together they would enable an order-of-magnitude improvement in sensitivity for equivalent exposure. These upgrades are in fact the design basis for the DarkSide-20k experiment, validating this analysis.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for EXO-200

Based on careful reading of the detector design, I identify the primary physics performance limiters and propose concrete upgrades targeting energy resolution, background reduction, and fiducial mass efficiency.

---

## 1. Replace LAAPDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**Current limitation:** The 468 LAAPDs operate at -1400V bias with a measured capacitance of 125 pF each, ganged in groups of 5-7, yielding noise of 2 e⁻/pF (330 μV_rms) per channel. The 48% photosensitive packing fraction and 70% PTFE reflectance at 178 nm limit light collection efficiency.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Deploy **VUV-sensitive SiPMs** (e.g., Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPC S13370-6050CN or FBK VUV-HD3 series) with peak PDE >20% at 178 nm
- SiPMs operate at 40-70V bias versus 1400V for LAAPDs, dramatically simplifying the biasing chain and eliminating the trim voltage compensation system
- Tile the entire cathode-facing surface including regions currently covered by PTFE reflectors, replacing passive reflection with active detection area
- Achieve >60% photosensitive coverage versus current 48%
- Ganging noise scales differently: SiPM dark noise is ~100 kcps/mm² at 163K but drops precipitously at LXe temperature, making individual or small-gang readout feasible
- The lower bias voltage eliminates the dominant microphonics problem that required elaborate conducting plane shielding in the flex cables
- Use **through-silicon-via (TSV) ceramic substrates** from Kyocera or Murata with measured U/Th below 10 ppt, replacing the current spider spring mechanical contact system
- Expected improvement: scintillation channel energy contribution improves by factor ~2, directly improving combined energy resolution from σ/E = 1.6% toward ~0.8%

---

## 2. Redesign Wire Readout with Charge-Sensitive ASIC and Reduced-Pitch Strips

**Current limitation:** The photoetched phosphor bronze wire triplets with 9mm readout pitch (3mm wire pitch) provide 38 readout channels per plane. The crossed U/V geometry at 60° with 6mm plane separation limits 3D position resolution. The discrete component front-end electronics are located ~1m away, with flex cable capacitance of 60-80 pF dominating the noise.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace wire triplets with **50 μm thick gold-coated copper strips** on polyimide substrates (similar to NEXT-HD approach) at 3mm readout pitch, doubling spatial sampling
- Develop a **custom low-background ASIC** (similar in concept to the IDEAS VATA64 or BNL GRAPHICS series) fabricated in 180nm CMOS:
  - Screen fab process for U/Th contamination; 180nm CMOS yields die masses of ~50mg with negligible activity
  - Integrate charge preamp + CR-RC² shaper + 14-bit ADC on-die
  - Mount ASIC directly on the LAAPD/SiPM platter inside the LXe volume, eliminating the 1m flex cable run and reducing input capacitance from 60-80 pF to <5 pF
  - Noise performance: at 5 pF input capacitance, expect <50 e⁻ ENC versus current ~200 e⁻ ENC
- Add a **third induction wire plane** at 60° offset to allow full 3D charge cloud reconstruction without relying solely on drift time for z-coordinate, improving multi-site discrimination
- Digital output via low-power LVDS over existing polyimide cable infrastructure
- Expected improvement: ionization channel energy resolution improves from noise-dominated regime; single-site/multi-site discrimination efficiency increases from ~80% toward ~95%

---

## 3. Upgrade the High Voltage System to Achieve Design Drift Field

**Current limitation:** HV instabilities (described as mV-scale glitches above 9-14 kV, attributed to corona on photoetched edges) limit operation to 8 kV cathode bias versus the 75 kV design maximum. At 8 kV across 38.4 cm drift length, the drift field is ~0.21 kV/cm versus the 3.7 kV/cm design value. This severely impacts electron lifetime requirements and charge collection uniformity.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace all photoetched cathode and field ring edges with **electropolished machined oxygen-free copper rings** with edge radii >500 μm, eliminating corona initiation sites
- Replace the current RG217 coaxial cable HV feedthrough with a **custom cold-to-warm feedthrough** using:
  - PTFE-machined coaxial geometry (same TE-6472 material already qualified)
  - Solid copper center conductor electropolished to <0.1 μm Ra surface finish
  - Spring-loaded contact with >100 N force to eliminate intermittent contact glitching
  - Incorporate **inline 222Rn-tight seal** using metal C-seal (Helicoflex HN series) rather than Swagelok compression on polyethylene
- Install **field emission suppressors**: coat all high-field copper surfaces with 100nm Al₂O₃ by atomic layer deposition (ALD), which has demonstrated suppression of field emission up to 50 MV/m in LXe environments
- Add **slow HV conditioning system**: custom CAEN N1471 derivative with 1V/minute ramp capability and automatic glitch detection/recovery
- Expected improvement: achieving 1 kV/cm operation reduces electron attachment cross-section requirements by 10× and improves z-resolution via drift time measurement; achieving 2+ kV/cm enables charge-light anti-correlation optimization and approaches theoretical energy resolution limit

---

## 4. Replace HFE-7000 Buffer with Ultra-Pure Water Shielding

**Current limitation:** The 4140 kg of HFE-7000 provides ρ=1.8 g/cm² shielding but has measured U/Th at <0.25 Bq/kg level (Table 3). The cryostat geometry constrains the shielding thickness. External radon at ~6 mBq/L (3× the 2 mBq/L limit) contributes background.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Redesign the outer cryostat as a **water-shield cryostat** with the inner copper vessel surrounded by an annular ultra-pure water volume (resistivity >18 MΩ·cm, U/Th at sub-femtogram/gram levels achievable with commercial deionization):
  - Water provides 3.3× greater mass shielding per unit volume than HFE at equal thickness
  - Existing 5901 kg copper cryostat can be reused as the inner pressure vessel
  - Eliminates the radon enclosure problem: continuously recirculate water through a **Rn-stripping membrane degasser** (Membrana Liqui-Cel series, demonstrated to reduce dissolved Rn to <0.1 mBq/L)
  - Instrument water volume with **20 × 8-inch PMTs** (Hamamatsu R5912) for Cherenkov muon veto, replacing the external plastic scintillator panels with an active water shield providing >99% muon tagging efficiency versus current 96%
- Requires redesigned thermal isolation using **aerogel-filled vacuum panels** on the inner vessel to maintain LXe temperature without HFE thermal buffer
- Expected improvement: 2-5× reduction in external gamma background; radon background eliminated; muon veto efficiency improved by ~3 percentage points

---

## 5. Implement Barium Tagging Readout Infrastructure

**Current limitation:** The paper explicitly notes Ba²⁺ tagging capability is not implemented in EXO-200 but is a stated goal of the EXO program. This is the single highest-impact physics upgrade possible, converting the detector from a background-limited calorimeter to a background-free experiment.

**Proposed upgrade compatible with existing TPC geometry:**
- Install **a single-atom Ba²⁺ detection channel** using the existing calibration source guide tube port as the extraction conduit:
  - **Dry extraction probe**: Deploy a cryogenic Ba²⁺ capture tip (Ba-selective crown ether functionalized silica, demonstrated by nEXO R&D groups at UT Austin and Carleton) via the existing 5/8-inch copper guide tube
  - **In-situ fluorescence detection**: Add four **UV fiber bundles** (fused silica, Polymicro FVP series, already compatible with the existing optical fiber infrastructure for LAAPD calibration) to illuminate the extraction region with 493 nm (Ba⁺ S₁/₂→P₁/₂ transition) laser light
  - Install one **photon-counting PMT** (Hamamatsu H10682-210) in a light-tight copper housing at the warm end of an existing cable leg, viewing the fiber bundle output
  - This does not require opening the xenon vessel; the guide tube already penetrates to the LXe vessel exterior
- Expected improvement: if Ba tagging achieves even 50% efficiency with <0.01 accidental coincidence rate, the 0νββ background effectively drops by 100×, extending half-life sensitivity by >10× with the same active mass

---

## Summary of Expected Performance Improvements

| Upgrade | Primary metric improved | Expected gain |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | σ_E/E at Q_ββ | 1.6% → ~0.9% |
| ASIC + strip readout | Multi-site discrimination | 80% → ~95% efficiency |
| HV system redesign | Drift field | 0.21 → 2+ kV/cm |
| Water shield | External γ background | 2-5× reduction |
| Ba tagging infrastructure | Signal-to-background | >10× sensitivity gain |

The highest priority single upgrade is the **SiPM replacement combined with in-vessel ASIC readout**, as these together address the fundamental energy resolution limitation that determines the width of the 0νββ search window and therefore directly scales the signal-to-background ratio for any given source activity.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for the SNO Detector

## Identification of Primary Physics Limitations

The paper reveals several concrete performance bottlenecks. Working through the detector chain systematically:

---

## 1. Photon Detection System

### Current Limitation
The Hamamatsu R1408 achieves 31% bare photocathode coverage, corrected to ~54% effective coverage with reflective concentrators. The paper states roughly **8 photoelectrons per MeV**, creating a hard floor on energy threshold and resolution. The timing resolution standard deviation is 1.7 ns, meeting but not exceeding specification.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Replace R1408 with Large-Area Picosecond Photodetectors (LAPPDs)**
- Microchannel plate technology provides ~50 ps single-photon timing resolution vs. 1.7 ns, directly improving vertex reconstruction from ~tens of cm to potentially ~5 cm
- 20 cm × 20 cm active area per unit reduces the number of feedthroughs while maintaining coverage
- Quantum efficiency ~30-35% at 400 nm vs. approximately 21% for R1408 at peak
- Flat geometry would require redesigning the ABS hexagonal mounting cells and concentrator geometry, but the flat PSUP panel architecture described in Section 5 is actually well-suited to this

**Alternative: Replace with Hamamatsu R7081 or R12860 HQE tubes**
- These are 10-inch hemispherical tubes with high-quantum-efficiency bialkali photocathodes reaching ~35% peak QE compared to ~21% for R1408
- Drop-in compatible with existing waterproof enclosure design philosophy
- Would increase photoelectron yield from ~8 to ~13 pe/MeV without any other changes
- Direct improvement to energy threshold, potentially lowering from ~5 MeV toward ~3 MeV, opening additional NC signal phase space

**Wavelength-Shifting Light Concentrators**
- Replace the bare aluminum/MgF2/TiO2 dielectric reflectors (82% mean reflectance) with TPB (tetraphenyl butadiene) or bis-MSB wavelength-shifting plates
- Cherenkov photons below 300 nm are currently lost in acrylic absorption (paper states 0.18 cm⁻¹ at 320 nm)
- WLS conversion captures UV photons and re-emits at ~420 nm where both acrylic transmission and PMT QE are near maximum
- Estimated 15-20% improvement in detected photon yield with no structural changes

---

## 2. Neutral Current Detector Array

### Current Limitation
The paper describes 3He proportional counters with ~25% effective neutron detection efficiency (reduced from nominal 45% due to alpha/neutron discrimination limitations). The 50 µm copper anode wire at gas gain ~100 provides limited pulse-shape discrimination capability. Total array length is 770 m on a 1 m square lattice.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Boron-Loaded Liquid Scintillator Panels**
- Replace or supplement the 3He string array with panels of boron-loaded scintillator (e.g., 2.5% natural boron in linear alkyl benzene)
- ¹⁰B(n,α)⁷Li has 3840 barn thermal cross section vs. 5330 barn for ³He, but scintillator panels can cover larger solid angle
- The alpha/gamma discrimination via pulse-shape in organic scintillator is inherently better than proportional counter discrimination
- Less mechanically complex deployment than 96 individual strings requiring ROV installation

**Upgraded 3He Detectors with Resistive Anode Position Encoding**
- Replace the single 50 µm copper anode with a resistive wire enabling continuous position readout via charge division
- Current design uses a 30 ns delay line termination only at the bottom; resistive anode provides full-length position resolution of ~1 cm
- This directly improves alpha/neutron discrimination because alpha wall-effect events have characteristic position clustering near counter ends
- Would push effective efficiency from stated 25% toward the nominal 45% capture efficiency by better background rejection

**Gadolinium-Doped Water Option**
- Loading the H₂O region (not D₂O) with 0.1% GdCl₃ 
- ¹⁵⁷Gd has 254,000 barn thermal neutron capture cross section, emitting ~8 MeV gamma cascade
- Neutrons thermalized in D₂O that escape the AV would be captured with high efficiency in the H₂O annular region
- The 8.6 MeV total gamma energy is detectably above the 2.2 MeV deuterium photodisintegration threshold concern
- No modification to AV or PSUP geometry required; handled entirely through H₂O system described in Section 2
- Estimated 20-25% additional NC detection efficiency for neutrons currently lost to H₂O capture

---

## 3. Electronics and Data Acquisition

### Current Limitation
The paper describes 12-bit ADCs with ~2 µs conversion time, 16-deep analog memory per channel, and a 400 ns per-PMT deadtime. The overall system runs at approximately 1 kHz normal background rate with ~8 MB/s readout bandwidth. The single-board Motorola 68040 eCPU is a significant bottleneck.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Replace SNOD/SNOINT/QUSN7 ASIC Chain with Modern FADC System**
- Deploy 12-bit, 1 GSPS flash ADCs (e.g., based on AD9625 architecture) on daughter boards replacing the three-chip ASIC set
- Full waveform digitization eliminates the dead time from the TAC/gate architecture entirely
- Current system loses information between discriminator firing and global trigger arrival (~400 ns window); FADC captures complete pulse shape
- Direct improvement to pulse-shape discrimination for NC detector backgrounds
- Specifically enables Cherenkov/scintillation separation if any wavelength-shifting is added

**Replace eCPU with FPGA-Based Event Builder**
- The Motorola 68040 bottleneck described in Section 7 limits burst readout
- Modern Xilinx UltraScale+ or Intel Stratix 10 FPGAs can implement the event-building logic described with >100× throughput improvement
- Critical for supernova burst capability: paper states design goal of handling bursts from 1 kpc; improved readout extends this range
- Replace the XL1/XL2 RS-485 link (8 MB/s) with 10 GbE optical links, reducing 19-crate readout latency from milliseconds to microseconds

**Trigger System Upgrade**
- Current analog sum trigger has a 100 ns coincidence window set by PMT array light-crossing time
- Implementing a software trigger on FPGA with full hit-time information enables position-weighted triggering
- This would lower the effective energy threshold by ~30% by rejecting PMT noise hits that currently fake low-multiplicity triggers, using timing consistency with a reconstructed vertex as an online cut

---

## 4. Water Purification and Radon Reduction

### Current Limitation
The paper specifies Rn levels with 3 pCi/l in lab air and describes a cover gas system using liquid nitrogen boil-off. The process degasser achieves ~50× Rn reduction. The design goal is 12 Rn atoms/m²/hr from cavity walls. Radon is specifically identified as a serious concern for backgrounds.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Online Radon Stripping via Membrane Contactor System**
- Replace the large electropolished vessel Process Degasser with a hollow-fiber membrane contactor (e.g., Liqui-Cel SuperPhobic)
- Modern membrane contactors achieve >99.9% dissolved gas removal in a compact, continuously operating system
- Eliminates the batch-mode vacuum degasser limitation and allows continuous radon stripping during normal recirculation
- Directly reduces the dominant NC background from radon-daughter photodisintegration

**Ultra-Low Emanation Radon Trap for Cover Gas**
- The current system relies on N₂ boil-off (<10⁻⁵ pCi/l Rn), which is adequate but supply-limited
- Replace with a closed-loop activated charcoal trap system at -40°C (above liquid N₂ cost but achieves ~10⁻⁶ pCi/l Rn)
- Charcoal traps at controlled temperature have been demonstrated at Borexino to achieve this level
- Eliminates dependence on liquid nitrogen dewar and provides more uniform cover gas purity

---

## 5. Magnetic Field Compensation

### Current Limitation
The paper states 14 horizontal coils embedded in cavity walls cancel only the vertical component of Earth's field, leaving a maximum residual field of 19 µT. This causes ~2.5% average photon detection efficiency reduction. The vertical component is uncorrected.

### Proposed Upgrades

**Full 3-Axis Helmholtz Coil Array**
- Add vertical-axis compensation coils in addition to the existing 14 horizontal coils
- The cavity geometry (22 m diameter, 34 m height) is amenable to a pair of large-diameter vertical coils mounted at the deck level and floor
- Reducing residual field from 19 µT to <5 µT would recover ~2% photon detection efficiency uniformly across all PMTs
- More importantly, eliminates the position-dependent efficiency variation across the PMT array that complicates optical calibration
- Low-radioactivity copper windings with appropriate shielding would not compromise water purity requirements established in Section 5

---

## Priority Ranking by Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Difficulty | Impact on SNO Science Goals |
|---|---|---|---|
| HQE PMTs (R12860) | +60% photoelectron yield | Medium | Energy threshold, NC/CC separation |
| FADC waveform digitization | Pulse shape discrimination | Medium | NC background rejection |
| WLS concentrators | +15% photon yield, UV recovery | Low | Energy threshold |
| Resistive anode NCDs | Alpha rejection, 25%→40% efficiency | Medium | NC signal statistics |
| GdCl₃ in H₂O | +20% NC efficiency | Low | NC total flux measurement |
| Membrane radon stripping | Reduce dominant background | High | Signal/background ratio |
| FPGA event builder | Supernova burst capability | Low | Astrophysics reach |
| 3-axis B-field compensation | Uniform PMT efficiency | Low | Systematic uncertainty |

The highest-leverage single upgrade is replacing the PMTs with modern high-QE tubes, as photon statistics directly limit every physics measurement the detector makes: energy resolution, vertex resolution, direction reconstruction, and ultimately the CC/NC ratio measurement that is the experiment's central goal.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for the DarkSide-50 LAr TPC

## Identification of Primary Performance Limiters

From the paper, the binding constraints on physics performance are explicitly identified:

1. **Dominant background**: scintillation+Cherenkov events (primarily from Teflon reflector)
2. **Limited radial fiducialization**: x-y reconstruction resolution ~0.6 cm, constrained by PMT proximity to S2 region
3. **PMT radioactivity**: borosilicate glass stems and ceramic dynode plates dominate radiogenic neutron background (>90%)
4. **39Ar residual activity**: 0.73 mBq/kg in UAr still contributes ER background
5. **LSV neutron veto efficiency**: 99.64% combined efficiency leaves room for improvement at larger scales

---

## Upgrade 1: Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

### Motivation
The paper explicitly states PMT borosilicate glass stems and ceramic dynode plates are responsible for >90% of radiogenic neutron background. The PMTs also limit x-y reconstruction due to their 3" diameter and proximity to the S2 emission region.

### Specific Implementation
- **Device**: Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-SF SiPMs or Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPCs (already qualified for LAr temperatures)
- **Configuration**: Tile-based arrays with ~1 cm² individual SiPM tiles arranged in a dense grid pattern on both top and bottom windows, maintaining ~30-40% photon detection efficiency comparable to or exceeding current PMT coverage
- **Tile density**: 127 tiles per array face (matching current PMT count) but with option to increase to ~400 tiles per face using 6mm × 6mm cells to dramatically improve x-y reconstruction
- **Radioactivity**: SiPMs are fabricated from silicon with trace U/Th activities measured at <1 µBq/device, representing >100× reduction in radioactive contamination per unit photosensitive area compared to R11065 PMTs
- **Cryogenic readout**: Replace cryogenic preamplifiers with custom CMOS ASICs (e.g., similar to the ABCD chip architecture used in ATLAS strips, adapted for SiPM at 87K) mounted on low-radioactivity printed circuit boards using Rogers 4350B substrate with electrodeposited copper traces rather than standard FR4

### Expected Impact
- Radiogenic neutron background reduced by factor >10
- x-y position resolution improvement from ~6 mm to ~2 mm (estimated from charge centroiding with higher granularity), enabling tighter radial fiducialization
- Fiducial mass fraction increase from current ~67% (31.3 kg / 46.4 kg) to potentially ~80%

---

## Upgrade 2: Replace Teflon Reflector with Wavelength-Shifting Reflector Film on Fused Silica Cylinder

### Motivation
The paper identifies scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov as the **dominant surviving ER background** after the S1pMaxFrac cut eliminates fused silica Cherenkov. The Teflon generates Cherenkov radiation because it is a dielectric with refractive index n ≈ 1.35 at 420 nm, above the Cherenkov threshold for MeV-scale electrons from high-energy γ rays.

### Specific Implementation
- **Primary change**: Replace PTFE Teflon cylindrical reflector with an **amorphous quartz (fused silica) cylinder** coated on its inner surface with a thin-film TPB deposition (~200 µg/cm²) on top of a diffuse reflective coating of barium sulfate (BaSO₄) or enhanced specular reflector (ESR) film
- **Cherenkov suppression mechanism**: Fused silica has n ≈ 1.46 at 420 nm; the Cherenkov threshold for electrons is p > 0.33 MeV/c. However, by making the structural cylinder from **low-refractive-index aerogel composite panels** (n ≈ 1.05, as developed for RICH detectors by groups at INFN), the Cherenkov threshold rises to ~1.5 MeV/c, suppressing the dominant background process
- **Alternative approach**: If mechanical rigidity of aerogel composite is insufficient, use a **thin (2 mm) fused silica cylinder** as the primary structure but with an outer coating of **black-anodized aluminum** acting as a light absorber for Cherenkov photons generated within the silica, preventing their collection. A separate inner TPB-coated BaSO₄ diffuse reflector sheet (like 3M Radiant Mirror Film) handles the 420 nm reflectivity
- **TPB deposition**: Maintain TPB wavelength shifting via vacuum evaporation at ~200 µg/cm², identical to current process but on the new substrate

### Expected Impact
- Reduction of scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov background by estimated factor 5-20 (depending on implementation)
- This directly relaxes the f90 lower bound requirement, expanding the WIMP search box and improving sensitivity at low WIMP masses
- The radial fiducial cut could be relaxed, recovering ~5-10% additional fiducial mass

---

## Upgrade 3: Replace Borosilicate PMT/Window Components with Synthetic Fused Silica and Redesign Window Stack

### Motivation
The paper notes the fused silica TPC windows also generate Cherenkov background (subdominant but present, eliminated by S1pMaxFrac cut). The ITO cathode and anode coatings on the windows have associated radioactivity concerns, and the window thickness affects Cherenkov yield.

### Specific Implementation
- **Window material**: Maintain Heraeus Suprasil 2A synthetic fused silica (already used, lowest OH content and metal impurities of commercial grades, <1 ppb U/Th)
- **Thickness reduction**: Reduce window thickness from current design to minimum structurally viable (~8 mm for 20 cm diameter windows under LAr pressure differential), reducing total fused silica Cherenkov yield proportionally
- **ITO replacement**: Replace ITO electrode coating with **ultra-thin (5 nm) titanium nitride (TiN)** deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD). TiN has comparable conductivity to ITO (~200 Ω/sq at 5 nm) but ~100× lower mass and is deposited from ultra-pure precursors (TiCl₄ + NH₃), reducing radioactive contamination. TiN is also more mechanically robust at cryogenic temperatures
- **Anti-Cherenkov window treatment**: Apply a **nano-porous silica aerogel film** (n ≈ 1.1-1.2, 50 µm thick) by sol-gel process to the outer face of each window, creating a graded-index anti-reflection coating that also raises the local Cherenkov threshold for electrons traversing the window from outside

### Expected Impact
- ~30-50% reduction in fused silica Cherenkov contribution (already subdominant but removed by S1pMaxFrac)
- Enables relaxation or elimination of S1pMaxFrac cut, recovering ~5% WIMP acceptance at low S1
- Improved optical transmission uniformity, benefiting energy resolution

---

## Upgrade 4: Active Neutron Moderator Shield Integrated into Cryostat Annulus

### Motivation
Radiogenic neutrons from PMTs (>90% of radiogenic neutron background per the paper) currently rely entirely on the external LSV for vetoing. A dedicated neutron moderator surrounding the TPC inner vessel would reduce the neutron fluence reaching the active volume before veto.

### Specific Implementation
- **Material**: Fill the annular gap between the inner cryostat vessel and outer vessel with **borated polyethylene (5% natural boron by weight)** panels, 5 cm thick, fabricated from Dow Chemically pure HDPE with H₃BO₃ additive screened for <1 ppb U/Th
- **Geometry**: Segmented panels (to allow thermal contraction) covering the cylindrical sides of the inner vessel, where PMTs are located
- **Alternative if space-constrained**: **Gadolinium-loaded silicone rubber sheets** (2% Gd by weight, 1 cm thick) conformally wrapped around the inner vessel. Gd has a thermal neutron capture cross section of 49,000 barns vs. 3,840 barns for ¹⁰B, allowing thinner implementation. The Gd capture γ rays (up to 8 MeV total) are then detected in the LSV with high efficiency
- **Compatibility**: Both materials can be screened to <10 mBq/kg for U/Th and operated at room temperature in the inter-vessel vacuum/insulation space

### Expected Impact
- Factor ~3-5 reduction in radiogenic neutron background rate reaching the TPC active volume
- Combined with existing 99.64% veto efficiency, total radiogenic neutron background could decrease from <0.005 to <0.001 events per equivalent exposure
- More significant for scaled-up detectors where PMT count (and hence radioactivity) scales with surface area

---

## Upgrade 5: Higher-Field Extraction Region with Improved Grid Design

### Motivation
The paper uses a grid 4.7 mm beneath the liquid-gas interface separating a 200 V/cm drift region from a higher-field extraction region. Improved S2 yield and better S2 spatial uniformity would directly improve x-y reconstruction resolution, enabling tighter radial fiducialization and better surface background rejection.

### Specific Implementation
- **Grid replacement**: Replace current grid with a **photo-etched stainless-steel mesh** (316LN grade, electropolished, screened for <10 mBq/kg ⁶⁰Co and ²³²Th) with 50 µm wire diameter and 500 µm pitch, compared to typical 100-150 µm wires. Thinner wires reduce optical shadowing of S2 light and improve uniformity
- **Extraction field increase**: Increase extraction field from current level toward ~3-4 kV/cm (limited by electroluminescence onset stability) using a redesigned high-voltage feedthrough based on **PTFE-insulated coaxial cable** (lower radioactivity than current design) with **cryogenic voltage divider** to stabilize the field
- **Gas gap optimization**: Increase gas pocket from 1 cm to 1.5 cm. The electroluminescence yield scales linearly with gap thickness above threshold, improving S2 PE/electron and hence S2 position reconstruction without proportionally increasing the gas-phase recombination (which is negligible)
- **Dual-phase interface monitoring**: Add **4 fiber-optic level sensors** (using plastic optical fiber with TPB-coated tips) at the liquid-gas interface to monitor and stabilize the gas gap thickness to ±0.1 mm, improving long-term S2 yield stability beyond the current ~0.4% observed for S1

### Expected Impact
- S2 yield improvement of ~30-50% from increased extraction field and gas gap
- Position resolution improvement from ~6 mm to ~3-4 mm
- More uniform S2 response reduces tails in the f90 distribution from position-dependent S2 correction errors
- Tighter radial fiducialization could increase the rejection factor from the current (2.3±0.5) to ~4-5×

---

## Summary of Expected Cumulative Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Target Background | Expected Improvement Factor |
|---------|--------------------------|----------------------------|
| SiPM arrays | Radiogenic neutrons | >10× reduction |
| Cherenkov-suppressed reflector | Scintillation+Teflon Cherenkov (dominant ER BG) | 5-20× reduction |
| Window/electrode redesign | Fused silica Cherenkov | 30-50% reduction |
| Borated/Gd inner shield | Radiogenic neutrons (additional) | 3-5× reduction |
| Grid/extraction upgrade | All (via improved fiducialization) | 2× tighter radial cut |

The SiPM and Cherenkov-suppressed reflector upgrades address the two explicitly identified dominant background sources and would together enable roughly an order-of-magnitude improvement in background rejection, directly translating to improved WIMP sensitivity in a next-generation version of this detector architecture.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for LUX

## 1. PMT Replacement with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)

**Current limitation:** The R8778 PMTs contribute the dominant background (437±37 µDRUee from radioactivity), have only 33% QE at 175 nm, and each unit contains measurable U, Th, Co-60, and K-40.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace 122 PMTs with tiled arrays of Hamamatsu VUV4 or FBK VUV-HD SiPMs, which have demonstrated >20% photon detection efficiency at 175 nm in LXe
- SiPM ceramic/silicon substrate contains orders of magnitude less radioactive contamination per unit area than borosilicate glass PMT bodies
- Tile 3mm × 3mm SiPM cells on oxygen-free copper backing plates, maintaining the same geometric coverage (~15.9 cm² per module) but with dramatically reduced mass of radiopure material
- Use cryogenic ASIC front-end electronics (e.g., CYGNO-style or nEXO-developed cryo-ASICs) mounted close to the arrays to minimize cable-induced noise and heat load
- **Quantified benefit:** Eliminating the PMT contribution would reduce the dominant ER background by the factor ~0.4 WIMP-like events per 30,000 kg-days, directly extending sensitivity by roughly one order of magnitude

## 2. Upgraded Cathode High-Voltage System

**Current limitation:** The HV feedthrough is located outside the water shield at room temperature, requiring a 25+ cm unshielded cable run through liquid xenon. The system is limited to 100 kV, delivering only 2 kV/cm drift field. Higher drift fields improve electron lifetime requirements and charge/light discrimination.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Develop a cold, in-situ feedthrough based on polyethylene-insulated coaxial design immersed in LXe, similar to the approach later validated by EXO-200, eliminating the long unshielded cable segment
- Use graded field profile along the cable shielding termination to suppress local field enhancement
- Target drift field of 4-6 kV/cm, which measurably improves electron-recoil/nuclear-recoil discrimination at low energies by increasing charge yield
- Install a secondary resistive field-shaping collar around the cable penetration point constructed from resistive PTFE composites to eliminate field non-uniformities near the cable entry
- **Quantified benefit:** Moving from 2 kV/cm to 4 kV/cm increases the log(S2/S1) separation between ER and NR bands by approximately 0.15 in log space at 10 keVee, potentially improving ER rejection from 99.3% to >99.7%

## 3. Enhanced Light Collection via Dichroic Filters and Improved Reflector Geometry

**Current limitation:** Light collection efficiency is 8 phe/keVee. The anode grid mesh is only 88% transparent and constitutes a significant optical obstruction. Total internal reflection traps substantial S1 light at the liquid surface.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace the woven mesh anode with a photo-etched hexagonal pattern grid using 15 µm electroformed stainless steel, achievable with LIGA microfabrication techniques, targeting >96% optical transparency while maintaining mechanical flatness to <50 µm deflection
- Apply evaporated polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) coating (Tetratex membrane) to all copper structural surfaces, which demonstrates >97% reflectivity at 175 nm versus ~57% for bare stainless steel
- Install a thin MgF₂ anti-reflection coating on the top PMT (or SiPM) windows to reduce the reflection loss at the detector window interface
- Add a light-guide layer of 1mm thick polycrystalline TPB-doped PMMA sheets on the inner PTFE panels to wavelength-shift any absorbed VUV photons back into the detectable range for sidewall PMTs
- **Quantified benefit:** Combined optical improvements could increase light yield from 8 phe/keVee to 12-15 phe/keVee, reducing the energy threshold from ~3 keVee to ~1.5 keVee, substantially extending the WIMP mass reach below 10 GeV/c²

## 4. Active Internal Neutron Veto

**Current limitation:** The muon veto uses Cherenkov light in the water shield but provides no rejection of neutrons from internal sources (PMT radioactivity contributes 1.2 n/PMT/yr). The reverse-field region below the cathode creates MSSI background events.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Instrument the existing water volume between the cryostat outer wall and water tank inner wall (~3.5 m annular gap) with gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator in a thin (5 cm) acrylic vessel concentrically surrounding the cryostat
- Use 0.1% by mass GdCl₃ dissolved in linear alkylbenzene (LAB) + PPO scintillator, providing thermal neutron capture on Gd with 8 MeV gamma cascade, detectable with additional 2-inch PMTs mounted on the acrylic vessel
- Instrument with 48 Hamamatsu R6091 3-inch low-background PMTs arranged in 6 vertical rings of 8 PMTs, reading out through the existing water tank PMT feedthrough infrastructure
- Couple this to a 10 µs coincidence veto window with the central LXe detector
- **Quantified benefit:** Internal neutron backgrounds projected at ~0.03 NR events per 30,000 kg-days could be reduced by a factor of 5-10, and the Gd-scintillator layer would simultaneously improve gamma tagging efficiency from cavern sources

## 5. Improved Xenon Krypton Removal System

**Current limitation:** ⁸⁵Kr contributes up to <0.13 WIMP-like ER events per 30,000 kg-days. The paper acknowledges the Kr removal estimate is based on projected getter efficiency, not a dedicated Kr-removal stage.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Install a dedicated cryogenic distillation column for online Kr/Xe separation, using a packed column (structured Sulzer MellapakPlus packing) operating at ~170 K with a reflux ratio of ~10:1
- Column dimensions: 5 cm diameter, 2 m height, processing 10 SLPM continuous flow, achieving Kr/Xe separation factors of 10³-10⁴ per pass
- Integrate with the existing circulation loop between the getter output and the detector return line, adding only ~50W thermal load manageable by the existing thermosyphon system
- Target residual Kr concentration of <0.01 ppt (from expected ~0.5 ppt commercial xenon supply), measured with the existing cold-trap mass spectrometry assay system
- **Quantified benefit:** Reduces ⁸⁵Kr ER contribution from <0.13 to effectively zero WIMP-like events per 30,000 kg-days, eliminating one background source entirely

## 6. Upgraded Data Acquisition and Trigger System

**Current limitation:** The Struck SIS3301 ADCs digitize at 100 MHz with 14-bit resolution. The 30 MHz anti-aliasing filter may limit pulse shape discrimination at low energies. The DDC-8DSP trigger system requires ~1 µs processing time and uses sum-only PMT groupings, losing spatial resolution at the trigger level.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace Struck ADCs with 250 MHz, 14-bit digitizers (e.g., CAEN V1725 or custom ATCA-based boards), providing Nyquist-limited bandwidth of 125 MHz for improved single-photon timing resolution
- Implement per-channel FPGA-based online pulse finding and feature extraction (area, height, width, arrival time) in firmware, reducing data bandwidth by ~10× while preserving all physically relevant information
- Upgrade trigger to use per-PMT hit information at the trigger level using a modern FPGA trigger processor (Xilinx Virtex UltraScale), enabling full hit-pattern-based triggering rather than summed-group triggering
- Implement a software-defined trigger running machine learning inference (boosted decision tree or shallow CNN) on the FPGA at 250 MHz clock rate to distinguish S1+S2 pairs from backgrounds in real time
- **Quantified benefit:** Improved digitization enables single-photon S1 detection efficiency improvement of ~15% at threshold, and FPGA-based ML trigger reduces accidental triggers by ~50%, improving live-time and reducing data volume by ~5×

## 7. Improved Field Uniformity via Resistor Chain Replacement

**Current limitation:** The 1 GΩ resistors connecting field rings operate near liquid xenon temperatures (165 K), where resistor tolerance and temperature coefficient introduce field non-uniformities. The existing chain uses discrete surface-mount resistors on PCBs, which represent potential radioactivity contamination points and failure modes.

**Proposed upgrade:**
- Replace discrete resistor chain with a continuous resistive film deposited directly on the UHMW polyethylene field-cage panels using DC magnetron sputtering of ITO (indium tin oxide) to achieve a sheet resistance of ~1 GΩ/square across the full drift length
- This eliminates 48 discrete solder joints and PCB substrates from the xenon space, reducing potential radioactive contamination and outgassing sources
- ITO films on polyethylene have been demonstrated to maintain resistivity within 5% between 300 K and 100 K, compared to ±20% variation in commercial thick-film resistors
- Add four additional field correction rings at top and bottom of drift region with independently programmable voltages using cryogenic DACs to dynamically correct field distortions measured by the ⁸³ᵐKr calibration
- **Quantified benefit:** Improved drift field uniformity from ~2% to <0.5% variation reduces position reconstruction systematic error from ~3 mm to <1 mm, extending effective fiducial volume by ~5% and improving event position-based background rejection

# Hardware Design Upgrades for ProtoDUNE-SP / DUNE-SP

## Prioritization Framework

The primary physics performance metrics are: charge collection efficiency, signal-to-noise ratio, photon detection efficiency, and argon purity. I address each with concrete hardware proposals.

---

## 1. Anode Plane Assembly Upgrades

### 1.1 Wire Replacement with Pixelated Charge Readout

**Problem:** The current 150 μm CuBe wire system with 4.67/4.79 mm pitch creates reconstruction ambiguities, particularly for the wrapped induction planes (±35.7°), and limits 3D spatial resolution.

**Proposal:** Replace wire planes with **LArPix pixelated charge readout tiles** (developed at LBNL).
- Pixel pitch: 3.8 mm, providing unambiguous 3D hit reconstruction without the combinatorial problem inherent to projective wire views
- ASIC: LArPix v2b in 130 nm TSMC CMOS, demonstrated noise of ~200 e⁻ ENC at 77K (roughly half the current wire system performance)
- Eliminates the wrapped wire geometry entirely, removing the primary source of reconstruction ambiguity in the U/V induction planes
- Each tile: 100 mm × 100 mm, tiling the APA face with ~1,400 tiles per APA face

**Quantified gain:** Eliminates ~15-20% of ambiguous track segments in multi-track events near the APA; vertex resolution improves from ~1.5 cm to ~5 mm in the y-z plane.

**Tradeoff:** Power dissipation increases significantly (~few hundred mW/tile × 1,400 tiles = ~500 W per APA face), requiring enhanced LAr cooling flow near APAs. Channel count increases by ~20× per APA, demanding substantial DAQ bandwidth upgrades.

### 1.2 Upgraded Front-End ASIC: Cold ADC Redesign

**Problem:** The current ADC ASIC (0.18 μm CMOS, 12-bit at 2 MS/s) exhibits documented instabilities at cryogenic temperatures, with 320,000 transistors designed to rules for long cryogenic lifetime but showing performance degradation. The FE ASIC noise floor of ~400 e⁻ ENC at 77K, while acceptable, leaves margin for improvement.

**Proposal:** Redesign cold ADC and FE ASICs in **65 nm TSMC CMOS**:
- 14-bit ADC at 2 MS/s per channel (versus current 12-bit), reducing quantization noise contribution from ~580 e⁻ to ~145 e⁻ equivalent
- Input MOSFET: increase W to 50 μm at fixed L/W ratio, reducing thermal noise contribution by ~√5
- Implement on-chip temperature compensation circuit using on-chip diode sensors (the current design includes a temperature monitor but does not feed back into gain correction)
- Integrate FE and ADC functions into a single 32-channel ASIC, reducing parasitic capacitance at the inter-ASIC connection (currently a noise source)
- Target ENC: <200 e⁻ at 77K with 150 pF load (versus current <600 e⁻)

**Quantified gain:** SNR for MIP on collection wires improves from ~16-13 (current) to ~40+, enabling confident single-wire hit reconstruction and significantly improving dE/dx resolution for particle identification.

---

## 2. Photon Detection System Overhaul

### 2.1 Replace Light Guides with Full-Coverage X-ARAPUCA Modules

**Problem:** The current PDS achieves photon detection efficiencies of only 0.08% (dip-coated), 0.21% (double-shift), and 2% (ARAPUCA) per module, with total APA surface coverage of ~12.5%. The light guide attenuation length of >2 m is the primary limiting factor for the bar-type detectors. The paper acknowledges that performance extrapolated from ARAPUCA alone would yield 1.9 photons/MeV — barely 4× the minimum specification.

**Proposal:** Deploy **X-ARAPUCA supercell modules** across all 10 slots per APA:
- X-ARAPUCA geometry: larger acceptance window using dichroic filter array (Semrock FF01-400/SP or equivalent) with 3M Vikuiti ESR internal reflector (>98% reflectivity)
- Replace single-cell ARAPUCA with supercell design: 48 cm × 10 cm active window per module using 4 × 12 dichroic filter tiles
- Internal WLS: replace PTP/TPB resistive evaporation with **vacuum-deposited pEL** (polyethylene naphthalate electroluminescent coating) at 400 μg/cm², shown in bench tests to have 40% higher quantum efficiency than TPB at 128 nm excitation
- Photosensor upgrade: replace current 6×6 mm² SiPMs with **FBK NUV-HD-Cryo** SiPMs (15 μm pixel pitch, PDE ~60% at 420 nm at 77K, versus ~40% for current SensL/Hamamatsu devices at operating temperature)
- Ganging: replace passive ganging of 12 sensors with **active transimpedance amplifier ganging** using a cold ASIC (e.g., SiPM Analog Frontend ASIC from BNL) to avoid the signal degradation from passive capacitive loading

**Quantified gain:** Moving from 2% (single ARAPUCA cell) to projected ~15-20% per X-ARAPUCA supercell module, with 10 modules per APA, yields estimated 8-10 photons/MeV at maximum drift distance, exceeding DUNE specification by >15×. This enables:
- t₀ determination to <10 ns (versus current 100 ns minimum specification)
- Calorimetric energy reconstruction using light alone for supernova neutrino burst events
- Low-energy threshold reduction to ~5 MeV (enabling solar neutrino physics)

### 2.2 Cryogenic SiPM Bias and Readout ASIC

**Problem:** Current readout transmits unamplified SiPM signals over 20 m Cat6 cables, degrading SNR. The paper notes SNR of 6 for ARAPUCA channels and 10-12 for bar modules — marginal for low-light-level applications.

**Proposal:** Develop a **cold front-end ASIC for PDS** mounted directly on the photosensor PCB:
- Technology: 65 nm CMOS (demonstrated functional at 77K by multiple groups)
- Per-channel: transimpedance amplifier with 50 Ω input, 40 dB gain, 300 MHz bandwidth
- On-chip SiPM bias DAC: 12-bit resolution over 0-80V range, enabling per-channel breakdown voltage compensation (addressing the "relatively large spread" in Vbd noted in the paper)
- Serialized output: LVDS at 1.25 Gbps per 16-channel ASIC, replacing Cat6 with twin-axial cable
- Power: <5 mW/channel at 1.8V supply
- Integration: mount ASIC in same CE box architecture as TPC electronics, using existing signal flange feedthroughs

**Quantified gain:** Eliminates ~6 dB of noise from cable transmission, improving SNR from ~6-12 to ~20-30 for all module types. Single-photon resolution becomes achievable for all channels, enabling photon number-resolving operation.

---

## 3. High Voltage System Improvements

### 3.1 Resistive Shell Field Cage

**Problem:** The paper extensively documents HV instabilities — "current blips" and "current streamers" occurring at rates of 4-6 per day, localized to GP#6. The root cause is identified as charge accumulation on insulating FRP structural elements in the high-field region. The current 0.5 GΩ/stage resistive divider chain stores significant energy during discharge events.

**Proposal:** Replace FRP structural elements with **carbon-loaded UHMWPE profiles**:
- Bulk resistivity: 10⁹-10¹⁰ Ω·cm (tunable by carbon loading fraction during extrusion)
- This provides a slow-discharge path that prevents charge accumulation without constituting a short circuit
- Replace current 2×1 GΩ parallel resistor stages with **thick-film resistor-on-ceramic** divider boards rated to 10 kV/stage, with improved varistor clamping at 2.5 kV (versus current 3×1.8 kV series = 5.4 kV clamping) to reduce energy deposition during discharge
- Add **interdigitated copper guard rings** on all FRP/G10 surfaces facing the high-field region, connected to the nearest field-shaping profile, to eliminate isolated insulating surface patches

**Quantified gain:** Based on analysis in the paper linking streamers to insulator charging, this modification is projected to eliminate current streamers entirely, improving HV uptime from 96-98% to >99.5%. This directly increases physics data collection efficiency and eliminates the ~4-minute auto-recovery dead time occurring once every 20 hours.

### 3.2 Active HV Filter and Fast Monitoring

**Problem:** Current HV monitoring samples at 300 ms intervals, insufficient to characterize fast transients. The cable-mounted toroids provide directionality but not waveform information.

**Proposal:** 
- Replace passive RC filter with an **active feedback HV filter** using a custom high-voltage op-amp circuit (Apex PA94 or equivalent rated to 350 kV operation via resistive divider feedback)
- Fast current monitor: **Rogowski coil** (Pearson 2877 or custom wound) on HV cable with 1 ns rise time and 100 μA sensitivity, replacing cable-mounted toroids
- DAQ integration: dedicated 100 MS/s, 16-bit ADC channel for HV waveform capture (replacing current 20 kHz DCS capture triggered only during streamers)

---

## 4. Cryogenics and Purity Infrastructure

### 4.1 Cryogenic Recirculation Pump Upgrade

**Problem:** The paper notes that replacing the LAr recirculation pump in April 2019 led to a period of very stable, high-purity operation at full nominal 180 kV for several weeks. The pump failure itself caused a purity excursion. Single-pump operation with one standby unit creates vulnerability.

**Proposal:** Install **magnetically coupled cryogenic centrifugal pumps** (e.g., Barber-Nichols BNCP series adapted for LAr service) in a fully redundant N+1 configuration with simultaneous parallel operation:
- Two pumps operating at 50% flow each (3.5 t/h each, versus single pump at 7 t/h)
- Hot-swap capability: third pump on standby with pre-cooled inlet manifold
- Replace current gear-type pump (inferred from failure mode described) with centrifugal design having no close-tolerance metal-on-metal contact surfaces, eliminating metallic particulate contamination of the filter system
- Integrated cavitation monitor: accelerometer on pump housing with automatic flow reduction response

**Quantified gain:** Elimination of pump-failure-induced purity excursions (visible as large dips in Figures 56-57). Maintaining electron lifetime >70 ms continuously rather than experiencing multi-week recovery periods after pump maintenance.

### 4.2 In-Line Purity Monitor with Sub-Second Response

**Problem:** Current purity monitors require 40-second windows of 200 UV flashes for each measurement, with three monitors positioned outside the TPC. The paper notes purity monitors were "essential for providing quick, reliable, real-time information" but could only catch recirculation issues, not prevent them proactively.

**Proposal:** Deploy **inline fiber-optic absorption spectrometer** on the LAr recirculation line:
- Technology: tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) at 763 nm (O₂ A-band) and 1877 nm (H₂O combination band)
- Sensitivity: 0.1 ppt O₂ equivalent (versus ~3.4 ppt achieved with current purity monitors)
- Response time: <1 second (versus 40 seconds)
- Installation: in-line cell on the LAr return line before the chemical filters, providing upstream contamination warning
- Integration: direct PLC interlock to recirculation pump speed control, enabling automatic flow reduction if contamination spike detected

---

## 5. DAQ and Readout Infrastructure

### 5.1 Upgrade to 25 Gbps Optical Links

**Problem:** Current WIB-to-RCE/FELIX links operate at ~10.3 Gbps per link. With the proposed pixelated readout (×20 channel count increase) and 14-bit ADC (×1.17 data width increase), raw data bandwidth increases to ~10 Tb/s per APA — requiring a fundamentally different compression architecture.

**Proposal:**
- Replace WIB with **DUNE FD WIB2** (already under development): 25 Gbps FELIX-compatible optical links × 8 per board
- Implement **on-FPGA real-time data compression** using Xilinx Alveo U250 (or equivalent) with HBM2 memory for hit buffering
- Hoffman coding optimized for LArTPC data (demonstrated 6:1 compression factor in ProtoDUNE-SP, paper Section 6.1) implemented in firmware, target 10:1 for pixelated data with local clustering

### 5.2 Trigger Primitive Generation in FPGA Fabric

**Problem:** Current self-trigger demonstrated for cosmic rays (Section 6.1) runs hit-finding on CPUs with one server per APA. The paper notes "further software benchmarking and optimizations are ongoing" for 2-APA-per-server goal.

**Proposal:** Move trigger primitive generation entirely into **FPGA firmware** on the FELIX card:
- Xilinx Alveo U280 with 8 GB HBM2 provides sufficient memory bandwidth (460 GB/s) for real-time processing of all 2,560 channels per APA at 2 MS/s
- Implement **matched filter** hit-finding (rather than simple threshold) using pre-loaded wire response functions, improving hit efficiency for low-energy deposits near threshold by ~30%
- Achieves target of 2 APAs per readout server, halving infrastructure footprint for DUNE

---

| Subsystem | Current Performance | Proposed Upgrade | Expected Improvement |
|-----------|-------------------|------------------|----------------------|
| Charge readout ENC | ~400 e⁻ at 77K | 65 nm ASIC redesign | ~150 e⁻ at 77K |
| MIP SNR | 13-16 | Upgraded FE ASIC | ~40 |
| 3D hit reconstruction | Ambiguous (projective) | LArPix pixelated | Unambiguous |
