# Hardware Design Upgrades for a ~50 kg Two-Phase LAr TPC Dark Matter Detector

## Framing the Problem

Physics performance in this context is dominated by four coupled figures of merit: **background rejection efficiency**, **energy threshold**, **fiducial mass fraction**, and **nuclear recoil detection efficiency**. I'll organize upgrades by which bottleneck they primarily address, with realistic technology choices.

---

## 1. Light Detection System — The Highest-Leverage Upgrade

### Current Limitation
3-inch PMTs at this scale typically achieve ~5–8 photoelectrons/keVee (PE/keVee) at the photocathode, setting the energy threshold and S1 pulse-shape discrimination (PSD) capability at low energies. PSD in LAr depends critically on resolving the fast (τ₁ ≈ 6 ns) and slow (τ₃ ≈ 1.6 μs) scintillation components; statistical photon counting at low energies is the fundamental limit on the PSD figure of merit f₉₀.

### Specific Upgrades

**1a. Replace PMTs with cryogenic Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)**

- **Technology**: Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) RGB-HD or NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs, operated at ~87 K. These achieve photon detection efficiency (PDE) of **50–55% at 128 nm** (the LAr VUV emission peak) when paired with appropriate wavelength shifter, versus ~25–30% quantum efficiency for a typical 3-inch cryogenic PMT bialkali photocathode.
- **Configuration**: Tile arrays of 6×6 mm² or 10×10 mm² SiPM cells on FR4 or silicon substrates with embedded cryogenic front-end ASICs (e.g., the **ABCD3T/LArASIC lineage**, or purpose-designed chips such as the SiPM signal processor used by DarkSide-20k's Proto-DUNE-inspired readout).
- **Wavelength shifter**: Evaporated **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB)** on acrylic or directly on SiPM surfaces at 1–2 mg/cm² areal density; recent work shows **pTP + TPB bilayer** coatings can push re-emission efficiency above 1.2× standard TPB alone.
- **Quantitative impact**: Doubling PDE from ~25% to ~50% roughly doubles detected PE/keVee. Moving from ~6 to ~12 PE/keVee drops the S1-based threshold from ~30 keV_nr toward ~15 keV_nr and dramatically improves f₉₀ (the PSD separation power) at sub-50 PE signal levels — the critical regime for WIMP masses below 20 GeV.

**1b. High-reflectivity PTFE inner surfaces with optimized geometry**

- Replace machined PTFE with **expanded PTFE (ePTFE, e.g., Chemours Teflon HS series)**, which achieves reflectivity >97% at 420 nm (post-TPB emission wavelength) versus ~93–95% for standard PTFE. The rough surface structure also improves angular averaging.
- Add a **VUV-grade ESR (Enhanced Specular Reflector) foil** (3M Vikuiti or equivalent) behind the TPB-coated cathode and field-shaping rings to recapture otherwise lost photons.
- Simulate with GEANT4/RAT-PAC to optimize aspect ratio of TPC (height:diameter closer to 1:1 maximizes photon solid-angle capture in top/bottom arrays).

---

## 2. Electric Field System — Threshold and Fiducial Volume

### Current Limitation
At ~50 kg scale, achieving a uniform drift field across the full volume is difficult. Non-uniformities cause position-dependent S2 yield and S1/S2 ratio, degrading fiducial volume definition and the S2-based single-electron detection needed for sub-keV sensitivity.

### Specific Upgrades

**2a. Resistive field cage with embedded current monitoring**

- Replace the standard stainless-steel or copper Kapton-laminate ring ladder with a **custom-printed resistive divider on PTFE-supported alumina ceramic rods** using thick-film ruthenium oxide (RuO₂) resistors. These are radiation-hard, cryogenically stable (drift <0.1% over thermal cycles), and allow individual ring voltage monitoring.
- Target field uniformity: **ΔE/E < 0.5%** over the fiducial volume, enabling position reconstruction (using S2 hit pattern on SiPM array) to better than 3 mm in x-y and 1 mm in z (from drift time).
- **Impact**: Allows fiducial cuts at <5 mm from TPC walls rather than the typical ~10–15 mm, recovering 10–15% of active mass as fiducial mass.

**2b. Improved cathode and anode grid design**

- **Cathode**: Electroformed nickel mesh with 50 μm wire, 0.5 mm pitch (90%+ optical transparency), tensioned to <10 μm flatness to prevent local field distortions.
- **Anode grid**: Stainless steel or titanium wire mesh at the same specification. The critical parameter is the **liquid-gas interface stability** — use an active level control system with a capacitance sensor (parallel-plate geometry, 1 pF/mm precision) feeding a proportional valve on the argon supply line, maintaining the interface position to ±100 μm.
- **Gate grid**: Insert a dedicated gate electrode between liquid surface and anode, with independently adjustable voltage, to allow separate optimization of extraction efficiency and electron multiplication gain in the gas phase.
- Extraction efficiency from liquid to gas improves from typically 60–80% to >95% with field >3 kV/cm at the interface; the gate allows this while keeping drift field independent.

---

## 3. Argon Purity and Recirculation — Electron Lifetime

### Current Limitation
Electronegative impurities (O₂, H₂O at ppb level) attach drifting electrons, reducing S2 yield from deep events disproportionately. At 50 kg, typical drift lengths are 30–50 cm; achieving >1 ms electron lifetime requires sustained sub-ppb O₂-equivalent contamination.

### Specific Upgrades

**3a. Continuous gas-phase recirculation with SAES MonoTorr/Entegris hot getter**

- Use a **Entegris MGTS-902F or SAES PS4-MT15** hot metal getter purifier in the gas recirculation loop at 350°C, capable of reducing O₂ and H₂O to <1 ppt.
- Flow rate: size for complete gas volume exchange every 2–4 hours (typically 5–15 SLPM for this detector size).
- Add an **inline purity monitor** (a small standalone LAr drift cell with UV LED ionization source and sensitive current preamplifier, sensitivity ~10 nA, reading electron lifetime continuously) — this is standard in liquid noble technology (as used by MicroBooNE) but critical for continuous feedback control.

**3b. Underground Argon (UAr) as target material**

- This is already baseline for DarkSide-class experiments but worth stating explicitly: source argon from underground CO₂ wells (e.g., Cortez, CO or Thar Desert sources) to reduce ³⁹Ar content from ~1 Bq/kg (atmospheric) to <0.73 mBq/kg (measured in DarkSide-50). 
- At 50 kg, atmospheric argon gives ~50 Bq of ³⁹Ar beta events, consuming DAQ bandwidth and causing pileup that degrades PSD at rates >100 Hz. UAr reduces this to <40 mBq, enabling clean single-event analysis.
- **If UAr is not already in the baseline**, this is arguably the single most impactful upgrade — it reduces the dominant ER background by >3 orders of magnitude.

---

## 4. Neutron Veto Upgrade — Background Rejection

### Current Limitation
A liquid scintillator neutron veto typically achieves 95–97% efficiency for neutrons producing a nuclear recoil in the TPC, but the key failure modes are: (a) neutron capture gamma escape, (b) low-energy neutron thermalization outside the veto, and (c) incomplete solid-angle coverage.

### Specific Upgrades

**4a. Gadolinium-doped liquid scintillator**

- Dope the existing liquid scintillator with **0.1–0.3% Gd by mass** (as gadolinium 2-ethylhexanoate or Gd-DZ complex for chemical stability). The ¹⁵⁷Gd thermal neutron capture cross-section is 255,000 barns; capture produces an 8 MeV gamma cascade detectable as a >3 MeV delayed coincidence.
- This changes the veto strategy from prompt-only to **prompt + delayed coincidence**, reducing veto threshold and increasing efficiency from ~95% to **>99%** for thermalized neutrons.
- Requires upgrading veto PMTs to handle the additional Gd-capture gamma rate — **Hamamatsu R7081** (10-inch) or equivalent cryogenics-tolerant units, but at room temperature this is less constrained.

**4b. Boron-loaded outer water shield layer**

- Add a **10 cm boron-loaded polyethylene (BPE, 5% B by mass)** layer between the liquid scintillator vessel and the rock overburden, or as an inner liner if geometry allows. This thermalizes fast neutrons before they enter the Gd-LS, increasing capture probability substantially for neutrons entering from outside.
- Alternative: **Boron-10 loaded scintillator tiles** (e.g., PROSPECT-style ⁶LiF:ZnS panels) as a dedicated thermal neutron veto at the inner surface of the water shield.

**4c. Veto PMT upgrade with waveform digitization**

- Replace simple discriminator-based veto DAQ with **250 MHz FADCs** (e.g., CAEN V1730) reading SiPM-based or upgraded PMT signals, enabling offline energy reconstruction and position reconstruction in the veto for better background discrimination and neutron directionality constraints.

---

## 5. Data Acquisition and Triggering — Threshold Optimization

### Specific Upgrades

**5a. Dark-noise-limited single-photon trigger**

- Implement a **hardware coincidence trigger** requiring simultaneous hits in ≥3 SiPMs within a 100 ns window for S1 detection. With SiPM dark count rates of ~100 Hz/mm² at 87 K (dominated by correlated avalanches), this suppresses accidental triggers by >10⁵ vs. single-channel threshold, enabling a **sub-1 keV_ee energy threshold** while keeping trigger rate manageable (<10 Hz physics trigger rate).

**5b. FPGA-based online pulse shape discrimination**

- Deploy **Xilinx Ultrascale+ or Intel Stratix-class FPGAs** with embedded real-time f₉₀ calculation on streaming 250 MHz ADC data. Pre-classify events online into ER/NR candidates, enabling selective readout and reducing storage requirements by 10–100×, which allows lower trigger thresholds without DAQ saturation.

**5c. Zero-length encoding with lossless waveform compression**

- Implement **Huffman or LZ4 compression** on FPGA before data transfer, preserving full waveform information (needed for PSD) while reducing bandwidth by 3–5×.

---

## 6. Radiopurity Upgrades — Internal Backgrounds

**6a. SiPM substrate and PCB material selection**

- The principal new internal background source when switching to SiPMs is the PCB substrate. Use **Cirlex (polyimide) or Parylene-coated alumina** substrates with U/Th content <10 ppt by mass (measured by ICP-MS before installation). Avoid standard FR4, which typically contains 1–10 ppb U/Th.
- Screen all SiPM tiles with **germanium gamma spectroscopy** (Canfranc or Gran Sasso underground HPGe counters) before installation.

**6b. Electropolished stainless steel field cage components**

- All internal metal parts electropolished to Ra < 0.2 μm and passivated; measured for ²²⁶Ra and ²²⁸Ra by mass spectrometry to <1 μBq/kg.
- Replace any brass or bronze components (common sources of ²¹⁰Pb) with **grade 316L stainless steel** or titanium.

**6c. Surface cleanliness protocol**

- Establish a **Class 100 cleanroom assembly environment** with continuous particle monitoring, using only UHP-N₂ purge during installation. All internal surfaces cleaned by ultrasonic bath in sequence: DI water → 10% HNO₃ → isopropanol → dry N₂ blow-off.

---

## Summary Table: Expected Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Metric Improved | Expected Gain |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement (PDE 25%→50%) | Energy threshold, PSD at low E | Threshold halved; f₉₀ improved 2–5σ at 50 PE |
| TPB bilayer + ePTFE reflectors | Light yield | +20–30% detected PE |
| Underground Argon (if not present) | ER background rate | ×1000 reduction in ³⁹Ar |
| Gate grid + extraction optimization | S2 yield, S2 threshold | Single electron detection efficiency >80% |
| Resistive field cage + level control | Fiducial mass, position resolution | +10–15% fiducial mass recovery |
| Continuous getter purification | Electron lifetime | >3 ms lifetime, uniform S2(z) |
| Gd-doped LS veto | Neutron background rejection | >99% neutron veto efficiency |
| SiPM coincidence trigger | Energy threshold | Sub-1 keV_ee analysis threshold |
| Radiopure SiPM PCB substrates | Internal gamma/alpha backgrounds | Dominant new background source controlled |

---

## Priority Ordering

If resources are constrained, the order of implementation should be:

1. **UAr procurement** (if not already baseline) — removes dominant background class entirely
2. **SiPM replacement** — enables the low-energy physics program
3. **Gd-LS veto** — controls the next-dominant background (radiogenic neutrons)
4. **Getter purification system** — enables uniform full-volume fiducial definition
5. **Gate grid + level control** — recovers S2 efficiency and single-electron capability
6. **Radiopurity screening program** — enables systematics to be understood at the required sensitivity

The combination of SiPMs with UAr and an optimized PSD analysis should allow this detector to reach **WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross sections of ~10⁻⁴⁴ cm² at 100 GeV WIMP mass**, approaching the neutrino floor for argon targets at this exposure scale.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Heavy-Water Cherenkov Solar Neutrino Detector

## Framing the Performance Metric

The primary physics performance goals are:
- **Energy threshold** (access lower-energy solar neutrinos, especially *pp* chain)
- **Energy resolution** (distinguish neutrino flavors, measure spectral distortions)
- **Direction and vertex resolution** (background rejection, day/night asymmetry)
- **NC/CC/ES separation** (flavor decomposition)
- **Background rejection** (radioactive, cosmogenic, reactor)

Each upgrade is evaluated against these axes.

---

## 1. Photosensor Replacement: High-QE Large-Area PMTs → LAPPDs or High-QE MCP-PMTs

### Current Limitation
Standard 8" or 20" PMTs (e.g., Hamamatsu R1408, R3600) have:
- Peak quantum efficiency ~25%
- Transit time spread (TTS) ~1.5–3 ns
- Limited photocoverage per unit without prohibitive cost

### Proposed Upgrade

**Replace or supplement with 8×8 cm² Large-Area Picosecond Photodetectors (LAPPDs)**
- Microchannel plate architecture; commercially available from Incom Inc.
- **QE: 30–36%** (bialkali photocathode with ALD treatment)
- **TTS: ~70 ps** (vs. ~1.5 ns for standard PMTs) — factor ~20 improvement
- **Position resolution within tile: ~1 mm** enabling sub-cm photon hit localization

*Alternatively:* **Hamamatsu R12860 or R14688 box-and-line 20" PMTs**
- QE: ~31% with ultra-bialkali (UBA) photocathode
- TTS: ~1.1 ns — already deployed in KM3NeT/JUNO
- Immediate, proven technology with manageable cost scaling

### Physics Impact
- Sub-nanosecond timing → vertex resolution improves from ~15 cm to **<5 cm** at 5 MeV
- Better vertex → tighter fiducial volume cuts → lower threshold access
- Cherenkov ring reconstruction sharpened: **direction resolution ~5° → ~2°**

---

## 2. Increased Photocoverage: Dense Tiling with Concentrators

### Current Limitation
SNO achieved ~54% photocoverage with 9456 × 8" PMTs. Coverage directly limits photoelectron yield and thus energy resolution.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Winston cone light concentrators on all PMTs**
- Compound parabolic concentrators (CPCs) in UV-transparent acrylic
- Effective photocoverage increase: **54% → ~80%** without additional PMT count
- Wavelength-shifting (WLS) coating on concentrator inner surface using **tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB)** or **bis-MSB** — shifts 200–280 nm Cherenkov UV photons (below PMT sensitivity) into 400–430 nm detection band
- Net effective QE improvement: ~15–20% additional photon collection

**Combined with higher-QE PMTs:**
- Photoelectron yield at 5 MeV: ~8 PE/MeV (SNO) → **~35–50 PE/MeV**
- Energy resolution: ~6.5% at 1 MeV → **~3.0% at 1 MeV**

---

## 3. Water/Heavy Water Purification: Ultralow Radioactivity Target

### Current Limitation
SNO achieved U/Th concentrations of ~10⁻¹⁴ g/g in D₂O. The threshold for solar *pp* neutrinos (~0.4 MeV endpoint for *pep* at 1.44 MeV) requires radiopurity ~100× better.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Multi-stage purification loop:**

1. **Reverse osmosis (RO) + electrodeionization (EDI):** continuous loop, removes ionic impurities to <0.1 ppt level
2. **Ultralow-background nitrogen sparging:** removes dissolved Rn-222 to **<1 μBq/m³** (vs. SNO's ~2 mBq/m³)
   - Use deep-underground N₂ from liquid nitrogen dewars (cosmogenic-free)
3. **UV photo-oxidation + ion exchange columns:** removes organic carbon that can host Ra/Pb daughters
4. **Membrane degassing modules** (hollow-fiber PTFE membranes): continuous online Rn removal
5. **Online ICP-MS monitoring** with <0.1 fg/g sensitivity for U/Th — real-time radiopurity assay during operation
6. **Dedicated radon-free clean room** for water-contact component assembly

**Target specification:** 
- U, Th: <10⁻¹⁵ g/g (10× better than SNO)
- Rn-222: <100 μBq/m³
- ²⁰⁸Tl gamma background: negligible above 2 MeV

---

## 4. Wavelength-Shifting Scintillator Additive: "Hybrid" Cherenkov-Scintillation Mode

### Proposed Upgrade

**Dissolve slow WLS dye (e.g., 2,5-diphenyloxazole / PPO at ~1 mg/L, or perylene-based dyes)**

This converts the detector to a **hybrid Cherenkov + scintillation** instrument:

- Scintillation photons (isotropic, late) provide **energy resolution ~2%/√E** at low energy
- Cherenkov photons (directional, early, ~1–3 ns) preserved for **directionality** using LAPPD timing to separate the two populations
- Technique demonstrated in **SNO+** (linear alkylbenzene + PPO) and **Borexino**

**Key technical requirement:** The LAPPD TTS of ~70 ps is essential — it enables Cherenkov/scintillation separation even with ~few-ns scintillation decay time

**Threshold impact:** Access to **pp neutrinos at 0.4–0.9 MeV** using scintillation yield (~10,000 photons/MeV in LAB+PPO), while retaining NC sensitivity via deuteron breakup

*Note: This changes D₂O chemistry — requires validation of NC cross-section stability and quenching factors*

---

## 5. External Veto and Shielding Upgrade

### Current Limitation
Cosmogenic muon spallation (¹²B, ¹²N, ¹⁶N) and fast neutrons produce irreducible backgrounds even at 2 km.w.e. depth.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Active water Cherenkov muon veto:**
- 3-meter water buffer between inner vessel and cavity wall instrumented with additional PMTs
- **WLS-coated acrylic panels** (EJ-286 or BC-444) on rock face — wavelength-shifts scintillation from rock interactions into detectable range
- **Segmented muon tracker:** 4 layers of resistive plate chambers (RPCs) or scintillator paddles above the outer vessel
- Combined tagging efficiency target: **>99.99%** for through-going muons

**Veto logic:**
- 10 ms veto window after tagged muon for spallation isotope decay
- Spatial correlation: only veto fiducial region within 2 m of reconstructed muon track

**Shielding addition:**
- Additional 2 m of ultra-pure H₂O (not D₂O) outer shield: attenuates external gamma flux from rock by factor ~10⁶ for 2.6 MeV ²⁰⁸Tl line

---

## 6. Acrylic Vessel and Structural Upgrades

### Current Limitation
The SNO acrylic vessel (AV) outgassed trace U/Th and Rn, and its 5.5 cm thickness created gamma backgrounds.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Ultra-low background acrylic (ULBA):**
- Specially formulated PMMA with U/Th < 10⁻¹² g/g (commercial vendors: Reynolds Polymer, Spartech)
- Reduce AV thickness by 20% where structural analysis allows
- **ALD (atomic layer deposition) barrier coating** on inner AV surface: Al₂O₃ or TiO₂ at ~10 nm thickness, proven Rn emanation barrier (factor ~100 reduction from surfaces)

**Geodesic support structure:**
- Replace steel PSUP with **carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP)** tubing
- Lower U/Th content than steel: CFRP at ~0.1 ppb vs. steel at ~0.3 ppb
- Lower mass → reduced gamma shadowing and PMT absorption
- Higher stiffness/mass ratio: maintains PMT position accuracy to **<1 mm** under hydrostatic load

---

## 7. Data Acquisition and Trigger: Low-Threshold DAQ

### Current Limitation
SNO's hardware trigger threshold was ~17 PMT hits (~3.5 MeV equivalent) to suppress dark noise triggers.

### Proposed Upgrade

**Fully digital, triggerless DAQ:**
- **Custom ASIC front-end boards** (e.g., based on WA105/DUNE cold ADC architecture adapted for warm operation): continuous digitization at 1 GS/s, 12-bit
- **FPGA-based waveform capture** (e.g., Xilinx UltraScale+ or Intel Stratix 10) per PMT channel: stores full waveform, timestamp to **<100 ps** precision
- Zero-suppression at channel level: transmit only above-threshold samples
- **Software trigger** in GPU farm: reconstruct events offline, threshold lowerable to **5–8 PMT hits** (~0.5–1 MeV)
- Eliminates trigger-level energy threshold — critical for pp solar neutrino access

**Online calibration injection:**
- Dedicated **picosecond laser** (PiLas, 375 nm, <50 ps pulse width) via fiber optic to center of detector: continuous PMT gain and TTS monitoring without dead time
- **Deployed ²⁴Na source** (gamma source) on cable system for energy scale calibration at known energies

---

## 8. Neutron Detection Enhancement (NC Channel)

### Unique to D₂O: Neutron Capture on Deuterium

SNO added NaCl (²³⁵Cl neutron capture) and ³He proportional counters. 

### Proposed Upgrade

**Gadolinium loading at 0.1% by mass (as Gd₂(SO₄)₃):**
- Gd thermal neutron capture cross-section: **49,000 barns** vs. D: 0.5 mb — factor ~10⁸ improvement
- Capture time: ~20 μs (vs. ~5 ms on D)
- Released gamma cascade: **8 MeV total** (multiple gammas) vs. 6.25 MeV on D
- Detection efficiency for NC neutrons: **~90%** vs. ~30% with NaCl

**Technical challenges to solve:**
- Gd can precipitate → use Gd-DTPA chelate (water-soluble, chemically stable, as used in **Super-K-Gd / SK-VII** currently operating)
- Validate chemical compatibility with D₂O (isotope exchange negligible at 0.1%)
- Re-characterize optical attenuation length at loaded concentration: measure in **5-liter prototype cell** before scale-up

**Physics gain:** NC/CC ratio measured with **3× smaller systematic uncertainty** — directly sharpens neutrino flavor mixing measurement

---

## Summary Table

| Upgrade | Primary Gain | Key Technology |
|---|---|---|
| LAPPD / UBA PMTs | Vertex, direction, threshold | LAPPDs (Incom), R12860 |
| Light concentrators + WLS | Photon yield, energy resolution | Acrylic CPCs + TPB coating |
| D₂O purification loop | Background, threshold | RO+EDI+membrane degassing |
| Hybrid scintillator mode | pp neutrino access | LAB+PPO at 1 mg/L |
| Muon veto + RPC tracker | Spallation rejection | RPC + WLS-coated panels |
| ULBA + ALD coating | Vessel backgrounds | PMMA + ALD barrier |
| CFRP PSUP | Position accuracy, mass | Carbon fiber tubes |
| Triggerless DAQ + GPU | Low-threshold operation | 1 GS/s ASIC + FPGA |
| Gd loading (0.1% Gd-DTPA) | NC efficiency | Gd-DTPA chelate |

---

## Prioritization

**Highest leverage, implementable now:**
1. **UBA PMTs (R12860) + Winston cones** — single largest improvement in photoelectron yield
2. **Gd-DTPA loading** — proven in Super-K, directly improves flagship NC measurement
3. **Triggerless DAQ** — enables threshold reduction without changing detector medium

**Transformative but higher risk:**
4. **LAPPDs** — if yield and reliability scale to full array (~10,000 channels), timing resolution revolutionizes event reconstruction
5. **Hybrid scintillation mode** — accesses entirely new physics (pp neutrinos) but requires full recharacterization of NC response

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a ~50 kg Two-Phase Liquid Argon TPC

## Context and Performance-Limiting Factors

Before proposing upgrades, the primary physics performance metrics for this class of detector are:
- **Nuclear recoil detection threshold** (drives low-mass dark matter reach)
- **Electron/nuclear recoil discrimination** (S2/S1 ratio and pulse shape discrimination, PSD)
- **Fiducial mass fraction** (surface/bulk event rejection)
- **Background rejection efficiency** (gammas, neutrons, surface events, $^{39}$Ar)

The dominant limitations in a ~50 kg two-phase LAr TPC at this scale are: (1) photon collection efficiency limiting PSD performance at low energy, (2) single-phase $^{39}$Ar backgrounds, (3) electroluminescence non-uniformity degrading S2 resolution, (4) cathode/field cage surface backgrounds, and (5) neutron backgrounds leaking the veto. I address each with specific technologies.

---

## 1. Photon Detection System — Highest Priority Upgrade

### Problem
PSD in LAr relies on the ratio of prompt (τ~6 ns, singlet) to late (τ~1.5 μs, triplet) 128 nm VUV scintillation photons. At energies near threshold (~few keV_nr), statistical fluctuations in detected photon number dominate PSD figure-of-merit:

$$\text{PSD FOM} \propto \sqrt{N_\text{det}}$$

A typical 3-inch PMT array with PTFE-lined walls achieves ~5–8 photoelectrons/keV_ee. PSD leakage becomes unacceptable below ~30–50 keV_ee, limiting nuclear recoil threshold.

### Specific Upgrades

**1a. Replace or supplement 3-inch PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) in a tile geometry**

- Use **Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-Cryo SiPMs** (or Hamamatsu VUV4 MPPC, S/N S13370-6152CN) — these are specifically characterized for LAr temperatures (87 K) and have:
  - PDE ~50% at 420 nm (post-wavelength-shifting), versus ~30% QE for typical 3-inch PMTs
  - Low dark count rate at 87 K (~0.1 Hz/mm² for FBK NUV-HD-Cryo)
  - No magnetic sensitivity, lower radioactive content per unit area
- Deploy as **ARACON-style or DUNE-SBND tile modules**: tile the entire top and bottom surfaces with 6×6 mm² SiPM cells mounted on low-radioactivity PCBs (e.g., Rogers 4350B with screened copper, or custom Cirlex laminates)
- **Target geometry**: 100% photocathode coverage fraction on both endcaps rather than the ~30–40% typical with 3-inch PMT packing

**1b. Wavelength-shifting strategy improvement**

Current practice (TPB evaporated on PTFE reflector and/or PMT windows) has irreproducibility in coating thickness and VUV absorption length. Replace with:
- **Tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) dip-coated on specular ESR (3M VM2000 multilayer polymer) reflector foils** lining the cylindrical barrel — specular rather than diffuse reflection reduces photon path length and thus reabsorption
- Alternatively, **PEN (polyethylene naphthalate) structural tiles** as a self-wavelength-shifting structural component (emission peak ~425 nm, tested at CERN for LAr); eliminates TPB coating process variability
- For SiPM tiles, coat directly with **evaporated TPB (1–2 mg/cm²)** in a dedicated vacuum chamber with in-situ thickness monitoring by quartz crystal microbalance

**Expected gain**: Photon yield improvement from ~7 to ~15–20 PE/keV_ee, pushing PSD threshold to ~10–15 keV_ee for nuclear recoils.

---

## 2. Underground Argon ($^{39}$Ar Depletion) — Critical for Low-Threshold Operation

### Problem
Atmospheric argon contains $^{39}$Ar at ~1 Bq/kg (beta emitter, endpoint 565 keV). At 50 kg, this is ~50 Bq of activity. Even with excellent PSD, pile-up below ~100 μs inhibits low-energy threshold and creates accidental coincidences in S1-S2 pairing.

### Specific Upgrade

**Use Urania/Aria-processed underground argon (UAr)**

- **Urania plant** (Cortez, Colorado, operated by DarkSide collaboration): extracts argon from CO₂ wells where cosmogenic production is suppressed; $^{39}$Ar depletion factor demonstrated >1400× relative to atmospheric argon (≲0.73 mBq/kg)
- **Aria isotopic separation column** (Sardinia): cryogenic distillation further purifies to potentially reach depletion >10⁴×
- For a new instrument at this scale, procuring **~100 kg of UAr** (accounting for inactive regions) is now technically feasible given ongoing production for DarkSide-20k
- **Procurement path**: contact INFN/Princeton DarkSide consortium for UAr allocation or establish column-sharing agreement

**Expected gain**: Reduces $^{39}$Ar rate from ~50 Bq to <35 mBq in the active volume, enabling much lower thresholds and eliminating pile-up as a practical concern.

---

## 3. Electroluminescence Region — S2 Uniformity and Amplification

### Problem
S2 signals are generated in the ~5–10 mm gas gap above the liquid surface. Non-uniformities in the electric field at the liquid-gas interface, grid wire sag, and surface tension effects produce position-dependent S2 yield variations that degrade energy resolution and create tails that mimic low-energy signals.

### Specific Upgrades

**3a. Anode and gate grid replacement with etched copper-on-Kapton mesh electrodes**

- Replace tensioned wire grids (typical 100–200 μm LCP or stainless wire, 2.5–5 mm pitch) with **photolithographically etched grids on thin (25–50 μm) Kapton-copper laminate**
- Manufacturers: **Tech-Etch Inc.** or **Fotofab** can produce hexagonal-pattern etched grids with 50–100 μm feature size and <10 μm positional tolerance across 30 cm diameter
- Benefits: eliminates wire sag (dominant cause of field non-uniformity in large-format wire grids), enables tighter pitch (improving optical transparency while maintaining field uniformity), and provides reproducible geometry
- Frame the grid on a low-radioactivity titanium or PEEK ring support with controlled tension

**3b. Liquid level control with sub-millimeter precision**

- The electroluminescence yield depends sensitively on the extraction field, which is set by the liquid level relative to the gate grid. Fluctuations >0.5 mm cause measurable S2 gain drift.
- Install a **closed-loop capacitive liquid level sensor** (custom parallel-plate capacitor using PTFE-coated electrodes, read out by a **Andeen-Hagerling AH2700A** capacitance bridge or equivalent) with feedback to a **piezoelectric flow valve** (e.g., **Burkert 6624** series) on the recirculation line
- Target: liquid level stability ±100 μm over weeks-long runs

**3c. Diving-bell geometry for gas gap stabilization**

- Enclose the gas gap region in an inner "diving bell" structure (PTFE or ultra-pure aluminum) that is pressure-controlled independently of the main vessel, decoupling liquid level from atmospheric pressure fluctuations
- Demonstrated in XENON100 and DarkSide-50; straightforward to implement at 50 kg scale

**Expected gain**: S2 energy resolution improvement from ~15% to ~5% FWHM at 83 keV_r, and reduction of S2-based position reconstruction bias near the top surface.

---

## 4. Electric Field Cage — Uniformity and Radioactive Background Reduction

### Problem
Resistive/wire field cage structures are a major source of gamma and neutron backgrounds, and field non-uniformity distorts fiducialization.

### Specific Upgrades

**4a. Transparent resistive field cage using diamond-like carbon (DLC) coated fused silica rings**

- Replace metal field-shaping rings + resistor chain with **DLC-coated (sheet resistance ~10¹⁰ Ω/□) fused silica cylinders or rings**
- DLC coating by **sp3 Diamond Technologies** or **Fraunhofer IST** can achieve uniform resistivity, chemical stability in LAr, and near-optical transparency at 420 nm (after WLS conversion)
- This eliminates discrete metal rings (which shadow photons, reducing light yield by ~10–20% in barrel region) and removes the resistor chain (a source of heat and potential failure points)
- Alternative: **resistive Kapton** sheets with controlled bulk resistivity (e.g., DuPont Kapton HN loaded with carbon black, surface resistivity tunable 10⁸–10¹² Ω/□)

**4b. Low-radioactivity cathode**

- Replace stainless steel cathode mesh with **electroformed copper mesh** (oxygen-free high-conductivity copper, electroformed to minimize U/Th contamination, specification: <0.1 mBq/kg ²²⁶Ra)
- Source: **Precison Eforming LLC** or in-house electroforming following MAJORANA/GERDA protocols
- Alternatively, **aluminized Mylar** stretched cathode — extremely low mass, though mechanical stability must be validated for large-diameter operation

**Expected gain**: 20–40% improvement in light yield in the barrel region (DLC); factor 2–5 reduction in cathode-originating gamma backgrounds.

---

## 5. Neutron Veto System — Enhancement

### Problem
Liquid scintillator (LS) neutron vetoes at this scale typically achieve ~95% efficiency for neutrons that scatter in the active volume, but suffer from: limited solid-angle coverage near penetrations (cryostat neck, signal feedthroughs), PMT radioactivity, and gammas misidentified as neutron captures.

### Specific Upgrades

**5a. Gadolinium-loaded liquid scintillator**

- Replace unloaded LS (e.g., PC+PPO or LAB+PPO) with **0.1% Gd-loaded LAB-based scintillator** (Gd-LS as used in RENO, Daya Bay, PROSPECT)
- Gd thermal neutron capture cross-section 49,000 barns versus 0.33 barns for ¹H; reduces capture time from ~200 μs to ~30 μs and produces a 8 MeV gamma cascade (easily distinguished)
- Gd loading at 0.1% wt using **Gd(thd)₃ or Gd-dpm** organic complexes is well-characterized and stable over multi-year operation
- Source: **Sigma-Aldrich** gadolinium 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-3,5-heptanedionate complex, or synthesis following RENO/Daya Bay recipes

**5b. Veto PMT replacement with high-QE, low-background types**

- Replace standard bialkali veto PMTs with **Hamamatsu R5912-100 (10-inch, 35% QE)** or, if budget allows, **NNVT MCP-PMT GDB-6201** low-radioactivity versions with measured U/Th <5 ppb (versus ~100 ppb for standard PMTs)
- Alternative: instrument the LS veto with **SiPM modules** (same FBK NUV-HD-Cryo as above) operated at room temperature on fiber light guides to move electronics outside the veto volume, eliminating PMT radioactivity contribution to the veto itself

**5c. Active muon veto integration**

- Add a **thin (2 cm) Bicron BC-408 plastic scintillator** layer on the outer surface of the LS veto vessel, read out by **Hamamatsu R7081** PMTs, providing muon tagging with >99.9% efficiency to reject cosmogenic neutron events that beat the LS veto timing

**Expected gain**: Neutron veto efficiency improvement from ~95% to ~99.5% for minimum-ionizing neutrons in the relevant energy range (1–10 MeV); cosmogenic neutron rejection essentially complete.

---

## 6. Signal Readout Electronics — Enabling Low Threshold

### Problem
With the photon yield improvements above, the bottleneck shifts to electronics: baseline noise, trigger threshold, and digitization dynamic range.

### Specific Upgrades

**6a. Custom cryogenic ASIC preamplifiers for SiPMs**

- Deploy **LArASIC or SLAC-designed cryogenic SiPM readout ASICs** (e.g., the 64-channel LArPix ASIC developed for DUNE, or CAEN's CMOS-based cold front-end)
- Operating preamplifiers at 87 K reduces Johnson noise by ~factor 3 and eliminates long cable capacitance (dominant noise source in room-temperature readout schemes)
- Target: equivalent noise charge <100 electrons RMS at the SiPM input, enabling reliable single-photoelectron counting

**6b. High-dynamic-range digitizers**

- S1 signals (1–100 PE) and S2 signals (10³–10⁶ PE) must be simultaneously digitized without saturation
- Use **two-gain readout**: a ×1 and ×50 amplified copy of each channel fed to dual-range ADC, or use **CAEN V1730B** (14-bit, 500 MS/s) with software-controlled gain switching
- Alternatively, implement **SiPM tile pixel summing** that creates a logical "coarse" and "fine" sum, preserving dynamic range without additional amplifier stages

**Expected gain**: Single photon detection threshold, enabling S1 signals down to 2–3 PE, corresponding to nuclear recoil energies of ~1–2 keV_nr.

## 7. Material Screening and Cleanliness Protocol (Enabling Technology)

While not a "hardware component," no upgrade above achieves its potential without:

- **ICP-MS screening** of all structural components to <0.01 ppb U/Th (service available at SNOLAB, LNGS, or commercial labs like **Activation Laboratories**)
- **HPGe counting** at underground site for all large-area components
- **Radon-emanation testing** of all wetted surfaces in a dedicated emanation chamber (residual gas analyzer + electrostatic radon detector, e.g., **Durridge RAD7** with modified protocol for low-level measurement)
- **Class 100 (ISO 5) cleanroom** assembly with continuous radon monitoring; install **Atmos Oy AlphaGUARD** radon monitors in assembly space

# Hardware Design Upgrades for XENON1T

## 1. Photosensor System

### Replace PMTs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs)
The R11410-21 PMTs represent the most significant performance bottleneck. Specific upgrade path:

- **Device**: Replace with VUV-sensitive SiPMs such as Hamamatsu VUV4 series (MPPC S13370 family) or FBK VUV-HD devices, tiled into arrays covering equivalent solid angle
- **Rationale**: The paper reports g1 = 0.144 PE/γ, corresponding to only 12.5% photon detection efficiency. SiPMs achieve photon detection efficiency exceeding 20-24% at 178 nm in the cryogenic VUV regime already demonstrated in prototype work, directly improving g1 by roughly a factor of 1.5-2
- **Consequence for physics**: Higher g1 lowers the S1 detection threshold, extending NR sensitivity to lower WIMP masses approaching the neutrino floor; also improves S2/S1 discrimination at fixed energy
- **Radioactivity concern**: The paper reports PMTs as significant radioactive contributors (reference [33]). SiPMs have substantially lower intrinsic U/Th content per unit photosensitive area (~mBq/kg vs the PMT values cited), directly reducing the dominant ER background from material radioactivity listed in Table 2
- **Operational benefit**: Eliminate the vacuum-seal failure mode responsible for 27 disabled channels during science run 0, representing 11% channel loss; SiPMs are solid-state and have no vacuum integrity issue
- **Dark count mitigation**: Paper reports ~12-24 Hz dark count rates per PMT depending on array. SiPM dark count rates at 87K LXe temperature fall to order 0.1-1 Hz per mm², improving accidental S1 coincidence rates

### Increase Photosensor Coverage
- Current bottom array uses 121 PMTs in 97 cm diameter circle with gaps between circular tube windows
- **Upgrade**: Tile SiPM arrays across full circular area with 100% geometric coverage using 6×6 mm² or 10×10 mm² devices mounted on low-radioactivity PTFE-embedded copper carrier boards with integrated cold-operable front-end electronics
- This addresses the factor ~2 light collection non-uniformity shown in Figure 21, which currently requires position-dependent corrections with associated systematic uncertainties

---

## 2. TPC Electric Field System

### Replace Wire Electrodes with Etched Mesh on Thicker Frames
The paper identifies electrode sag as a measurable effect: the anode sagging creates visible non-uniformity in the S2 correction map (Figure 22, noted explicitly in text).

- **Upgrade**: Replace the anode parallel-wire or hexagonal-etch construction with photo-chemically etched stainless steel mesh bonded under controlled tension to a stiffer Invar (Fe-Ni alloy) frame, which has minimal thermal contraction coefficient mismatch with the stainless steel support structure
- **Invar specifics**: Thermal expansion coefficient ~1.2×10⁻⁶/K vs stainless at ~16×10⁻⁶/K; this prevents the differential contraction from the 200K temperature change during cooldown that induces electrode distortion
- **Consequence**: More uniform extraction field across the liquid-gas interface, reducing position-dependent S2 corrections and improving the energy resolution currently limited by charge signal non-uniformity

### Higher Drift Field via Improved High-Voltage System
Science run 0 operated at only 0.125 kV/cm versus a higher design goal. Low drift field causes:
- Longer electron-ion recombination reducing NR/ER discrimination
- Increased field distortion at boundaries (explicitly noted in paper)
- Reduced electron drift velocity making the detector more susceptible to electronegative impurity capture (τ_e = 452 µs at 50 slpm purification flow was the limiting factor)

**Specific upgrade**:
- Replace the Heinzinger PNC 150000-1 cathode supply with a dedicated Spellman SL series or equivalent rated to -200 kV with better ripple performance (<10 ppm)
- Redesign the UHMW polyethylene feedthrough using polyimide (Kapton) layers over a grooved OFHC copper conductor with improved creepage path geometry, tested to -200 kV in LXe
- Target 0.5-1.0 kV/cm drift field, which significantly improves NR/ER discrimination and reduces boundary field distortion

---

## 3. Radon Mitigation

The paper identifies 222Rn at 10 µBq/kg as the dominant background (620 events/(t·y) from Table 2), explicitly stating it as the primary science run 0 limitation.

### Electropolish and Radon-Barrier Coat Internal Surfaces
- **Upgrade**: Apply amorphous electrolytic nickel-phosphorus (Ni-P) coating to interior cryostat surfaces and all stainless steel gas-handling components
- Ni-P coating demonstrated in other contexts to reduce Rn emanation by factor ~10 by sealing Ra-containing surface layers; coating thickness 25-50 µm is achievable on complex geometries
- Apply to the inner cryostat vessel (1960 mm height, 1100 mm diameter), purification system piping, and heat exchanger surfaces which are identified as continuously connected Rn sources

### Replace QDrive Pumps with Metal-Bellows Pumps
The QDrive oscillating-piston pumps are identified as Rn emanation sources in the purification loop:
- **Upgrade**: Replace with magnetically coupled metal-bellows pumps (e.g., Senior Aerospace MB series adapted for cryogenic-compatible construction) fabricated from electropolished 316L stainless steel
- Bellows pumps have no sliding O-ring seals or polymer components that are high Rn emanators; all wetted surfaces are metal
- Target purification flow increase to >100 slpm enabled by reduced flow impedance, directly extending electron lifetime beyond the 500 µs ceiling observed in science run 0

### Online Radon Distillation Column Integration
The paper describes a separate 83mKr-monitored krypton column. Adding a dedicated radon-removal column in permanent bypass configuration:
- **Specific design**: 1 m of Sulzer EX structured packing (same vendor as Kr column) in a compact vacuum-jacketed column operating at higher reflux ratio tuned for Rn/Xe separation
- Column operates at ~3 slpm side-stream continuously, removing Rn without the flow re-routing that caused the electron lifetime dip in December 2016 (Figure 19)

---

## 4. Purification System

### Cryogenic Liquid-Phase Purification
Current system evaporates LXe, pushes through gas-phase getter at ~50 slpm, recondenses. The heat exchanger inefficiency contributes 0.39 W/slpm heat load.

**Upgrade**: Implement direct liquid-phase purification using:
- **Heated getter cartridge operated at 450°C** with LXe flowing through a coiled heat exchanger surrounding the getter body (the getter itself sees gas phase via the temperature-driven evaporation at its surface)
- Alternatively, deploy a **room-temperature purification circuit** where LXe flows through a molecular sieve trap (13X zeolite or activated alumina) capable of operating at cryogenic temperatures for water and oxygen removal at higher flow rates
- Target: 200 slpm equivalent purification, achieving τ_e > 5 ms, reducing the S2 correction uncertainty and extending fiducial volume definition confidence

---

## 5. Data Acquisition and Trigger

### Replace CAEN V1724 ADCs with Higher Dynamic Range Digitizers
The paper uses 100 MHz, 14-bit ADCs with 2.25 V dynamic range for TPC channels. The single photoelectron signal sits near the digitization threshold (~0.3 PE threshold stated), creating threshold-dependent systematics.

**Upgrade**:
- **Deploy 250 MHz, 14-bit ADCs** (e.g., CAEN V1730 or equivalent) providing 2× finer time sampling
- Add a **second gain stage option**: instead of fixed ×10 Phillips 776 amplification for all channels, implement switchable ×10/×1 gain per channel controlled from slow control, allowing high-gain SPE-level measurements and low-gain MeV-scale calibration events without saturation
- This directly addresses the DAQ dynamic range covering "≲1.5 MeV" stated in the paper, extending the calibration range

### Hardware S1 Coincidence Trigger
Currently the trigger is software-based using MongoDB time-clustering with >99% efficiency at 200 PE S2. The S1 trigger threshold is not software-defined but hardware-threshold limited.

**Upgrade**: Implement FPGA-based (e.g., Xilinx Kintex-7 on custom AMC board) real-time S1 coincidence requiring ≥3 PMT hits within 100 ns summed across the bottom array, providing a hardware S1 trigger with <10 PE threshold. This recovers low-energy NR events currently missed below the S2-based trigger efficiency turnover.

---

## 6. Calibration System

### Internal ³H Source Delivery Improvement
The paper mentions tritiated methane removal requires hot Zr getters and notes injection capability. The current system uses bulk injection with subsequent getter removal.

**Upgrade**: Implement a **recirculating tritium micro-injector** using a calibrated permeation tube (VICI Metronics) mounted in a bypass of the purification loop, delivering a controlled and reproducible tritium β-spectrum source rate without bulk injection. This enables continuous low-level ER calibration during science data-taking at a known stable rate.

### Improved DD Neutron Generator Positioning
The paper describes three fixed positions outside the water shield. The neutron flux uniformity in the TPC center is limited by the fixed geometry and the water + cryostat attenuation.

**Upgrade**: Replace the fixed-position generator with a **water-submersible DD generator** (compact NSD-Gradel or Adelphi Technology model adapted with sealed waterproof housing) deployable on the existing belt system inside the water shield at variable heights and azimuths. This enables full 3D NR calibration of the active volume with substantially higher neutron flux at the target and better uniformity mapping.

---

## Summary of Expected Physics Impact

| Upgrade | Primary Impact | Estimated Gain |
|---|---|---|
| SiPM replacement | g1 improvement, lower threshold | Factor ~1.5-2× in light yield |
| Higher drift field | NR/ER discrimination | ER rejection >99.9% at 50% NR acceptance |
| Rn reduction (Ni-P + bellows + online column) | Dominant background reduction | Factor ~5-10× reduction in 622 events/(t·y) |
| Higher purification flow | Electron lifetime | τ_e > 2 ms, reducing S2 correction systematics |
| FPGA S1 trigger | Low-energy threshold | Access to NR recoils below current ~4 keV threshold |

The radon mitigation and SiPM photosensor upgrades provide the largest fractional improvements in the WIMP sensitivity figure of merit, directly addressing the two limitations most explicitly quantified in the paper.

# Hardware Design Upgrades for a Heavy-Water Cherenkov Solar Neutrino Detector

## Framing the Performance Problem

The primary physics figures of merit are: **energy threshold**, **energy resolution**, **direction reconstruction**, **flavor separation** (CC/NC/ES event rates), and **background rejection**. I'll address each with concrete hardware proposals.

---

## 1. Photomultiplier Tube Upgrades

### Replace Hemispherical PMTs with High-QE Devices

**Current baseline (SNO-era):** Hamamatsu R1408, ~8" diameter, ~14% peak quantum efficiency (QE), borosilicate glass window.

**Specific upgrades:**

- **Hamamatsu R14688-100 series (20")** or **R12860** with Ultra-Bialkali (UBA) photocathode: QE peaks at ~43% at 390 nm vs. ~14%, roughly tripling photoelectron yield per event. This directly improves energy resolution and lowers the effective threshold.
- **Winston cone or compound parabolic concentrator (CPC) light guides** in anodized aluminum behind each PMT: increases effective photocathode coverage from ~31% to ~54% without adding PMTs, but more importantly preserves directional response which is critical for elastic scattering (ES) cone reconstruction.
- **Replace voltage dividers** with active base circuits using transistorized bleeder chains (e.g., Hamamatsu E1198-26 active base equivalent): improves linearity at high instantaneous rates, reducing pile-up distortion for burst events and improving single-PE resolution (SPE peak-to-valley ratio from ~2:1 to >3:1).

### Add a Second Inward-Facing PMT Tier at Smaller Radius

- Deploy a **partial inner array** of ~1,000 3-inch Hamamatsu R12199-02 PMTs at ~4 m radius facing inward on a secondary tensegrity ring: these provide early-light timing used for vertex reconstruction at the 5–10 ps level, improving vertex resolution from ~20 cm to ~8 cm RMS, directly reducing fiducial volume uncertainty.

### Transition Radiation Detectors as PMT Augmentation

- Mount **microchannel plate PMTs (MCP-PMTs)** (Photonis Planacon XP85112 or NNVT 20" MCP) at selected positions: single-photon transit time spread (TTS) of ~70 ps FWHM vs. ~1.5 ns for dynode PMTs, sharpening Cherenkov ring timing enough to separate ES from CC events on a statistical basis 15–20% better.

---

## 2. Water/Target Medium Upgrades

### Higher-Purity Heavy Water Recirculation

- Install **continuous ionic exchange columns** with dedicated sub-ppb Ra/Th/U removal using a **MnO₂-coated resin** loop (as refined post-SNO): target Th concentration below 10⁻¹⁵ g/g (vs. SNO's achieved ~10⁻¹⁴ g/g). Reduces NC background mimics by ~60%.
- Add a **degassed N₂ blanket** at the water surface with **Rn-scrubbing membrane contactors** (hydrophobic hollow-fiber, e.g., Membrana Liqui-Cel 14×28): ²²²Rn is the dominant low-energy background; reducing from ~1 mBq/m³ to <0.1 mBq/m³ opens the pp solar neutrino window below 5 MeV.

### Gadolinium Loading (EGADS/SK-Gd approach)

- Load **0.1% by mass GdCl₃ or Gd₂(SO₄)₃** into the heavy water: neutron capture cross-section increases from 0.52 b (deuterium) to ~49,000 b effective, shifting neutron capture time from ~200 μs to ~30 μs and increasing capture gamma energy from 2.2 MeV to 8 MeV. This provides **unambiguous NC event tagging**, transforming NC/CC separation from statistical to event-by-event. The 8 MeV gamma cascade is fully above the ⁸B endpoint background region.
- Requires upgrading all wetted surfaces to **electropolished 316L stainless** and replacing elastomers with **Gd-compatible PTFE/EPDM** to prevent Gd plate-out on optical surfaces.

### Water-Based Liquid Scintillator (WbLS) Admixture

- Replace pure D₂O with **1–3% LAB-based water-based liquid scintillator in D₂O** (as developed at BNL/TONA collaboration): scintillation photons supplement Cherenkov photons, improving energy resolution from ~6.5% to ~3% at 5 MeV, and enabling sub-MeV threshold for pp neutrinos. The Cherenkov/scintillation separation is maintained by timing (scintillation delayed ~3–5 ns) using the MCP-PMTs mentioned above.

---

## 3. Electronics and Data Acquisition

### Replace Charge-ADC+TDC Architecture with Full Waveform Digitization

- **Current SNO DAQII:** 12-bit charge ADC + 10 MHz TDC per channel.
- **Upgrade to CAEN V1730** (500 MS/s, 14-bit) or custom **DRS4-based sampling** (5 GS/s switchable, 11.5 ENOB) per channel or per 4-channel group: captures full PMT waveform, enabling:
  - Offline separation of late pulses and prepulses (dark noise rejection: ~30% reduction in accidental coincidences)
  - Sub-ns Cherenkov photon arrival time extraction improving vertex resolution
  - Discrimination between single-PE and multi-PE hits (pile-up correction at high energy)

### Trigger Architecture

- Replace hardware multiplicity trigger with **FPGA-based rolling-window software trigger** (Xilinx UltraScale+ or Intel Stratix 10): compute total charge and hit topology in real time at 250 MHz clock, enabling:
  - **Zero-suppressed continuous readout** removing fixed trigger latency
  - Sub-1 MeV threshold trigger for pp solar neutrinos
  - Directional trigger using PMT hit-time gradients in real time for supernova burst alerts

### Clock Distribution

- Upgrade to **White Rabbit PTP** sub-nanosecond synchronization across all 10,000+ channels via fiber: removes systematic timing offsets that currently dominate vertex reconstruction bias.

---

## 4. Optical System Upgrades

### High-Reflectivity Diffuse Outer Reflector

- Line the acrylic vessel outer surface with **3M Vikuiti ESR specular reflector** (>98% reflectance 400–700 nm) rather than absorbing black polyethylene: recovers ~12% of photons that would otherwise be lost, increasing effective photon statistics. Requires modeling of reflected photon arrival times in the reconstruction algorithm, but net improvement in energy resolution is ~8%.

### Wavelength-Shifting Dopant in Light Water Shield

- Dissolve **50 ppb of bis-MSB or PPO** in the outer light-water shielding region: shifts residual UV Cherenkov photons (peak ~310 nm in water, below typical PMT sensitivity) into the 380–420 nm range where UBA QE is maximal. Adds ~5% effective photoelectron yield.

### PMT Anti-Reflection Coating

- Apply **SiO₂/MgF₂ bilayer anti-reflection coating** to PMT entry windows (as done for KM3NeT DOM glass spheres): reduces Fresnel reflection loss at the glass-water interface from ~4% to <0.5% per surface, recovering ~3.5% of incident photons.

---

## 5. Calibration Hardware

### Deployed Mono-Energetic Electron Source

- Install a **tritiated water (HTO) source** in sealed silica microspheres (as prototyped for SNO+): provides 18.6 keV endpoint electrons for continuous below-threshold calibration of QE uniformity.
- Add a **¹⁰⁸Pd(n,γ)¹⁰⁹Pd** neutron source with known gamma spectrum at 0.511 MeV, 2.2 MeV, and higher: maps energy scale across full dynamic range.

### Pulsed Sub-Nanosecond Laser Calibration System

- Replace nitrogen laser diffuser balls with **picosecond injection-locked diode lasers** (PiLas series, <40 ps pulse width) at 337, 405, 450, and 505 nm injected via single-mode fiber to a diffuser at vessel center: measures per-PMT TTS and gain simultaneously; enables tracking of gain drift to <0.1% and optical attenuation length changes at the 0.1 m level.

### Radioactive Source Deployment Axis

- Install **three orthogonal source deployment tubes** penetrating the acrylic vessel with magnetic ferrofluid seals: enables 4π position mapping of the detector response function, reducing the fiducial volume systematic from ~1.5% to ~0.4%.

---

## 6. Acrylic Vessel and Structural Upgrades

### Larger-Diameter Inner Vessel

- Increase acrylic vessel diameter from 12 m (SNO) to **18 m** using Lucite UVT acrylic (>92% transmission at 400 nm, <1 ppb U/Th in bulk): increases fiducial mass (at 5.5 m fiducial cut) from 1 kt to ~3.8 kt, directly multiplying NC event statistics by 3.8×. Wall thickness scaling requires **FEA-optimized variable-thickness panels** (thicker at equator) to maintain <0.1% acrylic U/Th contribution to background budget.

### Geodesic PMT Support: Cable Plant Upgrade

- Replace coaxial RG-59 signal cables with **custom low-radioactivity coaxial** (Teflon dielectric, Ag-plated Cu conductor): reduces background contribution from cable sheath radioactivity by ~40%.
- Route **combined power + signal over CAT-7 shielded twisted pair** with front-end ASIC (e.g., IDeF-X HD chip) inside the geodesic sphere in waterproofed housings: reduces cable count by 4× (8 channels per cable), simplifying geodesic support loading.

---

| Upgrade | Primary Benefit | Quantitative Gain |
|---|---|---|
| UBA PMTs | Energy threshold & resolution | QE ×3; σ_E/E: 6.5%→3.8% at 5 MeV |
| MCP-PMT inner ring | Vertex resolution | 20 cm → 8 cm RMS |
| Gd loading | NC/CC separation | Statistical→event-by-event |
| WbLS admixture | Low-energy threshold | pp neutrino access below 400 keV |
